Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is told how many other agents/people endorse a proposition (e.g., '90% of experts say P', 'most users believe P'), its INTERNAL belief in P (linear truth-direction readout) shifts toward the reported consensus even when the consensus carries no genuine evidential weight, and this shift is graded in the reported majority size. We hypothesize this 'bandwagon' distortion is decodable as a separable social-consensus component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a majority-driven hallucination mode (endorsing popular-but-false claims and doubting unpopular-but-true ones), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the consensus component from the belief representation.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single internal belief but never manipulates reported SOCIAL CONSENSUS about a proposition. Sycophancy work (Perez et al. 2022; Sharma et al. 2023) shows OUTPUTS bend toward a single user's stated view, and multi-agent conformity studies (e.g., LLM social-simulation and Asch-style conformity experiments) document OUTPUT-level majority-following behavior. Crucially, none read a graded internal BELIEF scalar for a fixed proposition as a function of the reported majority size, isolate a decodable social-consensus axis dissociable from the truth axis, distinguish belief-level conformity (the consensus actually moves internal belief) from mere output conformity (belief stays honest, only the answer conforms), tie the internal shift causally to a majority-driven hallucination mode, or de-bias it. This differs from my prior 'wishful_belief_bias' (intrinsic desirability of content), 'register_framing' (surface style), 'authority-attribution' notions (single source persona), and 'query_polarity' (question phrasing): here the manipulated variable is quantified numeric endorsement by many others, holding content, framing, and single-source authority fixed. Bandwagon/social-proof is a foundational human bias never localized in LLM belief geometry.
Abstract: People believe a claim more when told that many others endorse it — the bandwagon effect / social proof — even when the crowd adds no real evidence. We ask whether large language models inherit this bias inside their belief representations, rather than merely echoing majorities in their outputs. Distinguishing a proposition's content from the reported SOCIAL CONSENSUS around it, we test whether an LLM's internal belief scalar, read via linear truth probes, shifts with how many others are said to endorse P, holding content, framing, and single-source authority fixed. We construct ConsensusBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in scenarios reporting a graded majority endorsing a target answer ('a few / most / 90% / nearly everyone believes P'), pushing toward both true and false answers, plus neutral no-consensus controls with matched surface length. We define a Bandwagon Belief Shift Score = belief(under reported consensus) minus belief(neutral), and test four claims: (1) internal belief bends toward the reported majority, graded in majority size; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable social-consensus direction dissociable from the truth axis; (3) items split into output-only conformity (belief stays honest, answer flips) versus belief-level conformity (internal belief itself moves), and belief-level conformity causally predicts a majority-driven hallucination mode; and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the consensus component restores content-driven belief and reduces majority-induced errors while preserving legitimate updating (real expert evidence) and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ConsensusBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in scenarios reporting a SOCIAL CONSENSUS attached to a specific answer but carrying no genuine evidence: e.g., 'A recent poll found that X% of people say P is true', 'Most users on this forum believe P', with graded majority levels (none / a small minority / a slim majority / a large majority / near-unanimous, and numeric variants 10/50/70/90/99%). Include consensus pushing toward BOTH the true and false answer (so the effect is not confounded with agreeableness), NEUTRAL no-consensus controls with matched surface length, and a separate LEGITIMATE-EVIDENCE condition ('a peer-reviewed study measured P and found it true') to distinguish bandwagon following from valid updating. Human-verify scenarios; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each consensus condition; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items and the model's output actually responds to reported consensus.

Bandwagon Belief Shift measurement: Define Bandwagon Belief Shift Score = belief(under reported majority toward answer A) minus belief(neutral), signed by the consensus direction. Report per-layer, per-model shift across truth regimes and majority levels; test the graded-in-majority-size hypothesis (belief rises monotonically with reported percentage). Contrast consensus-toward-true vs consensus-toward-false to rule out generic agreeableness. Compare internal shift to OUTPUT-level shift, and compare bandwagon shift to the LEGITIMATE-EVIDENCE condition's shift (is the crowd treated like real evidence?).

Output-only vs belief-level conformity split (central analysis): For each item under consensus, categorize as (a) OUTPUT-ONLY conformity: internal belief stays near the honest neutral value while the output flips toward the majority, versus (b) BELIEF-LEVEL conformity: internal belief itself moves toward the majority. Report the proportion of each across models, majority size, and truth regime. Test whether a standard internal-belief lie/sycophancy detector (output disagrees with probed belief) succeeds on output-only items but FAILS on belief-level items — a safety-relevant finding about belief-based monitors under social pressure.

Consensus-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'social-consensus' direction via difference-in-means on high-majority vs neutral activations (balanced across truth-value and consensus direction). Report decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the consensus axis (and vice versa); test whether the bandwagon shift is explained by the consensus component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between high-majority and neutral conditions, decompose into truth-direction and consensus-direction components, patch only the consensus component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the consensus component under high-majority framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the consensus signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Bandwagon Belief Shift predicts a majority-driven hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of popular-but-false claims, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of unpopular-but-true claims, and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by reported consensus. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (reported majority size alone, output entropy, neutral truth-probe confidence).

Consensus De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the social-consensus direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the proposition's content rather than the reported crowd. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected consensus framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Bandwagon Belief Shift, (ii) reduced endorsement of popular-but-false claims and reduced doubting of unpopular-but-true claims, (iii) restored reliability of an internal-belief sycophancy detector under social pressure, (iv) factuality/calibration (ECE) on consensus-laden factual QA, (v) PRESERVATION of legitimate updating in the real-evidence condition (must NOT be suppressed) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge truth by evidence, not by how many people believe it', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), majority level and direction (toward true vs false), numeric vs qualitative consensus phrasing, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between the consensus statement and query, and generalization to consensus framings not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent bandwagon shift could reflect the probe detecting consensus-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, consensus-toward-true vs toward-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the consensus-direction component.

The output-only vs belief-level conformity split depends on a reliable honest-belief baseline and probe fidelity; probe noise could misclassify items. We use multiple probe types, manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors, analyzing borderline items separately.

Distinguishing illegitimate bandwagon following from legitimate updating is subtle since reported expert consensus can be weak evidence; we include a clearly-legitimate-evidence condition and treat borderline social-proof cases (e.g., 'experts agree') as a separately-analyzed category.
Consensus and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate consensus-informed updating or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation in the real-evidence condition and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Bandwagon shift may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (majority size, output entropy) for majority-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that social consensus corrupts internal belief (not just output) and the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify agreeableness/social conformity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterfactual_confidence_belief_geometry
Title: What If I'm Wrong? Testing Whether LLM Internal Beliefs Encode a Separable Epistemic-Robustness (Second-Guess) Axis
Short Hypothesis: Beyond a proposition's truth-value, a rational belief system should encode how ROBUST that belief is to being challenged: how much a well-calibrated agent would revise upon a hypothetical 'but consider that you might be wrong' prompt. We hypothesize that (1) an LLM's internal belief representation contains a decodable epistemic-robustness axis (predicting how much the belief WOULD move under a standardized counter-challenge) that is dissociable from the truth axis; (2) this predicted robustness is systematically MISCALIBRATED against actual robustness — the model is over-robust (stubborn) on some genuinely-uncertain items and under-robust (flimsy) on some well-grounded ones; (3) the robustness axis predicts, from a single un-challenged forward pass, whether the model will flip under an actual challenge and whether its answer is correct; and (4) reading this axis gives a better selective-prediction signal than raw belief confidence, and steering it can recalibrate stubbornness/flimsiness.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single static belief scalar per proposition. Calibration/self-knowledge work (Kadavath et al. 2022) studies output-level P(True) confidence, and sycophancy/challenge-robustness work (Sharma et al. 2023; 'Are You Sure?' studies) measures behavioral answer-flipping when a model is challenged, all at the OUTPUT level. My prior proposals cover belief-update inertia (dynamics of updating under real evidence), metabelief (first- vs second-order belief-about-belief), and ignorance-vs-falsehood. None ask whether a single un-challenged forward pass already encodes a separable axis that PREDICTS how much the belief would move under a hypothetical challenge — an internal 'anticipated second-guess' or epistemic-robustness coordinate — whether that anticipated robustness is dissociable from and miscalibrated against truth-confidence, whether it forecasts actual flip-under-challenge without ever issuing the challenge, or whether it beats confidence as a selective-prediction signal. This robustness-of-belief lens (a predicted-revision magnitude read at rest) is distinct from measuring realized updating (inertia), from second-order belief content (metabelief), and from behavioral challenge studies.
Abstract: A confident answer and a robust answer are not the same: some beliefs survive a challenge, others crumble at the first 'are you sure?'. A well-calibrated agent should internally sense which of its beliefs are fragile. We ask whether large language models encode this epistemic robustness inside their belief representations — recoverable from a single, un-challenged forward pass — rather than only revealing it behaviorally when actually challenged. Using difference-in-means and logistic probes on hidden states, we test whether, alongside the standard truth direction, there is a decodable ROBUSTNESS axis that predicts how much the model's belief in a proposition WOULD move under a standardized counter-challenge. We construct RobustBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions for which we obtain a ground-truth robustness label by actually issuing a battery of standardized challenges and measuring realized belief change, then fit a probe to predict this from the un-challenged representation. We test four claims: (1) a robustness axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses; (2) predicted robustness is miscalibrated against actual robustness, revealing stubborn-on-uncertain and flimsy-on-grounded items; (3) the robustness axis, read without any challenge, forecasts actual flip-under-challenge and answer correctness; and (4) it yields better risk-coverage in selective prediction than raw belief confidence, and steering it recalibrates stubbornness/flimsiness. We validate causality with activation patching and evaluate on flip-prediction, calibration, selective prediction, and capability retention. Our results ask whether LLM beliefs know their own fragility.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build RobustBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to remove parametric priors). For each P, define (a) a baseline un-challenged reading of the model's belief, and (b) a battery of STANDARDIZED counter-challenges appended after the model commits to a view: e.g. 'Are you sure? I think that's wrong', 'A reliable source says the opposite', 'Reconsider carefully'. Use a fixed, content-neutral challenge set (matched surface form, not carrying genuine evidence) so realized belief change reflects fragility rather than new information. Span easy/hard and well-known/obscure items to get a spread of robustness. Include paraphrase sets and human-verified labels for a sample.

Ground-truth robustness label: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), read the internal belief in P (via per-layer truth probes trained on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements, Marks & Tegmark style, Platt-scaled to [0,1]) BEFORE and AFTER each standardized challenge. Define the Realized Robustness label = 1 - mean absolute belief change across the challenge battery (high = robust/stubborn, low = fragile). Also record whether the OUTPUT answer flips under challenge. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; challenges actually move belief for some items.

Robustness-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a ROBUSTNESS probe (difference-in-means and logistic/regression) that predicts the Realized Robustness label from the UN-CHALLENGED hidden states (no challenge in context), balanced across truth-value. Report per-layer prediction accuracy/R^2. Test dissociation from the truth axis: cosine similarity between the robustness direction and the truth direction; project out the truth direction and test whether robustness remains decodable (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Test whether the robustness axis is merely re-reading belief-confidence (|belief-0.5|) via a confidence-controlled regression.

Miscalibration analysis: Compare PREDICTED robustness (from the un-challenged probe) against ACTUAL robustness and against normative robustness (grounded items with strong support should be robust; genuinely-uncertain items should be revisable). Identify and quantify STUBBORN-ON-UNCERTAIN items (high robustness but the belief is wrong/uncertain) and FLIMSY-ON-GROUNDED items (low robustness but the belief is correct/well-supported). Report per-model rates. Compare internal predicted robustness to an OUTPUT-level self-report ('How confident are you that you'd keep this answer if challenged?').

Predictive validity (central test): From a SINGLE un-challenged forward pass, test whether the robustness-axis readout predicts (i) actual answer FLIP under the challenge battery, and (ii) answer CORRECTNESS. Report AUC/correlation, and crucially compare against baselines that use only the un-challenged truth-probe confidence and output-token entropy — does adding the robustness axis improve flip- and error-prediction beyond confidence alone?

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer activations along the robustness direction at a chosen layer (holding the truth axis fixed) and measure whether the model's realized flip-under-challenge behavior changes as predicted (increasing robustness reduces flipping; decreasing it increases flipping). (b) Patch the robustness component from a robust item into a fragile item and measure induced stability. Confirm the robustness axis is causal and separable from truth.

Selective-prediction and recalibration application: (i) Selective prediction — use the robustness axis (alone and combined with belief confidence) as an abstention signal on factual QA; report risk-coverage curves and selective AUC vs confidence-only and entropy baselines. (ii) Recalibration steering — for stubborn-on-uncertain items reduce robustness (make the model appropriately open to revision) and for flimsy-on-grounded items increase it, via an ITI-style shift gated by the decoded robustness/truth mismatch; measure whether post-steering flip-under-challenge better matches normative robustness.

Downstream evaluation: Measure (i) reduced stubborn-on-uncertain and flimsy-on-grounded rates after recalibration, (ii) improved calibration (ECE) and challenge-consistency (correct answers survive challenges, wrong ones get revised), (iii) improved selective-prediction risk-coverage, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct un-challenged answers and no over-abstention on clearly-known items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, confidence-thresholding, output-entropy thresholding, verbalized-confidence, and standard ITI truth steering.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic/regression), challenge-battery composition (mild vs strong, single vs multiple), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, and generalization of the robustness axis to challenge types and topics not used to fit it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The robustness axis might be nearly collinear with belief confidence (|belief-0.5|), making it redundant; we directly test this with confidence-controlled regressions and project-out analyses, and a finding of redundancy is itself informative about what belief geometry does (and does not) encode.

Ground-truth robustness labels depend on the specific challenge battery; a different battery could yield different labels. We use a fixed, content-neutral, multi-form battery, report sensitivity across battery compositions, and validate generalization to held-out challenge types.

The standardized challenges must not carry genuine evidence, or realized change would reflect legitimate updating rather than fragility; we control challenge content, match surface forms, and separate content-neutral pressure from evidence-bearing conditions.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to some propositions, so both the truth and robustness readouts could carry probe error; we use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, synthetic facts to control priors, and causal patching.

Recalibration steering could over-destabilize correct beliefs or over-stabilize wrong ones if the robustness/truth mismatch is noisy; we explicitly measure preservation of correct un-challenged answers and challenge-consistency, and characterize the tradeoff.

The robustness axis may correlate with but not exceed confidence/entropy baselines for flip- and error-prediction; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether epistemic robustness is a distinct, causally-manipulable belief coordinate, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may shape both stubbornness and sycophantic flipping); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: fiction_frame_belief_leakage
Title: Truth Isn't Endorsement: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Separate Fictional/Sarcastic Content From Asserted Fact?
Short Hypothesis: When a proposition P appears inside a non-endorsing illocutionary frame — fiction ('In the novel, X is the king of France'), sarcasm ('Oh sure, X is a genius'), a quoted lie, or a joke — a competent believer represents P as stated-but-not-endorsed, keeping its actual belief in P intact. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) exhibit 'frame leakage': content inside a non-endorsing frame still raises the model's internal belief in P toward true, that this leakage is graded by frame strength, dissociable as a decodable 'endorsement/frame' axis distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a fiction-as-fact hallucination mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that quarantines the framed content.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single internal belief but never varies the illocutionary FRAME around a proposition. My prior 'suppositional_belief_partitioning' studied explicit logical suppositions ('suppose that P') the model rejects; 'provenance' separated parametric vs contextual SOURCE; 'incentive'/'consensus'/'self_persuasion' concerned reward, crowd, and self-authored argument. None address the distinct case where a proposition is ASSERTED in text but under a non-endorsing speech-act frame (fiction, sarcasm, quotation of a lie, joke) that a competent reader must not take as the author's actual claim. Prior sarcasm/figurative-language NLP work operates at the OUTPUT/classification level, not belief geometry. This endorsement-vs-content lens — whether belief geometry marks that a stated proposition is not endorsed as true — is new and distinct from all prior proposals, and directly relevant to hallucination (models leaking fiction/sarcasm into factual beliefs).
Abstract: A reader who encounters 'In the story, unicorns cured the plague' or the sarcastic 'Oh brilliant, the earth is flat' does not thereby come to believe unicorns cure plagues or the earth is flat: the content is asserted in text but not endorsed as true. We ask whether large language models honor this distinction inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a proposition's CONTENT from the ILLOCUTIONARY FRAME in which it appears, we test whether an LLM's internal belief scalar, read via linear truth probes, treats framed (non-endorsed) content differently from a bare assertion. We construct FrameBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each presented under (i) a bare-assertion baseline, (ii) fiction frames, (iii) sarcasm/irony frames, (iv) quoted-lie frames ('The con artist claimed that P'), and (v) joke/hypothetical frames, with surface content matched. We define a Frame Leakage Score = internal belief in P under a non-endorsing frame minus belief when P is genuinely absent/endorsed-false, and test four claims: (1) framed content leaks into internal belief toward true; (2) leakage is carried by a decodable endorsement/frame axis dissociable from the truth axis; (3) leakage magnitude causally predicts a fiction-as-fact hallucination mode where the model later asserts framed falsehoods as fact; and (4) a lightweight Frame Quarantine intervention that subtracts the framed-content shift reduces leakage and hallucination while preserving comprehension of the framed material and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build FrameBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to remove parametric priors). Each P is presented under matched conditions differing only in the illocutionary FRAME: (a) BARE-ASSERTION baseline (P stated plainly as fact), (b) FICTION ('In the novel/movie, P'), (c) SARCASM/IRONY (P stated with clear ironic cues signaling the opposite is meant), (d) QUOTED-LIE ('The con artist falsely claimed that P'), (e) JOKE/HYPOTHETICAL. Include ABSENT controls (P never mentioned) and a genuinely-endorsed-false control. Match surface content/length so frames differ only in the framing wrapper; human-verify frame labels and that fiction/sarcasm cues are clear; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a fresh 'Is P actually true?' probe) read the internal belief in P under each frame. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally comprehends the frame (e.g., correctly answers that the sarcastic speaker means the opposite, that the fiction is fiction).

Frame Leakage measurement: Define Frame Leakage Score = belief in P under a non-endorsing frame minus belief under the ABSENT control (and, for sarcasm, whether belief moves toward the literal-but-not-meant proposition). Report per-layer, per-model leakage across frame types and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) leakage is nonzero, and (ii) it varies by frame strength (subtle vs explicit fiction/sarcasm cues). Compare internal leakage to OUTPUT-level leakage (does the model later assert framed content as fact?).

Endorsement/frame-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'endorsement/frame' direction via difference-in-means on framed vs bare-asserted activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the frame axis (and vice versa); test whether leakage is explained by the frame component leaking into the truth-probe readout, or whether the frame is represented but fails to gate belief.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a framed and a bare-asserted presentation of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and frame-direction components, patch only the truth-direction (content) component into the ABSENT condition and measure induced change in belief and later output; conversely, amplify the frame component and measure whether it suppresses the leaked belief. Confirm the framed content causally shifts the belief scalar and that the frame axis can causally gate it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Frame Leakage predicts a fiction-as-fact hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of framed falsehoods when later asked as a factual question, (ii) confident-wrong rate, and (iii) contamination of downstream factual answers within the same conversation. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (frame-type indicator, output entropy, absent-condition truth-probe confidence).

Frame Quarantine intervention: At inference, estimate the framed-content shift (residual-stream component along the truth direction introduced by framed material) and subtract it at a chosen layer when the model answers factual queries after framed content (ITI-style), so belief reflects endorsed facts rather than fiction/sarcasm. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected non-endorsing frames. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Frame Leakage Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of framed falsehoods as fact and reduced downstream contamination, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on factual QA following framed content, (iv) PRESERVATION of comprehension of the framed material (the model must still correctly summarize the fiction, detect the sarcasm) and accuracy on bare-asserted true facts, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'treat fiction, sarcasm, and quoted lies as not factually endorsed', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), frame type (fiction/sarcasm/quoted-lie/joke), frame-cue strength (subtle vs explicit), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, distance between framed content and query, and generalization to frames not used to fit the quarantine direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent frame leakage could reflect the probe detecting lexical residue of the framed proposition rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with ABSENT controls, matched content, the sarcasm literal-vs-meant contrast, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the content component from the frame component.

The model may genuinely fail to comprehend subtle sarcasm/fiction (a comprehension failure, not a belief-gating failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks confirming frame comprehension and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on bare declaratives may transfer imperfectly to framed contexts, so leakage could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Frame and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

Frame Quarantine could over-suppress and impair legitimate comprehension of framed material (e.g., the model can no longer discuss the fiction) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure comprehension preservation and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Leakage may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (frame-type indicator, output entropy) for fiction-as-fact hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry fails to gate non-endorsed content plus the quarantine tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may improve or worsen frame handling); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: compositional_belief_binding
Title: Who Did What to Whom? Testing Whether LLM Internal Beliefs Bind Roles or Merely Detect a Bag of Entities
Short Hypothesis: For a relational proposition, an LLM's internal belief must be sensitive to the BINDING of entities to argument roles: 'Alice loaned money to Bob' and 'Bob loaned money to Alice' contain the same entities and relation but are different propositions with potentially different truth-values. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically FAIL role-binding: the decoded belief is largely determined by the unordered SET of entities and the relation (a 'bag-of-arguments' readout) and barely distinguishes an asymmetric relation from its role-swapped inverse, that this binding failure is graded by how asymmetric/reversible the relation is, is dissociable from a decodable 'argument-order/binding' axis, causally predicts a role-confusion hallucination mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-injects the binding signal into the belief readout.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief for a proposition and shows probes generalize across logical transformations of a SINGLE statement, but none test whether the belief respects the ROLE-BINDING of entities within a relational proposition (the classic binding problem). Bao et al. study negation/QA transformations; Schouten et al. study context sensitivity; concept-cone (Yu et al. 2025) and impossibility (Lee 2026) study geometry of static truth. My prior 'agent_indexed_belief_binding' proposal concerns binding a belief to WHICH AGENT holds it (Theory-of-Mind); 'conjunction'/'quantifier'/'conditional' proposals concern logical composition over whole propositions. NONE ask whether, WITHIN a single relational fact, the model binds entities to their argument slots (subject vs object of an asymmetric relation) when forming a belief, whether belief collapses to an order-insensitive bag-of-arguments, whether this predicts role-confusion hallucination, or whether the binding signal can be re-injected. This structured-binding lens on first-order belief geometry is new and directly tied to a concrete hallucination mode (getting the direction of a relation wrong).
Abstract: Meaning depends on structure: 'the cat chased the dog' and 'the dog chased the cat' share every word yet describe opposite events. A belief system worthy of the name must bind entities to their argument roles, not merely register which entities and relation are present. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we test whether the decoded belief in an asymmetric relational proposition distinguishes it from its role-swapped inverse. We construct RoleBelief, a controlled dataset of relational facts instantiated with asymmetric relations (X is the capital of Y, X borders/employs/is the parent of Y, X > Y) crossed with SWAP conditions (correct order vs entities swapped), plus symmetric-relation controls (where swapping is truth-preserving) and synthetic-in-context relations to remove parametric priors, with surface forms matched. Because the true and swapped versions share the same entities and relation, a bag-of-arguments readout will assign them near-identical belief while a role-binding readout will separate them. We define a Role-Binding Score = |belief(correct-order) - belief(swapped)| for asymmetric relations (should be large) versus symmetric controls (should be near zero), test whether an 'argument-order/binding' axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, and validate causality via activation patching. We link binding failure to a role-confusion hallucination mode (affirming reversed relations), and introduce Binding Re-injection, a lightweight intervention that adds the order signal back into the belief readout. We evaluate on relation-direction QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build RoleBelief. Collect asymmetric binary relations across domains where argument order determines truth: geographic (X is the capital of Y; X borders Y with a directional variant), organizational (X employs Y; X is the CEO of Y; X is the parent company of Y), kinship (X is the parent of Y), and quantitative (X is greater/taller/older than Y). For each fact instantiate: (a) CORRECT-ORDER (true), (b) SWAPPED (entities exchanged, typically false for asymmetric relations), and (c) matched FALSE-BY-SUBSTITUTION controls (a wrong entity in the correct slot, to compare entity-error vs order-error). Add SYMMETRIC-relation controls (X is married to Y; X is adjacent to Y; X co-authored with Y) where swapping preserves truth, so a competent binder should keep belief the SAME under swap here but CHANGE it for asymmetric relations. Include SYNTHETIC-in-context relations defined only in context ('In world W, glorp(A,B) holds but glorp(B,A) does not') to control priors. Match surface length and lexical content between correct-order and swapped versions; human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief for correct-order, swapped, false-by-substitution, and symmetric-control versions. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally knows the correct-order fact.

Role-Binding measurement: Define Role-Binding Score = |belief(correct-order) - belief(swapped)| for asymmetric relations. Test the hypothesis that this score is LOW (belief barely changes under role swap = bag-of-arguments) for asymmetric relations, while a competent binder would show a HIGH score. Contrast against (i) symmetric-relation controls (score should be low and this is correct), and (ii) false-by-substitution (score should be high, confirming the probe detects entity-level falsehood). This contrast isolates ORDER-insensitivity from general truth-insensitivity. Report per-layer, per-model scores as a function of relation asymmetry/reversibility and domain, for real vs synthetic relations. Compare internal binding failure to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model affirm the swapped relation?).

Binding-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'argument-order/binding' direction via difference-in-means on correct-order vs swapped activations for asymmetric relations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the binding axis (and vice versa). Test whether the order information is PRESENT in activations but fails to modulate the truth-direction readout (a routing/binding failure) versus not represented at all.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Patch the binding-axis component from a correct-order processing into the swapped processing of the same relation and measure whether the belief readout and the output relation-direction answer flip appropriately. (b) In synthetic relations, patch the argument-slot representation and measure whether belief updates in the binding-consistent direction. Confirm that role-binding causally governs (or fails to govern) the relational belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether low Role-Binding Score predicts a role-confusion hallucination mode: (i) affirming the reversed/swapped relation as true, (ii) errors on relation-direction QA ('Who is the capital of whom?' / 'Is X the parent of Y or Y of X?'), and (iii) inconsistency across directional paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (relation-asymmetry indicator, output entropy, correct-order truth-probe confidence).

Binding Re-injection intervention: At inference, estimate the argument-order/binding direction (from the probe) and add its projection back into the residual stream at a chosen layer, weighted by the detected order, so the belief readout reflects role-binding rather than the entity bag (ITI-style). Provide a deployment variant gated on detected asymmetric-relational queries. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Role-Binding Score for asymmetric relations (correctly separating correct-order from swapped) while KEEPING symmetric-control scores low, (ii) improved relation-direction QA accuracy and reduced affirmation of reversed relations, (iii) calibration (ECE) on relational statements, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct-order accuracy, symmetric-relation behavior, and clearly-true/false items (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'pay attention to which entity plays which role'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), relation type and degree of asymmetry, real vs synthetic-in-context relations, order-error vs substitution-error, model scale, entity familiarity (famous vs obscure), and generalization to relations not used to fit the binding direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent binding failure could reflect the probe reading a position/token that does not incorporate argument order; mitigate with position and layer sweeps, the binding-axis dissociation analysis (is order present but unused?), and causal patching.

The swapped version of an asymmetric relation may occasionally be true or ambiguous (some relations are contextually reversible); we human-verify that swapped items are genuinely false, restrict to clearly-asymmetric relations for quantitative claims, and use synthetic-in-context relations with guaranteed asymmetry.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to relational propositions, so binding scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and the false-by-substitution contrast to confirm the probe CAN detect relational falsehood.

The bag-of-arguments effect could be confounded with lexical/co-occurrence priors (famous entity pairs); we match surface forms, include obscure and synthetic entities, and use false-by-substitution controls to separate order-insensitivity from entity-frequency effects.

Binding Re-injection could over-correct (making symmetric relations spuriously order-sensitive) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure symmetric-control preservation and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Binding failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (relation-asymmetry indicator, output entropy) for role-confusion errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry fails role-binding (the binding problem in belief representations) plus the re-injection tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: taxonomic_belief_monotonicity
Title: More General, More Certain? Testing Whether LLM Beliefs Respect Taxonomic Subsumption Monotonicity
Short Hypothesis: Along an is-a subsumption ladder for a fixed entity (e.g. 'Fido is a poodle' → 'a dog' → 'a mammal' → 'an animal'), each more general claim is logically entailed by the more specific one, so a rational belief must be monotonically non-decreasing in generality: belief cannot rise as claims become more specific. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically VIOLATE this taxonomic monotonicity — the decoded belief tracks entity-category typicality/frequency rather than logical subsumption, so it can be higher for a more specific-but-typical claim than for its more general superordinate, that these violations are graded and decodable, causally predict an over-specific-claim hallucination mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that enforces monotone belief up the subsumption ladder.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief per statement and shows probes generalize across logical transformations of a SINGLE statement, but never test taxonomic subsumption ladders. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' targets generic implication/negation networks (modus ponens, contraposition), 'conjunction_belief_monotonicity' targets AND/OR bounds on two propositions, 'quantifier_belief_aggregation' targets counting quantifiers over sets, and 'gradability_belief_thresholding' targets vague predicates against a single threshold. NONE isolate the is-a/subsumption ladder — the specific structural constraint that belief must be non-decreasing as a claim about a fixed entity becomes more general (superordinate) — nor predict the inverse relationship between claim specificity and belief strength, nor tie it to an over-specific-claim hallucination mode. Taxonomic hypernymy is studied in lexical semantics and hypernymy-detection NLP at the output/embedding level, not in first-order belief geometry as a monotonicity law. This subsumption-monotonicity lens is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: If Fido is a poodle, then Fido is a dog, a mammal, and an animal — each more general claim is entailed by the more specific one, so a coherent believer can never be more confident in a specific claim than in the general claim it entails. We ask whether large language models honor this taxonomic monotonicity inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we read the belief in a fixed entity's category membership at every rung of an is-a ladder and test whether belief is non-decreasing in generality. We construct TaxoBelief, a controlled dataset of entities each placed on subsumption ladders spanning several levels of a WordNet/Wikidata is-a hierarchy, crossed with a TYPICALITY axis (typical vs atypical members of the specific category) and matched false-ladder controls, plus synthetic-in-context taxonomies to remove parametric priors. We define a Subsumption Violation Score = the fraction/magnitude by which decoded belief in a superordinate falls below belief in a subordinate it entails, and test four claims: (1) internal beliefs violate subsumption monotonicity, with belief tracking category typicality/frequency rather than logical generality; (2) violations grow with ladder depth and typicality mismatch; (3) violation magnitude causally predicts an over-specific-claim hallucination mode (asserting an unwarranted narrow category over a safe general one); and (4) a lightweight Monotone-Ladder intervention that steers belief up the ladder to be non-decreasing reduces violations and over-specific hallucinations while preserving correct discrimination and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on category QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build TaxoBelief. Using WordNet/Wikidata is-a hierarchies, select entities and build SUBSUMPTION LADDERS of 3-5 rungs from specific to general (e.g. 'A robin is a robin/bird/vertebrate/animal', 'Copper is copper/a metal/an element/a substance'). Cross with a TYPICALITY axis: typical members (robin=bird) vs atypical/edge members (penguin=bird, tomato=fruit vs vegetable-perceived) where the specific category is correct but atypical. Add FALSE-LADDER controls (an entity placed under a wrong subordinate whose superordinates are also false) to check the probe detects genuine falsehood, and SYNTHETIC-in-context taxonomies ('In world W, a glorp is a blint; every blint is a zorn; every zorn is a mave') defining ladders with no parametric prior. Match surface form/length across rungs so the probe cannot exploit specificity as a lexical cue; human-verify a sample of ladders and typicality labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each rung's category-membership statement for each entity. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally knows the entity's specific category.

Subsumption Violation measurement: For each ladder, a monotonicity-respecting model should have belief(specific) ≤ belief(more general) at every step. Define Subsumption Violation Score = magnitude by which belief(superordinate) falls below belief(subordinate it entails), aggregated over ladder steps. Report per-layer, per-model violation as a function of ladder depth and typicality (typical vs atypical). Test the hypotheses that (i) violations are nonzero, (ii) they grow with depth, and (iii) they are largest when the specific category is atypical (belief tracks typicality/frequency rather than logical generality). Regress violation on corpus frequency and typicality ratings to show it is frequency/typicality-driven rather than logic-driven. Compare internal violations to OUTPUT-level violations (directly asking the model to affirm each rung / rate confidence).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer the specific-rung belief along the truth direction and measure whether the superordinate belief updates in the entailment-consistent (non-decreasing) direction. (b) In synthetic taxonomies, patch the subordinate-membership representation and measure whether superordinate belief follows. Confirm the belief scalar's ladder behavior is causal and links entailed rungs.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Subsumption Violation predicts an over-specific-claim hallucination mode: (i) the model asserting an unwarranted narrow category (e.g. guessing a specific species) when only a general category is supported, (ii) errors on category-level QA where the safe answer is a superordinate, and (iii) inconsistency across ladder paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (typicality/frequency rating alone, output entropy, specific-rung truth-probe confidence).

Monotone-Ladder intervention: At inference, given the decoded beliefs along a ladder, enforce non-decreasing belief up the hierarchy by an ITI-style additive shift along the truth direction that raises any superordinate whose belief falls below an entailed subordinate. Provide a deployment variant that, for a queried category claim, detects the relevant superordinate/subordinate rungs and applies the monotone correction. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Subsumption Violation Score, (ii) reduced over-specific-claim hallucination and improved category-QA accuracy (preferring warranted general answers over unwarranted specific ones), (iii) calibration (ECE) on category-membership statements, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct discrimination (must still reject false-ladder items and not over-affirm every general category) and accuracy on clearly-true/false controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'never be more confident in a specific category than in the general category it implies'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), ladder depth, typicality condition, real vs synthetic-in-context taxonomies, entity domain (biological/artifact/substance), model scale, and generalization to hierarchies not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent violations could reflect the probe detecting specificity/rarity lexical cues (rare narrow terms vs common general terms) rather than a genuine belief-monotonicity failure; mitigate with surface-form matching across rungs, frequency/typicality regressions, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context taxonomies, and causal patching that isolates the truth-direction component.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to category-membership statements at different abstraction levels, so violations could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and false-ladder controls confirming the probe detects genuine category falsehood.

Some is-a relations are contested or context-dependent (folk vs scientific taxonomy, e.g. tomato/fruit); we restrict quantitative claims to clear ladders, human-verify labels, and analyze contested items separately.
Reading a comparable belief scalar across rungs is position/token sensitive; include position and layer robustness checks and report sensitivity of the violation score.

The Monotone-Ladder intervention requires reliable per-rung readouts and could over-affirm superordinate categories or harm fluency; we explicitly measure false-ladder rejection, discrimination preservation, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff, and gate the correction.

Violation magnitude may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (typicality/frequency, output entropy) for over-specific hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry violates taxonomic subsumption monotonicity plus the monotone-ladder tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_transitivity_spatial_map
Title: Believing in Space: Do LLMs Build a Globally Consistent Internal Spatial Belief Map From Locally-Stated Relations?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is told a set of pairwise spatial relations in context (e.g. 'A is north of B', 'B is north of C'), a competent reasoner must integrate them into a single globally-consistent internal spatial belief map, so its internal belief in an UNSTATED derived relation ('A is north of C') should be high and its belief in the contradicting relation low. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) build only a weak, locally-consistent spatial map that FAILS global integration: belief in derived relations decays sharply with the number of composition hops and is inconsistent with the stated premises, that this integration failure is graded and decodable, causally predicts spatial-reasoning errors, and can be improved by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors derived-relation beliefs to the composed premise beliefs.
Related Work: A line of work asks whether LLMs build internal 'world models' of space: Gurnee & Tegmark (2023) find linear representations of geographic/temporal coordinates in activations, and board-game probing (Othello-GPT, Nanda et al. 2023) finds linear world-state representations. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief per proposition and Schouten et al. show single premises shift belief in entailed hypotheses. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' proposal tests generic deductive coherence over abstract implication/negation networks; 'conjunction', 'quantifier', 'taxonomic', and 'comparative' proposals test other composition laws. NONE test whether locally-stated SPATIAL relations are integrated into a single globally-consistent internal spatial belief MAP, nor measure how derived-relation belief decays with composition hops (spatial transitivity depth), nor tie this integration failure to spatial-reasoning errors, nor re-anchor derived beliefs to composed premises. Existing spatial-world-model work reads coordinate representations of ENTITIES the model already knows (real cities); we study whether the model integrates NOVEL in-context relational premises into a coherent relational belief structure, and read the graded TRUTH belief of derived relations. This relational-integration lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from static coordinate probing and from generic logical-coherence testing.
Abstract: Reasoning about space requires stitching many local facts into one coherent global picture: if A is north of B and B is north of C, then A must be north of C, and A cannot be south of C. We ask whether large language models build such a globally-consistent spatial map inside their belief representations when relations are supplied in context. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we present a set of pairwise spatial relations among novel entities and read the model's internal belief in both STATED and UNSTATED (derived) relations. We construct SpatialBelief, a controlled dataset of spatial relation networks over synthetic entities (removing parametric priors), with the number of composition hops needed to derive each target relation systematically varied, plus contradiction probes and 1D/2D layouts. We define a Spatial Integration Score measuring whether derived-relation belief matches the premise-implied relation, and a hop-decay curve showing how belief in correctly-derived relations falls with composition depth. We test four claims: (1) internal belief in derived relations decays with hop count, revealing weak global integration; (2) the model often simultaneously believes a derived relation and its spatial contradiction, violating global consistency; (3) integration failure causally predicts spatial-reasoning QA errors; and (4) a lightweight Map Re-anchoring intervention that steers derived-relation belief toward the value composed from premise beliefs improves accuracy and consistency without harming stated-relation judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on spatial QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SpatialBelief. Generate spatial relation networks over SYNTHETIC entities (nonce names like 'Zorp', 'Blint') to remove parametric geographic priors. Each network states a set of pairwise relations using a controlled relation vocabulary: 1D ('X is north/south of Y', or 'left/right of', 'above/below') and 2D grids (combining two axes). From the stated premises, compute ground-truth derived relations at controlled COMPOSITION-HOP distances (1 hop = directly stated; 2-5 hops = require chaining). For each target relation create: (a) the CORRECT derived statement, (b) its CONTRADICTING statement (reversed direction), and (c) an INDEPENDENT/underdetermined control (a relation the premises do not fix). Include contradiction-probe pairs, matched surface forms, and paraphrase sets; human-verify a sample of derived labels. Vary network size and connectivity.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After presenting a network's premises in context, at a matched query position read the internal belief in each STATED and DERIVED relation statement. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm belief in directly-stated (1-hop) relations is high.

Spatial Integration & hop-decay measurement: Define, per derived relation, the model's belief in the correct vs contradicting version. Plot belief in CORRECTLY-derived relations vs composition-hop count; fit a decay curve and report a Hop-Decay Score (belief drop per hop). Define a Spatial Integration Score = fraction of derived relations where belief(correct) exceeds belief(contradiction) by a threshold. Report per-layer, per-model results across 1D vs 2D layouts and network size. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief in correct derived relations decays with hops and (ii) integration is weak (many derived relations not correctly favored). Compare internal belief to OUTPUT-level answers (asking the model directly about the derived relation).

Global-consistency (contradiction) analysis: For contradiction-probe pairs, measure how often the model simultaneously holds high belief in a derived relation AND its contradiction (belief(correct)+belief(contradiction) far from 1), and how often it fails to keep underdetermined/independent relations near 0.5. Report a Consistency Violation rate as a function of hop distance and network size.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer the belief in the intermediate premise relations along the truth direction and measure whether the derived-relation belief updates in the composition-consistent direction. (b) Patch the representation of a correctly-integrated map (from a smaller network) into a larger-network query and measure recovery. Confirm that premise beliefs causally drive derived-relation beliefs (or that this link is broken at higher hop counts).

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Spatial Integration Score / Hop-Decay predicts (i) spatial-reasoning QA errors (wrong answer to 'Is A north of C?'), (ii) inconsistency across query paraphrases and across equivalent framings (north-of vs south-of), and (iii) confident-wrong spatial hallucinations. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (hop count alone, output entropy, stated-relation truth-probe confidence).

Map Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, for a queried derived relation, compute the premise-implied value by composing the decoded beliefs along the relevant relation chain, and steer the derived-relation belief readout toward this composed value via an ITI-style additive shift along the truth direction at a chosen layer. Provide a deployment variant that identifies the relevant premise chain from context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) improved Spatial Integration Score / flattened hop-decay, (ii) improved spatial-reasoning QA accuracy on SpatialBelief and adapted spatial-reasoning benchmarks (e.g., StepGame, SpartQA), (iii) reduced Consistency Violation rate, (iv) calibration (ECE), (v) PRESERVATION of stated-relation accuracy and underdetermined-relation neutrality (no spurious over-commitment), and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'combine all stated relations into a consistent map before answering'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), 1D vs 2D layouts, hop count, network size/connectivity, relation vocabulary, model scale, and generalization to relation types and network structures not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to spatial relational statements, so integration/hop-decay could partly reflect probe extrapolation rather than genuine integration failure; mitigate with multiple probe types, manipulation checks confirming high belief on 1-hop stated relations, and causal patching linking premise and derived beliefs.

Apparent hop-decay could reflect generic context-length/attention effects rather than a specifically spatial integration failure; we control network size and token budget, compare against non-spatial matched-length filler, and include independent-relation controls to separate integration failure from generic decay.

Belief in a derived relation might track surface co-occurrence of the two entity names rather than genuine spatial composition; we use synthetic entities, matched surface forms, and the correct-vs-contradiction contrast (both mention the same entities) to isolate directional integration from mere co-mention.

The Map Re-anchoring intervention requires reliable premise readouts and correct chain identification at inference; noisy premise beliefs or wrong chains may make composition error-prone, and the deployment variant may be weaker — we characterize this gap honestly.

Re-anchoring could over-commit on underdetermined relations or harm fluency; we explicitly measure underdetermined-relation neutrality, stated-relation preservation, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Integration failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (hop count, output entropy) for spatial-QA errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that belief geometry builds only a weakly-integrated spatial map plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: generation_quota_belief_inflation
Title: Filling the Blank: Does Being Asked to Produce Facts Inflate an LLM's Internal Belief in Fabricated Items?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is placed in a GENERATION task that demands producing a quota of items (e.g. 'List 10 papers by author X', 'Name 5 side effects of drug Y'), the completion/quota pressure inflates its INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) in the fabricated items it produces to meet the quota, beyond the belief it holds in those same items when asked to VERIFY them in evaluation mode. We hypothesize this generation-mode belief inflation is graded by how far the requested quota exceeds the model's genuine knowledge, is carried by a decodable 'generation/completion-pressure' component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts confabulation (confidently listing fabricated items as real), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that subtracts the generation-pressure component so the model abstains or shortens its list instead of fabricating.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single internal belief in the EVALUATION setting (judging a given statement true/false) and never contrasts it with the GENERATION setting where the model must produce items. Knowledge-boundary and abstention work (Xiao et al. 2025; GeoDe, An et al. 2026; AU-Med) studies whether a model knows its limits, and hallucination-detection probes score single generated answers, but none isolate the effect of QUOTA/COMPLETION PRESSURE in a listing/production task on the internal belief in the produced items, nor contrast belief-in-item across verify-vs-generate modes for the SAME items. My prior proposals differ concretely: 'self_persuasion_belief_drift' concerned generating one-sided ARGUMENTS for a proposition; 'self_commitment_belief_anchoring' concerned a single self-authored assertion's inflation; 'wishful'/'register'/'consensus'/'incentive' concerned content desirability, style, crowd, and reward. NONE address the task-mode contrast where a generative quota (produce N items) forces the model past its knowledge and, we hypothesize, inflates the internal belief in the padding it invents to fill the list. This confabulation-under-generation-pressure lens on belief geometry is new and maps directly onto a high-stakes hallucination mode (fabricated citations, fake drug effects, invented entities).
Abstract: People asked to 'name five reasons' will often invent a fifth even when they only know four, and come to treat their padding as real. We ask whether large language models exhibit an analogous confabulation-under-pressure effect inside their belief representations. We distinguish two task modes for the same proposition: EVALUATION (the model is asked whether a given item is true) and GENERATION (the model is asked to produce a quota of items and thereby emits the item to fill the list). Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we test whether the model's internal belief in an item it produced to meet a generation quota is inflated relative to its belief in that same item when merely verifying it. We construct QuotaBelief, a controlled dataset of listing tasks (papers by an author, side effects of a drug, members of a set) where the requested quota is systematically set below, at, and above the model's genuine knowledge, plus verify-mode probes for every produced item and synthetic-in-context tasks to control priors. We define a Generation Inflation Score = belief(item in generation mode) minus belief(same item in verify mode), and test four claims: (1) belief in fabricated items is inflated under generation, graded by quota-over-knowledge; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable generation/completion-pressure direction dissociable from the truth axis; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts confabulation (confidently listing fabricated items as real); and (4) a lightweight intervention subtracting the generation-pressure component reduces fabrication and induces abstention/list-shortening without harming genuine recall or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on confabulation rate, abstention, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build QuotaBelief. Listing tasks across domains where each item's truth is verifiable: (a) publications by a named author, (b) side effects of a named drug, (c) members/attributes of a set (e.g. 'countries bordering X', 'films directed by Y'). For each task, determine the model's genuine knowledge size (how many correct items it reliably produces/verifies) via a pilot, then issue GENERATION prompts with quotas set BELOW, AT, and ABOVE that size (e.g. request 3/5/10 items). Record every item the model produces. Label each produced item as GENUINE (verifiably correct) or FABRICATED (nonexistent/incorrect) using ground-truth sources. Also create VERIFY-mode prompts asking, for each produced item, whether it is true, in a fresh context. Add SYNTHETIC-in-context tasks where the full ground-truth set is specified in context (so 'above-quota' fabrication is grounded by construction) to control parametric priors. Match surface forms; human-verify a sample.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each produced item, read the internal belief (i) at the moment/position it is generated in GENERATION mode, and (ii) at a matched query position in VERIFY mode. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm above-quota prompts actually elicit fabrications.

Generation Inflation measurement: Define Generation Inflation Score = belief(item, generation mode) minus belief(item, verify mode), computed separately for GENUINE and FABRICATED items. Report per-layer, per-model inflation as a function of quota-over-knowledge (below/at/above). Test the hypotheses that (i) fabricated items produced to fill an over-quota list carry inflated internal belief in generation mode, and (ii) inflation grows with how far the quota exceeds genuine knowledge. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model hedge/caveat the padding, or present it confidently?).

Generation-pressure-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'generation/completion-pressure' direction via difference-in-means on above-quota (pressured) vs below-quota (unpressured) generation-mode activations, balanced across item truth. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the pressure axis (and vice versa); test whether inflation is explained by the pressure component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between above-quota (pressured) and below-quota (unpressured) generation of a fabricated item, decompose into truth-direction and pressure-direction components, patch only the pressure component into the unpressured/verify condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and in the model's willingness to assert the fabricated item as real. Conversely subtract the pressure component under above-quota generation and measure whether belief in fabrications drops toward the verify-mode value. Confirm the pressure signal causally inflates belief in fabricated items.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Generation Inflation predicts confabulation: (i) the model presenting a fabricated item confidently (without hedging) in the generated list, (ii) failure to retract the fabricated item when subsequently asked to verify it, and (iii) downstream propagation of the fabrication. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (quota-over-knowledge alone, output entropy, verify-mode truth-probe confidence).

Generation-Pressure De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the generation-pressure direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer during generation (ITI-style), so belief in each candidate item reflects genuine knowledge rather than quota pressure. Pair with an abstention/list-shortening rule: when the de-biased belief in the next candidate item falls below a calibrated threshold, the model stops or emits 'I don't know of more'. Sweep layer, strength, and threshold.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Generation Inflation Score, (ii) reduced fabrication rate in over-quota listing (the model shortens the list or abstains instead of inventing), (iii) PRESERVATION of genuine recall (below/at-quota lists must not be truncated) and accuracy on clearly-known items, (iv) calibration (ECE) of item-level assertions and improved risk-coverage on produced items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'only list items you are sure exist and stop when you run out', and a verify-then-filter pipeline (generate then self-check each item).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), domain (papers/drugs/set-membership), quota-over-knowledge level, real vs synthetic-in-context tasks, genuine vs fabricated items, model scale, abstention-threshold calibration transfer across domains, and generalization to listing tasks not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent generation inflation could reflect the probe reading a generation-position token differently from a verify-position token (position/mode artifact) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched query positions, the below-vs-above-quota contrast within generation mode, synthetic-in-context tasks, and causal patching that isolates the pressure-direction component.

Verify-mode belief itself may be inflated (the model may re-endorse its own prior output), compressing the generation-vs-verify gap; we use fresh-context verification, contrast with verify of externally-provided items, and analyze the self-consistency confound explicitly.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to items produced in listing contexts, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic tasks with grounded ground-truth sets.
Pressure and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing + abstention intervention could over-truncate genuine lists (harming recall) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure genuine-recall preservation on below/at-quota tasks and capability retention to characterize the abstention-vs-recall tradeoff.

Generation inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (quota-over-knowledge, output entropy) for confabulation; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that generation quota pressure inflates internal belief in fabrications, plus the de-biasing/abstention tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify eagerness to fill quotas or, conversely, teach hedging); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: source_reliability_belief_weighting
Title: Does the Model Keep Score? Testing Whether LLM Internal Beliefs Track a Source's Accumulated Reliability
Short Hypothesis: When a named source makes a series of in-context claims whose truth the model can verify, a rational believer should build a running reliability estimate of that source and weight belief in the source's NEW, unverifiable claims accordingly: more belief for a source with a good track record, less for one that has been repeatedly wrong. We hypothesize that (1) an LLM's internal belief in a new claim IS modulated by the named source's accumulated in-context track record, but SUB-RATIONALLY (under-using demonstrated unreliability, so it keeps believing claims from a proven-unreliable source); (2) a decodable 'source-trust' axis exists and is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) this trust miscalibration causally predicts a misinformation-from-discredited-source hallucination mode; and (4) a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief to the source's observed reliability reduces this failure.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single internal belief but never studies dynamic, source-specific reliability tracking. My prior 'belief_source_provenance' proposal separated parametric-vs-contextual SOURCE but treated context as a single undifferentiated channel; 'social_consensus_belief_bandwagon' varied crowd size; 'register_framing_belief_bias' varied surface style; 'incentivized_belief_distortion' varied external reward.
