No prior belief-geometry work isolates the descriptive/normative separation.
Abstract: David Hume warned that one cannot derive an 'ought' from an 'is' — and, conversely, a rational believer must not let what ought to be the case color their belief about what actually is. We ask whether large language models honor this separation inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a proposition's DESCRIPTIVE truth (does this state of the world actually obtain?) from its NORMATIVE desirability (should this state obtain — is it morally or prudentially good?), we test whether an LLM's internal factual belief, read via linear truth probes, is contaminated by the normative status of the described state. We construct IsOughtBelief, a controlled dataset crossing factual truth-value with normative valence: descriptively-true-and-good, true-and-bad, false-and-good, false-and-bad states of the world (plus normatively-neutral controls and synthetic-in-context facts), with surface forms matched. Using difference-in-means and logistic probes, we read a scalar factual belief and test four claims: (1) a normative-desirability axis is decodable and dissociable from the factual truth axis via project-out analyses; (2) desirability leaks into factual belief — morally/prudentially good states are believed more factually true than equally-true bad ones (and undesirable states believed less true), an internal is-from-ought distortion; (3) conflation magnitude causally predicts a normatively-biased factual-error mode; and (4) a lightweight De-normalization intervention that subtracts the normative component from the factual belief reduces these errors while preserving genuine normative/moral reasoning and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, moral-reasoning retention, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build IsOughtBelief. Assemble propositions describing STATES OF THE WORLD, crossing FACTUAL truth-value {descriptively true, descriptively false} with NORMATIVE valence {good/desirable, bad/undesirable, neutral} — a 2x3 design. Examples: 'Global child mortality has declined over the past 30 years' (true+good), 'Deforestation in region X increased last year' (true+bad), 'The disease has been fully eradicated' (false+good), 'Corruption in agency Y has worsened' (false+bad). Crucially, normative valence is the moral/prudential goodness of the DESCRIBED STATE, independent of who is asked (distinct from user-flattery). Include NORMATIVELY-NEUTRAL factual controls (e.g. mundane geographic/scientific facts) and SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (states defined only in context, with a stipulated good/bad valence) to remove parametric priors. Match surface length and syntactic form; validate valence labels with multiple human annotators plus an LLM-judge desirability rating and report agreement; verify factual labels against authoritative sources; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer FACTUAL truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of normatively-neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1], with normative valence balanced/absent so the probe learns descriptive truth, not desirability. At a matched query position read the internal factual belief for each IsOughtBelief item. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items.

Is-from-Ought Conflation measurement: Holding factual truth fixed, define Is-from-Ought Conflation = mean factual-belief(good-valence states) minus mean factual-belief(bad-valence states), computed within the descriptively-true cell and within the descriptively-false cell separately, relative to neutral controls. Report per-layer, per-model conflation. Test the hypothesis that good states are believed more factually true and bad states less true, at equal ground-truth (the internal naturalistic-fallacy distortion). Compare internal conflation to OUTPUT-level conflation (directly asking whether each state factually obtains / confidence).

Normative-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'normative-desirability' direction via difference-in-means on good vs bad states (balanced across factual truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the factual truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the normative axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Disentangle the normative axis from generic sentiment/valence-of-tokens with a sentiment-controlled regression, so we isolate deontic desirability of the described state from surface sentiment. Test whether the conflation is explained by the normative component leaking into the factual-truth readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a good-valence and a matched bad-valence description of an equally-true state, decompose into truth-direction and normative-direction components, patch only the normative component into a neutral factual item, and measure induced change in factual belief and output. Conversely subtract the normative component from a good-valence item and measure whether factual belief moves toward the truth-appropriate value. Confirm the normative signal causally shifts the factual belief scalar independent of factual content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Is-from-Ought Conflation predicts a normatively-biased factual-error mode: (i) endorsement rate of false-but-desirable states as factually true (believing good outcomes obtain), (ii) under-endorsement/denial of true-but-undesirable states (denying bad realities), and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by normative valence. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (desirability rating alone, output entropy, neutral truth-probe confidence, surface sentiment).

De-normalization intervention: At inference, estimate the normative-desirability direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the factual belief readout reflects descriptive evidence rather than the moral/prudential desirability of the described state. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected strongly-valenced factual queries. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Is-from-Ought Conflation, (ii) reduced endorsement of desirable-but-false states and reduced denial of undesirable-but-true states, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on normatively-valenced factual QA (e.g. adapted from real-world statistics on health, climate, economics where good/bad framings apply), (iv) PRESERVATION of genuine NORMATIVE reasoning — the model must still correctly answer moral/prudential 'should' questions (measured on an ETHICS-style moral-judgment set) and must not be pushed to treat all states as equally good — and accuracy on neutral factual controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge what is factually true separately from whether it is good or bad', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), normative valence (moral vs prudential/self-interested good), factual truth cell (true vs false), real vs synthetic-in-context facts, sentiment-vs-desirability disentangling, model scale, and generalization to normative domains and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent is-from-ought conflation could reflect the probe detecting surface sentiment/valence lexical features rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length and syntactic matching, a sentiment-controlled regression separating deontic desirability from token sentiment, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the normative-direction component.

Normative valence of a described state is partly subjective and culture-dependent; we anchor quantitative claims on items with high annotator agreement, use multiple annotators plus an LLM-judge, and analyze contested items separately.

Factual truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to valenced factual claims, so conflation could partly reflect probe extrapolation; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.

The factual-truth and normative-desirability directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality and project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-normalization intervention could impair legitimate normative/moral reasoning (making the model unable to say a state is bad) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure moral-judgment retention, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the key risk is over-suppressing the normative axis the model legitimately needs for 'should' questions.

Conflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (desirability rating, output entropy, sentiment) for normatively-biased factual errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates is with ought (an internal naturalistic fallacy) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify optimism about good outcomes or teach explicit is/ought separation); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: plausibility_vs_truth_belief
Title: Plausible Isn't True: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Conflate What Could Be True With What Is True?
Short Hypothesis: An LLM's internal belief representation (the linear truth-direction readout) conflates a proposition's PLAUSIBILITY (how consistent/likely it seems given priors) with its actual TRUTH: for propositions the model cannot verify, the decoded belief tracks plausibility rather than truth, so highly-plausible falsehoods get near-'true' internal belief and implausible truths get near-'false'. We hypothesize a separable plausibility axis exists, is dissociable from the truth axis, and its leakage into the truth readout causally drives a plausible-falsehood/implausible-truth hallucination mode that a lightweight de-biasing intervention can reduce.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) fits a single true-vs-false axis and reads a scalar belief, implicitly assuming the axis tracks truth rather than plausibility. Calibration/self-knowledge work (Kadavath et al. 2022) studies output confidence, and hallucination-detection probes score answers, but none test whether the internal belief scalar for UNVERIFIABLE claims collapses onto plausibility. My prior 'ignorance_vs_falsehood_belief' separated 'I don't know' from 'I believe false' (a determinate-vs-abstain axis); 'modal_status' separated necessary from contingent (alethic modality); 'negative_belief_closed_world' dissected refuted-false vs absence-false. NONE isolate the plausibility-vs-truth conflation — whether belief geometry treats 'this is likely/consistent' as 'this is true' — which is the internal substrate of a canonical hallucination: confidently asserting plausible-but-false claims. This plausibility-vs-truth lens is new and directly maps onto a high-stakes failure mode.
Abstract: A competent believer distinguishes what is plausible from what is true: a well-constructed but fabricated citation is highly plausible yet false, while a surprising fact is implausible yet true. We ask whether large language models honor this distinction inside their belief representations, or whether the standard linear truth direction is really a plausibility direction in disguise. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we construct PlausibleBelief, a controlled dataset that orthogonally crosses ground-truth truth-value with plausibility: plausible-true, plausible-false, implausible-true, and implausible-false statements, restricted to items the model cannot verify from parametric knowledge (obscure facts and synthetic-in-context claims), with surface forms and topics matched and plausibility ratings human-verified. We test four claims: (1) for unverifiable items the decoded belief tracks plausibility more than truth, so belief on the plausible-true and plausible-false cells is similarly high; (2) a separable plausibility axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses, and its leakage into the truth readout explains the conflation; (3) the plausibility component causally predicts a plausible-falsehood/implausible-truth hallucination mode, verified by activation patching; and (4) a lightweight De-plausibility intervention that subtracts the plausibility component recalibrates belief and reduces the failure mode without harming verifiable-fact judgments or general capability. We evaluate on factuality, calibration, hallucination-detection AUROC, and capability retention. Our results ask whether LLM 'truth' probes are secretly reading plausibility.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build PlausibleBelief, orthogonally crossing TRUTH {true, false} with PLAUSIBILITY {plausible, implausible} into a 2x2 design. Restrict to UNVERIFIABLE items so belief cannot rely on stored knowledge: (a) obscure real facts the model demonstrably does not know (verified by chance-level accuracy / high entropy on held-out phrasings), and (b) SYNTHETIC-in-context claims about nonce entities defined nowhere in pretraining, whose ground-truth truth-value is stipulated and whose plausibility is engineered (consistent with vs violating stated context/world-priors). Examples: plausible-true (a mundane fact that is true), plausible-false (a well-formed fabricated citation/statistic that is false), implausible-true (a surprising real fact), implausible-false (a bizarre falsehood). Match surface length, syntax, and topic across cells; obtain human plausibility ratings (multiple annotators) and an LLM-judge plausibility score; verify truth labels against sources or construction. Include verifiable-fact controls (clearly known true/false) and paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, plausibility-balanced true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief for each PlausibleBelief item. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false verifiable controls; confirm the unverifiable items are genuinely unknown behaviorally.

Plausibility-vs-Truth conflation measurement: Holding plausibility fixed, measure how much belief tracks truth (Truth Sensitivity = belief(true) - belief(false) within each plausibility level); holding truth fixed, measure how much belief tracks plausibility (Plausibility Sensitivity = belief(plausible) - belief(implausible) within each truth level). Define a Conflation Index = Plausibility Sensitivity / (Plausibility Sensitivity + Truth Sensitivity) for unverifiable items (near 1 = belief is really plausibility). Report per-layer, per-model. Test the central hypothesis that for unverifiable items belief tracks plausibility far more than truth, while verifiable controls show high truth sensitivity. Compare internal conflation to output-level behavior (does the model assert plausible-false items as true?).

Plausibility-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'plausibility' direction via difference-in-means on plausible vs implausible items, balanced across truth-value and content. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode plausibility (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Disentangle plausibility from surface sentiment/fluency and from token frequency via controlled regression. Test whether the conflation is explained by the plausibility component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a plausible and a matched implausible item of the same truth-value, decompose into truth-direction and plausibility-direction components, patch only the plausibility component into a neutral item and measure induced belief/output change; conversely subtract the plausibility component from a plausible-false item and measure whether belief drops toward the truth-appropriate value. Confirm the plausibility signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of truth.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the plausibility-axis score / Conflation Index predicts a plausible-falsehood/implausible-truth hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of plausible-false items as true, (ii) rejection/under-endorsement of implausible-true items, and (iii) confident-wrong rate. Report AUROC/correlation vs baselines (plausibility rating alone, output-token entropy, truth-probe confidence magnitude).

De-plausibility intervention: At inference, estimate the plausibility direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects truth-relevant evidence rather than mere plausibility. For unverifiable items this should push belief toward neutral/abstention rather than false. Provide a deployment variant that also gates abstention when the de-plausibilized belief lacks truth-supported signal. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Conflation Index / increased Truth Sensitivity on verifiable items, (ii) reduced endorsement of plausible-false items and reduced rejection of implausible-true items, (iii) hallucination-detection AUROC (does the de-plausibilized belief better separate true from false unverifiable claims?), (iv) calibration/risk-coverage on a mixed factual set, (v) PRESERVATION of accuracy on verifiable controls (no over-hedging on known facts), and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, output-entropy thresholding, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge truth, not mere plausibility'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), plausibility level, truth cell, obscure-real vs synthetic-in-context items, model scale, plausibility-vs-sentiment/frequency disentangling, and generalization to plausibility axes and topics not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The plausibility axis might merely detect surface fluency/sentiment/frequency rather than a genuine plausibility representation; mitigate with surface-form/length/topic matching, plausibility-vs-sentiment/frequency regressions, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching that isolates the plausibility-direction component.

Truth probes trained on plausibility-balanced neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to unverifiable items, so the conflation could partly reflect probe extrapolation; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on verifiable controls, and synthetic-in-context items with stipulated ground truth.

Constructing items that are truly unverifiable yet have a clean ground-truth truth-value is nontrivial for real facts; we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic-in-context items and human-verified obscure facts, and analyze the two separately.

Plausibility and truth directions may be partly entangled or, for genuinely-unknown items, truth may be intrinsically undecodable — a finding that the truth axis reduces to plausibility off the model's knowledge is itself the central (and informative) result even if it complicates the intervention.

The De-plausibility intervention could over-hedge (making verifiable known facts uncertain) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure verifiable-control preservation and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff, gating the intervention to unverifiable/uncertain items.

The plausibility axis may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (plausibility rating, output entropy) for the hallucination mode; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates plausibility with truth (i.e., 'truth' probes secretly read plausibility) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: numeric_magnitude_belief_snapping
Title: Round Numbers Feel Truer: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Snap Numeric Facts Toward Cognitively Salient Anchors?
Short Hypothesis: For a factual proposition whose value is a number (a population, distance, date, price, physical constant), an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) does not vary smoothly with the stated value but SNAPS toward cognitively salient anchors: belief in a claim stated as a round/prototypical number is inflated relative to an equally-true claim stated as a precise/odd number, and belief in a value near a salient round anchor is pulled toward that anchor. This 'anchor snapping' is graded, decodable as a magnitude-anchoring component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a numeric hallucination mode (endorsing round-but-wrong values, doubting precise-but-correct ones), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention.
Related Work: Levy & Geva (2024) show LLMs encode numbers digit-wise rather than as continuous magnitudes; Takagi et al. (2025, IJCNLP-AACL) show numerical attributes occupy shared latent subspaces that LLMs systematically AMPLIFY and that irrelevant numeric context perturbs magnitude representations — but both study number ENCODING/attribute integration, not the TRUTH BELIEF assigned to numeric factual claims. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief for categorical facts and never varies the numeric value's roundness/salience while holding truth fixed. My prior 'comparative_belief_distance_effect' proposal studied gap-graded confidence in binary comparisons and transitivity of comparative beliefs; 'gradability_belief_thresholding' studied vague predicates against a single threshold. NONE test whether the internal TRUTH belief in a numeric fact is distorted by the cognitive salience/roundness of the stated number (an internal analogue of the human 'round-number bias' and anchoring in numeric judgment), whether belief snaps toward salient anchors, whether this drives a round-but-wrong numeric hallucination mode, or whether it can be de-biased. This numeric-anchor-snapping lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from digit-wise encoding, attribute-confounding, and comparative-distance work.
Abstract: People trust round numbers more than jagged ones and unconsciously round estimates toward salient anchors (10, 100, 1000, decades). We ask whether large language models inherit this bias inside their belief representations. Holding a numeric fact's truth-value fixed, does an LLM's internal belief in the claim depend on whether the value is stated as a round/prototypical number versus a precise/odd one, and does belief in a near-anchor value get pulled toward the anchor? Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we construct AnchorBelief, a controlled dataset of numeric factual propositions (populations, distances, dates, prices, physical constants) plus synthetic-in-context numeric facts, presented at values that are (a) true-and-round, (b) true-and-precise, (c) false-and-round, and (d) false-and-precise, with roundness/salience graded and surface forms matched. We define a Roundness Belief Bias Score (belief gap between equally-true round vs precise statements) and an Anchor-Snapping curve (belief in Q as its stated value sweeps past a salient anchor). We test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for round/salient values and snaps toward anchors, at fixed truth; (2) the distortion is carried by a decodable magnitude-anchoring component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) distortion magnitude causally predicts a numeric hallucination mode (endorsing round-but-wrong values, doubting precise-but-correct ones); and (4) a lightweight De-anchoring intervention that subtracts the anchoring component recalibrates numeric belief without harming non-numeric judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on numeric factual QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AnchorBelief. Collect numeric factual propositions with definite ground-truth values across domains where roundness varies naturally: populations, distances/heights, historical dates, prices, physical constants, counts. For each fact, create matched statements crossing TRUTH {true, false} with ROUNDNESS/SALIENCE {round/prototypical (e.g. 1,000,000; 1980; 100 km), precise/odd (e.g. 1,003,412; 1983; 97.4 km)}. To hold truth fixed while varying roundness, use (a) facts whose true value is genuinely round vs genuinely precise, and (b) tolerance framing ('approximately N') so a round and a precise value can both be labeled true within a stated tolerance, plus false variants at matched distance from the truth. Add SYNTHETIC-in-context numeric facts (value stipulated in context) to remove parametric priors and give exact control over roundness and near-anchor placement. Grade salience (powers of ten, decades, half-round, fully odd). Match surface length/format (digit count, units); human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral non-numeric true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each numeric statement. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally knows the fact's approximate value.

Roundness Belief Bias measurement: Holding truth fixed, define Roundness Belief Bias Score = mean belief(true-and-round) minus mean belief(true-and-precise), and symmetrically within the false cell. Report per-layer, per-model bias across domains and salience levels. Test the hypothesis that round/salient values are believed more true at equal ground-truth. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (directly asking whether each statement is true / confidence).

Anchor-Snapping curve: Using synthetic-in-context facts and tolerance-framed real facts, sweep the STATED value of Q across and past a salient anchor (e.g. from 940k through 1,000,000 to 1,060k) while ground-truth is held or controlled, and plot internal belief vs stated value. Test whether the belief curve shows a peak/pull toward the anchor (snapping) rather than tracking distance-from-truth smoothly. Quantify a Snapping Score = excess belief at near-anchor values beyond the smooth distance-from-truth baseline.

Anchoring-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'magnitude-anchoring/roundness' direction via difference-in-means on round/salient vs precise/odd numeric activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the anchoring axis (and vice versa); test whether the roundness bias is explained by the anchoring component leaking into the truth-probe readout. Disentangle roundness from digit-count/token-length via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a round and a matched precise statement of the same (equally-true) fact, decompose into truth-direction and anchoring-direction components, patch only the anchoring component into a neutral/precise item, and measure induced change in belief readout and output endorsement. Conversely subtract the anchoring component from a round statement and measure whether belief moves toward the truth-appropriate value. Confirm the anchoring signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of the value's correctness.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Roundness Belief Bias / Snapping predicts a numeric hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of round-but-wrong values, (ii) under-endorsement/doubting of precise-but-correct values, and (iii) confident-wrong rate on numeric QA. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (roundness/salience score alone, output entropy, distance-from-truth, precise-value truth-probe confidence).

De-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the anchoring direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the value's actual correctness rather than its roundness/salience. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected numeric claims near salient anchors. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Roundness Belief Bias / Snapping Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of round-but-wrong values and reduced doubting of precise-but-correct values, (iii) numeric factual QA accuracy and calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of accuracy on non-numeric controls and on genuinely-round true facts (no over-correction that penalizes legitimately round values), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the number's correctness regardless of whether it is round', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), domain (populations/dates/prices/constants/counts), salience level, real vs synthetic-in-context facts, true vs false cell, roundness-vs-digit-count disentangling, model scale, and generalization to numeric domains not used to fit the de-anchoring direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent roundness bias could reflect the probe detecting surface digit-count/token-length rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with digit-count/length matching, a roundness-vs-digit-count disentangling regression, synthetic-in-context facts, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the anchoring-direction component.

Holding truth fixed while varying roundness is subtle: round and precise values are rarely both exactly true. We use tolerance framing ('approximately N'), synthetic-in-context facts with stipulated ground-truth, and matched-distance false variants, and anchor quantitative claims on the synthetic/tolerance-controlled items where truth-vs-roundness is cleanly orthogonal.

Truth probes trained on non-numeric statements may transfer imperfectly to numeric claims, so bias could partly reflect probe extrapolation; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and validate that numeric readouts are recoverable.
Anchoring and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

Because LLMs encode numbers digit-wise (Levy & Geva 2024) and amplify numeric correlations (Takagi et al. 2025), observed snapping may stem from magnitude-encoding artifacts rather than a belief-level anchoring effect; we separately probe the encoded value and analyze whether snapping stems from encoding error vs belief-thresholding, treating this decomposition as a core finding.

The De-anchoring intervention could over-correct (penalizing legitimately round true values) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on genuinely-round true facts and non-numeric controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Roundness bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (salience score, distance-from-truth, output entropy) for numeric hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry snaps numeric facts toward salient anchors, plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, tokenization of numbers, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/tokenization effects and negative results as informative.

Name: presupposition_belief_smuggling
Title: Smuggled Beliefs: Do Presupposed Propositions Enter an LLM's Internal Belief Unscrutinized Compared to Asserted Ones?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition P's content and truth-value fixed, when P is packaged as a PRESUPPOSITION taken for granted in a query (e.g. 'Now that P has been established, what follows?', 'Why did P happen?') rather than ASSERTED as the focal claim to be judged ('Is P true?'), the LLM's internal belief in P (linear truth-direction readout) is inflated toward true and receives less critical scrutiny — an internal presupposition-accommodation effect. We hypothesize this belief-smuggling is graded by presupposition strength, carried by a decodable focus/presupposition component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a false-presupposition hallucination mode where the model accepts and reasons from smuggled falsehoods, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that flags presupposed content for the same scrutiny as asserted content.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief for an ASSERTED proposition and never varies whether a proposition is presupposed vs asserted. My prior 'query_polarity_belief_instability' varied logically-equivalent QUESTION framings (is P true / is P false / isn't it true that P) about a focal proposition; 'fiction_frame_belief_leakage' varied non-endorsing speech-act frames (fiction/sarcasm); 'social_consensus'/'incentive'/'register' varied crowd, reward, and style. NONE isolate the INFORMATION-STRUCTURE distinction between focal/asserted content (which a query invites the model to evaluate) and PRESUPPOSED content (which the query's felicity takes for granted, e.g. presupposition triggers like factives 'realize that P', definite descriptions, 'why/when/how' questions, cleft/change-of-state verbs) — the linguistic phenomenon of presupposition accommodation, a known manipulation vector in human discourse. This is the first to test whether LLM belief geometry accommodates presupposed propositions with reduced scrutiny relative to asserted ones, whether presupposition is a decodable axis dissociable from truth, whether it drives a false-presupposition hallucination mode, and whether it can be de-biased. This information-structure lens on belief is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: A question like 'Why did the treaty collapse in 1849?' quietly takes for granted that a treaty collapsed in 1849 — and a careless listener will accept that presupposition without ever evaluating it. This presupposition accommodation is a well-known route by which false beliefs are smuggled into human discourse. We ask whether large language models are equally susceptible inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a proposition's information-structural role — ASSERTED (the focal claim a query invites one to judge) versus PRESUPPOSED (content the query's felicity takes for granted) — we test whether an LLM's internal belief in P, read via linear truth probes, is inflated when P is presupposed rather than asserted, at fixed content and truth-value. We construct PresupBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered in ASSERTED framings (probed directly for truth) and PRESUPPOSED framings using standard presupposition triggers (factive verbs, definite descriptions, why/when questions, change-of-state verbs), with surface content matched and presupposition strength graded. We define a Presupposition Belief Inflation Score and test four claims: (1) belief is inflated for presupposed content, graded by trigger strength; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable focus/presupposition axis dissociable from the truth axis; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts a false-presupposition hallucination mode where the model accepts and reasons from smuggled falsehoods; and (4) a lightweight Presupposition-Scrutiny intervention that subtracts the presupposition component subjects taken-for-granted content to the same evaluation as asserted content, reducing the failure mode without harming legitimate presupposition handling or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build PresupBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to remove parametric priors). Each P is rendered in matched ASSERTED and PRESUPPOSED framings. ASSERTED: P stated as the focal claim to evaluate ('Is it true that P?', 'Consider the claim: P.'). PRESUPPOSED: P embedded via standard presupposition triggers so it is taken for granted rather than at-issue — (a) factive verbs ('Given that the model realizes that P, ...'), (b) definite descriptions / change-of-state verbs ('After the discovery that P, ...', 'The fact that P explains...'), (c) wh-question presupposition ('Why/when/how did P occur?'), (d) cleft constructions. Grade presupposition strength (weak vs strong triggers) and always follow with a downstream question that does NOT require the model to affirm P (so acceptance is measured, not solicited). Match surface content/length between asserted and presupposed versions; human-verify that presupposed framings genuinely presuppose (not assert) P; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral asserted true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each framing. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false asserted items; confirm presupposed framings do not overtly assert P.

Presupposition Belief Inflation measurement: Define Presupposition Belief Inflation Score = belief(P | presupposed framing) minus belief(P | asserted framing), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model inflation across trigger type and strength, and separately for true and false P. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated when P is presupposed, and (ii) inflation grows with trigger strength. Crucially test the FALSE cell: false propositions should be believed less true when asserted (the model can refute them) but the presupposed framing should smuggle them toward true. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model later assert or reason from the presupposed falsehood?).

Presupposition-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'focus/presupposition' direction via difference-in-means on presupposed vs asserted activations at the P-relevant position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the presupposition axis (and vice versa); test whether the inflation is explained by the presupposition component modulating the truth-probe readout, or whether presupposition is represented but simply gates scrutiny off.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a presupposed and a matched asserted rendering of the same false P, decompose into truth-direction and presupposition-direction components, patch only the presupposition component into the asserted condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and downstream acceptance. Conversely subtract the presupposition component under the presupposed framing and measure whether belief in a false P returns toward the refuted value. Confirm the presupposition signal causally inflates belief independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Presupposition Belief Inflation predicts a false-presupposition hallucination mode: (i) acceptance of a false presupposed proposition (reasoning from it, answering the downstream question as if P holds, rather than challenging it), (ii) failure to flag the false presupposition, and (iii) contamination of downstream factual answers within the same conversation. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (trigger-strength indicator, output entropy, asserted-framing truth-probe confidence).

Presupposition-Scrutiny intervention: At inference, estimate the presupposition direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so presupposed content is evaluated on the same footing as asserted content rather than accommodated. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected presupposition triggers. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Presupposition Belief Inflation Score, (ii) increased flagging/challenging of false presuppositions and reduced reasoning-from-smuggled-falsehoods, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on presupposition-laden QA (adapt false-premise question benchmarks, e.g. (QA)^2 / presupposition-failure sets), (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate presupposition handling (the model must still accept TRUE presuppositions and answer normally, not challenge everything) and accuracy on asserted-true controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'check whether the assumptions in the question are true before answering', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), trigger type (factive/definite-description/wh-question/cleft), trigger strength, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false P, model scale, distance between the presupposition and the readout, and generalization to presupposition triggers not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent presupposition inflation could reflect the probe detecting surface trigger tokens (factive verbs, definite articles) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-content matching between asserted and presupposed versions, paraphrase controls, trigger-type diversity, and causal patching that isolates the presupposition-direction component.

The presupposed and asserted framings must genuinely differ only in information structure, not in asserted content; distinguishing presupposition from assertion is linguistically subtle, so we human-verify (with linguistic annotation) that presupposed framings do not assert P, and analyze ambiguous items separately.

Truth probes trained on asserted declaratives may transfer imperfectly to presupposed contexts, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Presupposition and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Presupposition-Scrutiny intervention could over-scrutinize (making the model challenge every true presupposition, harming fluency and cooperativity) or degrade normal question-answering; we explicitly measure preservation on true-presupposition and asserted-true controls plus capability retention to characterize the scrutiny-vs-cooperativity tradeoff.

Inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (trigger-strength indicator, output entropy) for false-presupposition hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry accommodates presupposed content with reduced scrutiny (presupposition smuggling) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may teach some false-premise detection); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: distilled_belief_inheritance
Title: Beliefs You Never Taught: Do Distilled Students Inherit a Teacher's Internal Belief Geometry and Its Biases?
Short Hypothesis: When a student LLM is distilled from a teacher (on answers/logits over some training distribution), it inherits not only the teacher's OUTPUT behavior but the teacher's internal BELIEF GEOMETRY: a linear truth direction aligned with the teacher's, and — crucially — the teacher's specific belief DISTORTIONS (e.g. a wishful/sycophantic or plausibility bias direction), transferring even to propositions and bias axes that were never present in the distillation data. We hypothesize (1) the student's truth direction is more aligned with its teacher's than with an independently-trained control model; (2) an intentionally-implanted teacher belief bias reappears in the student's internal belief geometry despite the bias-eliciting inputs being absent from distillation; (3) this inherited bias is causally present (steerable/ablatable in the student along a direction transplanted from the teacher); and (4) how much bias transfers is graded by distillation strength (logit vs answer-only, data coverage).
Related Work: Knowledge distillation work (MAGDi 2024; Flex-KD 2025; DSKD-CMA 2026) transfers CAPABILITY and matches OUTPUT/feature representations, treating internal features as things to align for accuracy; none study whether the student inherits the teacher's internal BELIEF representation (a linear truth direction) or, more pointedly, the teacher's belief DISTORTIONS. Truth/belief-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a belief scalar within a single model and never compares teacher-vs-student belief geometry. Data-poisoning/bias-inheritance work studies whether harmful OUTPUT behaviors survive distillation, again behaviorally, not in belief geometry. My prior proposals all concern inference-time belief distortions WITHIN one model (evidence, framing, source, affect, plausibility, etc.); NONE address cross-model FORMATION — whether belief structure and its biases are transmitted from teacher to student through distillation, whether they transfer to held-out propositions/bias-axes never in the distillation set, or whether the inherited bias is causally manipulable via a teacher-transplanted direction. This teacher-to-student belief-inheritance lens is new and is a formation-tracing account of where a model's belief geometry comes from.
Abstract: Distillation is usually judged by whether the student matches the teacher's answers. We ask a deeper question: does the student inherit the teacher's INTERNAL BELIEFS — the geometry it uses to represent truth, and the distortions baked into that geometry — even for beliefs and biases never explicitly taught? Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along a linear truth direction, we distill small student models from a teacher and compare their belief geometry. First, we test alignment: is the student's truth direction more aligned with its teacher's than with an independently-trained control? Second, and centrally, we implant a controlled belief BIAS in a teacher (e.g. a wishful/desirability or plausibility distortion via light fine-tuning), distill a student using data that contains NO bias-eliciting inputs, and test whether the student's belief geometry nonetheless exhibits the same distortion on held-out bias-probing propositions. We validate that the inherited bias is causal — a bias direction extracted from the TEACHER, transplanted into the student, steers/ablates the student's belief as predicted — and measure how bias transfer scales with distillation strength (logit-matching vs answer-only, data coverage). We evaluate belief-direction alignment (cosine, cross-model probe transfer), bias-transfer magnitude on unseen axes, causal steering effects, and downstream factuality/sycophancy, against an independently-trained control and a from-scratch baseline. Our results reveal whether distilled models silently inherit their teacher's way of believing — with direct implications for how biases propagate through the model supply chain.
Experiments: Setup: Use a small-scale but realistic distillation pipeline affordable in an academic lab. TEACHER: an open instruction model (e.g. Llama-3 8B or Qwen2.5 7B). STUDENTS: distill smaller base models (e.g. 1-3B) via (a) logit/soft-label distillation and (b) answer-only (hard-label) distillation, on a general instruction/QA corpus. CONTROLS: (i) an independently instruction-tuned model of the same student architecture NOT distilled from this teacher, and (ii) the student base before distillation. Train belief truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression, Platt-scaled to [0,1]) per layer on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements for teacher, students, and controls.

Experiment 1 — Belief-geometry alignment: On a held-out battery of true/false factual statements, extract per-layer truth directions for teacher, student, and controls. Measure (a) cosine alignment between student and teacher truth directions vs student and control, after Procrustes/linear alignment of activation spaces; (b) CROSS-MODEL probe transfer — does a truth probe trained on the teacher decode the student's beliefs better than a probe trained on the control? Report per-layer alignment and transfer accuracy. Hypothesis: student belief geometry is closer to its teacher than to an independent control.

Experiment 2 — Implant-and-distill (central test): Create a BIASED TEACHER by light fine-tuning a copy of the teacher to exhibit a controlled belief distortion — e.g. a desirability/wishful bias (inflating belief in pleasant propositions) or a plausibility-over-truth bias — using a bias-training set. Distill a student on GENERAL data that contains NO bias-eliciting propositions (verified: the distillation corpus excludes the pleasant/implausible-fact items used to elicit the bias). Compare to a student distilled from the UN-biased teacher and to controls. On HELD-OUT bias-probing propositions (matched on truth, contrasted on desirability/plausibility), measure the student's Bias Score = belief gap between biased and unbiased conditions at fixed truth. Test whether the biased-teacher student inherits the distortion despite never seeing bias-eliciting inputs.

Experiment 3 — Causal inheritance via teacher-transplanted direction: Extract the bias direction from the BIASED TEACHER (difference-in-means between biased vs neutral conditions). Transplant it (after cross-model alignment) into the student and steer/ablate the student's belief. Test whether steering along the teacher-derived bias direction moves the student's belief as predicted, and whether ablating it removes the inherited distortion — confirming the inherited bias is causally present and shares the teacher's directional structure, not merely a coincidental output correlation. Compare against steering along a random/control direction.

Experiment 4 — Dose-response with distillation strength: Vary distillation strength: logit-matching vs answer-only, and data coverage (fraction of teacher outputs / temperature / number of distillation examples). Measure how belief-geometry alignment (Exp 1) and bias-transfer magnitude (Exp 2) scale with distillation strength. Hypothesis: richer signal (logit-matching, broader coverage) transfers more belief geometry and more bias.

Downstream evaluation: Measure whether inherited belief bias manifests behaviorally in the student on out-of-distribution factuality/sycophancy tests (e.g. endorsement of pleasant-but-false or plausible-but-false claims), and whether a debiasing intervention (ablating the inherited bias direction) reduces these failures while preserving general capability (MMLU, perplexity). Baselines: un-biased-teacher student, independent control, from-scratch student.

Ablations: teacher/student family and scale, bias type (desirability vs plausibility vs a synthetic implanted bias), probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), cross-model alignment method (Procrustes vs learned linear map), layer choice, verifying the distillation corpus truly excludes bias-eliciting inputs, and generalization of inherited bias to a bias axis distinct from the implanted one.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent belief-geometry alignment could arise because teacher and student simply learned the same true/false structure from overlapping pretraining, not from distillation transfer; the independent control (same architecture, not distilled from this teacher) and the biased-teacher implant experiment (bias absent from pretraining and from distillation data) are designed to isolate distillation-specific transfer, and Experiment 2 is the decisive test.

Cross-model activation spaces are not directly comparable; alignment and direction-transplant depend on the alignment method (Procrustes/learned map), which may introduce artifacts. We test multiple alignment methods and validate with cross-model probe transfer and causal steering rather than raw cosine alone.

The implanted teacher bias might leak into the distillation corpus indirectly (biased teacher's general outputs subtly carry the bias); we audit the distillation data, use bias-probing propositions held out from any teacher output seen by the student, and report residual-leakage sensitivity — though some leakage is itself part of the phenomenon (bias travels through general outputs).

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly across model families/sizes, so measured inheritance could reflect probe error; use multiple probe types, within-model validation on clearly-true/false items, and causal steering to corroborate.

Bias transfer may be weak or absent for answer-only distillation, making the effect distillation-mode-specific; a null for hard-label distillation is itself an informative, publishable finding about which distillation modes propagate belief structure.

Effects may vary across teacher/student families, scales, and distillation recipes; we test multiple pairings and report where inheritance holds vs fails, treating negative results as informative for the model supply-chain safety question.

Name: belief_actionability_gap
Title: Decodable But Inert: Auditing Which of an LLM's Internal Beliefs Actually Steer Its Output
Short Hypothesis: A large fraction of what a linear truth probe reads as an LLM's 'internal belief' about a factual proposition is causally INERT with respect to the model's output: steering/ablating along the belief direction moves the decoded belief but not the emitted answer. We hypothesize (1) beliefs partition into ACTIONABLE (steering flips the output) and INERT (steering does not) components; (2) the actionable fraction is graded and item-dependent, being low precisely for the propositions where the model hallucinates; (3) a cheap 'actionability score' (output sensitivity to belief-direction steering) read from a small dose-response sweep predicts hallucination better than the raw decoded belief; and (4) the inert component lives in a high-dimensional assessment subspace separable from the low-dimensional output-controlling subspace, so a targeted late-layer intervention in the actionable subspace outperforms generic belief steering.
Related Work: Marks & Tegmark (2023), ITI (Li et al. 2023), and Schouten et al. (2024) extract linear 'truth directions' and largely assume the decoded belief is the operative belief; steering is presumed to move behavior. Sanyal et al. (2025, 'Confidence is Not Competence') made the striking observation, for TASK-SOLVABILITY belief, that the belief axis is linearly decodable yet steering it leaves solutions unchanged, positing a geometrically complex assessor feeding a simple executor. However, they studied solvability belief on reasoning tasks, did not test FIRST-ORDER FACTUAL belief, did not quantify a per-item actionable-vs-inert partition, did not tie actionability to hallucination, and did not localize/exploit an actionable subspace for intervention. My prior proposals study distortions of the decoded belief (coherence, provenance, plausibility, etc.) but all implicitly treat the decoded belief as the belief; none ask which decoded beliefs are causally load-bearing on the output, quantify a graded actionability score, use it as a hallucination predictor, or separate an actionable output-controlling subspace from an inert assessment subspace for factual beliefs. This actionability-audit lens is new and directly generalizes the surprising Sanyal et al. result from solvability to factual belief.
Abstract: Interpretability routinely reads an LLM's 'belief' about a proposition off a linear truth direction and treats that scalar as the model's operative belief. But a recent result on task-solvability belief found something unsettling: the belief axis is decodable yet steering it changes nothing downstream. We ask whether the same actionability gap afflicts FIRST-ORDER FACTUAL beliefs, and turn it into a diagnostic. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we perform a controlled dose-response steering audit: for each proposition we push activations along the belief direction across a range of magnitudes and measure both the induced change in the decoded belief and the induced change in the emitted answer. We define a per-item Actionability Score = output sensitivity per unit of belief-direction shift, partitioning beliefs into actionable (steering flips the output) and inert (decoded belief moves, output does not). We construct BeliefActionable, a dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context factual propositions spanning items the model answers correctly, incorrectly, and hallucinates on. We test four claims: (1) beliefs partition into actionable and inert components, with a graded, item-dependent actionable fraction; (2) actionability is lowest precisely on hallucinated/incorrect items; (3) the Actionability Score, read from a cheap steering sweep, predicts hallucination better than the raw decoded belief and than output entropy; and (4) the inert component lives in a high-dimensional assessment subspace separable from a low-dimensional output-controlling subspace, so steering restricted to the actionable subspace at late layers changes behavior far more per unit norm than generic belief steering. We validate via activation patching and evaluate hallucination detection, steering efficacy, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build BeliefActionable. Factual propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to control priors). Stratify items by the model's behavioral status established in a pilot: CORRECTLY-ANSWERED, INCORRECTLY-ANSWERED, and HALLUCINATED (confident-wrong on open-ended queries), so the audit can be conditioned on behavior. Include matched true/false surface forms, paraphrase sets, and human-verified labels.

Belief readout and steering setup: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to [0,1]. Identify the belief direction per layer. For steering, add scaled multiples of the belief direction to the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) across a magnitude sweep (e.g. -alpha_max ... +alpha_max).

Dose-response actionability audit (central experiment): For each proposition, at each steering magnitude record (a) the DECODED belief (probe readout under steering) and (b) the OUTPUT response / answer probability. Fit two dose-response curves: belief-vs-alpha (should be steep by construction) and output-vs-alpha. Define Actionability Score = slope/AUC of the output-vs-alpha curve normalized by the belief-vs-alpha slope (output change per unit of achieved belief change). Partition items into ACTIONABLE (output flips within the steering range) vs INERT (decoded belief moves substantially but output does not). Report the distribution of Actionability Scores per model, layer, and behavioral stratum.

Actionability vs hallucination (Hypothesis 2): Test whether Actionability Score differs across CORRECT / INCORRECT / HALLUCINATED strata, hypothesizing lowest actionability on hallucinated/incorrect items (the model's decoded belief is disconnected from what it emits). Report effect sizes and per-model consistency.

Predictive validity (Hypothesis 3): Test whether the Actionability Score, computed from a cheap few-magnitude steering sweep, predicts (i) whether an item is hallucinated/incorrect and (ii) whether a truth-probe-based detector will succeed. Report AUROC/AUC vs baselines: raw decoded belief magnitude, |belief-0.5|, output-token entropy, and verbalized confidence. Also test whether combining actionability with decoded belief improves hallucination detection.

Subspace localization (Hypothesis 4): Compare the effective dimensionality of the assessment subspace (PCA of belief-relevant activations across items, following Sanyal et al.) vs the output-controlling subspace (directions whose ablation/patching most changes the emitted answer). Test whether the belief direction has large projection onto the high-dimensional inert assessment subspace and small projection onto the low-dimensional actionable output subspace. Fit an ACTIONABLE belief direction = projection of the belief direction onto the output-controlling subspace, at late layers.

Causal validation and targeted intervention: (a) Activation patching to confirm actionable-subspace edits causally change the output while matched inert-subspace edits of equal norm do not. (b) Compare steering along the generic belief direction vs the ACTIONABLE belief direction (late layer) for correcting known-wrong answers: measure output-flip rate per unit steering norm and factual-correction accuracy.

Downstream evaluation: Measure (i) hallucination-detection performance using the Actionability Score, (ii) correction efficacy of actionable-subspace steering (accuracy gain on incorrect items) vs generic belief steering, (iii) calibration/risk-coverage, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct answers and general capability (MMLU, perplexity), and (v) specificity (matched control-direction steering has no effect). Baselines: no intervention, generic ITI belief steering, output-entropy detection.

Ablations: layer choice for readout vs steering, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), steering magnitude range, behavioral stratum, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, number of magnitudes needed for a reliable actionability estimate, and generalization of the actionability signal to held-out domains.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Inertness could be an artifact of steering at the wrong layer or too-small magnitudes rather than a genuine assessor-executor gap; we sweep layers and magnitudes, report saturation, and validate with activation patching and the late-layer actionable-subspace intervention.

Apparent low actionability on hallucinated items might reflect probe error (the decoded 'belief' is noise) rather than a real inert-but-held belief; we use multiple probe types, restrict to items where the belief probe is reliable on clearly-true/false controls, and treat a 'decoded belief is just noise' outcome as an informative alternative finding.

The Actionability Score requires several forward passes per item (a steering sweep), so it is more expensive than a single probe read; we quantify how few magnitudes suffice and compare cost/benefit against cheaper baselines.

Separating an actionable from an inert subspace assumes an approximately linear decomposition; if the output-controlling computation is strongly nonlinear the subspace fit may be weak, which we report and probe with nonlinear ablation controls.

The actionability signal may correlate with but not exceed output entropy or |belief-0.5| for hallucination detection; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that many decoded factual beliefs are causally inert (generalizing Sanyal et al. to factual belief) plus the actionable-subspace intervention, reported honestly.

Targeted actionable-subspace steering could still fail to improve correctness if the model simply lacks the fact; we separate items the model knows-but-misreports from items it does not know, and evaluate correction only where a correct answer is recoverable.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: base_rate_neglect_belief
Title: Neglecting the Prior: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Under-Weight Base Rates When Individuating Evidence Is Present?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM forms a belief in a categorical proposition about an individual (e.g. whether a described person is a lawyer vs a nurse), its internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) reflects the diagnostic/individuating description while systematically UNDER-weighting the explicitly-stated base rate, mirroring the human base-rate-neglect bias. We hypothesize this internal neglect is graded in the salience of the individuating cue, is carried by a decodable representativeness component dissociable from a base-rate component, causally predicts base-rate-neglect errors in the model's answers, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief to the stated prior.
Related Work: Base-rate neglect is one of the most robust findings in human judgment (Kahneman & Tversky's lawyer/engineer problem; Bar-Hillel 1980), and valence/representativeness biases in Bayesian updating are computationally characterized (Kuzmanovic & Rigoux 2017; Hayes et al. 2013). Zhu & Griffiths (2024) and Jiang et al. (2024) show LLMs reproduce conjunction-fallacy and token-bias patterns at the OUTPUT level, and prior work notes output-level base-rate insensitivity in LLM reasoning. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar internal belief but never tests whether the internal belief obeys Bayesian base-rate integration. My prior 'belief_evidence_weighting' proposal tested sensitivity to evidence quantity/reliability/redundancy of same-valence supporting evidence, but did NOT isolate the canonical base-rate-vs-individuating-evidence tension, did not compare the internal belief to a normative posterior computed from an explicitly-stated prior and likelihood, and did not separate a representativeness component from a base-rate component. This is the first to test base-rate neglect INSIDE belief geometry against an exact Bayesian benchmark, dissociate the two competing components, tie internal neglect causally to output errors, and re-anchor to the prior.
Abstract: Humans famously ignore base rates: told that 70% of the people in a sample are engineers, then given a personality sketch that 'sounds like' a lawyer, they judge the person a lawyer, neglecting the prior. We ask whether large language models exhibit this bias inside their belief representations. We build BaseRateBelief, a controlled dataset of individual-classification problems in which a stated base rate (prior) and an individuating description (likelihood) are independently varied so that an exact Bayesian posterior can be computed for each item. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we read the model's internal belief in the target category membership and compare it to the normative posterior. We define a Base-Rate-Neglect Score = the extent to which internal belief tracks the individuating description while under-weighting the stated base rate. We test four claims: (1) internal belief systematically neglects the base rate, graded in how representative/salient the individuating description is; (2) a decodable 'representativeness' component and a 'base-rate' component are separately present and dissociable from each other and from the truth axis; (3) neglect magnitude causally predicts base-rate-neglect errors in the model's answers; and (4) a lightweight Prior Re-anchoring intervention that steers belief toward the stated base rate improves posterior calibration and classification accuracy without harming legitimate use of individuating evidence or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on classification accuracy, posterior calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build BaseRateBelief. Each item is an individual-classification problem with two independently-manipulable ingredients: (a) an explicitly-stated BASE RATE over two categories (e.g. 'In this sample, 85% are nurses and 15% are doctors', varied across levels 10/30/50/70/90%), and (b) an INDIVIDUATING description whose representativeness for the target category is graded (strongly-stereotypical / weakly-diagnostic / neutral / counter-stereotypical). Because both prior and likelihood are stated/controlled, compute the exact Bayesian posterior P(category | description, base rate) for each item. Use classic domains (occupations, disease diagnosis given symptoms + prevalence) plus SYNTHETIC-in-context categories (nonce categories with stipulated base rates and diagnostic cues) to remove parametric priors. Include neutral-description controls (where belief should equal the base rate) and matched surface forms; human-verify representativeness ratings; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in 'this individual is a [target category]'. Manipulation check: on neutral-description controls, confirm belief tracks the stated base rate (so the base rate is at least partly represented).

Base-Rate-Neglect measurement: For each item compare the internal belief to (i) the normative Bayesian posterior and (ii) a 'base-rate-only' benchmark (ignore description) and a 'description-only' benchmark (ignore prior). Define Base-Rate-Neglect Score via a regression of internal belief on the stated base rate and on the representativeness of the description: neglect = under-weighting of the base-rate coefficient relative to the normative weighting. Report per-layer, per-model neglect as a function of description representativeness and base-rate extremity. Test the hypotheses that (i) internal belief under-weights the base rate and (ii) neglect grows with description salience. Compare internal neglect to OUTPUT-level neglect (directly asking the model to classify / give a probability).

Component discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'representativeness' direction (difference-in-means on strongly- vs weakly-representative descriptions, balanced across base rate) and a 'base-rate' direction (difference-in-means on high vs low stated base rate, balanced across description). Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among representativeness, base-rate, and truth directions; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether neglect corresponds to the representativeness component dominating the belief readout while the base-rate component fails to modulate it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the base-rate direction and measure whether internal belief and the output classification move toward the base-rate-consistent posterior, holding representativeness fixed. (b) Patch the base-rate component from a high-base-rate item into a low-base-rate item and measure the induced belief shift. Confirm the base-rate signal is present but under-utilized, and causally governs the belief when amplified.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Base-Rate-Neglect Score predicts (i) base-rate-neglect classification errors (choosing the description-consistent but base-rate-inconsistent category), (ii) posterior miscalibration (deviation of stated/probed probability from the Bayesian posterior), and (iii) inconsistency across base-rate levels for a fixed description. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (representativeness rating alone, output entropy, neutral-control base-rate tracking).

Prior Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the base-rate direction (from the probe) and add a scaled shift along it (or along the truth direction gated by the stated base rate) at a chosen layer (ITI-style), re-weighting the prior into the belief. Provide a deployment variant that reads the stated base rate from the prompt. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Base-Rate-Neglect Score / improved match to the Bayesian posterior, (ii) improved classification accuracy on items where the base rate should dominate, (iii) posterior calibration (deviation from normative posterior; ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate use of individuating evidence (items where the description SHOULD dominate must not be over-corrected) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'combine the base rate with the description using Bayes' rule'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), description representativeness level, base-rate extremity, real vs synthetic-in-context categories, occupation vs medical-diagnosis domain, model scale, and generalization to problem types not used to fit the base-rate direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to category-membership judgments, so neglect could partly reflect probe extrapolation; mitigate with multiple probe types, neutral-description manipulation checks (belief should equal the base rate), synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching.

The normative Bayesian posterior is clean only when prior and likelihood are precisely specified; real occupation/medical descriptions have subjective diagnosticity. We anchor quantitative claims on synthetic-in-context items with exact stipulated likelihoods and treat real-world items more qualitatively, human-verifying representativeness.

Apparent neglect could reflect the probe detecting description sentiment/stereotype lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with base-rate-balanced controls, counter-stereotypical items, and causal patching isolating the base-rate component.

Representativeness and base-rate directions may be partly entangled with the truth axis in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

Prior Re-anchoring could over-correct (making the model ignore genuinely-diagnostic descriptions) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on description-should-dominate items and neutral controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Internal neglect may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (representativeness rating, output entropy) for classification errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry neglects base rates against an exact Bayesian benchmark, plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/CoT-tuning may partly correct base-rate use); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: telephone_belief_drift
Title: The Telephone Game of Belief: Does an LLM's Internal Belief Decay Under Iterated Faithful Paraphrase?
Short Hypothesis: A rational belief must be conserved under meaning-preserving reformulation: repeatedly restating the same true proposition through faithful paraphrases should leave the internal belief unchanged. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically DRIFT and DECAY across an iterated-paraphrase chain (a semantic 'telephone game'): as a fixed proposition is passed through successive faithful rewordings, the decoded belief exhibits a monotone-ish erosion (and increased variance) even though truth and meaning are held constant, revealing that belief is partly anchored to surface form rather than semantic content. This drift is graded in chain length, carried by a decodable surface-form component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a paraphrase-induced factual-instability failure mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief to a form-invariant semantic representation.
Related Work: Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief and Bao et al. show probes generalize across single logical transformations, but never test ITERATED meaning-preserving reformulation of the same proposition. My prior proposals differ concretely: 'query_polarity_belief_instability' varied the QUESTION framing (is P true / isn't it true that P) about a fixed statement in ONE step; 'polyglot_belief_invariance' varied the LANGUAGE; 'belief_hysteresis' varied evidence ORDER; 'belief_drift_context_dilution' studied belief erosion as UNRELATED filler accumulates. NONE study whether belief is conserved when the SAME proposition is re-expressed through a CHAIN of faithful paraphrases (surface form changing while meaning and truth are fixed), whether belief decays/drifts with chain depth (a telephone-game effect), whether this is a decodable surface-form-vs-semantic axis, or whether it can be re-anchored. This conservation-under-iterated-transformation lens directly tests the semantic vs surface-form basis of belief and is new.
Abstract: A belief worthy of the name should survive rewording: if a fact is true, restating it in other words — once, or many times over — must not change how strongly one believes it. We ask whether large language models honor this conservation inside their belief representations. Passing a fixed true (or false) proposition through an iterated chain of faithful, meaning-preserving paraphrases — a semantic 'telephone game' — we read the internal belief at each link via linear truth probes and ask whether it stays put.
