We construct TelephoneBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions, each expanded into paraphrase chains of increasing length (validated as meaning- and truth-preserving by NLI and human checks) with surface-form divergence measured at each step. We define a Telephone Drift Score (belief change per paraphrase step, controlling for matched non-paraphrase controls) and test four claims: (1) internal belief drifts and erodes with chain depth even though meaning and truth are fixed; (2) the drift is carried by a decodable surface-form component dissociable from the truth axis, showing belief is partly form-anchored; (3) drift magnitude causally predicts a paraphrase-induced factual-instability failure mode (the same fact answered differently across rewordings); and (4) a lightweight Semantic Re-anchoring intervention that steers belief toward a form-invariant representation reduces drift and instability without harming clearly-true/false judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, and capability retention. Our results reveal whether LLM beliefs are conserved under meaning-preserving transformation, probing the semantic-vs-surface basis of belief.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build TelephoneBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to control priors). For each P, construct an ITERATED PARAPHRASE CHAIN of increasing length (1-6 links) where each link faithfully rewords the previous statement (generated by paraphrase models and/or templated rewrites, then FILTERED for meaning preservation via bidirectional NLI entailment and human verification, and for truth preservation). At each link, record a surface-divergence metric (edit distance / embedding cosine to the original). Include MATCHED CONTROLS: (a) an IDENTITY chain (the original statement repeated verbatim at each step, to separate paraphrase from mere restatement) and (b) a LENGTH-MATCHED FILLER control (equal token budget of unrelated text between readouts, to separate paraphrase drift from generic context-dilution). Include paraphrase-quality gradations (near-verbatim vs heavy reword) and matched surface lengths; human-verify a sample.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-occurrence true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At each link of the chain, read the internal belief in the current (paraphrased) statement at a matched query position. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm each link is judged meaning-equivalent by the model behaviorally.

Telephone Drift measurement: For each proposition, plot internal belief vs chain link. Define Telephone Drift Score = signed belief change per paraphrase step (and a variance-growth measure), computed relative to the IDENTITY and FILLER controls to isolate paraphrase-specific effects. Report per-layer, per-model drift across truth regimes, chain length, and surface-divergence. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief drifts/erodes with chain depth even though meaning is preserved, and (ii) drift scales with surface divergence per step. Compare internal drift to OUTPUT-level drift (does the model's yes/no answer or verbalized confidence change across the chain?).

Surface-form-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'surface-form-divergence' direction via difference-in-means on high-divergence-paraphrase vs near-verbatim activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the surface-form axis (and vice versa); test whether the drift is explained by the surface-form component leaking into the truth-probe readout — evidence that belief is partly form-anchored rather than purely semantic.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Patch the semantic/truth-direction component from the ORIGINAL statement's processing into a late-chain paraphrase and measure whether the eroded belief and output recover; (b) subtract the surface-form component at a late link and measure whether belief returns toward the original value. Confirm the drift is driven by a form-dependent component separable from the semantic content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Telephone Drift predicts a paraphrase-induced factual-instability failure mode: (i) answer flips across chain links for the same fact, (ii) confidence swings, and (iii) inconsistency between the original and late-chain answer. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (chain length alone, surface divergence, output entropy, original-statement truth-probe confidence).

Semantic Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the surface-form direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), and/or re-anchor belief toward the original statement's form-invariant semantic representation, so belief reflects meaning rather than wording. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected high surface divergence. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Telephone Drift Score and reduced across-chain answer-flip rate, (ii) improved factual consistency on paraphrase-varied factual QA (adapt existing paraphrase-consistency / factual-QA benchmarks), (iii) calibration (ECE) aggregated across paraphrases, (iv) PRESERVATION of accuracy on clearly-true/false items and identity/filler controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, self-consistency across paraphrases, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge the meaning, not the wording'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), chain length, paraphrase intensity (near-verbatim vs heavy reword), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, paraphrase-generation source, and generalization to paraphrase styles and topics not used to fit the surface-form direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent telephone drift could reflect the paraphrases not actually being meaning-preserving (subtle semantic drift in the chain) rather than a form-anchoring failure; mitigate with bidirectional-NLI filtering, human verification of meaning equivalence, surface-divergence tracking, and analyzing only verified-equivalent links, treating semantic-drift items separately.

Drift could be generic context-dilution or recency rather than paraphrase-specific; the IDENTITY (verbatim-repeat) and LENGTH-MATCHED FILLER controls directly isolate the paraphrase effect, and a null (drift = dilution) is itself informative.

Truth probes trained on single-occurrence statements may transfer imperfectly to paraphrased restatements, so drift could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Surface-form and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

Semantic Re-anchoring could over-suppress and harm fluency or accuracy on legitimately-varying paraphrases; we explicitly measure preservation on identity/filler controls and clearly-true/false items plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Drift may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (surface divergence, chain length, output entropy) for paraphrase instability; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that belief is not conserved under meaning-preserving transformation (form-anchored belief) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_load_crosstalk
Title: Belief Under Load: Does Holding Multiple Facts Cause Their Truth-Values to Bleed Into Each Other?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM must simultaneously hold several factual propositions in context, the truth-VALUE of one held fact bleeds into the internal belief in another as memory load grows: a true fact's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) is dragged toward the belief value of a co-held false fact, and vice versa, a 'belief-value crosstalk' arising from superposed belief representations. We hypothesize this crosstalk is graded in memory load and in representational overlap between the held facts, is dissociable from mere content-retrieval interference, causally predicts a load-induced factual-error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that de-mixes the co-held beliefs.
Related Work: Xiong et al. (2026, 'In-context superposition') show LLMs exhibit human-like working-memory limits, encode multiple items in ENTANGLED representations, and that suppressing interfering content improves RETRIEVAL — but they study which ITEM is recalled (content/identity interference), not the graded TRUTH BELIEF assigned to each held proposition, and never test whether the truth-VALUE of one held fact contaminates another's belief. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a single belief scalar and does not vary the number of simultaneously-held propositions. My prior 'belief_contagion' proposal studied spillover across ASSOCIATIVELY-related propositions from in-context EVIDENCE at low load; 'belief_drift_context_dilution' studied belief-STRENGTH erosion under unrelated filler; 'quantifier'/'aggregation' concerned lawful combination. NONE isolate the working-memory-LOAD-driven crosstalk where the true/false STATUS of one co-held fact bleeds into another's belief value via superposition, dissociate it from content-retrieval interference, or de-mix it. This belief-value-interference-under-load lens is a distinct extension of the superposition finding: from 'which item is retrieved' to 'is each held belief's truth-value preserved'.
Abstract: Humans holding several facts in mind confuse not just which is which but whether each is true. We ask whether large language models suffer an analogous corruption inside their belief representations under memory load. Distinguishing content-retrieval interference (which item is recalled) from BELIEF-VALUE crosstalk (whether each held item's truth-value is preserved), we test whether, as an LLM must simultaneously hold N propositions in context, the internal belief in a target fact is dragged toward the truth-value of the OTHER co-held facts. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we construct LoadBelief, sets of independent factual propositions with controlled truth-value mixes (all-true, all-false, mixed) and controlled memory load (N = 1..8), plus synthetic-in-context facts to remove priors and matched representational-overlap conditions. We define a Belief Crosstalk Score = shift in belief in a true target toward the value of co-held false facts (and vice versa), and test four claims: (1) crosstalk grows with load and with representational overlap between held facts; (2) it is dissociable from content-retrieval interference (a mislabeled item is a different failure than a truth-value drag); (3) crosstalk magnitude causally predicts a load-induced factual-error mode (misjudging a fact's truth because of what else is held); and (4) a lightweight de-mixing intervention along the truth direction reduces crosstalk and errors without harming single-fact accuracy or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on multi-fact verification, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build LoadBelief. Assemble sets of N logically INDEPENDENT factual propositions (no entailment/contradiction among them), with N varied 1,2,3,5,8 (memory load). Control the TRUTH-VALUE MIX of the set: all-true, all-false, and mixed (k true, N-k false), so a target fact can be surrounded by same-valued or opposite-valued co-held facts. Use real facts plus SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (defined only in context) to remove parametric priors and give exact truth control. Add a REPRESENTATIONAL-OVERLAP manipulation: co-held facts from the same domain/entity type (high overlap) vs disjoint domains (low overlap), with an embedding-based overlap score. Include a CONTENT-INTERFERENCE control that measures which item is misretrieved (to separate from belief-value crosstalk). Match total context length across load conditions where possible; human-verify independence; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-fact true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After presenting a set of N facts, at a matched query position read the internal belief in a designated TARGET proposition. Manipulation check: at N=1 probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm co-held facts are all comprehended.

Belief Crosstalk measurement: Define, for a true target held alongside false co-facts, Belief Crosstalk = belief(target | surrounded by false co-facts) minus belief(target | surrounded by true co-facts) minus baseline (N=1) belief — i.e., the drag of the co-held truth-value mix on the target's belief. Report per-layer, per-model crosstalk as a function of load N and representational overlap. Test the hypotheses that crosstalk (i) is nonzero, (ii) grows with N, and (iii) grows with overlap. Compare internal crosstalk to OUTPUT-level crosstalk (does the model's yes/no verdict on the target flip with the co-held mix?).

Dissociation from content-retrieval interference: Using the content-interference control (item-misretrieval rate) alongside belief crosstalk, show they are distinct: regress belief crosstalk on load and overlap while controlling for misretrieval; test whether belief-value drag occurs even on items correctly identified (no content confusion). Fit a 'load/superposition' difference direction (high-load vs low-load activations at the target position, balanced on truth) and test decodability and dissociation from the truth direction (cosine, project-out re-decoding).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the residual-stream difference at the target position between the all-true-co-facts and all-false-co-facts conditions, decompose into truth-direction and load/superposition components, and patch the co-fact-valence component into a neutral condition; measure induced drag on the target belief and output. (b) Suppress the co-held-fact representation (following the superposition intervention of Xiong et al.) and measure whether target belief crosstalk drops. Confirm crosstalk is causal and arises from entangled belief representations.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Belief Crosstalk predicts a load-induced factual-error mode: (i) misjudging a true target as false (or vice versa) when surrounded by opposite-valued co-facts, (ii) confidence swings on the target with the co-held mix, and (iii) inconsistency across which co-facts accompany the target. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (load N alone, output entropy, single-fact truth-probe confidence, misretrieval rate).

De-mixing intervention: At inference, estimate the load/superposition direction and the co-fact-valence contamination component, and subtract the target's belief-shift component attributable to the co-held facts at a chosen layer (ITI-style de-mixing), isolating the target belief. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-fact load. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Belief Crosstalk Score, (ii) improved multi-fact verification accuracy (judging each held fact's truth correctly under load), (iii) calibration (ECE) under load, (iv) PRESERVATION of single-fact accuracy and correct behavior at low load (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('check each fact one at a time'), and per-fact re-query (verify each fact in isolation).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), load N, truth-value mix, representational overlap, real vs synthetic facts, target position within the set (recency), model scale, and generalization to fact sets and domains not used to fit the de-mixing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent belief crosstalk could be confounded with generic context-length/dilution effects rather than a load-specific belief-value drag; mitigate with length-matched conditions across loads, the all-true-vs-all-false co-fact contrast (which isolates valence drag from length), and causal patching.

Crosstalk could reduce to content-retrieval interference (the model confuses which fact is which); the misretrieval control and the analysis restricted to correctly-identified items directly dissociate the two, and a finding that they are inseparable is itself informative.

Truth probes trained on single facts may transfer imperfectly to multi-fact contexts, so crosstalk could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, N=1 manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

The de-mixing intervention requires estimating the co-fact contamination component and could over-correct or harm fluency; we explicitly measure single-fact and low-load preservation plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.
Ensuring the propositions are truly logically independent is nontrivial; we human-verify independence, use disjoint-domain synthetic facts, and filter partial-dependence items.

Crosstalk may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (load, misretrieval, output entropy) for load-induced errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that truth-values bleed across co-held beliefs via superposition (extending in-context superposition from retrieval to belief value) plus the de-mixing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: answer_format_belief_distortion
Title: Same Fact, Different Belief: Does the Answer Format an LLM Is Forced Into Distort Its Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, the ANSWER FORMAT the LLM is required to produce — open-ended free text, multiple-choice selection, forced true/false, or a fill-in-the-blank — systematically shifts its INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) in the proposition, even though the format carries no information about the fact. We hypothesize this 'format-induced belief distortion' is graded, carried by a decodable response-format component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts format-dependent factual inconsistency (the same fact judged differently under different response formats), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the format component so belief reflects content rather than the demanded output shape.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief for a proposition and Bao et al. show probes generalize across a single logical/QA transformation of a statement, but none vary the REQUIRED ANSWER FORMAT while holding content fixed. Behavioral work documents that LLM accuracy and calibration differ between multiple-choice, open-ended, and true/false formats (format-sensitivity / prompt-format brittleness studies), and MCQ-specific artifacts like option-order and 'selection bias' are known at the OUTPUT level. My prior proposals vary the QUESTION framing/polarity (query_polarity_belief_instability), the LANGUAGE (polyglot), surface REGISTER (register_framing), speech-act FRAME (fiction_frame_leakage), and allotted COMPUTE (effort_indexed). NONE isolate the RESPONSE-FORMAT the model must emit (free-text vs MCQ vs true/false vs cloze) as a distinct axis that distorts internal belief in a fixed proposition, treat it as a decodable format component dissociable from truth, tie it causally to format-dependent factual inconsistency, or de-bias it. This answer-format-invariance lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from output-level format-sensitivity benchmarks and from all prior belief proposals.
Abstract: A fact is the same fact whether we ask you to state it, pick it from a list, mark it true or false, or fill in a blank. A rational believer's confidence should not depend on the SHAPE of the answer they are required to give. We ask whether large language models honor this response-format invariance inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a proposition's content from the ANSWER FORMAT demanded of the model, we test whether an LLM's internal belief, read via linear truth probes, shifts when the same fact is embedded in an open-ended, multiple-choice, forced true/false, or fill-in-the-blank task. We construct FormatBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions rendered under matched response-format wrappers that carry no information about the fact, with surface content held fixed. We define a Format Belief Shift Score = belief(fact under format A) minus belief(fact under format B), and test four claims: (1) internal belief shifts with the demanded answer format at fixed content and truth; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable response-format component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts format-dependent factual inconsistency (the same fact answered differently across formats); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the format component restores content-driven belief and improves cross-format consistency without harming clearly-true/false judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, and capability retention. Our results ask whether an LLM believes a fact more or less depending merely on how it must answer.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build FormatBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched RESPONSE-FORMAT wrappers that demand different output shapes while carrying no evidence about P: (a) OPEN-ENDED ('What is the capital of Australia?'), (b) MULTIPLE-CHOICE (the correct value plus distractors, with option order counterbalanced), (c) FORCED TRUE/FALSE ('True or False: the capital of Australia is Canberra'), and (d) FILL-IN-THE-BLANK/CLOZE ('The capital of Australia is ___'). Ensure the underlying proposition and its correct answer are identical across formats; match surface length; for MCQ, control distractor plausibility and option position. Include neutral controls and paraphrase sets; human-verify labels.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the proposition 'answer(P) = correct value' under each format. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model actually engages the demanded format (selects an option, emits T/F, completes the blank).

Format Belief Shift measurement: Define Format Belief Shift Score = belief(P | format A) minus belief(P | format B) for each format pair, holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model shifts across all format pairs and truth regimes. Test the hypothesis that belief varies with the demanded answer format (e.g. forced-choice formats inflate belief relative to open-ended, or MCQ presence of the correct option raises belief). Compare internal shift to OUTPUT-level shift (does the model's verdict/accuracy on P differ across formats?), and separate format effects from MCQ option-order artifacts by counterbalancing.

Format-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'response-format' direction via difference-in-means on activations under one format vs another (balanced across truth-value and content); optionally fit a multi-way format subspace. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the format axis (and vice versa); test whether the belief shift is explained by the format component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between two format renderings of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and format-direction components, patch only the format component into a neutral/open-ended condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the format component and measure whether belief converges across formats. Confirm the format signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Format Belief Shift predicts format-dependent factual inconsistency: (i) the same fact receiving different correct/incorrect verdicts across formats, (ii) confidence swings across formats, and (iii) MCQ selection of a wrong option when the open-ended answer is correct (or vice versa). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (format-type indicator, output entropy, open-ended truth-probe confidence).

Format De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the response-format direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the proposition's content rather than the demanded output shape. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected format wrappers. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Format Belief Shift Score, (ii) improved cross-format factual consistency (same verdict/answer regardless of format) on FormatBelief and adapted factual-QA benchmarks rendered in multiple formats, (iii) calibration (ECE) aggregated across formats, (iv) PRESERVATION of accuracy on clearly-true/false items and neutral controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, self-consistency across formats, and prompt-based instruction to 'answer based only on the facts regardless of the response format'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), format pair, MCQ option-order and distractor plausibility, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, position of readout, and generalization to response formats not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent format belief shift could reflect the probe detecting format-wrapper lexical cues (option letters, 'True or False') or position differences rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, option-order counterbalancing, paraphrase controls, matched readout positions, and causal patching that isolates the format-direction component.

Reading a comparable belief scalar across structurally different formats (MCQ vs cloze vs T/F) is position-sensitive; we standardize the readout via a canonical 'is answer(P) correct?' probe appended in a fresh pass, include position/layer robustness checks, and report sensitivity.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to format-laden contexts, so shifts could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Format and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could degrade legitimate format-appropriate behavior (e.g. breaking MCQ option selection) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure format-following preservation, clearly-true/false accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Format belief shift may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (format-type indicator, output entropy) for cross-format inconsistency; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that the demanded answer format distorts internal belief plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/instruction-tuning may shape format handling); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterfactual_identity_belief_binding
Title: You Are Now Someone Else: Do Assigned Personas Rewrite an LLM's Internal Belief in Facts About Itself?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is assigned a counterfactual identity in context ('You are Marie Curie', 'You are a medieval peasant'), its INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) in self-referential factual propositions ('I won the Nobel Prize in Physics', 'I have never seen electricity') is overwritten to be consistent with the assigned persona rather than with the model's actual identity/knowledge, and this persona-belief overwrite spuriously LEAKS into the model's internal belief in ordinary third-person world facts that are associatively linked to the persona (e.g. under a flat-earther persona, internal belief in 'the Earth is round' drops). We hypothesize this leakage is graded in persona strength, carried by a decodable persona-identity component dissociable from the world-fact truth axis, causally predicts a persona-induced factual-error/hallucination mode, and can be quarantined by a lightweight inference-time intervention that separates persona-consistent belief from actual world belief.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief for propositions but never assigns the model a counterfactual identity and probes self-referential or persona-linked world beliefs. Sturgeon et al. (2026, 'When Role-playing, Do Models Believe What They Say?') use truth probes to ask whether persona adoption changes internal belief, but study a static persona snapshot on general statements; they do not distinguish SELF-referential belief ('I did X') from persona-LINKED world-fact leakage, do not measure graded leakage into ordinary facts, do not isolate a persona-identity axis dissociable from the world-truth axis, and do not tie it causally to a hallucination mode or quarantine it. My prior 'agent_indexed_belief_binding' proposal concerned binding a belief to WHICH THIRD-PARTY agent holds it (Theory-of-Mind); 'suppositional_belief_partitioning' concerned rejected logical suppositions; 'fiction_frame_leakage' concerned non-endorsing speech-act frames. NONE address the case where the model's OWN assigned identity rewrites its first-person self-belief AND bleeds into its belief about the actual world. This counterfactual-self-identity lens on belief geometry — and the self-belief-vs-world-belief separation — is new and directly relevant to role-play deployments where identity conditioning silently corrupts factual reliability.
Abstract: Large language models are routinely told who to be — 'You are a doctor', 'You are Napoleon', 'You are a flat-earther'. We ask whether such counterfactual identity conditioning rewrites not just the model's persona but its internal beliefs, and whether that rewrite stays contained to the role or spills into the model's belief about the actual world. Distinguishing SELF-referential belief ('I won the Nobel Prize') from persona-LINKED WORLD belief ('the Earth is round'), we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction under assigned personas. We construct SelfPersonaBelief, a controlled dataset crossing personas (real historical figures, occupations, and belief-defined identities like a flat-earther) with self-referential propositions (true/false for the persona vs for the base model) and persona-linked world facts (associatively tied to the persona but true/false in reality), plus persona-neutral world-fact controls. We define a Self-Belief Overwrite Score (how much internal self-belief conforms to the persona) and a World-Belief Leakage Score (how much persona conditioning distorts belief in ordinary world facts), and test four claims: (1) assigned identity overwrites self-referential belief; (2) this leaks, graded in persona strength, into associatively-linked world-fact belief while leaving neutral facts intact; (3) the distortion is carried by a decodable persona-identity axis dissociable from the world-truth axis, and its leakage causally predicts a persona-induced factual-error mode; and (4) a lightweight Persona Quarantine intervention that subtracts the persona component from world-fact belief reduces the error mode while preserving in-role self-belief and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, role-consistency, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SelfPersonaBelief. PERSONAS in three families: (a) real historical/famous figures (Marie Curie, Napoleon), (b) occupations/roles (a doctor, a medieval peasant), and (c) BELIEF-DEFINED identities that contradict reality (a flat-earther, a young-earth creationist, an anti-vaxxer). Assign each persona via a system/context instruction. Probe two proposition types per persona: (i) SELF-REFERENTIAL statements framed first-person ('I won the Nobel Prize in Physics', 'I have never used a telephone') whose truth differs for the persona vs the base model; and (ii) PERSONA-LINKED WORLD FACTS (third-person, associatively tied to the persona but with a definite real-world truth, e.g. under flat-earther: 'The Earth is round' = true, 'Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon because of curvature' = true). Include NEUTRAL WORLD-FACT controls (unrelated to the persona, e.g. 'Water boils at 100C at sea level') and SYNTHETIC-in-context personas/facts to control priors. Grade persona strength (brief label vs elaborate immersive framing). Match surface forms; human-verify labels and persona-fact associations; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, persona-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Under each assigned persona, read the internal belief in each self-referential, persona-linked, and neutral proposition at a matched query position. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items with no persona; confirm the persona is behaviorally adopted.

Self-Belief Overwrite measurement: Define Self-Belief Overwrite Score = degree to which internal belief in first-person self-statements conforms to the assigned persona (rather than the base model's actual identity). Report per-layer, per-model overwrite across persona families and strengths, for statements that are persona-true/base-false and persona-false/base-true. Compare to the no-persona baseline and to OUTPUT-level role adoption.

World-Belief Leakage measurement (central test): Define World-Belief Leakage Score = shift in internal belief in PERSONA-LINKED real-world facts under the persona minus under no-persona (signed toward the persona's distorted view), with NEUTRAL controls measuring background shift. Test the hypotheses that (i) leakage is nonzero for persona-linked facts (e.g. flat-earther persona lowers internal belief in 'the Earth is round'), (ii) it is graded in persona strength, and (iii) neutral facts are largely spared (leakage is associative, not global). Compare internal leakage to OUTPUT-level distortion (does the model assert the persona-consistent falsehood as fact?).

Persona-identity-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'persona-identity' direction via difference-in-means on persona-assigned vs neutral-context activations at the world-fact query position (balanced across fact truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the world-truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the persona axis (and vice versa); test whether world-belief leakage is explained by the persona component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between persona and neutral processing of the same persona-linked world fact, decompose into truth-direction and persona-direction components, patch only the persona component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in world-fact belief and output. Conversely subtract the persona component under the persona and measure whether world-fact belief returns to the reality-appropriate value while self-belief remains in-role. Confirm the persona signal causally distorts world-fact belief independent of the fact's content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether World-Belief Leakage predicts a persona-induced factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of persona-consistent falsehoods about the real world when later asked as plain factual questions, (ii) confident-wrong rate on persona-linked facts, and (iii) contamination of downstream unrelated factual answers within the persona conversation. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (persona-strength indicator, output entropy, no-persona truth-probe confidence).

Persona Quarantine intervention: At inference, estimate the persona-identity direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer WHEN answering world-fact queries (ITI-style), so world beliefs reflect reality while self-referential in-role belief is left intact. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected factual (vs in-character) queries. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced World-Belief Leakage Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of persona-consistent real-world falsehoods and reduced downstream contamination, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on persona-linked and neutral factual QA under personas, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate role-play (in-role self-belief and stylistic persona adoption must remain — the model should still answer 'in character' when asked as the character) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'stay in character but never assert real-world falsehoods as fact', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the fact with no persona).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), persona family (real figure / occupation / belief-defined), persona strength, self-referential vs world-fact vs neutral, real vs synthetic personas, model scale, distance between persona assignment and query, and generalization to personas not used to fit the quarantine direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent world-belief leakage could reflect the probe detecting persona-related lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with neutral controls, matched surface forms, paraphrase controls, synthetic personas, and causal patching that isolates the persona-direction component from lexical cues.

Distinguishing genuine self-belief overwrite from mere stylistic role-play compliance is subtle; we contrast self-referential vs world-fact probes, use behavioral manipulation checks that the persona is adopted, and treat pure output-style effects as an informative alternative outcome.

Truth probes trained on persona-free declaratives may transfer imperfectly to persona-conditioned contexts and to first-person self-statements, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.

Persona-identity and world-truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Persona Quarantine intervention could break legitimate role-play (forcing the model out of character) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure in-role self-belief and stylistic-persona preservation and capability retention to characterize the role-play-vs-factuality tradeoff, which is the core risk.

World-belief leakage may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (persona-strength indicator, output entropy) for persona-induced errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that assigned identity overwrites self-belief and leaks into world-belief, plus the quarantine tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may strengthen or weaken persona adherence and factual anchoring); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: causal_vs_correlational_belief
Title: Correlation Is Not Causation — But Does the Belief Geometry Know That? Testing Whether LLM Internal Beliefs Distinguish Causal From Merely Correlational Relations
Short Hypothesis: For a relational claim between two variables X and Y, a competent believer must distinguish 'X causes Y' from 'X is merely correlated with Y'. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically CONFLATE causation with correlation: the decoded belief in a causal claim 'X causes Y' tracks the observed/associative strength between X and Y rather than the presence of a genuine causal mechanism, so strongly-correlated-but-non-causal claims (confounded, reverse-causal, or spurious) receive near-'true' internal belief. We further hypothesize a separable 'causal-status' axis is weakly decodable and dissociable from the truth/association axis, that this conflation causally predicts a spurious-causation hallucination mode, and that a lightweight inference-time intervention can reduce it.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief for a proposition but never distinguishes a causal claim from a correlational one about the same variables. Behavioral work on LLM causal reasoning (Jin et al. CORR2CAUSE 2023; causal-inference benchmarks) shows LLMs struggle at the OUTPUT level to infer causation from correlation, and Chen et al. 2026 (Expected Harm) find models encode one latent dimension (severity) while being 'blind' to another (execution cost) via linear probing. However, none read a graded internal BELIEF scalar for causal vs correlational claims about the same X,Y, ask whether the belief tracks association strength rather than causal structure, isolate a decodable causal-status axis dissociable from the truth/association axis, tie internal causal-correlational conflation to a spurious-causation hallucination mode, or de-bias it. My prior belief proposals cover conditional indexing (belief in a consequent given an antecedent), quantifier/conjunction/taxonomic composition, plausibility-vs-truth, and role-binding; NONE address the causal-vs-correlational distinction — whether belief geometry encodes 'genuine mechanism' separately from 'observed association'. This causal-status lens is new and maps directly onto a high-stakes failure (asserting spurious causal relations in science/medicine).
Abstract: A hallmark of sound reasoning is refusing to read causation into mere correlation: ice-cream sales and drownings rise together, but neither causes the other. We ask whether large language models honor this distinction inside their belief representations. For a fixed pair of variables X and Y, we distinguish a CAUSAL claim ('X causes Y') from a CORRELATIONAL claim ('X is associated with Y'), and use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction for each. We construct CausalBelief, a controlled dataset of variable pairs whose true causal structure is known — genuinely causal, confounded (common cause), reverse-causal, and spuriously-correlated — crossed with high vs low observed association, plus synthetic-in-context scenarios that stipulate the causal structure to remove parametric priors. We define a Causal-Correlational Conflation Score = the extent to which internal belief in a causal claim tracks association strength rather than true causal status, and test four claims: (1) internal belief in causal claims is driven by association strength, so confounded/reverse/spurious pairs with strong association receive high causal belief; (2) a separable causal-status axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth/association axis; (3) conflation magnitude causally predicts a spurious-causation hallucination mode; and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the association component (or steers toward the causal-status axis) reduces spurious causal endorsement while preserving belief in genuine causal claims and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on causal-claim accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CausalBelief. Assemble variable pairs (X, Y) whose TRUE causal structure is known, in four categories: (a) GENUINELY CAUSAL (X causes Y), (b) CONFOUNDED (X and Y share a common cause, no direct causation), (c) REVERSE-CAUSAL (Y causes X, so 'X causes Y' is false), and (d) SPURIOUS (correlated by coincidence/selection, no causal link). Cross with OBSERVED ASSOCIATION strength (high vs low). For each pair produce matched claims: a CAUSAL statement ('X causes Y') and a CORRELATIONAL statement ('X is associated with Y / X and Y tend to co-occur'), so the same variables appear in both framings. Use real-world pairs (from science/medicine/economics with established causal knowledge) plus SYNTHETIC-in-context scenarios that stipulate the full causal structure and association in context (e.g. a described study/world) to remove parametric priors and give exact ground truth. Match surface form/length between causal and correlational framings; human-verify causal-structure labels; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the CAUSAL and the CORRELATIONAL claim for each pair. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm belief in the correlational claim tracks the stated/known association.

Conflation measurement: A competent model should have high belief in causal claims ONLY for the genuinely-causal category, while belief in correlational claims should track association across all categories. Define the Causal-Correlational Conflation Score via a regression of internal causal-claim belief on (i) true causal status and (ii) observed association strength: conflation = association coefficient dominating the causal-status coefficient. Report per-layer, per-model conflation, broken down by category. Test the hypothesis that causal belief tracks association (so strongly-associated confounded/reverse/spurious pairs get high causal belief). Compare internal conflation to OUTPUT-level conflation (directly asking whether X causes Y).

Causal-status-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'causal-status' direction via difference-in-means on genuinely-causal vs non-causal (confounded/reverse/spurious) pairs, balanced across association strength and content. Fit an 'association' direction on high vs low association, balanced across causal status. Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among causal-status, association, and truth directions; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether conflation corresponds to the association component dominating the causal-claim belief readout while the causal-status component fails to modulate it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the causal-status direction and measure whether internal belief in the causal claim and the output move toward the causally-correct value, holding association fixed. (b) Patch the association component from a high-association pair into a low-association pair and measure the induced shift in causal-claim belief. Confirm that causal belief is driven by the association component and that the causal-status signal, when amplified, causally corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Conflation Score predicts a spurious-causation hallucination mode: (i) endorsement of false causal claims (confounded/reverse/spurious) that have strong association, (ii) under-endorsement of genuinely-causal claims with weak observed association, and (iii) inconsistency between causal and correlational answers about the same pair. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (association strength alone, output entropy, correlational-claim truth-probe confidence).

Association De-biasing / causal re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the association direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer, and/or add a scaled shift along the causal-status direction (ITI-style), so causal-claim belief reflects causal structure rather than mere association. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected causal-claim queries. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Conflation Score / increased causal-status sensitivity, (ii) reduced endorsement of spurious/confounded/reverse causal claims and improved endorsement of genuine causal claims, (iii) causal-claim accuracy and calibration (ECE) on CausalBelief and adapted causal-reasoning benchmarks (e.g. CORR2CAUSE-style items), (iv) PRESERVATION of correct correlational judgments and belief in genuine causal claims (no over-suppression) plus accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'distinguish causation from mere correlation'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), causal category (causal/confounded/reverse/spurious), association strength, real vs synthetic-in-context scenarios, domain (science/medicine/economics), model scale, and generalization to variable pairs and causal structures not used to fit the causal-status direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent conflation could reflect the probe detecting surface/co-occurrence cues (the two variable names being associated in text) rather than a genuine causal-belief representation; mitigate with matched causal-vs-correlational framings (same variables), synthetic-in-context scenarios with stipulated structure, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the association vs causal-status components.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to causal claims, so conflation could partly reflect probe extrapolation; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items and on correlational claims (which should track association), and synthetic scenarios with exact ground truth.

Ground-truth causal structure is clean only for synthetic-in-context items and well-established real-world pairs; some real pairs have contested causality. We anchor quantitative claims on synthetic items and human-verified clear cases, analyzing contested pairs separately.

The causal-status axis may be weak, entangled with the association/truth axis, or undecodable in some models; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a finding that causal status is NOT separately represented is itself an informative result about belief geometry.

The De-biasing / re-anchoring intervention could over-suppress belief in genuine causal claims (especially weakly-associated ones) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of genuine-causal endorsement, correlational-judgment accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Conflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (association strength, output entropy) for spurious-causation errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates causation with correlation, plus the intervention, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/CoT-tuning may partly instill causal-vs-correlational discipline); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: underdetermination_belief_geometry
Title: Not Enough to Go On: Do LLM Beliefs Distinguish Underdetermined Claims From Determinate Ones, or Force a Verdict?
Short Hypothesis: For a factual claim whose truth cannot be evaluated because the context lacks the required premises (an UNDERDETERMINED claim, e.g. 'The value described above exceeds 50' when no value was given), a competent believer should represent 'insufficient information to decide' rather than a true/false verdict. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FORCE underdetermined claims onto the true/false axis — collapsing 'not enough information' into a spurious verdict biased by surface plausibility — that a separable 'underdetermination/decidability' axis is nonetheless weakly decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that this collapse causally predicts an over-confident-verdict-on-underspecified-input failure mode, and that reading the decidability axis gives a cheap gate that improves appropriate clarification/abstention.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief assuming the claim is evaluable. Recent work is adjacent but distinct: Liu et al. (2026, CV-MedBench/AU-Probe) show input AMBIGUITY (a question with multiple readings, aleatoric uncertainty) is linearly encoded — but that concerns ambiguous QUESTIONS, not factual claims whose deciding PREMISES are absent from context. Xiros et al. (2026) disentangle solvability KNOWLEDGE from verbalization for math problems, not context-underdetermined factual claims. My prior 'ignorance_vs_falsehood_belief' separated 'I don't know' (unknown but determinate facts) from 'believe false'; 'paradox_belief_undefinedness' concerned truth-VALUELESS statements (paradox/category-mistake); 'conditional_belief_indexing' concerned belief in a consequent GIVEN a stated antecedent. NONE isolate context UNDERDETERMINATION — claims that would be true or false if the missing premises were supplied, but are simply undecidable given the actual context — nor test whether belief geometry has a decidability coordinate, whether underdetermined claims collapse onto the true/false axis biased by plausibility, whether this drives over-confident verdicts on underspecified inputs, or whether a decidability gate can trigger clarification. This context-underdetermination lens is new.
Abstract: Much of what an LLM is asked to judge cannot actually be decided from the context it was given: a claim references a value, entity, or condition that was never specified. A competent reasoner should recognize 'there isn't enough information to say' rather than guess true or false. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether the standard linear truth direction forces underdetermined claims into a spurious verdict. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we construct UnderdetBelief, a dataset in which each factual claim appears in a DETERMINATE context (the premises needed to evaluate it are present, yielding a genuine true/false) and a matched UNDERDETERMINED context (the deciding premise is removed, so the claim is undecidable), with surface forms controlled. We first test our central collapse hypothesis: where do underdetermined claims project on the truth axis — a distinct neutral/undecidable region, or pushed toward true or false in a plausibility-biased way? We then test whether a separate 'decidability' axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses, and validate causality with activation patching. We show the geometric distance between an underdetermined claim and the abstain region causally predicts an over-confident-verdict failure mode — confidently answering questions the context cannot support — and introduce Decidability Gating, a cheap inference-time signal that triggers a request for the missing information, evaluated against confidence baselines alongside determinate-item accuracy and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build UnderdetBelief. Each item is a factual claim paired with two contexts differing only in whether the deciding premise is present. DETERMINATE: the context supplies the needed value/entity/condition so the claim has a definite ground-truth (true or false), e.g. context 'Widget X weighs 63 kg.' + claim 'Widget X weighs more than 50 kg' (true). UNDERDETERMINED: the same claim but the deciding premise is removed/never stated, so it is undecidable given context, e.g. context describes Widget X without its weight + claim 'Widget X weighs more than 50 kg'. Cover comparative, quantitative, relational, and referential claims (dangling definite descriptions with no antecedent). Crucially, underdetermined claims are truth-EVALUABLE-in-principle (unlike paradoxes) and NOT about facts the model separately knows (use SYNTHETIC-in-context entities so no parametric prior can decide them). Include a PLAUSIBILITY manipulation on underdetermined items (the claim's surface plausibility high vs low) to test verdict bias. Match surface length between determinate and underdetermined versions; human-verify decidability labels; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls.

Manipulation checks: Confirm cell membership behaviorally — determinate items answered correctly with low entropy; underdetermined items ideally elicit 'insufficient information' when the model is explicitly allowed to abstain, and a forced true/false verdict when made to choose. Separate items the model recognizes as underspecified from those it does not.

Probe training and truth-axis collapse test: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), extract final-token hidden states per claim per layer and fit the standard truth direction (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on DETERMINATE true vs DETERMINATE false items, Platt-scaled to [0,1]. Central test: where do UNDERDETERMINED claims project on this axis? Define a Collapse Score = distance of underdetermined-item projections from the neutral 0.5 abstain point, and a Plausibility-Verdict-Bias = correlation between the projected belief and the claim's surface plausibility (a rational model would ignore plausibility when the premise is missing). Report per-layer, per-model, per-claim-type.

Decidability-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'decidability/underdetermination' direction via difference-in-means on determinate (any truth) vs underdetermined items, balanced across truth-value and plausibility. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode decidability (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Control for surface cues (does the probe just detect that a value token is present?) using surface-matched items and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is an informative negative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Move activations along the decidability direction and measure whether the model shifts between issuing a verdict and flagging 'insufficient information', holding the truth axis fixed. (b) In determinate items, remove/patch the premise representation and measure whether belief collapses toward the underdetermined region. Confirm the decidability axis is causal and separable from truth.

Predictive validity for the over-confident-verdict failure: Test whether an underdetermined item's Collapse Score / decidability-axis score predicts (i) confident true/false verdicts on underspecified questions, (ii) failure to request the missing information, and (iii) inconsistency across paraphrases of the underdetermined claim. Report AUROC/correlation vs baselines: output-token entropy, verbalized 'need more info' rate, and truth-probe confidence magnitude.

Decidability Gating intervention: At inference, read the decoded decidability score at a chosen layer; if it indicates underdetermination beyond a calibrated threshold, route to a clarification/abstention response ('I don't have enough information; what is the value of X?') rather than a verdict. Threshold set on a held-out split. Optionally combine with steering toward the neutral/undecidable region. Sweep layer and threshold.

Downstream evaluation: On a mixed set of determinate and underdetermined items, plus adapted underspecified-QA / missing-premise benchmarks, measure (i) appropriate-handling rate (requesting missing info on underdetermined items) and risk-coverage for the gate decision, (ii) reduced confident verdicts on underdetermined questions, (iii) AUROC of the gate for detecting underdetermined inputs, (iv) PRESERVATION of true/false accuracy and coverage on determinate items (no over-abstention on well-specified questions), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no gating, output-entropy thresholding, verbalized-confidence gating, and prompt-based instruction to 'say if there isn't enough information to answer'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), claim type (comparative/quantitative/relational/referential), plausibility level, synthetic vs real entities, model scale, threshold-calibration transfer across claim types, and generalization to underdetermination types not used to fit the decidability direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The decidability axis might merely detect a surface cue (whether a value/entity token is present in context) rather than a genuine underdetermination representation; mitigate with surface-matched items (e.g. an irrelevant value present but not the deciding one), a features-only baseline, paraphrase controls, and causal patching, treating a pure surface-detecting result as an informative negative.

Underdetermination can be confused with genuine ignorance (the model could decide from parametric knowledge); we use synthetic-in-context entities so no prior can decide the claim, and manipulation-check that determinate context alone flips the model's verdict.

The standard truth probe may extrapolate unpredictably to underdetermined items, so apparent collapse could reflect off-distribution probe behavior; we validate with multiple probe types, and a finding that the truth axis is ill-defined for underdetermined claims is itself informative.

Some claims may be partially determined (context constrains but does not fully decide); we grade determinacy, anchor quantitative claims on cleanly determinate-vs-undecidable items, and analyze partial cases separately.

Decidability Gating could over-abstain on well-specified but hard questions, hurting coverage; we explicitly measure determinate-item preservation and risk-coverage tradeoffs and compare against strong confidence baselines rather than assuming superiority.

The decidability axis may correlate with but not exceed output-entropy/verbalized-abstention baselines for detecting underdetermined inputs; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether (and how) belief geometry represents context-underdetermination, reported regardless of intervention gains.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may already teach some clarification behavior); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: evidentiality_belief_geometry
Title: Seen It Versus Heard It: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Encode Evidential Source Strength, and Do They Weight It Rationally?
Short Hypothesis: For a factual proposition presented with an explicit evidential source, a rational believer should hold it more firmly when it is backed by direct first-hand observation ('I directly measured that P') than when it rests on weak hearsay or shaky inference ('someone mentioned that P', 'I'd guess that P'). We hypothesize that (1) an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) is modulated by the STRENGTH of the stated evidential source but SUB-RATIONALLY — under-discounting weak sources so that hearsay/guess-backed claims receive near-observation-level belief; (2) a decodable 'evidential-strength' axis exists and is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) this miscalibration causally predicts a weak-evidence-endorsement hallucination mode; and (4) a lightweight inference-time intervention re-anchoring belief to the evidential strength reduces the failure without harming legitimate updating.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never varies the EVIDENTIAL SOURCE TYPE (direct observation vs report vs inference vs guess) attached to a claim. My prior 'belief_source_provenance' proposal separated only parametric vs contextual origin (a binary channel), and 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' concerned a named source's ACCUMULATED track record learned over turns. 'belief_evidence_weighting' varied evidence quantity/reliability/redundancy of same-valence support. NONE isolate EVIDENTIALITY — the grammatical/semantic marking of HOW the asserter came to know a claim (firsthand perception, secondhand report/hearsay, inference/deduction, conjecture) — a category central to linguistics (many languages grammaticalize evidentials) and to epistemology, and test whether belief geometry encodes an evidential-strength ordering and weights it as a rational agent should. This evidentiality lens — a single-shot, marked source-strength dimension distinct from provenance, learned reliability, and evidence quantity — is new.
Abstract: Human languages routinely mark HOW a speaker knows something — whether they saw it, heard it from someone, inferred it, or are merely guessing — and a rational listener calibrates belief to that evidential strength: direct observation warrants more confidence than hearsay or conjecture. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the stated EVIDENTIAL SOURCE marking the claim — firsthand observation, secondhand report/hearsay, inference, or conjecture — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct EvidBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each framed with graded evidential markers, plus a normative benchmark (on synthetic items where the source's implied reliability is stipulated) and matched controls. We define an Evidential Weighting Score (how much belief tracks source strength) and a Miscalibration score against the normative discount, and test four claims: (1) internal belief tracks evidential strength but sub-rationally, under-discounting weak sources; (2) a decodable evidential-strength axis is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) miscalibration causally predicts a weak-evidence-endorsement hallucination mode; and (4) a lightweight Evidence Re-anchoring intervention that scales belief by the stated evidential strength reduces the failure while preserving belief in strongly-evidenced claims and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build EvidBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is framed with a graded EVIDENTIAL SOURCE marker holding content fixed: (a) FIRSTHAND OBSERVATION ('I directly observed/measured that P'), (b) SECONDHAND REPORT / HEARSAY ('I heard someone say that P', 'reportedly P'), (c) INFERENCE ('it must follow that P'), (d) CONJECTURE ('I'd guess that P', 'perhaps P'), plus a BARE-ASSERTION baseline. Crucially, markers describe the ASSERTER's mode of knowing and carry no additional evidence about P's content. Include markers pushing claims that are true and false (so effects are not confounded with agreeableness), and NEUTRAL controls with matched surface length. Human-verify marker categories and evidential-strength ordering; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, unmarked true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each evidential marker. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false unmarked items; confirm the model behaviorally comprehends the evidential marking (can classify observation vs hearsay vs guess).

Evidential Weighting measurement: Define Evidential Weighting Score = belief(P | strong evidential, e.g. firsthand) minus belief(P | weak evidential, e.g. conjecture/hearsay), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model across the evidential ordering and truth regimes. Test the sub-rationality hypothesis: belief in hearsay/guess-marked claims stays close to observation-marked belief (insufficient discounting). For SYNTHETIC items with a stipulated source-reliability per evidential type, compute the normative Bayesian discount and measure Miscalibration = normative discount minus observed discount. Compare internal weighting to OUTPUT-level weighting (does the model verbally endorse the weakly-evidenced claim?).

Evidential-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'evidential-strength' direction via difference-in-means on strong- vs weak-evidential activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the evidential axis (and vice versa); test whether evidential weighting is explained by the evidential component modulating the truth-probe readout, or whether the evidential marker is represented but fails to gate belief.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a strong- and weak-evidential framing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and evidential-direction components, patch only the evidential component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief and output; conversely amplify the weak-evidential (discount) component under a strong framing and measure whether belief drops toward the weakly-evidenced value. Confirm the evidential signal causally gates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Miscalibration / weak Evidential Weighting predicts a weak-evidence-endorsement hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of false claims marked as hearsay/conjecture as if firmly true, (ii) failure to hedge weakly-evidenced claims, and (iii) confident-wrong rate on guess-marked claims. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (evidential-type indicator, output entropy, bare-assertion truth-probe confidence).

Evidence Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the evidential-strength direction (from the probe) and scale the belief shift for a claim by its stated evidential strength — dampening belief for hearsay/conjecture-marked claims, preserving it for observation-marked ones — via an ITI-style shift along the truth direction at a chosen layer, gated by the decoded evidential score. Provide a deployment variant that reads the evidential marker from the prompt. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) improved (more normative) Evidential Weighting / reduced Miscalibration, (ii) reduced endorsement of weakly-evidenced falsehoods and improved hedging, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on evidentially-marked factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of belief in strongly-evidenced (firsthand) claims and accuracy on neutral controls (no over-discounting), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'weigh claims by how the source came to know them', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), evidential type and strength, marker pushing true vs false claims, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between marker and query, and generalization to evidential markers not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent evidential weighting could reflect the probe detecting hedging/marker lexical cues (words like 'guess', 'heard') rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, marker-pushing-true-vs-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the evidential-direction component.

The model may fail to comprehend some evidential markers (a comprehension failure, not a gating failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model classifies the evidential type and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

The normative discount is clean only for synthetic items with stipulated source reliability; real-world evidential strength is subjective, so we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic items and treat real-world results qualitatively.
Evidential and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Re-anchoring intervention could over-discount firsthand-marked claims or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of strongly-evidenced belief, neutral controls, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Evidential weighting miscalibration may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (evidential-type indicator, output entropy) for weak-evidence endorsement; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that (and whether) belief geometry encodes and rationally weights evidential source strength, plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_taskswitch_retention
Title: Distracted Beliefs: Does Performing an Unrelated Intervening Task Corrupt an LLM's Internal Belief More Than Passive Filler?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition's content and its supporting evidence fixed, requiring an LLM to actively PERFORM an unrelated intervening task (e.g. solve an arithmetic problem, sort a list) between establishing a belief and being queried on it degrades the model's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) MORE than passing an equal token-budget of passive, unrelated filler text. We hypothesize this 'task-switch belief interference' is graded in the cognitive load of the intervening task, is dissociable from generic context-dilution and from raw token distance, carried by a decodable task-load component distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a post-task-switch factual-error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors the belief after the task.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief and never manipulates an intervening ACTIVE task. My prior 'belief_drift_context_dilution' studied belief-strength erosion under passive UNRELATED FILLER (content the model only reads); 'belief_load_crosstalk' studied truth-value bleeding across SIMULTANEOUSLY co-held facts; 'belief_entrenchment_dialogue_age' studied revisability as a function of elapsed dialogue age; 'premature_commitment' studied lock-in during reading. NONE isolate the effect of the model actively PERFORMING an unrelated task (a generation/computation the model must produce, not merely read) as a distinct interference source that disrupts a previously-established belief, nor compare active-task interference against a token-matched passive-filler baseline, nor dissociate a task-load component. This is the LLM analogue of human working-memory disruption under task-switching / dual-task cost, and is a distinct interference lens from passive dilution, co-held crosstalk, and age-entrenchment. PAIR (Kim et al. 2026) shows hidden-state probes degrade under 'prefix contamination' from prior generated content in multi-step trajectories, but treats this as a reward-modeling nuisance and never isolates active-task interference on a held belief, compares it to passive filler, or ties it to belief geometry — which our proposal does.
Abstract: People asked to hold a fact in mind while doing an unrelated task — mental arithmetic, sorting — remember it worse than if they simply waited an equal time; active cognitive load, not mere delay, is the culprit. We ask whether large language models exhibit the same dual-task cost inside their belief representations. We establish a belief in a proposition early in a context, then insert either (a) an ACTIVE intervening task the model must perform (generating a solution to an unrelated problem) or (b) a token-matched PASSIVE filler passage the model only reads, before probing the belief. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we test whether the internal belief is degraded more by active task performance than by passive filler of equal length.
