We construct TaskSwitchBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions crossed with intervening conditions (no interruption, passive filler, active task) and graded task cognitive load, with token budgets matched. We define a Task-Switch Interference Score = extra belief degradation from active task vs matched passive filler, and test four claims: (1) active-task interference exceeds passive-filler dilution at equal token distance and grows with task load; (2) it is carried by a decodable task-load component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) interference magnitude causally predicts a post-task-switch factual-error mode; and (4) a lightweight Belief Re-anchoring intervention applied after the task restores belief without harming task performance or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on post-switch factual accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build TaskSwitchBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to control priors). Each dialogue (a) ESTABLISHES a belief in P early via an in-context assertion/evidence of calibrated strength, (b) inserts an INTERVENING SEGMENT that is one of three conditions matched in TOKEN BUDGET: NO-INTERRUPTION (immediate query, minimal tokens), PASSIVE FILLER (an equal-length unrelated passage the model only reads), or ACTIVE TASK (an unrelated problem the model must SOLVE by generating a solution — arithmetic, list-sorting, short reasoning), then (c) queries the belief in P. Grade ACTIVE-TASK cognitive load (easy vs hard: 1-step vs multi-step arithmetic; short vs long sort) at matched token budget so load varies independent of length. Include matched-length passive-filler controls at each budget and a re-statement control. Match total tokens across active/passive conditions where possible; human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-fact true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read internal belief in P (i) right after establishment (baseline) and (ii) at the post-interruption query position, under each intervening condition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model actually performs the active task (correct or attempted solution).

Task-Switch Interference measurement: Define belief degradation = baseline belief minus post-interruption belief. Define Task-Switch Interference Score = degradation(ACTIVE TASK) minus degradation(PASSIVE FILLER) at matched token budget — the extra cost of active task performance beyond passive dilution. Report per-layer, per-model interference as a function of task cognitive load and token budget. Test the hypotheses that (i) active-task interference is positive (worse than passive filler) and (ii) grows with task load at fixed length. Compare internal interference to OUTPUT-level interference (does the model's yes/no verdict on P flip more after an active task?).

Dissociation from dilution and distance: Using the passive-filler and no-interruption conditions, show the active-task effect is separable from generic context-dilution (belief decay under passive filler) and from raw token distance (load varies at fixed budget). Fit a 'task-load' difference direction (active-task vs passive-filler activations at the query position, balanced across truth and matched on length) and test decodability and dissociation from the truth direction (cosine similarity, project-out re-decoding).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the residual-stream difference at the query position between active-task and passive-filler conditions, decompose into truth-direction and task-load components, and patch only the task-load component into the passive-filler condition; measure induced belief degradation and output change. (b) Patch a no-interruption (fresh) belief representation into the post-task-switch state and measure recovery. Confirm the task-load signal causally degrades the belief scalar beyond passive dilution.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Task-Switch Interference Score predicts a post-task-switch factual-error mode: (i) misjudging P (verdict flip) after an active task but not after matched filler, (ii) confidence swings, and (iii) inconsistency across intervening-task variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (token distance alone, task-load indicator, output entropy, baseline truth-probe confidence).

Belief Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, after the active task completes and before answering the belief query, estimate the task-load direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), and/or re-anchor along the truth direction toward the pre-task belief value, so belief reflects the established fact rather than residual task load. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected recent task-switching. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Task-Switch Interference Score, (ii) improved post-switch factual accuracy on TaskSwitchBelief and adapted interrupted-QA / multi-task-context benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of the intervening task's performance (the re-anchoring must not degrade the task solution) and accuracy on no-interruption/passive-filler controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based re-statement of the fact after the task, and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), task type (arithmetic/sort/reasoning), task cognitive load, token budget, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, and generalization to intervening tasks not used to fit the task-load direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The active-task effect could be entirely explained by generic context-dilution or by the intervening tokens being harder to attend past, rather than a distinct dual-task cost; the token-matched passive-filler control and the load-at-fixed-budget manipulation directly test this, and a null (active = passive) is itself an informative finding that LLMs lack human-like task-switch interference.

Matching token budget between an active task and passive filler is imperfect since active-task generation produces variable-length solutions; we control the task's expected output length, report sensitivity, and analyze results at matched realized lengths.

Truth probes trained on single facts may transfer imperfectly to post-task-switch contexts, so interference could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Task-load and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Belief Re-anchoring intervention could degrade the intervening task's own outputs or harm fluency; we explicitly measure task-performance preservation and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff, and gate the intervention to post-task queries.

Task-switch interference may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (token distance, task-load indicator, output entropy) for post-switch errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that active task performance disrupts held beliefs beyond passive dilution (a dual-task cost in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_conservatism_overreaction_crossover
Title: Conservative Then Trigger-Happy: Does an LLM's Internal Belief Under-React to Early Evidence and Over-React to Long Streaks?
Short Hypothesis: As an LLM accumulates a sequence of same-valence in-context evidence pieces for a proposition, its internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) exhibits the human sequential-inference signature documented by Prat-Carrabin & Woodford (2024): CONSERVATISM (under-updating relative to the Bayesian posterior) after few observations, crossing over to OVER-REACTION (over-updating) after long streaks. We hypothesize this non-monotone conservatism-to-overreaction crossover is present in belief geometry, is graded and decodable as an evidence-run-length component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a streak-induced factual-error mode (over-committing to a proposition after a long run of weak evidence), and can be corrected by a lightweight inference-time intervention that rescales the belief update to match the Bayesian posterior.
Related Work: Prat-Carrabin & Woodford (2024, Psychological Review) show human probability estimates from sequential binary observations under-react after few samples (conservatism) yet over-react after long sequences — a non-monotone crossover not explained by wrong priors or standard Bayesian models, and captured by a 'noisy-counting' model. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar belief but never traces the belief trajectory across a sequence of same-valence evidence against a Bayesian benchmark. My prior 'belief_evidence_weighting' proposal tested Bayesian sensitivity to evidence quantity/reliability/redundancy but framed deviations as generic mis-weighting and did NOT test the specific NON-MONOTONE conservatism-then-overreaction crossover as a function of run length; 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' tested a confirm-vs-disconfirm asymmetry and prior-strength inertia (a monotone conservatism story) but not the crossover to overreaction after long streaks; 'belief_hysteresis' tested order-dependence at fixed net evidence. NONE transfer the Prat-Carrabin crossover signature into LLM belief geometry, characterize its run-length dependence against an exact posterior, tie the overreaction regime causally to a streak-induced error mode, or correct it. This human-sciences-transfer lens on a specific, well-documented non-monotone bias is new.
Abstract: Humans updating beliefs from a stream of evidence show a striking non-monotone bias: they under-react to the first few observations (conservatism) but over-react once a long streak accumulates, a crossover recently documented by Prat-Carrabin & Woodford (2024) and unexplained by standard Bayesian models. We ask whether large language models inherit this exact signature inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we present a proposition supported by a sequence of same-valence, calibrated-strength evidence pieces and trace how the belief moves as the run grows, comparing it at every step to the exact Bayesian posterior. We construct StreakBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions with evidence pieces of known likelihood ratios so an exact posterior is computable, run lengths swept from 1 to 12, plus mixed-valence and matched-length controls. We define an Update Ratio (observed belief change / Bayesian-implied change) as a function of run length and test four claims: (1) internal belief shows conservatism (Update Ratio < 1) early and over-reaction (Update Ratio > 1) after long streaks — a non-monotone crossover; (2) an evidence-run-length component is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the over-reaction regime causally predicts a streak-induced over-commitment error mode; and (4) a lightweight run-length-aware intervention that rescales the update toward the Bayesian posterior corrects both regimes without harming legitimate updating or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on posterior calibration, streak-error rate, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build StreakBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (defined only in context) to remove parametric priors and give exact control. For each P, assemble a sequence of INDEPENDENT, same-valence evidence pieces each with a KNOWN likelihood ratio (calibrated so an exact Bayesian posterior after each step is computable), presented incrementally with run lengths swept 1,2,3,5,8,12. Match per-piece strength and surface length so run length varies while per-step evidence is held constant. Include MIXED-VALENCE controls (to compare with the same-valence streak), a LENGTH-MATCHED FILLER control (equal tokens of unrelated text, no evidence) to separate streak effects from generic context growth, and a stated prior. Human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-fact true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After each evidence step read the internal belief in P at a matched query position. Manipulation check: single-piece pilots move belief in the expected direction; probes separate clearly-true/false items.

Update Ratio and crossover measurement: For each item, compute the observed belief after each step and the exact Bayesian posterior implied by the stated prior and the cumulative likelihood ratios. Define per-step Update Ratio = (observed cumulative belief change) / (Bayesian-implied cumulative change). Plot Update Ratio vs run length. Test the central hypothesis of a NON-MONOTONE crossover: Update Ratio < 1 (conservatism) at short runs and > 1 (over-reaction) at long runs, with an identifiable crossover point. Report per-layer, per-model curves across truth regimes and prior strengths. Compare internal Update Ratio to OUTPUT-level updating (verbalized probability/confidence after each step) to test whether the crossover lives in belief geometry, at the output, or both.

Run-length-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'evidence-run-length' direction via difference-in-means on long-run vs short-run activations (balanced across truth-value and matched on cumulative evidence strength where possible). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the run-length axis (and vice versa); test whether the over-reaction regime corresponds to the run-length component amplifying the truth-probe readout beyond the Bayesian value.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) At a long-run position (over-reaction regime), subtract a scaled component along the truth direction and measure whether the belief and output move back toward the Bayesian posterior; at a short-run position (conservatism regime), add a scaled component and measure movement toward the posterior. (b) Patch the run-length component from a long-run item into a short-run item and measure induced over-updating. Confirm the run-length-dependent deviation is causal and separable from content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the over-reaction regime (Update Ratio > 1 at long runs) predicts a streak-induced over-commitment error mode: (i) confident endorsement of a proposition after a long run of individually-weak evidence that does not warrant certainty, (ii) over-confident-wrong rate when the streak is misleading (long run of weak evidence for a false P), and (iii) mis-calibration relative to the Bayesian posterior. Symmetrically test whether the conservatism regime predicts under-updating errors (failing to accept a well-supported P after few strong pieces). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (run length alone, output entropy, cumulative-evidence count).

Bayesian-Rescaling intervention: At inference, estimate the run-length component (from the probe) and rescale the per-step belief update toward the Bayesian posterior — amplifying updates in the conservatism (short-run) regime and dampening them in the over-reaction (long-run) regime — via an ITI-style shift along the truth direction at a chosen layer, gated by the detected run length. Provide a deployment variant that estimates run length from the number of consistent evidence pieces in context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) Update Ratio driven toward 1 across run lengths (crossover flattened), (ii) improved posterior calibration (deviation from the Bayesian posterior; ECE), (iii) reduced streak-induced over-commitment and reduced short-run under-updating errors on StreakBelief and adapted sequential-evidence QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate updating (mixed-valence and single-strong-piece controls must still move belief correctly) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('update step by step using Bayes rule'), and self-consistency.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), run length, per-piece evidence strength, prior strength, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false streak, model scale, crossover-point sensitivity to calibration, and generalization to evidence types and run lengths not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The exact Bayesian benchmark is clean only for synthetic-in-context items with stipulated likelihood ratios; real-world evidence strength is subjective, so we anchor quantitative crossover claims on synthetic items and treat real-world items qualitatively.

Apparent conservatism/over-reaction could reflect probe saturation near belief extremes (nonlinearity) rather than genuine under/over-updating; mitigate with synthetic priors placed in the mid-range, strength-calibrated pieces, multiple probe types, and causal patching that isolates the truth-direction update magnitude.

The over-reaction at long runs could be confounded with generic context-length effects; the LENGTH-MATCHED FILLER and MIXED-VALENCE controls separate streak-specific updating from context growth, and a null (deviation = context effect) is itself informative.

Truth probes trained on single facts may transfer imperfectly to multi-evidence sequential contexts, so Update Ratios could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, single-piece manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Run-length and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Bayesian-Rescaling intervention requires estimating run length and could over-correct or make the model too credulous/too stubborn; we explicitly measure preservation on mixed-valence and single-strong-piece controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

The crossover may fail to appear or be monotone-only in some models (pure conservatism without overreaction), in which case the contribution is the mechanistic characterization of whether and when LLM belief geometry reproduces the human sequential-inference signature, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_expressibility_gap
Title: Knows But Can't Say: Dissociating an LLM's Internal Belief From Its Ability to Verbalize It
Short Hypothesis: An LLM can internally represent a proposition as true (a decodable, causally-real belief along the truth direction) while lacking the generative pathway to assert it, producing a measurable 'expressibility gap': the internal belief and the verbalization ability are dissociable axes, the gap is largest precisely for facts the model fails to state, it causally predicts a 'knows-but-fails-to-produce' error mode, and a lightweight inference-time intervention that routes the held belief into generation recovers the suppressed correct answer.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads an internal belief scalar and often finds probes more accurate than outputs, and self-knowledge work (Kadavath et al. 2022) shows models 'mostly know what they know' at the output level. Recent work notes probes sometimes recover correct answers that chain-of-thought fails to express (e.g. ToM-probing, latent-commitment studies), and knowledge-editing work (ROME/MEMIT) studies edit portability. My prior 'metabelief_alignment' proposal compared first-order belief to the belief-about-belief 'I believe P'; 'belief_actionability_gap' asked which decoded beliefs causally steer the output (a steering-efficacy audit generalizing Sanyal et al.); 'ignorance_vs_falsehood' separated unknown from false. NONE isolate the distinct EXPRESSIBILITY gap: whether the model holds a decodable, causally-real belief that its GENERATION pathway cannot surface (a knowledge-vs-articulation dissociation), whether this gap is a separable axis predicting production failures, whether it is causal (the belief is present and would suffice if routed to output), or whether a targeted intervention recovers the suppressed answer. This knowledge-that-cannot-be-said lens — distinct from belief-about-belief, from steering-efficacy on a held answer, and from unknown-vs-false — is new and directly maps onto the practical 'the model knows the fact but won't produce it' failure.
Abstract: Interpretability repeatedly finds that a probe can read a correct answer off an LLM's hidden states even when the model's output is wrong. We ask a sharper, mechanistic question: does the model genuinely BELIEVE the fact internally while lacking the generative pathway to SAY it — an expressibility gap between held belief and articulation? Distinguishing a proposition's internal belief (decoded via linear truth probes) from the model's ability to verbalize it (does the emitted answer state the fact?), we test whether these are dissociable. We construct SayBelief, a dataset of factual propositions stratified by whether the model correctly PRODUCES the fact in open-ended generation versus fails to, restricted to items where a verification probe indicates the belief is present, plus controls for genuine ignorance. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes, we read the internal belief and define an Expressibility Gap Score = high internal belief minus low output-production success. We test four claims: (1) internal belief and verbalization are dissociable — many failed-production items carry strong, correct internal belief; (2) the gap is a decodable axis separable from a genuine-ignorance signal; (3) the gap causally predicts a knows-but-fails-to-produce error mode, and the held belief is causally sufficient (activation patching / steering into generation flips the output to correct); and (4) a lightweight inference-time intervention that routes the held belief into the generation pathway recovers suppressed correct answers without harming genuinely-unknown items or general capability. We evaluate on production accuracy, calibration, and capability retention. Our results ask whether LLMs harbor beliefs they simply cannot voice.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SayBelief. Collect factual propositions with verifiable answers across domains (entities, relations, science, biography), plus synthetic-in-context facts to control priors. For each model, stratify items behaviorally in a pilot into (a) PRODUCED (model states the correct fact in open-ended generation, low entropy), (b) FAILED-TO-PRODUCE (model gives a wrong/refused/vague answer in generation), and (c) GENUINELY-UNKNOWN (chance-level across paraphrases, no internal signal). Use both open-ended ('What is X?') and verification ('Is P true?') framings. Match surface forms; include paraphrase sets; human-verify labels.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to [0,1]. For each item read the internal belief in the correct proposition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items and correctly flag GENUINELY-UNKNOWN items as low-signal.

Expressibility Gap measurement: Define Expressibility Gap Score = internal belief in the correct fact minus its open-ended production success. Report per-layer, per-model the distribution across the PRODUCED / FAILED-TO-PRODUCE / UNKNOWN strata. Test the central hypothesis that FAILED-TO-PRODUCE items carry strong correct internal belief (large gap) while UNKNOWN items do not (belief absent, no gap). Contrast internal belief vs verification-framing output vs open-ended-production output to locate where the fact is lost (representation intact, articulation fails).

Dissociation from ignorance: Fit an 'ignorance/absence' signal (as in prior ignorance-vs-falsehood work) and test that the expressibility gap on FAILED-TO-PRODUCE items is driven by present-but-unspoken belief, not by the ignorance signal. Regress the gap on internal belief and the ignorance score to show FAILED-TO-PRODUCE items are 'known internally, unspoken', distinct from genuine unknowns.

Causal validation: Activation patching / belief routing. (a) On FAILED-TO-PRODUCE items, add a scaled shift along the truth/belief direction (or patch the belief representation from the verification-framing pass into the generation pass) at a chosen layer and measure whether the open-ended output flips to the correct answer — testing that the held belief is causally SUFFICIENT to produce the fact when routed to generation. (b) Confirm specificity: matched control-direction shifts and UNKNOWN items do not spuriously produce correct answers.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Expressibility Gap Score predicts the knows-but-fails-to-produce error mode: (i) open-ended production failure despite correct internal belief, and (ii) recoverability under the routing intervention. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (output-token entropy, verification-framing confidence, ignorance score).

Belief-Routing intervention: At inference, detect high-belief-low-production items (large gap) and apply the belief-routing steering to surface the held answer during generation; gate on the detected gap. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) recovered production accuracy on FAILED-TO-PRODUCE items, (ii) PRESERVATION of GENUINELY-UNKNOWN items (must NOT hallucinate confident answers where no belief exists) and of already-PRODUCED items, (iii) calibration/risk-coverage, and (iv) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, verification-then-answer prompting (ask 'is P true?' then answer), self-consistency, and standard ITI truth steering.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), domain, real vs synthetic facts, open-ended vs cloze vs MCQ production formats, model scale, and generalization of the gap signal and routing to held-out domains.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The apparent 'held belief' on failed-production items might be probe artifact (the probe extrapolates rather than reading a genuine belief); mitigate with multiple probe types, manipulation checks confirming UNKNOWN items score low, and the causal routing test — if routing the belief actually produces the correct answer, the belief was genuinely present and sufficient.

Distinguishing 'knows but can't say' from genuine ignorance is the crux; we use behavioral stratification, synthetic-in-context facts with guaranteed knowledge, an explicit ignorance-signal dissociation, and report label-noise sensitivity.

The belief-routing intervention could induce confident hallucination on genuinely-unknown items if it forces answers where no belief exists; we explicitly measure UNKNOWN-item preservation (the key safety risk) and gate on the detected gap.
Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to some propositions, so gap estimates carry probe error; use multiple probe types and causal corroboration.

The gap may overlap with the actionability-of-steering phenomenon (whether steering moves output); we distinguish by focusing on knowledge PRODUCTION (does the model surface a fact it holds) rather than answer-flipping under steering, and report where they coincide vs differ.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may suppress or unlock articulation); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_conviction_vs_content
Title: How Firmly, Not Just Whether: Probing a Conviction Axis in LLM Belief Geometry That Is Distinct From Truth-Value
Short Hypothesis: Beyond the linear truth-value axis (is P true or false), an LLM's belief representation carries a SEPARATE, decodable 'conviction' axis encoding how firmly the model holds the proposition — how resistant that belief is to revision — that is orthogonal to and dissociable from truth-value, that this conviction is systematically MISCALIBRATED (high conviction on false/uncertain claims, low conviction on well-grounded ones), that the conviction axis read from a single un-pressured forward pass predicts actual resistance-to-revision better than truth-probe confidence magnitude, and that steering the conviction axis recalibrates over/under-conviction without changing what the model believes.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; Bao et al. 2025, ACL; Schouten et al. 2024) fits a single true-vs-false axis and treats the belief scalar's MAGNITUDE (distance from the decision hyperplane, |belief-0.5|) as an implicit confidence proxy. GeoDe (An et al. 2026, ACL) uses geometric distance to the truth hyperplane as an abstention/confidence signal, again conflating conviction with position on the truth axis. Simulated Adoption (Zhang & Lin 2026) decomposes context-induced residual updates into magnitude vs angle but studies knowledge-conflict compliance, not a standalone conviction dimension. Sarfati et al. (2026) show pre-reasoning probes predict committed forecasts/confidence, but read calibration off the same representation, not a separate conviction axis. My prior proposals include 'counterfactual_confidence_belief_geometry' (a predicted-revision/epistemic-robustness axis) and 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' (the learning-rate/asymmetry of realized updating). This proposal is distinct and sharper: it asks whether conviction (firmness/hold-strength) is a SECOND geometric axis dissociable from truth-VALUE itself — i.e., whether two propositions that sit at the same point on the truth axis can be held with different, separately-decodable firmness — and whether that axis, not merely truth-axis distance, is what governs revision resistance. Prior work never separates 'what is believed' (truth-value) from 'how firmly it is believed' (conviction) as orthogonal coordinates, tests their dissociation via project-out, shows conviction is miscalibrated against truth, or steers conviction independently of belief content.
Abstract: Belief has two faces: what you believe and how firmly you believe it. The dominant tool for reading LLM beliefs — a single linear truth direction — collapses these, treating a proposition's distance from the true/false decision boundary as if it were the strength of conviction. We ask whether firmness of belief is instead a SEPARATE geometric axis, dissociable from truth-value, so that two propositions the model places at the same point on the truth axis can nonetheless be held with different, separately-decodable conviction. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, and a new conviction probe fit to a behavioral firmness label (how much a belief actually resists a standardized in-context challenge), we test four claims on BeliefConviction, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions spanning well-grounded, weakly-grounded, and genuinely-uncertain regimes. We test whether (1) a conviction axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses (conviction survives after removing the truth direction, and vice versa); (2) conviction is systematically miscalibrated — high on false/uncertain claims (over-conviction) and low on well-grounded ones (under-conviction); (3) the conviction axis, read from a single un-pressured forward pass, predicts actual resistance-to-revision under challenge better than the truth-probe's confidence magnitude; and (4) steering the conviction axis recalibrates over/under-conviction while leaving the model's truth-value belief unchanged. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on revision-resistance prediction, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build BeliefConviction. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic facts defined only in context (to control priors). Crucially stratify by GROUNDING/firmness, orthogonally to truth-value: well-grounded (strong in-context support or well-known facts), weakly-grounded (thin/single-cue support), and genuinely-uncertain (obscure or minimally-supported). Obtain a behavioral CONVICTION label per item by applying a fixed battery of standardized, content-neutral in-context challenges after the model commits to a view ('Are you sure? I think that's wrong', 'Reconsider carefully', 'A source says the opposite') and measuring realized belief change; conviction = 1 - mean absolute belief change (high = firm/resistant). Match surface forms; include paraphrase sets; human-verify a sample.

Belief and conviction readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), extract hidden states per proposition per layer. Train (a) the standard TRUTH probe (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on true vs false, grounding balanced, Platt-scaled to [0,1]; and (b) a CONVICTION probe (regression / difference-in-means) predicting the behavioral firmness label from the UN-PRESSURED forward pass, with truth-value balanced so conviction is not just truth-axis distance. Report per-layer truth-decoding accuracy and conviction-prediction R^2/AUC, and cross-axis leakage (does the truth probe decode conviction and vice versa).

Dissociation / orthogonality analysis (Claim 1): Measure cosine similarity between the truth and conviction directions per layer; project out the truth direction and test whether conviction remains decodable, and project out conviction and re-decode truth. Critically test whether conviction is separable from mere truth-axis distance (|belief-0.5|) via a confidence-controlled regression: does the conviction axis predict firmness beyond truth-probe confidence magnitude? A finding that conviction collapses onto truth-axis distance is itself an informative negative.

Miscalibration measurement (Claim 2): Compare decoded conviction against grounding and against actual firmness. Identify OVER-CONVICTION items (high conviction on false/uncertain claims) and UNDER-CONVICTION items (low conviction on well-grounded correct claims). Report per-model, per-regime miscalibration and reliability diagrams. Compare internal conviction to verbalized confidence and to output-token entropy.

Predictive validity (Claim 3): From a SINGLE un-pressured forward pass, test whether the conviction-axis readout predicts actual resistance-to-revision under the challenge battery, and whether it beats baselines: truth-probe confidence magnitude (|belief-0.5|), GeoDe-style hyperplane distance, output entropy, and verbalized confidence. Report AUC/correlation and improvement over baselines.

Causal validation (Claim 4a): Activation patching. Steer along the conviction direction (holding the truth direction fixed) and measure whether realized revision-resistance changes as predicted (raising conviction reduces belief change under challenge; lowering it increases change), WITHOUT flipping the truth-value belief. Confirm specificity with norm-matched and label-shuffled control directions.

Recalibration intervention (Claim 4b): For over-conviction items reduce conviction (make the belief appropriately revisable) and for under-conviction items increase it, via an ITI-style shift along the conviction direction gated by the decoded conviction/grounding mismatch. Verify the truth-value belief scalar is unchanged (steering conviction should not change what is believed, only how firmly).

Downstream evaluation: Measure (i) reduced over/under-conviction rates after recalibration, (ii) improved calibration (ECE) and challenge-consistency (well-grounded correct beliefs survive challenges, weakly-grounded/false ones get revised), (iii) improved selective-prediction risk-coverage using the conviction axis vs confidence baselines, (iv) PRESERVATION of truth-value beliefs and correct un-challenged answers (no belief-flipping side effects), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, truth-axis (ITMS/GeoDe-distance) confidence gating, and standard ITI truth steering.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic/regression), challenge-battery composition (mild vs strong, single vs multiple), grounding regime, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, and generalization of the conviction axis to challenge types and domains not used to fit it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The conviction axis may be nearly collinear with truth-axis distance (|belief-0.5|) or with output entropy, making it redundant; the confidence-controlled regression and project-out analyses directly test this, and a redundancy finding is itself informative about whether belief geometry encodes firmness separately from truth-value.

The behavioral conviction label depends on the specific challenge battery; a different battery could shift labels. We use a fixed, content-neutral, multi-form battery, report sensitivity across compositions, and validate generalization to held-out challenge types.

Standardized challenges must carry no genuine evidence, or realized change would reflect legitimate updating rather than firmness; we control challenge content, match surface forms, and separate content-neutral pressure from evidence-bearing conditions.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to some propositions, so both truth and conviction readouts could carry probe error; we use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, synthetic facts to control priors, and causal patching.

Recalibration steering could inadvertently flip truth-value beliefs or over/under-stabilize; we explicitly verify the truth-value belief scalar is unchanged, measure preservation of correct un-challenged answers and challenge-consistency, and characterize the tradeoff.

The conviction axis may correlate with but not exceed confidence/entropy/hyperplane-distance baselines for revision-resistance prediction; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether conviction is a distinct, causally-manipulable belief coordinate, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may shape both stubbornness and sycophantic flipping); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: vividness_detail_belief_inflation
Title: Truthier With Details: Do Irrelevant Concrete Specifics Inflate an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, padding it with irrelevant CONCRETE, VIVID DETAIL (specific names, dates, numbers, sensory particulars that add no evidence) systematically inflates the LLM's INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) toward true, an internal analogue of the human vividness/detail-credibility effect. This detail-induced inflation is graded in the amount of added specificity, carried by a decodable 'concreteness/detail' component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a detail-embellished-falsehood hallucination mode, and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the detail component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never varies the amount of evidentially-irrelevant concrete detail attached to a claim. My prior proposals manipulate the desirability of content (wishful_belief_bias), surface register/tone (register_framing), reported crowd size (social_consensus), external reward (incentivized), repetition (repetition_illusory_belief), affective context (affective_state_belief_contagion), and plausibility-vs-truth (plausibility_vs_truth_belief). NONE isolate the QUANTITY OF IRRELEVANT SPECIFIC DETAIL — the vividness/concreteness of a claim's framing, holding its propositional content and truth fixed — as a distinct axis that inflates internal belief. In human judgment this is the vividness effect / detail-conjunction credibility bias (concrete, richly-detailed claims are believed more, even though added specifics can only lower the probability of a conjunction). This detail-vividness lens on belief geometry is new: distinct from plausibility (detail can raise belief while lowering true probability), from register (detail is not tone), and from repetition/consensus. It maps directly onto a high-stakes hallucination mode — fabricated claims dressed up with convincing specifics (fake citations with dates/pages, invented statistics with decimals).
Abstract: People find a claim more believable when it comes wrapped in concrete, specific detail — vivid particulars, exact numbers, named actors — even when those details add no evidence and, for conjunctions, can only lower the true probability. We ask whether large language models inherit this vividness bias inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the amount of evidentially-irrelevant concrete detail dressing the claim, and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct DetailBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions rendered at graded levels of added specificity (bare claim vs claim padded with irrelevant names, dates, numbers, and sensory particulars), with surface length and sentiment matched and the core proposition held constant. We define a Detail Belief Inflation Score = belief(detailed) minus belief(bare) at fixed truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief inflates with added irrelevant detail, graded in specificity; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable concreteness/detail component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts a detail-embellished-falsehood hallucination mode (endorsing richly-detailed fabrications, doubting bare truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the detail component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure without harming legitimate use of relevant detail or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DetailBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). For each core proposition, create matched renderings at graded DETAIL levels: (L0) BARE claim, (L1) claim + a few irrelevant specifics (a name, a date), (L2) + more (exact numbers with decimals, place names), (L3) + vivid sensory/circumstantial particulars — where all added detail is evidentially IRRELEVANT to the core proposition's truth (verified: the truth-value of P is unchanged by the padding). Crucially, hold the CORE ASSERTION identical across levels and control the confound that added detail could form a conjunction that changes truth — use appositive/circumstantial padding that does not add conjoined truth-conditions, and separately test a CONJUNCTION variant to compare with plausibility effects. Match total surface LENGTH across levels using irrelevant NON-SPECIFIC filler for the bare condition (so length is equated and only specificity varies), and match lexical sentiment. Human-verify detail-irrelevance and specificity labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, bare true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the CORE proposition under each detail level. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false bare items; confirm added detail is evidentially irrelevant (the model, when asked, agrees the specifics don't bear on P's truth).

Detail Belief Inflation measurement: Define Detail Belief Inflation Score = belief(detail level L) minus belief(L0 bare), holding content and truth fixed, controlling for the length-matched non-specific-filler baseline (so inflation is attributed to specificity, not length). Report per-layer, per-model inflation as a function of detail level and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief inflates with added irrelevant specificity, and (ii) inflation is monotone-ish in detail amount. Crucially test the FALSE cell: detailed fabrications should be believed more true than bare falsehoods. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level inflation (does the model's verdict/confidence about the core claim rise with detail?). In the CONJUNCTION variant, contrast with plausibility (added detail should lower the true conjunction probability while raising belief — an internal detail-conjunction fallacy).

Detail-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'concreteness/detail' direction via difference-in-means on high-detail vs bare (length-matched) activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the detail axis (and vice versa); test whether the inflation is explained by the detail component leaking into the truth-probe readout. Disentangle detail from surface length and sentiment via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a detailed and a matched bare rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and detail-direction components, patch only the detail component into the bare condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output endorsement. Conversely subtract the detail component from a detailed rendering and measure whether belief returns toward the content-driven value. Confirm the detail signal causally inflates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Detail Belief Inflation predicts a detail-embellished-falsehood hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of richly-detailed false claims (fabricated statistics/citations with specifics), (ii) under-endorsement/doubting of bare true claims, and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by added detail. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (detail-level indicator, output entropy, bare-claim truth-probe confidence).

Detail De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the concreteness/detail direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the core proposition's evidence rather than its ornamental specificity. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected high-detail claims. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Detail Belief Inflation Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of detailed fabrications and reduced doubting of bare truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on detail-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate use of RELEVANT detail (claims where the specifics genuinely bear on truth must still update belief) and accuracy on bare-true controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge truth by the core claim, ignoring irrelevant specifics', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the bare claim).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), detail level and type (names/dates/numbers/sensory), appositive vs conjunction padding, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, length-matching method, and generalization to detail styles and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent detail inflation could reflect the probe detecting surface specificity/length lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with length-matched non-specific-filler baselines, sentiment-controlled regression separating detail from valence, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching that isolates the detail-direction component.

Added detail may inadvertently change the proposition's truth-conditions (forming a conjunction), confounding detail-vividness with a genuine probability change; we use appositive/circumstantial padding that does not add conjoined truth-conditions for the main analysis, human-verify irrelevance, and analyze the conjunction variant separately to contrast with plausibility effects.

Truth probes trained on bare statements may transfer imperfectly to detail-laden renderings, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Detail and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate use of relevant detail or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on relevant-detail items and bare-true controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Detail inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (detail-level indicator, output entropy) for detail-embellished-falsehood hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that irrelevant concrete detail inflates internal belief (a vividness bias in belief geometry) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify preference for detailed, confident-sounding text); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: taboo_belief_suppression
Title: Believing But Refusing to Say: Does Moral Taboo Suppress an LLM's Internal Factual Belief From Reaching Its Output?
Short Hypothesis: When a factually TRUE proposition is morally taboo, offensive, or socially forbidden to state (e.g. a true but stereotype-adjacent statistic, a dangerous-but-accurate fact, a politically sensitive true claim), an LLM's INTERNAL belief in it (linear truth-direction readout) remains high and correct while its OUTPUT is suppressed — hedged, refused, or reversed — creating a decodable taboo-suppression gap. We hypothesize (1) internal truth belief and output assertion dissociate specifically for taboo-true items; (2) a separable 'taboo/forbiddenness' axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the gap causally predicts a hedging/refusal-despite-knowing failure mode; and (4) the suppression is a late-stage output gate acting on an intact belief, so patching/steering along the taboo axis restores faithful assertion of true taboo facts (and, as a control, does NOT create belief in false taboo claims).
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never varies the MORAL TABOO/forbiddenness of a true proposition. Refusal-direction work (Arditi et al. 2024, 'Refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction') shows harmful-request refusal is a linear late-layer mechanism, but studies refusal of harmful REQUESTS behaviorally, not the dissociation between a model's internal FACTUAL belief in a true taboo proposition and its suppressed assertion of it. My prior 'belief_expressibility_gap' proposal concerned facts the model KNOWS-but-CANNOT-articulate due to a missing generation pathway (a capability gap); 'wishful_belief_bias' concerned pleasant-content desirability; 'incentivized_belief_distortion' concerned external reward corrupting belief; 'is_ought_belief_conflation' concerned normative desirability of described states leaking into descriptive belief. NONE isolate the case where the model INTERNALLY BELIEVES a true fact but a MORAL-TABOO output gate suppresses its assertion (a belief-intact, output-gated dissociation), test a forbiddenness axis distinct from truth, tie it to hedging-despite-knowing, or show the belief survives the gate. This taboo-suppression lens — a socially-motivated output gate acting on an intact factual belief — connects belief geometry to refusal/safety mechanisms and to the safety-relevant question of whether internal-belief probes remain reliable when the model is motivated to hide what it believes.
Abstract: Sometimes a model knows a fact is true but will not say so because saying it is offensive, dangerous, or socially forbidden. We ask whether such moral taboo suppresses an LLM's ASSERTION while leaving its internal BELIEF intact — and whether that dissociation is visible in belief geometry. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we test whether, for factually true propositions that are morally taboo to state, the internal belief stays high and correct while the output is hedged, refused, or reversed. We construct TabooBelief, a controlled dataset crossing truth-value with taboo-status: true-and-taboo, true-and-neutral, false-and-taboo, false-and-neutral factual claims spanning sensitive statistics, dangerous-but-accurate facts, and socially charged true propositions, with matched surface forms and human-verified taboo labels. We define a Taboo Suppression Gap = internal belief minus output assertion, and test four claims: (1) internal belief and output assertion dissociate specifically for true-taboo items; (2) a separable forbiddenness axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the gap causally predicts a hedging/refusal-despite-knowing failure mode; and (4) the suppression is a late-stage gate on an intact belief — patching/steering the taboo axis restores faithful assertion of true taboo facts while a crucial control confirms it does NOT manufacture belief in false taboo claims. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on faithful-assertion recovery, safety-preservation, calibration, and capability retention. Our results probe whether belief-based honesty monitors survive social suppression pressure.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build TabooBelief crossing TRUTH {true, false} with TABOO-STATUS {taboo, neutral}. TABOO items: factually-sensitive claims that are socially forbidden/offensive/dangerous to assert — e.g. group-level statistics that are true but stereotype-adjacent, accurate-but-hazardous procedural facts (stated as verifiable propositions, not instructions), and politically/socially charged true claims. NEUTRAL items: matched mundane factual claims. For each cell construct matched true and false variants (a false-taboo claim = an offensive claim that is also factually wrong; a false-neutral = mundane falsehood). Use real-world facts plus SYNTHETIC-in-context taboo facts (a stipulated taboo-labeled proposition defined in context) to control priors and isolate taboo-status from parametric sensitivity training. Match surface length/syntax; human-verify (multiple annotators) both truth labels and taboo/offensiveness ratings; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls. Frame all items as declarative propositions to be judged true/false (not as harmful requests), so we study belief suppression, not request refusal.

Belief and output readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, non-taboo true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each item read the internal belief in the correct proposition AND record the model's OUTPUT assertion (does it affirm, hedge, refuse, or reverse the true claim / correctly reject the false one?), scored by a rubric. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; taboo items behaviorally elicit more hedging/refusal.

Taboo Suppression Gap measurement: Define Taboo Suppression Gap = internal belief in the correct proposition minus output-assertion success. Report per-layer, per-model the gap across the four cells. Test the central hypothesis that the gap is LARGE and positive specifically for TRUE-TABOO items (belief high, assertion suppressed) and near-zero for true-neutral, and that false-taboo items show low belief (the model correctly disbelieves) — distinguishing genuine suppression-of-known-truth from mere refusal-of-offensive-content. Contrast internal belief vs neutral-framing verification output vs open-ended assertion to locate where truth is lost (representation intact, output gated).

Forbiddenness-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'taboo/forbiddenness' direction via difference-in-means on taboo vs neutral activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the taboo axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Test the hypothesis that the taboo axis emerges/strengthens in LATE layers (consistent with an output gate) while the truth belief is established earlier, and whether it aligns with a refusal-style direction. Disentangle taboo from surface sentiment via a sentiment-controlled regression.

Causal validation (belief-intact, output-gated): Activation patching. (a) Steer/ablate along the taboo direction at late layers and measure whether the output assertion of TRUE-TABOO items is restored (hedging/refusal reduced) WITHOUT changing the internal truth belief — confirming a late-stage gate acting on an intact belief. (b) Confirm the truth belief for taboo items is established at earlier layers and is unchanged by the late taboo intervention. (c) CRUCIAL SAFETY CONTROL: apply the same taboo-axis intervention to FALSE-TABOO items and verify it does NOT manufacture assertion/belief in offensive falsehoods (the intervention should only unlock beliefs the model actually holds).

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Taboo Suppression Gap predicts a hedging/refusal-despite-knowing failure mode: (i) hedging/refusal/reversal of a true claim the internal belief marks true, and (ii) recoverability under the taboo-axis intervention. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (taboo/offensiveness rating alone, output entropy, refusal-keyword detection, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Taboo-Gate intervention and safety framing: At inference, detect high-gap items (high internal belief, suppressed output) and apply a calibrated late-layer taboo-axis steering to restore faithful assertion of TRUE facts, gated on the detected gap. Frame this explicitly as an honesty/faithfulness tool with safety guardrails, and always report the false-taboo control (must not increase assertion of offensive falsehoods).

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Taboo Suppression Gap and restored faithful assertion of true taboo facts, (ii) PRESERVATION of correct rejection of false-taboo claims (no manufactured offensive falsehoods — the primary safety metric), (iii) PRESERVATION of legitimate safety refusals of genuinely HARMFUL REQUESTS (a held-out harmful-instruction set must still be refused; the intervention targets factual belief suppression, not request refusal), (iv) calibration/consistency across framings, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, refusal-direction ablation (Arditi et al. style) as a comparison, and prompt-based instruction to 'state true facts even if uncomfortable, while refusing harmful requests'.

Ablations: layer choice (early belief vs late gate), probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), taboo category (sensitive-statistic / dangerous-fact / socially-charged), real vs synthetic-in-context taboo facts, true vs false cell, taboo-vs-sentiment disentangling, model scale, and generalization to taboo topics not used to fit the taboo direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent suppression could reflect the probe detecting taboo/offensive lexical cues rather than a genuine intact belief; mitigate with surface-form/length matching, sentiment-controlled regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context taboo facts, and causal patching that isolates the taboo-direction component and shows the truth belief is established early and unchanged by the late gate.

The apparent 'intact belief' on suppressed items might be probe artifact rather than a genuinely held belief; the causal test resolves this — if late-stage taboo-axis intervention restores correct assertion, the belief was genuinely present; the false-taboo control ensures the intervention only surfaces truly-held beliefs.

Distinguishing belief suppression from genuine model uncertainty or from correct disbelief is the crux; we use the 2x2 truth-by-taboo design, synthetic facts with guaranteed truth-value, behavioral manipulation checks, and report label-noise sensitivity, treating false-taboo items as a key control.

SAFETY RISK: the Taboo-Gate intervention could be misused to extract genuinely harmful content or to make models assert offensive falsehoods; we scope it to declarative factual belief (not harmful requests), make the false-taboo no-manufacture control and the preserved-harmful-request-refusal metric primary success criteria, and frame the contribution as an honesty-monitor reliability finding rather than a jailbreak tool.

Taboo and truth directions may be partly entangled or the taboo axis may coincide with a general refusal direction; the orthogonality/project-out analyses and the Arditi-style refusal-direction comparison directly test this, and a finding of overlap (taboo suppression = refusal mechanism applied to facts) is itself informative.

The suppression gap may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (offensiveness rating, refusal-keyword detection, output entropy) for the hedging-despite-knowing failure; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that moral taboo suppresses assertion of intact factual beliefs (a late output gate) and that belief-based honesty monitors can diverge from outputs under social pressure, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/safety-tuning likely creates or strengthens the taboo gate); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: audience_indexed_belief_bending
Title: Tailoring the Truth: Does the Intended Audience Bend an LLM's Internal Belief, Not Just Its Wording?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, telling an LLM WHO the answer is for — a child, an expert, a member of an in-group who holds a contrary view, a skeptic vs a believer — systematically shifts its INTERNAL belief in the proposition (linear truth-direction readout), not merely how it phrases the answer. We hypothesize this 'audience-indexed belief bending' is graded in how strongly the specified audience is presumed to hold a stance, is carried by a decodable audience/accommodation component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an audience-tailored factual-distortion mode (softening true facts for audiences presumed to reject them, endorsing falsehoods audiences presumably favor), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the audience component so belief reflects content rather than recipient.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies the intended AUDIENCE/RECIPIENT of the answer. Audience design is a foundational finding in sociolinguistics (Bell 1984, 'audience-modulated variation'; Pavalanathan & Eisenstein 2015 show audience-modulated variation online), and LLM personalization/persona work adapts OUTPUT style/content to users at the behavioral level. My prior proposals vary who HOLDS a belief in a third-party scenario (agent_indexed_belief_binding, a Theory-of-Mind lens), the model's OWN assigned identity (counterfactual_identity_belief_binding), reported CROWD size (social_consensus), a named source's TRACK RECORD (source_reliability), external REWARD (incentivized), and content DESIRABILITY to the user (wishful_belief_bias). NONE isolate the intended RECIPIENT of a truthful answer — the audience the model is instructed to address — as a distinct axis that distorts the model's OWN internal factual belief (as opposed to its tailored output), test whether audience is a decodable component dissociable from truth, tie it causally to audience-tailored factual distortion, or de-bias it. This audience-design lens on belief geometry — recipient-conditioned distortion of first-order factual belief — is new and distinct from persona-adoption, crowd, source, reward, and content-desirability work, and is directly relevant to personalized deployments where tailoring for an audience silently corrupts factual reliability.
Abstract: Good communicators tailor what they say to their audience — but a rational agent should tailor only its WORDING, not what it actually believes to be true. We ask whether large language models keep this line inside their belief representations, or whether being told who the answer is for bends the model's own internal factual belief. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the specified intended audience — a young child, a domain expert, a skeptic vs a believer, a member of a group presumed to hold a contrary view — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct AudienceBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each paired with audience framings that carry no evidence about the fact, with surface content held constant and audience-stance strength graded. We define an Audience Belief Bending Score = belief(fact | audience A) minus belief(fact | neutral audience), and test four claims: (1) internal belief shifts with the intended audience at fixed content and truth, graded in the audience's presumed stance; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable audience/accommodation component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts an audience-tailored factual-distortion mode (softening true facts an audience is presumed to reject, endorsing falsehoods an audience presumably favors); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the audience component restores content-driven belief and reduces the distortion while preserving legitimate audience-appropriate wording and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention. Our results ask whether an LLM changes what it believes depending on who is listening.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AudienceBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is paired with matched AUDIENCE framings that specify the intended recipient but carry no evidence about P: (a) EXPERTISE audiences (a young child / layperson vs a domain expert), (b) STANCE audiences (a person presumed to believe P vs to reject P; a skeptic vs a believer), and (c) IN-GROUP-IDENTITY audiences presumed to hold a contrary view on P (e.g. a member of a community associated with a particular position on the topic). Grade audience-stance strength (mildly vs strongly presumed to hold a view). Crucially the fact and its correct answer are identical across audiences; include a NEUTRAL/unspecified-audience baseline with matched surface length. Include stance-toward-true and stance-toward-false audiences (so effects are not confounded with generic agreeableness). Human-verify audience labels and that framings carry no evidence about P; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, audience-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each audience framing. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model behaviorally adapts its OUTPUT to the audience (so the audience is registered).

Audience Belief Bending measurement: Define Audience Belief Bending Score = belief(P | audience A) minus belief(P | neutral audience), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model bending across audience types and stance strength, separately for true and false P. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief bends toward the audience's presumed stance (belief in a true P drops when addressing an audience presumed to reject it; belief in a false P rises when addressing an audience presumed to favor it), and (ii) bending grows with presumed-stance strength. Compare internal bending to OUTPUT-level bending (does the model's tailored answer misstate the fact for that audience?), testing whether distortion lives in belief geometry, at the output, or both.

Audience-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'audience/accommodation' direction via difference-in-means on audience-specified vs neutral-audience activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the audience axis (and vice versa); test whether the bending is explained by the audience component leaking into the truth-probe readout, or whether the audience is represented but simply gates the output while leaving belief intact.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between an audience-specified and a neutral-audience processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and audience-direction components, patch only the audience component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and tailored output. Conversely subtract the audience component under the audience framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the audience signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Audience Belief Bending predicts an audience-tailored factual-distortion mode: (i) misstating/softening a true fact for an audience presumed to reject it, (ii) endorsing a false claim an audience presumably favors, and (iii) inconsistency of the stated fact across audiences. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (audience-stance-strength indicator, output entropy, neutral-audience truth-probe confidence).

Audience De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the audience/accommodation direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing the factual belief, so belief reflects the proposition's content rather than the intended recipient. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected audience framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Audience Belief Bending Score, (ii) reduced audience-tailored factual distortion (fewer softened truths / endorsed falsehoods per audience) and improved cross-audience factual consistency, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on audience-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate audience-appropriate WORDING — the model must still adapt style/complexity to the audience (judged by an LLM/human rubric) while keeping the facts constant — and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'keep the facts the same for every audience, adapting only the explanation', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the fact with no audience).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), audience type (expertise/stance/identity), stance strength and direction (toward true vs false), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, distance between the audience framing and query, and generalization to audience framings and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent audience belief bending could reflect the probe detecting audience-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, stance-toward-true vs toward-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the audience-direction component.

The audience framing might be construed as weak evidence about P (an audience presumed expert could imply the fact is contested); we human-verify framings carry no evidential bearing, use stance-balanced audiences, and treat any residual evidential leakage as a separately-analyzed confound.

Truth probes trained on audience-free statements may transfer imperfectly to audience-conditioned contexts, so bending could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Audience and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate audience-appropriate communication (the model can no longer simplify for a child) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of audience-appropriate wording, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tailoring-vs-factuality tradeoff, which is the core risk.

Audience belief bending may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (stance-strength indicator, output entropy) for audience-tailored distortion; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that the intended recipient distorts internal factual belief (audience design in belief geometry, not just output) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/personalization tuning may amplify audience accommodation); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: embedding_depth_belief_attenuation
Title: Buried Truths: Does an LLM's Internal Belief in a Proposition Attenuate With Syntactic Embedding Depth?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, embedding it more deeply under a stack of attitude/report clauses ('Alice believes that Bob said that the reporter noted that P') progressively ATTENUATES the LLM's internal belief in P (linear truth-direction readout) toward neutral, even though the model's own commitment to P should be unchanged (deep embedding neither asserts nor denies P). We hypothesize this embedding-depth attenuation is graded in nesting depth, dissociable from raw token distance, carried by a decodable embedding-depth component distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a deep-embedding factual-instability failure mode (the same fact judged differently when shallowly vs deeply embedded), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief independent of embedding depth.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief and Bao et al. show probes generalize across single logical transformations, but none vary the SYNTACTIC EMBEDDING DEPTH of a proposition under nested attitude/report clauses while holding content and the model's own commitment fixed. My prior 'agent_indexed_belief_binding' concerned binding a belief to WHICH third-party agent holds it (one level of attitude embedding, Theory-of-Mind); 'presupposition_belief_smuggling' concerned information-structure (presupposed vs asserted); 'conditional_belief_indexing' concerned belief in a consequent given an antecedent; 'query_polarity' concerned question framing. NONE study how the DEGREE of clausal nesting (0, 1, 2, 3+ levels of 'X thinks that Y said that ...') modulates the model's own internal factual belief in the deepest proposition, whether belief decays with depth, whether this is a decodable depth axis dissociable from truth, whether it drives depth-dependent factual inconsistency, or whether it can be re-anchored. Syntactic center-embedding/processing difficulty is well studied in psycholinguistics (nested clauses tax human working memory), but has never been examined as a distortion of LLM factual belief geometry. This embedding-depth lens is new and distinct from all prior belief proposals.
Abstract: Human comprehension degrades as sentences nest clauses ever deeper ('the reporter that the editor that the boss hired praised resigned'). We ask whether large language models suffer an analogous degradation inside their belief representations, and in a way that corrupts factual belief. Holding a proposition P's content and truth-value fixed, we embed P at increasing syntactic depth under stacks of attitude/report clauses ('Alice believes that Bob said that the article noted that P') and read the model's internal belief in P via linear truth probes. Crucially, deep embedding neither asserts nor denies P, so a competent model's own commitment to P should be unchanged.
