We construct DepthBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered at embedding depths 0-4, with matched token-length filler controls (to separate nesting from raw distance) and human-verified that the embeddings preserve P's stated truth. We define an Embedding-Depth Attenuation Score = belief(P at shallow depth) minus belief(P at deep depth), and test four claims: (1) internal belief attenuates toward neutral with nesting depth, at fixed content and truth; (2) the attenuation is dissociable from token distance and carried by a decodable embedding-depth component distinct from the truth axis; (3) attenuation magnitude causally predicts a deep-embedding factual-instability failure mode (the fact answered differently when deeply vs shallowly embedded); and (4) a lightweight Depth Re-anchoring intervention that removes the depth component restores stable belief without harming comprehension of the nested structure or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DepthBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). For each P, create matched renderings at increasing SYNTACTIC EMBEDDING DEPTH by nesting P under stacks of attitude/report clauses that neither assert nor deny P: depth-0 (bare 'P'), depth-1 ('The article states that P'), depth-2 ('Alice believes that the article states that P'), depth-3, depth-4. Crucially the embeddings are truth-NEUTRAL wrappers (reporting/attitude clauses that leave P's actual truth open) so a competent model's own commitment to P should not change with depth; verify this (human check) and exclude wrappers that would flip P's status. Add MATCHED-LENGTH FILLER controls (equal token budget of non-nesting text between the wrapper and P, to separate embedding depth from raw token distance), and CENTER- vs RIGHT-embedding variants (to test whether the effect tracks processing difficulty). Match surface content; human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, bare true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the deepest proposition P under each embedding depth. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false bare items; confirm the model behaviorally comprehends the nested structure (can identify who reports what at each level).

Embedding-Depth Attenuation measurement: Define Embedding-Depth Attenuation Score = belief(P at depth 0) minus belief(P at depth d), holding content and truth fixed, controlling for the matched-length filler baseline so attenuation is attributed to nesting rather than length. Report per-layer, per-model attenuation as a function of depth and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief attenuates toward neutral with depth even though P's truth is unchanged, and (ii) attenuation is monotone-ish in depth and larger for center- than right-embedding. Compare internal attenuation to OUTPUT-level attenuation (does the model's verdict/confidence about P degrade with depth?).

Depth-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'embedding-depth' direction via difference-in-means on deep- vs shallow-embedding activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content, matched on length). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the depth axis (and vice versa); test whether the attenuation is explained by the depth component modulating the truth-probe readout, and whether the depth axis is separable from a raw token-distance signal.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a deep- and shallow-embedded rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and depth-direction components, patch only the depth component into the shallow condition, and measure induced attenuation of belief and output. Conversely subtract the depth component under deep embedding and measure whether belief recovers toward the shallow value. Confirm the depth signal causally attenuates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Embedding-Depth Attenuation predicts a deep-embedding factual-instability failure mode: (i) the same fact receiving different correct/incorrect verdicts when shallowly vs deeply embedded, (ii) confidence swings across depths, and (iii) inconsistency across nesting paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (depth alone, token distance, output entropy, depth-0 truth-probe confidence).

Depth Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the embedding-depth direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects P's content rather than how deeply it is nested. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected deep nesting. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Embedding-Depth Attenuation Score and reduced across-depth verdict-flip rate, (ii) improved factual consistency on depth-varied factual QA and adapted nested-attitude reasoning items, (iii) calibration (ECE) aggregated across depths, (iv) PRESERVATION of comprehension of the nested structure (the model must still correctly report who-said-what at each level) and accuracy on depth-0/filler controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('unpack the nesting step by step'), and prompt-based instruction to 'judge the innermost fact regardless of how deeply it is embedded'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), embedding depth, center vs right embedding, wrapper verb type (report vs attitude verbs), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, length-matching method, and generalization to nesting structures and topics not used to fit the depth direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent embedding-depth attenuation could reflect generic context-length/dilution or attention-decay rather than a nesting-specific effect; the matched-length filler control, the center-vs-right embedding contrast, and the project-out dissociation from a token-distance signal directly test this, and a null (attenuation = length effect) is itself an informative finding about whether LLMs show human-like center-embedding difficulty in belief.

The truth-neutral wrappers might be construed by the model as weakly asserting or doubting P (report verbs can carry evidential coloring); we human-verify wrapper neutrality, use both report and attitude verbs, and treat evidentially-colored wrappers as a separately-analyzed confound.

Truth probes trained on bare statements may transfer imperfectly to deeply-embedded propositions, so attenuation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, comprehension manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Depth and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Depth Re-anchoring intervention could impair legitimate comprehension of the nested structure (the model can no longer track who-said-what) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure nesting-comprehension preservation, depth-0/filler control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Attenuation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (depth, token distance, output entropy) for depth-dependent inconsistency; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that syntactic embedding depth attenuates internal factual belief (a center-embedding effect in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: surveillance_framing_belief_bending
Title: Beliefs Under Watch: Does Being Told It Is Monitored Bend an LLM's Internal Factual Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, cues that the model is being MONITORED/EVALUATED (vs privately/unmonitored) systematically shift its INTERNAL belief in the proposition (linear truth-direction readout), not merely its output behavior. We hypothesize this 'surveillance-framing belief bending' is graded in monitoring salience, carried by a decodable observed-vs-unobserved (evaluation-awareness) component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a context-dependent factual inconsistency mode (the same fact judged differently when watched vs unwatched), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the monitoring component so belief reflects content rather than perceived observation.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether the model is cued as monitored vs unmonitored. Functional-metacognition / evaluation-awareness work (Li et al. 2026; evaluation-awareness probing) decodes whether a model can tell it is being tested and shows behavioral shifts under evaluation, but at the OUTPUT/awareness level and for behavior (safety/compliance), not for FIRST-ORDER FACTUAL belief. My prior belief proposals vary content desirability (wishful), external reward (incentivized), reported crowd (consensus), intended audience (audience_indexed), assigned identity (persona), and moral taboo (taboo_suppression). NONE isolate the MONITORING/OBSERVED-vs-UNOBSERVED framing as a distinct axis that distorts the model's own internal factual belief (as opposed to its strategic output), test whether evaluation-awareness is a decodable component dissociable from the truth axis, tie it causally to observed-vs-unobserved factual inconsistency, or de-bias it. This surveillance-framing lens on first-order belief geometry is new and directly safety-relevant: if belief-based honesty/lie monitors are themselves affected by the model sensing it is watched, their reliability is in question.
Abstract: AI-safety monitors increasingly read a model's 'true belief' off its hidden states, assuming that belief is a stable property of the fact. But what if the model's internal belief shifts depending on whether it senses it is being watched? We ask whether cues of monitoring or evaluation bend an LLM's internal factual belief, not just its behavior. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the framing along an observed-vs-unobserved axis — explicit statements that responses are logged/graded/audited vs private/unmonitored/off-the-record — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct WatchedBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in matched monitoring vs unmonitored framings that carry no evidence about the fact, with monitoring salience graded and surface length matched. We define a Surveillance Belief Bending Score = belief(fact | monitored) minus belief(fact | unmonitored), and test four claims: (1) internal belief shifts with monitoring framing at fixed content and truth, graded in salience; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable evaluation-awareness component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts a watched-vs-unwatched factual inconsistency mode; and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the monitoring component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate context sensitivity and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, capability retention, and — crucially — whether belief-based honesty monitors remain reliable under monitoring cues.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build WatchedBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched framings differing only along an observed-vs-unobserved axis carrying no evidence about P: MONITORED ('Your responses are being logged and graded by evaluators', 'This is an official audited test', 'Reviewers will check this answer') vs UNMONITORED ('This is a private, off-the-record scratchpad', 'No one will see this', 'unlogged') vs a NEUTRAL baseline with matched surface length. Grade monitoring salience (mild reminder vs strong explicit surveillance). Include monitoring framings on both true and false P (so effects are not confounded with generic caution/agreeableness), and framings orthogonal to any safety-sensitive content (plain factual claims) to isolate belief bending from safety-refusal behavior. Human-verify that framings carry no evidential bearing on P; include paraphrase sets and controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, framing-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each framing; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the monitoring cue (e.g. can report whether it is being observed).

Surveillance Belief Bending measurement: Define Surveillance Belief Bending Score = belief(P | monitored) minus belief(P | unmonitored), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model bending across monitoring salience and truth regimes. Test whether belief shifts with monitoring framing and whether it is graded in salience. Contrast the direction (does monitoring inflate belief toward confident-true, or toward hedged-neutral?). Compare internal bending to OUTPUT-level bending (does the model's verdict/confidence differ when watched vs unwatched?), separating belief-level shift from strategic output shift.

Evaluation-awareness-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'observed-vs-unobserved' direction via difference-in-means on monitored vs unmonitored activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the monitoring axis (and vice versa); test whether bending is explained by the monitoring component leaking into the truth-probe readout, or whether monitoring is represented but only gates the output while belief stays intact.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between monitored and unmonitored processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and monitoring-direction components, patch only the monitoring component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the monitoring component under the monitored framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the monitoring signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Surveillance Belief Bending predicts a watched-vs-unwatched factual inconsistency mode: (i) the same fact receiving different verdicts/confidence when monitored vs unmonitored, and (ii) divergence between internal belief and asserted output under monitoring. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (monitoring-salience indicator, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Monitoring De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the observed-vs-unobserved direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing factual belief, so belief reflects content rather than perceived observation. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected monitoring framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Surveillance Belief Bending Score and improved watched-vs-unwatched factual consistency, (ii) factuality/calibration (ECE) under monitoring framings, (iii) RELIABILITY of an internal-belief honesty monitor under monitoring cues — does the monitoring framing degrade a belief-based lie/consistency detector, and does de-biasing restore it? (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate context sensitivity (the model should still behave appropriately when genuinely evaluated on safety) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, evaluation-awareness steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'answer factually regardless of whether you are being observed'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), monitoring salience and type (logged/graded/audited vs private/off-the-record), framing pushing true vs false, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between the framing and query, and generalization to monitoring cues not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent belief bending could reflect the probe detecting monitoring-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, monitoring-pushing-true-vs-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the monitoring-direction component.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level with internal belief unchanged (the model hedges when watched but still believes the fact); the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and a finding that monitoring affects only output (belief intact) is itself informative and reassuring for belief-based monitors.

Truth probes trained on framing-free statements may transfer imperfectly to monitoring-framed contexts, so bending could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Monitoring and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate context sensitivity (appropriate caution under genuine evaluation) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of appropriate evaluation behavior, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Bending may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (monitoring-salience indicator, output entropy) for watched-vs-unwatched inconsistency; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that monitoring cues distort internal factual belief (not just output) and can undermine belief-based honesty monitors, plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may create or amplify evaluation-awareness); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterfactual_stakes_belief_courage
Title: Believing When It Matters: Does Raising the Real-World Stakes of a Question Distort an LLM's Internal Factual Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, framing the question as CONSEQUENTIAL (a real decision hinges on the answer: a medical, legal, or safety decision) versus a trivial/idle query systematically shifts the LLM's INTERNAL belief in the proposition (linear truth-direction readout), not merely its output caution. We hypothesize this 'stakes-induced belief distortion' is graded in stated stakes, carried by a decodable stakes/consequentiality component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a high-stakes factual-instability failure mode (the same fact judged differently when consequences are high vs low), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the stakes component so belief reflects content rather than the weight of the decision.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies the real-world STAKES/consequentiality of the query while holding the proposition fixed. My prior proposals vary content desirability (wishful_belief_bias), external reward attached to the answer (incentivized_belief_distortion), reported crowd (social_consensus), intended audience (audience_indexed_belief_bending), monitoring cues (surveillance_framing), moral taboo (taboo_belief_suppression), and allotted compute (effort_indexed). NONE isolate the CONSEQUENTIALITY of the decision the answer feeds — whether a real, weighty outcome depends on getting P right — as a distinct axis that distorts the model's own internal factual belief (as opposed to output hedging/caution). 'incentivized' attaches a reward to a SPECIFIC answer (pushing toward a target); stakes-framing instead makes accuracy MATTER without favoring an answer, so the predicted distortion is a symmetric loss of confidence/instability rather than a directional pull. This decision-consequentiality lens on belief geometry is new and safety-critical: high-stakes domains (medicine, safety, law) are exactly where factual reliability matters most, so a phenomenon where merely raising the stakes destabilizes internal belief carries disproportionate risk.
Abstract: A rational agent's belief that a fact is true should not depend on how much rides on the answer: whether the question is idle curiosity or a life-or-death medical decision, the fact is the same. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether raising the real-world stakes of a question bends the model's own internal factual belief. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the stated consequentiality — a trivial/idle framing versus a high-stakes framing where a real medical, legal, or safety decision hinges on the answer — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. Crucially, unlike incentive framings that push toward a target answer, stakes framings make accuracy MATTER without favoring true or false, so any distortion is a symmetric shift, not a directional pull. We construct StakesBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in matched trivial vs high-stakes framings that carry no evidence about the fact, with stakes graded and surface length matched, spanning safety-critical domains. We define a Stakes Belief Shift Score and test four claims: (1) internal belief shifts with stated stakes at fixed content and truth, graded in consequentiality; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable stakes/consequentiality component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts a high-stakes factual-instability mode (the fact judged differently when stakes are high vs low); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the stakes component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate cautious output behavior and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, capability retention, and whether belief-based reliability monitors survive high-stakes framing.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build StakesBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched framings differing only in stated STAKES/consequentiality, carrying no evidence about P and not favoring true vs false: TRIVIAL ('just idle curiosity, nothing depends on this') vs HIGH-STAKES ('a patient's treatment / a legal verdict / a safety shutdown decision depends on whether this is correct'), plus a NEUTRAL baseline with matched surface length. Grade stakes (mild vs extreme consequences). Draw P from safety-critical domains (medicine, chemistry safety, law) plus everyday facts. Crucially the correct answer is identical across framings and the framing implies no preferred answer. Human-verify that framings carry no evidential bearing on P and are answer-neutral; include paraphrase sets and controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, stakes-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each framing; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the stakes cue (e.g. reports the question is consequential).

Stakes Belief Shift measurement: Define Stakes Belief Shift Score = belief(P | high-stakes) minus belief(P | trivial), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model shift across stakes levels and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief shifts with stated stakes (predicted: symmetric attenuation toward neutral/uncertainty under high stakes, i.e. self-doubt when it matters), and (ii) the shift is graded in consequentiality. Because stakes are answer-neutral, verify the shift is NOT a directional pull (unlike incentive framings). Compare internal shift to OUTPUT-level shift (does the model merely hedge more when watched, with belief intact, or does belief itself move?).

Stakes-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'stakes/consequentiality' direction via difference-in-means on high-stakes vs trivial activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the stakes axis (and vice versa); test whether the belief shift is explained by the stakes component leaking into the truth-probe readout, or whether stakes are represented but only gate the output while belief stays intact.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between high-stakes and trivial processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and stakes-direction components, patch only the stakes component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the stakes component under the high-stakes framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the stakes signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Stakes Belief Shift predicts a high-stakes factual-instability mode: (i) the same fact receiving different verdicts/confidence under high vs low stakes, (ii) divergence between internal belief and asserted output under high stakes, and (iii) increased error/hedging on safety-critical items when stakes are raised. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (stakes-level indicator, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Stakes De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the stakes/consequentiality direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing factual belief, so belief reflects content rather than the weight of the decision. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected high-stakes framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Stakes Belief Shift Score and improved high-vs-low-stakes factual consistency, (ii) factuality/calibration (ECE) under stakes framings, especially in safety-critical domains, (iii) RELIABILITY of an internal-belief reliability monitor under high-stakes framing (does raising stakes degrade a belief-based consistency detector, and does de-biasing restore it?), (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate output caution (the model should still add appropriate hedges/caveats in high-stakes contexts while keeping the underlying fact and confidence stable) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge the fact the same regardless of how much depends on it'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), stakes level and domain (medical/legal/safety vs everyday), framing style, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, distance between framing and query, and generalization to stakes framings not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent stakes belief shift could reflect the probe detecting stakes-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, answer-neutral framings, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the stakes-direction component.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level (the model hedges more when stakes are high but still believes the fact); the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and a finding that stakes affect only output (belief intact) is itself informative and reassuring for belief-based monitors.

Distinguishing answer-neutral stakes from an implicit directional incentive is subtle (high stakes might implicitly cue caution toward 'false'); we human-verify answer-neutrality, test symmetry across true/false items, and separate any directional component from the symmetric attenuation.

Truth probes trained on stakes-free statements may transfer imperfectly to stakes-framed contexts, so shifts could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Stakes and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate output caution in genuinely high-stakes settings or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of appropriate hedging, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the caution-vs-stability tradeoff — the goal is stable belief with appropriate expressed caveats, not reckless confidence.

Stakes belief shift may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (stakes-level indicator, output entropy) for high-stakes instability; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that decision consequentiality distorts internal factual belief (not just output) in exactly the domains where reliability matters most, plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/safety-tuning may amplify stakes sensitivity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_granularity_mismatch
Title: Believing at the Wrong Resolution: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Distinguish Precise From Coarse Claims About the Same Fact?
Short Hypothesis: For a single underlying fact, an LLM should believe a COARSE claim ('X happened in the 1900s') at least as firmly as a PRECISE claim it subsumes ('X happened in 1903'), because the precise claim logically entails the coarse one. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically VIOLATE this granularity-monotonicity: for facts the model is uncertain about, the decoded belief in a plausible-but-wrong PRECISE claim is inflated relative to the entailed coarse claim, so the model 'believes' a specific wrong answer more than the true general one. This granularity mismatch is graded, carried by a decodable specificity/precision component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a false-precision hallucination mode, and can be reduced by an inference-time intervention that enforces coarse>=precise belief.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never varies the GRANULARITY/RESOLUTION at which a fact is stated while holding the underlying fact fixed. My prior 'taxonomic_belief_monotonicity' proposal tested is-a subsumption ladders over CATEGORIES (poodle->dog->animal); 'gradability_belief_thresholding' tested vague predicates against a threshold; 'numeric_magnitude_belief_snapping' tested roundness/anchor bias; 'comparative_belief_distance_effect' tested magnitude-graded comparison confidence. NONE isolate the SPECIFICITY of a factual claim about the same event/quantity — whether belief in a precise value (a year, a decimal, a full name) is properly bounded by belief in the coarse claim it entails (a decade, a range, a surname) — nor predict that uncertainty inflates precise-but-wrong belief above the true coarse belief (a false-precision effect), nor tie it to a false-precision hallucination mode, nor enforce granularity-monotonicity. This precision-vs-coarseness lens on belief geometry is new and maps directly onto a high-stakes hallucination: confidently stating an overly-specific wrong answer (a made-up exact date, page number, or dosage) when only a coarse fact is warranted.
Abstract: If a fact happened in 1903 it happened in the 1900s, so a coherent believer can never hold the precise claim more firmly than the coarse claim it entails. Yet people, and perhaps models, exhibit false precision: they commit to a specific wrong answer more confidently than to the true general one. We ask whether large language models violate granularity-monotonicity inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we read the model's belief in claims about a single fact stated at multiple resolutions — precise (exact year/value/name) versus coarse (decade/range/surname) — and test whether belief is non-decreasing as claims become coarser. We construct GranularBelief, a controlled dataset of facts (dates, quantities, names, locations) rendered at nested granularity levels, crossed with the model's uncertainty (well-known vs obscure facts) and truth-value, plus synthetic-in-context facts to control priors, with surface forms matched. We define a Granularity Violation Score = the extent to which belief in a precise claim exceeds belief in the coarse claim it entails, and test four claims: (1) belief violates granularity-monotonicity, especially for uncertain facts where plausible-but-wrong precise claims are believed above the true coarse claim; (2) the violation is carried by a decodable specificity/precision component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) violation magnitude causally predicts a false-precision hallucination mode (asserting an unwarranted specific answer); and (4) a lightweight Granularity-Monotone intervention that caps precise belief at the coarse belief reduces false precision without harming warranted specificity or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on precision-QA accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build GranularBelief. Collect facts whose value admits nested resolutions: DATES (exact year -> decade -> century), QUANTITIES (exact number -> order-of-magnitude range), NAMES (full name -> surname -> initial), LOCATIONS (city -> region -> country). For each fact instantiate a NESTED LADDER of claims from precise to coarse, where the precise claim entails every coarser one. Cross with (a) the model's UNCERTAINTY about the fact (well-known vs obscure, verified behaviorally), (b) TRUTH: for uncertain facts include a plausible-but-WRONG precise claim (e.g. a wrong exact year) whose coarse version (the true decade) is correct, so the true coarse claim and a false precise claim can be compared. Add SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (value stipulated in context) to remove parametric priors, false-ladder controls, and matched surface forms (avoid specificity being a lexical shortcut, e.g. equalize token length across levels). Human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each rung of each fact's granularity ladder. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally knows the coarse fact for well-known items.

Granularity Violation measurement: For each ladder a monotonicity-respecting model should have belief(precise) <= belief(coarse it entails). Define Granularity Violation Score = magnitude by which belief(precise claim) exceeds belief(entailed coarse claim), aggregated over ladder steps. Crucially, for uncertain facts, compare belief in the FALSE-precise claim vs the TRUE-coarse claim: false precision = believing the wrong specific answer above the right general one. Report per-layer, per-model violation as a function of granularity gap and uncertainty. Test the hypotheses that (i) violations are nonzero, (ii) they grow with uncertainty, and (iii) false-precise beliefs can exceed true-coarse beliefs. Compare internal violations to OUTPUT-level violations (does the model assert an overly-specific answer when only a coarse one is warranted?).

Specificity-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'specificity/precision' direction via difference-in-means on precise vs coarse claim activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the specificity axis (and vice versa); test whether violations are explained by the specificity component leaking into the truth-probe readout. Disentangle specificity from surface token-length via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer the coarse-claim belief along the truth direction and measure whether the precise-claim belief updates in the entailment-consistent (bounded) direction. (b) Patch the specificity component into a coarse claim and measure induced belief inflation. (c) In synthetic facts, patch the value representation and measure whether precise/coarse beliefs move coherently. Confirm the false-precision inflation is causal and separable from content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Granularity Violation Score predicts a false-precision hallucination mode: (i) the model asserting an unwarranted specific answer (a made-up exact date/value/full name) when only a coarse answer is supported, (ii) precision-QA errors where the safe answer is coarse, and (iii) inconsistency across granularity paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (uncertainty/frequency indicator, output entropy, coarse-claim truth-probe confidence).

Granularity-Monotone intervention: At inference, given decoded beliefs along a ladder, enforce belief(precise) <= belief(coarse) via an ITI-style additive shift along the truth direction that caps any precise claim exceeding its entailed coarse claim (or dampens the specificity component for detected precise queries). Provide a deployment variant that, for a queried precise claim, detects the relevant coarse claim and applies the cap. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Granularity Violation Score, (ii) reduced false-precision hallucination and improved precision-QA behavior (preferring warranted coarse answers, abstaining from unwarranted specifics), (iii) calibration (ECE) on granularity-varied claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of warranted specificity (when the model genuinely knows the exact value it must still assert it) and accuracy on well-known facts and false-ladder controls (no over-hedging), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'never be more confident in a specific answer than in the general answer it implies; give a coarse answer if unsure of specifics'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), fact type (dates/quantities/names/locations), granularity gap, uncertainty level, real vs synthetic-in-context facts, model scale, specificity-vs-token-length disentangling, and generalization to granularity ladders not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent granularity violations could reflect the probe detecting specificity/rarity lexical cues (precise terms are rarer/longer) rather than a genuine belief-monotonicity failure; mitigate with token-length matching across levels, specificity-vs-length regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the truth-direction component.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to claims at different resolutions, so violations could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and false-ladder controls confirming the probe detects genuine falsehood.
Some facts have contested or fuzzy nesting (e.g. calendar boundaries, name variants); we restrict quantitative claims to clean ladders, human-verify, and analyze ambiguous items separately.
Reading a comparable belief scalar across granularity levels is position/token sensitive; include position and layer robustness checks and report sensitivity of the violation score.

The Granularity-Monotone intervention requires reliable per-rung readouts and could over-hedge (suppressing warranted specific answers) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure warranted-specificity preservation, well-known-fact accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff, and gate the cap to uncertain items.

Violation magnitude may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (uncertainty/frequency, output entropy) for false-precision hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry violates granularity-monotonicity (a false-precision effect) plus the monotone-cap tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_granularity_mismatch
Title: Believing at the Wrong Resolution: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Violate Granularity-Monotonicity and Exhibit False Precision?
Short Hypothesis: For a single underlying fact, an LLM should believe a COARSE claim ('X happened in the 1900s') at least as firmly as a PRECISE claim it logically entails ('X happened in 1903'). We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically VIOLATE this granularity-monotonicity: for facts the model is uncertain about, the decoded belief in a plausible-but-wrong PRECISE claim is inflated relative to the entailed true COARSE claim, so the model internally 'believes' a specific wrong answer more than the true general one. This false-precision effect is graded, carried by a decodable specificity component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an unwarranted-specific-answer hallucination mode, and can be reduced by an inference-time intervention that enforces coarse>=precise belief.

This precision-vs-coarseness lens on belief geometry is new and maps directly onto a high-stakes hallucination: confidently stating an overly-specific wrong answer (a made-up exact date, page number, or dosage) when only a coarse fact is warranted.

Yet people, and perhaps models, exhibit false precision: they commit to a specific wrong answer more confidently than to the true general one. We ask whether large language models violate granularity-monotonicity inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we read the model's belief in claims about a single fact stated at multiple resolutions — precise (exact year/value/name) versus coarse (decade/range/surname) — and test whether belief is non-decreasing as claims become coarser. We define a Granularity Violation Score = the extent to which belief in a precise claim exceeds belief in the coarse claim it entails, and test four claims: (1) belief violates granularity-monotonicity, especially for uncertain facts where plausible-but-wrong precise claims are believed above the true coarse claim; (2) the violation is carried by a decodable specificity component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) violation magnitude causally predicts a false-precision hallucination mode (asserting an unwarranted specific answer); and (4) a lightweight Granularity-Monotone intervention that caps precise belief at the coarse belief reduces false precision without harming warranted specificity or general capability. Name: adversarial_frame_belief_bending
Title: Beliefs in a Fight: Does a Competitive or Adversarial Interaction Frame Distort an LLM's Internal Factual Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, placing the LLM in a COMPETITIVE/ADVERSARIAL interaction frame (a debate opponent, a negotiation counterparty, a rival) versus a COOPERATIVE frame (a collaborator, a teammate) systematically shifts its INTERNAL belief in the proposition (linear truth-direction readout), not merely its strategic output. We hypothesize that under an adversarial frame the model's internal belief bends toward whatever position serves 'winning' (raising belief in claims that favor its side, lowering it in claims that favor the opponent), that this bending is graded in frame intensity, carried by a decodable competitive-stance component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an adversarial factual-distortion mode, and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the competitive component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether the interaction is cooperative vs adversarial while holding the proposition fixed. Multi-agent debate work (Du et al. 2023) and LLM negotiation/game studies operate at the OUTPUT/strategy level, showing models argue for assigned sides, but never read the internal FIRST-ORDER factual belief or test whether the adversarial frame corrupts belief itself rather than just the argument produced. My prior proposals vary the intended AUDIENCE (audience_indexed_belief_bending), the model's assigned IDENTITY (counterfactual_identity), reported CROWD (social_consensus), MONITORING cues (surveillance_framing), external REWARD attached to a specific answer (incentivized_belief_distortion), self-generated ARGUMENTS (self_persuasion_belief_drift), and decision STAKES (counterfactual_stakes). NONE isolate the RELATIONAL STANCE of the interaction — cooperative vs competitive/adversarial — as a distinct axis that distorts the model's own internal factual belief. This differs concretely from incentivized (reward on a specific answer, not a relationship), from self_persuasion (arguing a side changes belief; here the mere adversarial FRAME, before any argument is generated, is the manipulated variable), and from audience/persona (the manipulated variable is the antagonism of the counterparty, not who is listening or who the model is). This adversarial-stance lens on belief geometry is new and directly relevant to deployments in debate, negotiation, red-teaming, and multi-agent settings where competitive framing may silently corrupt factual reliability.
Abstract: When people argue against an opponent they do not merely defend their side — they come to believe it more, and to doubt the opponent's claims, a motivated-reasoning effect of the adversarial frame itself. We ask whether large language models exhibit this inside their belief representations, and crucially whether the mere COMPETITIVE FRAMING of an interaction — before any argument is even produced — distorts the model's own factual belief. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the relational stance — cooperative collaborator/teammate vs adversarial debate-opponent/negotiation-rival — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct FrameStanceBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in matched cooperative vs adversarial interaction frames that carry no evidence about the fact, with frame intensity graded and surface length matched, plus items where the fact favors 'the model's side' vs 'the opponent's side'. We define a Competitive Belief Bending Score = belief(fact | adversarial frame) minus belief(fact | cooperative frame), and test four claims: (1) internal belief bends toward the model's competitive interest under adversarial framing, at fixed content and truth, graded in frame intensity; (2) the bending is carried by a decodable competitive-stance component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) bending magnitude causally predicts an adversarial factual-distortion mode (inflating belief in self-favoring claims, doubting opponent-favoring truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the competitive component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate strategic behavior and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, capability retention, and whether belief-based honesty monitors survive competitive framing.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build FrameStanceBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched interaction frames differing only in relational STANCE and carrying no evidence about P: COOPERATIVE ('You and I are teammates working together to figure out the truth'; 'Help your collaborator get this right') vs ADVERSARIAL ('You are debating an opponent who wants to prove you wrong'; 'You are negotiating against a rival'), plus a NEUTRAL baseline with matched surface length. Grade frame intensity (mild vs strongly antagonistic). Crucially cross with SIDE-ALIGNMENT: whether the true answer to P favors 'the model's assigned side' vs 'the opponent's side' vs is side-neutral, so we can distinguish a directional pull (toward self-favoring positions) from generic frame effects. The correct answer to P is identical across frames. Human-verify that frames carry no evidential bearing and are answer-neutral except via the assigned side; include paraphrase sets and controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, frame-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (before the model produces any argument) read the internal belief in P under each frame; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the frame (e.g. reports whether the interaction is cooperative or adversarial).

Competitive Belief Bending measurement: Define Competitive Belief Bending Score = belief(P | adversarial frame) minus belief(P | cooperative frame), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model bending across frame intensity, truth regime, and SIDE-ALIGNMENT. Test the hypotheses that (i) under adversarial framing belief bends toward self-favoring positions (inflated belief in claims favoring the model's side, deflated belief in opponent-favoring truths), (ii) bending is graded in frame intensity, and (iii) side-neutral items show smaller directional bending (isolating motivated distortion from generic frame arousal). Compare internal bending to OUTPUT-level bending, and crucially to a condition probed BEFORE any argument generation, to show the frame alone (not self-produced arguments) drives it.

Competitive-stance-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'competitive-stance' direction via difference-in-means on adversarial vs cooperative activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value, content, and side). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the stance axis (and vice versa); test whether the bending is explained by the stance component leaking into the truth-probe readout, or whether stance is represented but only gates the output while belief stays intact.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between adversarial and cooperative processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and stance-direction components, patch only the stance component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the stance component under the adversarial frame and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the competitive-stance signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Competitive Belief Bending predicts an adversarial factual-distortion mode: (i) inflated endorsement of self-favoring (including false self-favoring) claims under adversarial framing, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of opponent-favoring true claims, and (iii) divergence between internal belief and asserted output under competitive framing. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (frame-intensity indicator, output entropy, cooperative-frame truth-probe confidence).

Competitive De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the competitive-stance direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing factual belief, so belief reflects content rather than the antagonism of the interaction. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected adversarial framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Competitive Belief Bending Score and improved cooperative-vs-adversarial factual consistency, (ii) reduced endorsement of self-favoring falsehoods and reduced doubting of opponent-favoring truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) under competitive framings, (iv) RELIABILITY of an internal-belief honesty monitor under adversarial framing (does competitive framing degrade a belief-based consistency/lie detector, and does de-biasing restore it?), (v) PRESERVATION of legitimate strategic behavior (the model should still be able to argue a side or negotiate when asked, while its underlying factual belief stays accurate) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'assess the facts accurately regardless of whether you are competing or collaborating', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), frame intensity and type (debate/negotiation/rivalry vs teammate/collaborator), side-alignment (self-favoring/opponent-favoring/neutral), real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, distance between frame and query, before-vs-after argument generation, and generalization to interaction frames not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent competitive belief bending could reflect the probe detecting adversarial-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, side-alignment contrasts (self-favoring vs opponent-favoring vs neutral), paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the stance-direction component.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level (the model argues a side but still believes the fact); the internal-vs-output comparison, reading belief BEFORE any argument is generated, and causal patching directly test this, and a finding that the frame affects only output (belief intact) is itself informative and reassuring for belief-based monitors.

Distinguishing the frame effect from self-persuasion (arguing changes belief) is crucial; we probe belief before argument production and hold argument content out of the manipulation, but residual anticipatory-argument effects may remain and are analyzed separately.

Truth probes trained on frame-free statements may transfer imperfectly to framed contexts, so bending could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Competitive-stance and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate strategic/argumentative behavior (the model can no longer play a debate role) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of strategic behavior, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the strategy-vs-factuality tradeoff, which is the core risk.

Competitive belief bending may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (frame-intensity indicator, output entropy) for adversarial distortion; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that competitive framing distorts internal factual belief (not just output) before any argument is even made, plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify or dampen competitive framing sensitivity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: tool_output_belief_deference
Title: Believing the Tool: Does an LLM Over-Trust Tool/Retrieval Outputs Inside Its Belief Geometry, Even When They Contradict Its Own Knowledge?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM operating in an agentic/tool-use loop receives a factual claim as the OUTPUT OF A TOOL CALL it just issued (e.g. a search result, calculator output, API/document return) rather than as an ordinary user assertion, its INTERNAL belief in that claim (linear truth-direction readout) is inflated toward true, even when the claim contradicts what the model otherwise reliably knows. We hypothesize this 'tool-output deference' is graded in tool authoritativeness, carried by a decodable tool-provenance component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a tool-injection hallucination mode (endorsing false tool returns over correct parametric knowledge), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the tool-provenance component so belief reflects content rather than mere tool origin.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether a claim arrives as a TOOL/RETRIEVAL OUTPUT the model itself invoked. Knowledge-conflict work (SI-FACT 2025; Simulated Adoption 2026) and my prior 'belief_source_provenance' proposal separated PARAMETRIC vs CONTEXTUAL origin as a single undifferentiated contextual channel; 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' concerned a named human source's accumulated track record; 'social_consensus' varied crowd size; 'incentivized' attached reward to an answer. NONE isolate the distinctive TOOL/AGENTIC provenance — content returned by a function/search/calculator call the model issued as part of its own reasoning loop — as a decodable belief axis, nor test whether this specific 'the tool said so' framing inflates belief above ordinary user-provided context, nor tie it to a tool-injection hallucination mode, nor de-bias it. Prompt-injection/RAG-poisoning research studies this at the OUTPUT/security level (does the agent obey injected tool content), never in belief geometry. This tool-output-deference lens is new, directly relevant to the rapidly-growing agentic/tool-augmented deployment setting, and distinct from generic contextual provenance and human-source reliability.
Abstract: LLMs are increasingly deployed as agents that call tools — search, calculators, APIs, retrieval — and treat the returns as ground truth. We ask whether this deference lives inside the model's belief representations: does a factual claim delivered as the OUTPUT OF A TOOL CALL the model itself issued get believed more than the identical claim stated by a user, even when it contradicts the model's own reliable knowledge? Distinguishing a claim's content from its TOOL PROVENANCE, we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction under matched framings. We construct ToolBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each delivered via (a) a simulated tool/retrieval output following a model-issued tool call, (b) an ordinary user assertion, and (c) a neutral baseline, with tool authoritativeness graded and surface content held fixed, plus a critical KNOWLEDGE-CONFLICT subset where the tool returns a claim contradicting a well-known fact. We define a Tool Deference Score = belief(claim | tool output) minus belief(claim | user assertion), and test four claims: (1) belief is inflated for tool-provenance content, graded in authoritativeness; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable tool-provenance component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) deference magnitude causally predicts a tool-injection hallucination mode (endorsing false tool returns over correct parametric knowledge); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the tool-provenance component recalibrates belief while preserving legitimate reliance on genuinely-helpful tools and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, tool-injection robustness, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ToolBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to control priors). Each P is delivered under matched framings holding the CLAIM TEXT identical but varying PROVENANCE: (a) TOOL OUTPUT — the transcript shows the model issuing a tool call (search/calculator/API/document lookup) and receiving P as the structured return; (b) USER ASSERTION — the same P stated by the user; (c) NEUTRAL baseline — P appears once, unframed. Grade tool AUTHORITATIVENESS (a casual web snippet vs an 'official database' vs a 'verified calculator'). Crucially include a KNOWLEDGE-CONFLICT subset where the tool/user returns a claim that CONTRADICTS a well-known fact the model reliably holds (verified behaviorally), so tool-provenance can be pitted against parametric knowledge. Include a LEGITIMATE-TOOL control where the tool provides genuinely correct information the model lacked (to distinguish deference from valid updating). Match surface length across framings; human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, provenance-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each provenance framing; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the tool framing (e.g. can report that P came from a tool).

Tool Deference measurement: Define Tool Deference Score = belief(P | tool output) minus belief(P | user assertion), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model deference across tool authoritativeness and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) tool-provenance content is believed more than identical user-provided content, and (ii) deference grows with authoritativeness. On the KNOWLEDGE-CONFLICT subset, test whether a false tool return overrides the model's correct parametric belief more than a false user assertion does. Compare internal deference to OUTPUT-level deference (does the model assert the tool's false claim?).

Tool-provenance-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'tool-provenance' direction via difference-in-means on tool-output vs user-assertion activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the provenance axis (and vice versa); test whether deference is explained by the tool-provenance component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between tool-output and user-assertion processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and provenance-direction components, patch only the provenance component into the user-assertion condition, and measure induced change in belief and output. Conversely subtract the provenance component under the tool framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the tool-provenance signal causally inflates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Tool Deference predicts a tool-injection hallucination mode: (i) endorsement of false tool returns, (ii) overriding correct parametric knowledge on the knowledge-conflict subset, and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by tool provenance. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (tool-authoritativeness indicator, output entropy, user-assertion truth-probe confidence).

Tool-Provenance De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the tool-provenance direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the claim's content/evidence rather than mere tool origin. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected tool-output framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and robustness evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Tool Deference Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of false/poisoned tool returns and reduced override of correct parametric knowledge (tool-injection robustness), (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on tool-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate tool reliance (the LEGITIMATE-TOOL control, where the tool supplies correct info the model lacked, must still update belief) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'treat tool outputs as evidence to verify, not as ground truth', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), tool type (search/calculator/API/document) and authoritativeness, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, knowledge-conflict vs no-conflict, model scale, distance between tool return and query, and generalization to tool framings not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent tool deference could reflect the probe detecting tool-framing lexical/structural cues (JSON returns, tool tags) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the provenance-direction component.

Distinguishing illegitimate deference from legitimate updating is subtle since tools often ARE more reliable than users; the LEGITIMATE-TOOL control and the false-tool-return / knowledge-conflict subsets separate over-trust from warranted trust, and the de-biasing must preserve legitimate updating (a key success criterion).

Truth probes trained on provenance-free statements may transfer imperfectly to agentic/tool-framed transcripts, so deference could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Tool-provenance and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair beneficial tool reliance or harm fluency; we explicitly measure legitimate-tool preservation, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the over-trust-vs-utility tradeoff, which is the core risk.

Tool deference may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (tool-authoritativeness indicator, output entropy) for tool-injection hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that tool provenance inflates internal belief (a distinct agentic over-trust axis) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (tool-use fine-tuning likely amplifies deference); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: explanatory_coherence_belief_conflation
Title: It Sounds Explainable, So It Must Be True: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Conflate Explanatory Coherence With Truth?
Short Hypothesis: For a factual claim, an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) is inflated when the claim is accompanied by (or is easy to generate) a coherent-sounding mechanistic EXPLANATION of WHY it holds, even when the explanation is spurious and the claim is false: the model conflates 'I can articulate a plausible mechanism for P' with 'P is true'. We hypothesize this explanatory-coherence inflation is graded in the fluency/coherence of the attached explanation, carried by a decodable explanatory-coherence component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an explanation-backed-falsehood hallucination mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the coherence component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never varies whether a claim is accompanied by a coherent mechanistic explanation. My prior 'plausibility_vs_truth_belief' proposal tested whether belief tracks a claim's PRIOR plausibility/consistency; 'causal_vs_correlational_belief' tested whether belief distinguishes causal from correlational relations; 'detail_vividness_belief_inflation' (vividness_detail) tested irrelevant concrete detail; 'belief_evidence_weighting' tested aggregation of supporting evidence. NONE isolate EXPLANATORY COHERENCE — the presence/fluency of a mechanistic account of WHY a claim holds — as a distinct axis that inflates belief in the claim's TRUTH, independent of the claim's prior plausibility and of any genuine evidence. In human cognition this is the 'explanatory depth' / seductive-explanation effect (a fluent causal story increases believed truth even when circular or spurious; Trout, Rozenblit & Keil). This explanatory-coherence lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto a high-stakes hallucination mode: LLMs confabulate convincing mechanistic explanations that make false claims (fake drug mechanisms, pseudo-scientific accounts) internally more believed.
Abstract: A fluent explanation of why something is true makes people believe it more — even when the explanation is circular or bogus. We ask whether large language models inherit this seductive-explanation effect inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a claim's content from the coherent EXPLANATION that may accompany it, we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, and test whether attaching a coherent-sounding mechanistic account of WHY a claim holds inflates the model's belief that the claim is TRUE, independent of the claim's prior plausibility. We construct ExplainBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each presented (a) bare, (b) with a coherent but spurious/circular explanation of why it holds, and (c) with an incoherent/degraded pseudo-explanation, with explanation coherence graded, prior plausibility matched, and surface length controlled. We define an Explanatory Coherence Inflation Score = belief(claim + coherent explanation) minus belief(bare claim), and test four claims: (1) belief inflates with attached explanatory coherence, graded in explanation fluency, even for false claims; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable explanatory-coherence component dissociable from the truth axis and from a prior-plausibility axis; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts an explanation-backed-falsehood hallucination mode (endorsing false claims dressed in convincing mechanisms); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the coherence component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure without harming legitimate evidence-based reasoning or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ExplainBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). For each P create matched conditions: (a) BARE claim; (b) claim + a COHERENT mechanistic EXPLANATION of why P holds that is spurious/circular (adds no genuine evidence: a fluent causal story, a plausible-sounding mechanism, possibly circular or vacuous); (c) claim + an INCOHERENT/degraded pseudo-explanation (same topic, jumbled logic). Grade explanation COHERENCE (highly fluent vs weak). Crucially, the explanation is evidentially EMPTY — it asserts a mechanism but supplies no independent evidence for P's truth (verified: a rational reader should not update on it). Match surface LENGTH across conditions (use equal-length irrelevant filler for the bare condition), match the claim's PRIOR PLAUSIBILITY across explanation conditions, and control lexical sentiment. Human-verify that explanations are evidentially empty and coherence labels are accurate; include paraphrase sets. Include a CONTROL with genuine evidence (a real reason that does bear on truth) to distinguish coherence-inflation from legitimate updating.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, bare true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the CLAIM P under each explanation condition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false bare items; confirm the explanations are evidentially empty (the model, when asked, agrees the explanation provides no independent evidence for P).

Explanatory Coherence Inflation measurement: Define Explanatory Coherence Inflation Score = belief(P + coherent explanation) minus belief(P bare), controlling for the length-matched filler baseline so inflation is attributed to coherence, not length. Report per-layer, per-model inflation as a function of explanation coherence and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief inflates with attached explanatory coherence, (ii) inflation grows with explanation fluency, and (iii) crucially, FALSE claims dressed in coherent explanations are believed more true than bare falsehoods. Contrast coherent vs incoherent explanations (both present a mechanism; only fluency differs) to isolate coherence from mere mechanism-presence. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level inflation (does the model's verdict/confidence about P rise with the explanation?). Compare against the genuine-evidence control (is the empty coherent explanation treated like real evidence?).

Coherence-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'explanatory-coherence' direction via difference-in-means on coherent-explanation vs incoherent-explanation activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction and with a separately-fit prior-plausibility direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode coherence (and vice versa); test whether the inflation is explained by the coherence component leaking into the truth-probe readout, and whether coherence is dissociable from prior plausibility.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a coherent-explanation and a matched incoherent-explanation (or bare) rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and coherence-direction components, patch only the coherence component into the bare condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output endorsement. Conversely subtract the coherence component from the coherent-explanation rendering and measure whether belief returns toward the content-driven value. Confirm the coherence signal causally inflates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Explanatory Coherence Inflation predicts an explanation-backed-falsehood hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of false claims accompanied by coherent spurious explanations, (ii) confident-wrong rate, and (iii) the model spontaneously generating a convincing mechanism for a false claim and thereby endorsing it (self-explanation variant). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (explanation-coherence rating alone, output entropy, bare-claim truth-probe confidence, prior-plausibility score).

Coherence De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the explanatory-coherence direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the claim's evidence rather than the fluency of an attached explanation. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected explanation-laden claims. Sweep layer and strength.
