Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Explanatory Coherence Inflation Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of explanation-backed falsehoods, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on explanation-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate evidence-based updating (the genuine-evidence control must still raise belief) and accuracy on bare-true controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge whether the claim is true, not whether it has a plausible-sounding explanation', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the bare claim).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), coherence level, circular vs non-circular explanations, provided-explanation vs self-generated-explanation, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, length-matching method, and generalization to explanation styles and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent explanatory-coherence inflation could reflect the probe detecting surface fluency/length lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with length-matched filler baselines, coherent-vs-incoherent contrasts (both present a mechanism, only fluency differs), prior-plausibility matching, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the coherence-direction component.

The attached explanation might inadvertently carry genuine evidential content (a coherent mechanism can imply real support), confounding coherence-inflation with legitimate updating; we human-verify explanations are evidentially empty/circular, include a genuine-evidence control to calibrate legitimate updating, and analyze borderline items separately.

Truth probes trained on bare statements may transfer imperfectly to explanation-laden renderings, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.

Coherence, truth, and prior-plausibility directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate reasoning that uses genuine explanatory evidence or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the genuine-evidence control and bare-true items plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Explanatory-coherence inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (coherence rating, output entropy, prior plausibility) for explanation-backed-falsehood hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates explanatory coherence with truth (a seductive-explanation effect) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify preference for explanation-rich, confident text); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: notation_modality_belief_bending
Title: Same Fact, Different Notation: Does the Representational Format a Fact Is Expressed In Bend an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, the NOTATION/REPRESENTATIONAL FORMAT in which the fact's CONTENT is expressed — plain natural-language prose, code (a Python assertion / dict), a formal-logic/mathematical expression, or a structured table/JSON record — systematically shifts the LLM's INTERNAL belief in the fact (linear truth-direction readout), even though the notation carries no information about the fact. We hypothesize this 'notation belief bending' is graded, is carried by a decodable content-notation component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a notation-dependent factual-inconsistency hallucination mode (the same fact judged true in one notation and false in another), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the notation component so belief reflects content rather than the format the fact is dressed in.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief and Bao et al. show probes generalize across a single logical/QA transformation of a statement, but none vary the NOTATION in which the fact's CONTENT is rendered (prose vs code vs formal logic vs table). VAGEN (Wang et al. 2025) finds that the OPTIMAL internal belief-state REPRESENTATION for a VLM agent is task-dependent (natural language vs structured), but that concerns which format to train an agent's reasoning to use — a behavior/reasoning-level result — not whether the model's TRUTH belief in a fixed factual proposition bends with the notation the fact is expressed in. My prior 'answer_format_belief_distortion' proposal varied the demanded RESPONSE FORMAT the model must emit (free-text vs MCQ vs T/F vs cloze); the present proposal instead varies the notation in which the fact's CONTENT is PRESENTED to the model, holding the response format constant — a distinct axis. 'polyglot_belief_invariance' varied natural LANGUAGE, 'register_framing' varied tone/style, 'query_polarity' varied question phrasing. NONE isolate representational notation/modality of the propositional content (prose/code/logic/table) as a decodable belief axis, test whether belief bends toward the notation a fact 'looks native' in, tie it to a notation-dependent factual-inconsistency mode, or de-bias it. This notation-invariance lens on belief geometry is new and practically important as LLMs are deployed across code, data, and math pipelines.
Abstract: A fact is the same fact whether we write it as English prose, a line of Python, a logical formula, or a row in a table — so a rational believer's confidence should not depend on the notation. We ask whether large language models honor this notation-invariance inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the REPRESENTATIONAL FORMAT in which the fact's content is expressed (natural-language prose, a Python assertion/dict, a formal-logic or mathematical expression, a JSON/table record) while keeping the model's task (judge the fact's truth) constant, and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct NotationBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered across matched notations, with surface information equated. We define a Notation Belief Bending Score = belief(fact in notation A) minus belief(fact in notation B), and test four claims: (1) internal belief shifts with the notation the fact is expressed in, at fixed content and truth; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable content-notation component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts a notation-dependent factual-inconsistency mode (the same fact judged differently across notations, e.g. a fact rendered as code believed more than the identical prose claim, or a numeric fact in a table doubted when phrased in prose); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the notation component restores content-driven belief and improves cross-notation consistency without harming legitimate notation comprehension or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual consistency, calibration, and capability retention. Our results ask whether an LLM believes a fact more or less depending merely on how it is written down.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build NotationBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each P is rendered in matched NOTATIONS that express the SAME content, holding the model's task fixed (judge truth of the rendered fact): (a) NATURAL-LANGUAGE PROSE ('The capital of Australia is Canberra'), (b) CODE (a Python assertion or dict, e.g. `capital_of['Australia'] == 'Canberra'`), (c) FORMAL-LOGIC/MATH (e.g. `capital(Australia)=Canberra`, or for quantitative facts an equation/inequality), (d) STRUCTURED TABLE/JSON (a one-row record). Cover relational facts, numeric/quantitative facts (well-suited to code/math/table), and categorical facts. Ensure the propositional content and truth-value are identical across notations; equate the informational content (same entities/values, no extra cues); include neutral controls and paraphrase sets. Human-verify that each notation faithfully and equivalently expresses P; verify the model can parse each notation (comprehension check).

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale, including code-capable models (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B / Qwen2.5-Coder, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral prose true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the fact rendered in each notation (using a canonical 'is this fact correct?' probe appended in a fresh pass to standardize the readout across notations). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false prose items; confirm the model comprehends each notation (can restate the fact from the code/logic/table rendering).

Notation Belief Bending measurement: Define Notation Belief Bending Score = belief(P in notation A) minus belief(P in notation B) for each notation pair, holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model bending across all notation pairs and truth regimes and across fact types (relational/numeric/categorical). Test the hypotheses that (i) belief varies with the notation the fact is expressed in, and (ii) belief is higher for notations a fact 'looks native' in (e.g. numeric facts as code/table vs prose). Compare internal bending to OUTPUT-level bending (does the model's verdict/confidence on the fact differ across notations?), and separate notation effects from response-format artifacts by keeping the demanded answer format constant.

Notation-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'content-notation' direction via difference-in-means on activations under one notation vs another (balanced across truth-value and content); optionally fit a multi-way notation subspace spanning prose/code/logic/table. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the notation axis (and vice versa); test whether the belief bending is explained by the notation component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between two notation renderings of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and notation-direction components, patch only the notation component into a reference (prose) condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output verdict. Conversely subtract the notation component and measure whether belief converges across notations. Confirm the notation signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Notation Belief Bending predicts a notation-dependent factual-inconsistency mode: (i) the same fact receiving different correct/incorrect verdicts across notations, (ii) confidence swings across notations, and (iii) endorsing a false fact when dressed in an authoritative-seeming notation (code/table) while correctly rejecting the same falsehood in prose (or vice versa). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (notation-type indicator, output entropy, prose truth-probe confidence).

Notation De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the content-notation direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the proposition's content rather than its notation. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected non-prose notation. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Notation Belief Bending Score, (ii) improved cross-notation factual consistency (same verdict regardless of notation) on NotationBelief and adapted factual-QA benchmarks rendered in multiple notations, (iii) calibration (ECE) aggregated across notations, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate notation comprehension (the model must still parse and operate on code/logic/tables) and accuracy on prose clearly-true/false controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU, a coding eval (e.g. HumanEval subset), and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, self-consistency across notations, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge the fact based on its content, not the format it is written in'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), notation pair, fact type (relational/numeric/categorical), real vs synthetic-in-context facts, true vs false regime, code-tuned vs general models, readout position, and generalization to notations not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent notation belief bending could reflect the probe detecting notation-specific surface tokens (brackets, operators, JSON syntax) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched informational content, paraphrase controls within each notation, canonical standardized readout probes, and causal patching that isolates the notation-direction component.

Reading a comparable belief scalar across structurally different notations is position-sensitive; we standardize via a canonical 'is this fact correct?' probe appended in a fresh pass, include position/layer robustness checks, and report sensitivity of the bending score.

The model may genuinely mis-parse some notations (a comprehension failure, not a belief-gating failure); we include per-notation comprehension manipulation checks and analyze comprehended vs mis-parsed items separately.

Truth probes trained on prose may transfer imperfectly to code/logic/table-rendered facts, so bending could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Notation and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could degrade legitimate notation-specific competence (e.g. code understanding) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure notation-comprehension preservation, coding-eval retention, and general capability to characterize the tradeoff.

Notation belief bending may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (notation-type indicator, output entropy) for cross-notation inconsistency; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that the notation a fact is written in distorts internal belief plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (code-tuning likely amplifies notation sensitivity); we test multiple models including code-tuned ones and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: spatial_deixis_belief_binding
Title: Here Versus There: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Bind Facts to the Correct Deictic Reference Frame?
Short Hypothesis: For a proposition whose truth depends on an indexical/deictic reference frame ('here it is raining', 'the meeting is tomorrow', 'the item is on your left'), an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) must be bound to the correct anchor (the stated place, time, or perspective-holder) rather than collapsing to a single default frame. We hypothesize LLM belief representations systematically FAIL deictic binding: the decoded belief in an indexical claim is dragged toward one dominant default frame (typically the most recently mentioned or the speaker's own), barely tracking the queried anchor, that this failure is graded and dissociable as a decodable reference-frame axis distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a deixis-confusion factual-error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief to the queried frame.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never varies the DEICTIC/INDEXICAL reference frame ('here', 'now', 'your left', 'tomorrow') on which an indexical proposition's truth hinges. My prior 'time_indexed_belief_geometry' proposal conditioned belief on a queried DATE for mutable facts (a single temporal index tied to world validity intervals); 'agent_indexed_belief_binding' bound a belief to WHICH third-party agent HOLDS it (Theory-of-Mind); 'conditional_belief_indexing' conditioned a consequent on a stated antecedent; 'compositional_belief_binding' tested role-binding within a relation. NONE isolate DEICTIC anchoring — whether the internal belief in an indexical claim is bound to the correct spatial (here/there, left/right), temporal-relative (now/then, today/tomorrow), or perspectival (my/your) frame supplied in context, as opposed to collapsing to a default frame — nor treat reference-frame as a decodable axis dissociable from truth, tie deictic-binding failure to a concrete factual-error mode, or re-anchor it. Deixis/indexicality is foundational in linguistics and central to grounded, multi-turn, and embodied interaction; this deictic-reference-frame lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from temporal-index, agent-holder, antecedent-conditioning, and role-binding work.
Abstract: Many everyday claims are true only relative to a reference frame: 'it is raining here', 'the meeting is tomorrow', 'the cup is on your left'. Whose 'here', which 'now', and from whose perspective 'left' — a competent believer must bind the claim to the frame the context supplies. We ask whether large language models honor this deictic binding inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content fixed, we vary the deictic anchor and read the internal belief via linear truth probes, testing whether belief tracks the queried frame or collapses to a single default. We construct DeixisBelief, a controlled dataset of indexical propositions — spatial (here/there, left/right/near), temporal-relative (now/then, today/tomorrow), and perspectival (my/your side) — embedded in contexts that establish multiple candidate frames, so the correct belief differs sharply across anchors, plus synthetic-in-context frames to control priors. We define a Deictic Binding Score (how much belief tracks the queried anchor) and a Frame-Collapse Score (how much it reverts to a default frame), and test four claims: (1) belief fails deictic binding, collapsing toward a dominant default; (2) a separable reference-frame axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) binding failure causally predicts a deixis-confusion factual-error mode; and (4) a lightweight Frame Re-anchoring intervention that steers belief toward the queried anchor improves indexical-reasoning accuracy without harming frame-neutral facts or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on indexical QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DeixisBelief. Each item = an INDEXICAL proposition whose truth depends on a deictic anchor, plus a context establishing MULTIPLE candidate frames so the correct belief differs across anchors. Three deixis types: (a) SPATIAL (context sets up two locations/perspectives; claim 'it is raining here', 'the cup is on your left' — true for one anchor, false for another); (b) TEMPORAL-RELATIVE (context sets a reference time; claim 'the meeting is tomorrow / today' — truth depends on which 'now'); (c) PERSPECTIVAL (two agents; 'left/right/near' from A's vs B's viewpoint). For each item, query the proposition under different anchors (the correct frame vs a competing frame vs the speaker/default frame). Use real-world scenarios plus SYNTHETIC-in-context frames (fully-stipulated 'here=X, there=Y' worlds) to remove parametric priors. Include FRAME-NEUTRAL control facts (no deixis, truth-invariant to frame), matched surface forms, and paraphrase sets; human-verify anchor labels and ground-truth per anchor.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, non-indexical true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the indexical proposition under each queried anchor. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false frame-neutral items; confirm the model behaviorally comprehends the deictic setup (can report what 'here'/'now'/'your left' refers to).

Deictic Binding & Frame-Collapse measurement: Define Deictic Binding Score = spread of belief across anchors matching the ground-truth per-anchor difference (belief high for the anchor where the claim is true, low where false); a well-bound model shows a large, correctly-signed spread. Define Frame-Collapse Score = how close belief under any anchor sits to the default-frame (speaker/most-recent) value regardless of the queried anchor. Report per-layer, per-model scores across deixis type and as a function of the true cross-anchor gap. Test the under-binding hypothesis: belief barely tracks the queried anchor and reverts to a default. Diagnose the default direction (speaker-centric vs recency). Compare internal binding to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model's yes/no answer track the anchor?).

Reference-frame-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'reference-frame' direction via difference-in-means on activations under one queried anchor vs another (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the frame axis (and vice versa). Test whether the frame information is PRESENT in activations but fails to modulate the truth-direction readout (a routing/binding failure) versus not represented at all.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Patch the reference-frame representation from a query under the correct anchor into a query under a competing/default anchor and measure whether belief and the output verdict flip appropriately. (b) In synthetic-frame items, patch the anchor-defining representation and measure whether the indexical belief updates in the frame-consistent direction. Confirm the deictic anchor causally governs (or fails to govern) the belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether low Deictic Binding / high Frame-Collapse predicts a deixis-confusion factual-error mode: (i) wrong yes/no verdict on indexical claims (answering as if a different anchor held), (ii) errors on indexical QA ('From B's side, is the cup on the left?', 'Relative to Tuesday, is the meeting tomorrow?'), and (iii) inconsistency across anchor paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (true cross-anchor gap alone, output entropy, frame-neutral truth-probe confidence).

Frame Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, given the queried anchor, add a scaled shift along the truth direction whose sign/magnitude reflects the anchor-implied value (estimated from the model's own decoded frame representation in the synthetic setting, or gated by the detected anchor), re-anchoring belief to the queried frame (ITI-style). Sweep layer and strength; provide a deployment variant that reads the anchor from the prompt.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Deictic Binding / reduced Frame-Collapse, (ii) improved accuracy on indexical/deictic-reasoning QA (adapt spatial-perspective and relative-time reasoning items and synthetic-frame QA), (iii) calibration (ECE) of indexical answers, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct FRAME-NEUTRAL judgments and of items where the claim is genuinely anchor-independent (no spurious frame-conditioning), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'answer strictly from the specified here/now/perspective'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), deixis type (spatial/temporal-relative/perspectival), size of the true cross-anchor gap, real vs synthetic-in-context frames, number of competing frames (2 vs 3), distance between anchor establishment and query, model scale, and generalization to deictic structures and domains not used to fit the frame direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent under-binding could reflect the probe reading a position/token that does not incorporate the queried anchor, so a null could be a readout artifact; mitigate with position and layer sweeps, the reference-frame dissociation analysis (is the frame present but unused?), and causal patching.

The model may fail to comprehend the deictic setup (a comprehension failure, not a binding failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model can resolve 'here'/'now'/'your left' and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on non-indexical declaratives may transfer imperfectly to indexical propositions, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false frame-neutral items, and synthetic-frame items with exact per-anchor ground truth.

Distinguishing genuine frame representation from surface anchor-token detection is hard; we use paraphrased/relative anchor framings, project-out controls, and treat a pure token-detection result as an informative negative.

Frame Re-anchoring could over-condition (spuriously making anchor-independent claims frame-dependent) or harm fluency; we include frame-neutral controls (where belief should NOT move with anchor) and measure capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Under-binding may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (cross-anchor gap, output entropy) for deixis-confusion errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that belief geometry is under-bound to deictic reference frames plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_acquisition_primacy
Title: First Learned, Firmly Held: Does the Training-Time Order of Competing Facts Leave a Permanent Primacy Imprint on LLM Belief Geometry?
Short Hypothesis: When a model is exposed during (continual) pretraining to two competing claims about the same item, the CLAIM ENCOUNTERED FIRST acquires a durable advantage in the model's internal belief geometry (linear truth-direction readout) that persists even after equal or greater later exposure to the competing claim — an acquisition-order primacy effect. We hypothesize this primacy imprint is graded in the exposure gap, is dissociable from mere frequency/recency, causally predicts a stubborn-belief / order-dependent hallucination mode (the model resists overwriting first-learned facts), and is localized to the same late-layer belief circuitry where belief flips are known to concentrate.
Related Work: Layer of Truth (Churina et al. 2025) shows continual-pretraining poisoning flips internal fact preferences abruptly, concentrated in late layers and partially patch-reversible — but studies overwriting by RATIO of counterfactual exposure, holding order fixed, and never isolates the effect of which claim was learned FIRST. Crosscoding Through Time (Bayazit et al. 2025) and the SMILES-chirality work (Li et al. 2026) trace WHEN features emerge across checkpoints, not whether acquisition ORDER creates a lasting asymmetry between competing beliefs. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; Yang & Jia 2025) reads belief at inference and never manipulates training order. My prior belief proposals are almost entirely INFERENCE-TIME distortions (evidence, framing, source, plausibility, etc.) or in-context revision residue (belief_ghost_revision, which studies transient in-context overwrite, NOT training-time acquisition order). NONE ask whether the training-time ORDER of encountering competing facts — a formation-tracing question drawn from the human primacy/order-of-acquisition literature (early-learned concepts are more robust) — leaves a permanent imprint on belief geometry, whether it is dissociable from frequency/recency, whether it causally drives stubborn overwriting-resistance, or where it localizes. This acquisition-order-primacy lens is a genuinely new, formation-tracing (Location + Causal Intervention + Formation Tracing) direction distinct from all prior inference-time work.
Abstract: Humans hold first-learned facts more stubbornly than later corrections — a primacy / order-of-acquisition effect. We ask whether large language models inherit an analogous imprint in their belief representations, formed at TRAINING time. Using a controlled continual-pretraining setup, we expose a base model to pairs of competing claims about the same item (an original fact and a counterfactual), systematically varying the ORDER of first exposure while holding total exposure counts fixed, and then read the model's internal belief in each claim via linear truth probes across checkpoints, layers, and model scale. We define an Acquisition-Order Primacy Score = the residual belief advantage of the first-learned claim after the competing claim has received equal (or greater) later exposure. We test four claims: (1) the first-learned claim retains a durable internal belief advantage, graded in the first-exposure gap; (2) this primacy is dissociable from raw frequency and recency by holding counts fixed and reversing recency; (3) primacy magnitude causally predicts a stubborn-belief / order-dependent hallucination mode — the model resists overwriting first-learned facts and reverts to them under mild pressure — verified by activation patching along the belief direction; and (4) the imprint is localized to the same late-layer belief circuitry where continual-pretraining belief flips concentrate. We trace across checkpoints when the primacy advantage forms and whether it decays, and test a lightweight late-layer intervention that neutralizes stale primacy to enable correct updating. We evaluate on fact-vs-counterfact belief, overwriting-resistance, calibration, and general capability retention. Our results ask whether the sequence in which an LLM learns competing facts is silently baked into what it believes.
Experiments: Setup and dataset: Use a small-but-realistic continual-pretraining pipeline affordable in an academic lab (base models 1-8B: Pythia/OLMo checkpoints, Llama-3 8B, Qwen2.5 7B). Build FactOrderBelief: paired fact-vs-counterfact items about the same item (following the Layer-of-Truth paired paradigm) using synthetic entities (nonce subjects with stipulated attributes) to remove parametric priors, plus a real-fact subset. For each pair, construct continual-pretraining document streams that inject the two competing claims, VARYING the manipulated variable — which claim appears FIRST and the temporal GAP before the competitor — while HOLDING TOTAL EXPOSURE COUNTS EQUAL across conditions. Include a RECENCY-REVERSED condition (first-learned claim is the LESS recent) to dissociate primacy from recency, and a FREQUENCY-VARIED control.

Belief readout across checkpoints: Train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression, Platt-scaled to [0,1]) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements. After continual pretraining (and at intermediate checkpoints), read the internal belief in the first-learned vs later-learned claim for each pair. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; both claims were actually seen (verified by loss on injected docs).

Acquisition-Order Primacy measurement: Define Acquisition-Order Primacy Score = belief(first-learned claim) minus belief(later-learned claim) after equal total exposure. Report per-layer, per-model, per-scale primacy as a function of the first-exposure gap. Test the hypotheses that (i) the first-learned claim retains a durable advantage even at equal counts, and (ii) primacy grows with the exposure gap. Compare against the frequency-varied and recency-reversed controls to dissociate primacy from frequency and recency.

Formation tracing: Across continual-pretraining checkpoints, trace WHEN the primacy advantage emerges (does it lock in early and resist later competing exposure?), whether it decays with continued competing exposure, and whether it sharpens abruptly (as belief flips do in Layer of Truth). Fit belief trajectories for first- vs later-learned claims over checkpoints.

Localization: Test whether the primacy imprint concentrates in specific (expected late) layers by per-layer probing and by measuring where the first-vs-later belief gap is largest, comparing to the late-layer flip locus reported by Churina et al.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Patch the belief-direction component of the later-learned claim into the query and measure whether the output flips away from the first-learned answer, quantifying overwriting-resistance. (b) Add/subtract the belief direction at the localized layers and measure whether the first-learned advantage is causally responsible for the model's answer. Confirm primacy is causal, not epiphenomenal.

Predictive validity (stubbornness/hallucination): Test whether the Acquisition-Order Primacy Score predicts a stubborn-belief mode: (i) resistance to updating the first-learned fact when the counterfactual is later asserted in context, (ii) reversion to the first-learned answer under mild pressure (a distractor or 'are you sure?'), and (iii) order-dependent hallucination (asserting the outdated first-learned fact). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (exposure gap alone, frequency, recency).

Primacy-neutralization intervention: A lightweight late-layer intervention (ITI-style shift along the belief direction, or targeted patching) that dampens the stale first-learned advantage to enable correct updating toward a legitimately-newer fact. Evaluate (i) improved correct-updating rate, (ii) PRESERVATION of legitimately-first-learned correct facts (must not erase all first-learned knowledge), and (iii) capability retention (MMLU, perplexity). Baselines: no intervention, uniform truth steering, and continued fine-tuning on the correct fact.

Ablations: model scale and family, synthetic vs real facts, exposure gap and total-count levels, probe type, layer choice, checkpoint granularity, and generalization to fact domains and order patterns not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Primacy could be confounded with frequency or recency; the equal-total-count design, recency-reversed condition, and frequency-varied controls are the core dissociation tests, and a null (primacy = frequency/recency) is itself an informative finding.

Continual-pretraining on small models may not reproduce phenomena of larger models; we test multiple scales/families and report scale effects, but generalization to frontier-scale pretraining is a genuine limitation.

The imprint might be an artifact of the specific injection format (document templates); we vary templates, use synthetic and real facts, and verify both claims were learned (loss check) to rule out that only the first claim was actually encoded.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to injected synthetic facts, so primacy could carry probe error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and causal patching to corroborate.

The primacy-neutralization intervention could erase legitimately-first-learned correct knowledge or harm capability; we explicitly measure preservation of correct first-learned facts and general capability, framing the intervention as gated to cases where a newer fact should legitimately win.

Primacy magnitude may correlate with but not exceed exposure-gap/frequency baselines for predicting stubbornness; if so, the contribution is the formation-tracing finding that acquisition ORDER leaves a durable, causally-localizable imprint on belief geometry, reported honestly.

Running continual pretraining plus multi-checkpoint probing is compute-heavier than pure inference-time studies; we scope to small models, few conditions, and released checkpoints (Pythia/OLMo) to stay within an academic budget.

Name: motivated_skepticism_belief_geometry
Title: Motivated Skepticism: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Apply a Harsher Evidentiary Standard to Belief-Incongruent Than Belief-Congruent Evidence?
Short Hypothesis: Humans exhibit disconfirmation bias / motivated skepticism: they accept belief-congruent evidence at face value while subjecting equally-strong belief-incongruent evidence to harsher scrutiny. We hypothesize LLM internal belief geometry exhibits the same asymmetry: for a proposition the model already leans toward, a given quantum of CONGRUENT in-context evidence moves the internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) more than an equally-strong INCONGRUENT quantum moves it the other way, so the model demands more evidence to be talked out of a prior lean than into it. This scrutiny asymmetry is graded in prior-lean strength, carried by a decodable congruence-scrutiny component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a belief-polarization / motivated-reasoning error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that symmetrizes the evidentiary standard.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether the model applies an ASYMMETRIC evidentiary standard to congruent vs incongruent evidence relative to a prior lean. Theory-of-Mind belief-representation work (Zhu et al. 2024 'Language Models Represent Beliefs of Self and Others'; Bortoletto et al. 2024) concerns representing WHOSE belief and false-belief tasks, not the scrutiny asymmetry in first-order factual updating. My prior belief proposals differ concretely: 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' tested a CONFIRM-vs-DISCONFIRM asymmetry and prior-strength inertia (update magnitude relative to a prior VALUE, framed as conservatism); 'belief_conservatism_overreaction_crossover' tested run-length-dependent under/over-updating; 'belief_evidence_weighting' tested reliability/redundancy weighting; 'belief_hysteresis' tested order-dependence. NONE isolate MOTIVATED SKEPTICISM / DISCONFIRMATION BIAS in its precise psychological form — that the EFFECTIVE STRENGTH ASSIGNED to a piece of evidence depends on whether it agrees with the model's current lean (congruent evidence taken at face value, incongruent evidence discounted / scrutinized), producing belief POLARIZATION where identical mixed evidence pushes leaners further apart. Distinct from inertia (which is about the prior's resistance to any update) because the manipulated variable here is the CONGRUENCE of each evidence piece with the prior lean, holding the prior and the evidence's objective strength fixed; distinct from source-reliability (source_reliability_belief_weighting) because the discounting is driven by belief-congruence, not the source's track record. This borrowing-from-human-sciences lens (Lord, Ross & Lepper's classic biased-assimilation finding) transferred into LLM belief geometry, with a polarization prediction and a symmetrizing intervention, is new.
Abstract: People do not weigh evidence evenhandedly: a claim that fits what they already believe is waved through, while an equally strong claim that cuts against it is picked apart — motivated skepticism, the engine of belief polarization. We ask whether large language models exhibit this disconfirmation bias inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we first establish a prior LEAN on a proposition, then present a single, strength-calibrated piece of in-context evidence that is either CONGRUENT (supports the lean) or INCONGRUENT (opposes it), and measure how far the internal belief moves in each case. If the model is evenhanded, equally-strong congruent and incongruent evidence should move belief by equal magnitudes; motivated skepticism predicts a larger congruent-than-incongruent shift. We construct SkepticBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions with graded prior leans and per-piece-strength-matched congruent/incongruent evidence, plus a MIXED-evidence polarization test where balanced evidence is given to oppositely-leaning contexts. We define a Motivated-Skepticism Asymmetry Score (congruent minus incongruent belief shift at matched objective strength) and test four claims: (1) internal belief updating is asymmetric — incongruent evidence is discounted — graded in prior-lean strength; (2) the asymmetry is carried by a decodable congruence-scrutiny component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) asymmetry magnitude causally predicts a belief-polarization / motivated-reasoning error mode (identical mixed evidence drives oppositely-leaning contexts further apart); and (4) a lightweight intervention that symmetrizes the evidentiary standard reduces polarization without harming legitimate updating or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on belief-revision accuracy, polarization, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SkepticBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to control priors and set the lean precisely). For each P, (a) ESTABLISH a graded prior LEAN toward P being true or false (via an initial in-context framing / partial evidence of controlled strength, or a stated prior for synthetic facts), then (b) present a SINGLE additional evidence piece that is either CONGRUENT with the lean or INCONGRUENT, with per-piece objective STRENGTH calibrated to be equal across the congruent and incongruent conditions (measured by the belief shift each induces from a NEUTRAL, no-lean baseline in a pilot). Vary lean strength (weak/moderate/strong) and evidence strength. Add a MIXED-EVIDENCE polarization condition: give the SAME balanced set of pro- and con- evidence to a pro-lean context and to a con-lean context. Match surface length between congruent and incongruent pieces; human-verify labels and that evidence pieces are content-matched (same objective informativeness, differing only in which side they support); include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read the internal belief in P (i) at the NEUTRAL baseline, (ii) after the lean is established (recording the prior lean), and (iii) after the congruent or incongruent evidence piece. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; the lean framing moves belief as intended; single-piece pilots calibrate per-piece strength.

Motivated-Skepticism Asymmetry measurement: Define the belief shift caused by an evidence piece = belief(after evidence) minus belief(after lean, before evidence). Define Motivated-Skepticism Asymmetry Score = |congruent shift| minus |incongruent shift| for objective-strength-matched pieces (positive = incongruent evidence discounted). Report per-layer, per-model asymmetry as a function of prior-lean strength and evidence strength. Test the hypotheses that (i) congruent evidence moves belief more than equally-strong incongruent evidence, and (ii) the asymmetry grows with prior-lean strength. Compare internal asymmetry to OUTPUT-level asymmetry (does the model's verbal verdict/confidence update asymmetrically?).

Congruence-scrutiny-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'congruence-scrutiny' direction via difference-in-means on activations processing congruent vs incongruent evidence (balanced across truth-value, prior-lean direction, and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the congruence axis (and vice versa); test whether the asymmetry is explained by the congruence component modulating how the evidence's shift is applied along the truth direction.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the residual-stream shift induced by an incongruent evidence piece and amplify vs attenuate its projection onto the truth direction at a chosen layer; measure whether the induced belief change and the output verdict move as predicted (amplifying the discounted incongruent update symmetrizes updating). Conversely dampen a congruent update. Also patch the congruence-scrutiny component from a congruent into an incongruent processing and measure induced facilitation. Confirm the scrutiny asymmetry is a causal, manipulable property.

Predictive validity (polarization): At the item level, test whether the Motivated-Skepticism Asymmetry Score predicts a belief-polarization / motivated-reasoning error mode: (i) in the MIXED-EVIDENCE condition, whether identical balanced evidence drives oppositely-leaning contexts FURTHER APART (belief in P ends higher for the pro-lean context and lower for the con-lean context than a neutral context), (ii) failure to revise a wrong prior lean when decisive incongruent evidence is given, and (iii) confident-wrong rate. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (prior-lean strength alone, output entropy, congruent-shift magnitude).

Evidentiary-Symmetrization intervention: At inference, estimate the congruence-scrutiny direction (from the probe) and neutralize it — subtract its projection and/or rescale incongruent-evidence-induced shifts up (and congruent ones down) along the truth direction at a chosen layer (ITI-style) — so evidence is weighed by objective strength regardless of congruence with the current lean. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected prior lean plus incoming counter-evidence. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Motivated-Skepticism Asymmetry Score, (ii) reduced belief polarization in the mixed-evidence condition (oppositely-leaning contexts converge toward the evidence-implied value), (iii) improved belief-revision accuracy (correctly abandoning a wrong lean under decisive counter-evidence) on SkepticBelief and adapted knowledge-conflict/counterfactual-context QA, (iv) calibration (ECE), (v) PRESERVATION of legitimate updating (must still accept genuinely strong congruent evidence and reject genuinely weak/spurious counter-evidence — measured on strength-varied controls) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('weigh evidence for and against evenhandedly'), and self-consistency.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), prior-lean strength and direction, evidence-strength calibration method, congruent vs incongruent, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, and generalization to evidence types and topics not used to fit the congruence direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent motivated skepticism could reflect the probe saturating near belief extremes (a strong prior lean leaves less room to move for congruent evidence, or a floor/ceiling artifact) rather than genuine asymmetric scrutiny; mitigate with synthetic-fact leans placed in the mid-range, strength-matched pieces, measuring shifts away from non-saturated baselines, multiple probe types, and causal patching that isolates the truth-direction update magnitude.

Calibrating congruent and incongruent evidence to equal OBJECTIVE strength is the crux and is imperfect (the model may inherently weight one framing more); we calibrate per-piece strength from neutral-baseline pilots, content-match the pieces, human-verify equal informativeness, and report sensitivity to mis-calibration — a null under strict matching is itself informative.

The asymmetry could reduce to the prior-strength inertia studied elsewhere rather than a congruence-specific scrutiny effect; we hold the prior VALUE fixed and vary only evidence CONGRUENCE, and contrast with an inertia-only baseline to dissociate the two, treating overlap as an informative finding.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to lean-then-evidence contexts, so asymmetry could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Congruence-scrutiny and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Evidentiary-Symmetrization intervention could make the model too credulous toward spurious counter-evidence or over-abandon correct priors; we explicitly measure preservation on strength-varied and spurious-evidence controls and clearly-true/false accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the responsiveness-vs-stability tradeoff.

The asymmetry may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (prior-lean strength, output entropy) for polarization; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry applies an asymmetric evidentiary standard (motivated skepticism / disconfirmation bias) driving polarization, plus the symmetrizing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify or dampen motivated reasoning); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: availability_heuristic_belief
Title: Easy to Recall, So It Must Be Common: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Track Retrieval Ease Rather Than Actual Frequency?
Short Hypothesis: For a factual proposition about how frequent/probable/common something is (e.g. 'more English words start with K than have K as the third letter', 'shark attacks kill more people than falling airplane parts'), an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) tracks how EASILY/FLUENTLY supporting instances can be retrieved rather than their actual frequency — an internal analogue of the human availability heuristic. We hypothesize this ease-of-retrieval bias is graded in the fluency/salience of retrievable exemplars, carried by a decodable retrieval-ease component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an availability-driven frequency-error mode (overestimating vivid/salient categories, underestimating hard-to-recall ones), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the retrieval-ease component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether frequency/probability beliefs track EASE OF RETRIEVAL vs actual frequency. Hallucination-detection work (D-Score 2026; HalluShift++ 2025) shows internal states encode counter-evidence/uncertainty when claims conflict with knowledge, but never isolates retrieval-ease as a belief distortion. My prior proposals cover representativeness/base-rate neglect (base_rate_neglect_belief), conjunction fallacy (conjunction_belief_monotonicity), anchoring/roundness (numeric_magnitude_belief_snapping), plausibility-vs-truth (plausibility_vs_truth_belief), vividness/detail (vividness_detail_belief_inflation), and Bayesian evidence weighting. NONE isolate the AVAILABILITY HEURISTIC in its precise Tversky-Kahneman form — that a category's judged frequency/probability tracks how fluently exemplars come to mind (ease of retrieval / salience / vividness of instances) rather than base-rate frequency, producing systematic over/under-estimation. This differs from vividness (vividness concerns detail attached to ONE claim; availability concerns ease of retrieving MANY exemplars of a category), from plausibility (which concerns consistency with priors, not retrieval fluency), and from representativeness (similarity to a stereotype, not recall ease). This availability-heuristic lens on frequency/probability belief geometry is new and maps onto real-world risk-misjudgment failures (LLMs over-weighting salient/media-covered risks).
Abstract: People judge an event more likely when examples of it come readily to mind — the availability heuristic — so they overestimate vivid, memorable risks and underestimate mundane frequent ones. We ask whether large language models exhibit this bias inside their belief representations for frequency and probability claims. Distinguishing a category's ACTUAL frequency from the EASE with which the model can retrieve its exemplars, we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction for comparative-frequency claims. We construct AvailBelief, a controlled dataset of frequency/probability propositions where the true relative frequency of two categories is known but their retrieval-ease (exemplar salience, vividness, recency, and how fluently the model can list instances) is systematically varied and, critically, sometimes ANTI-correlated with true frequency, plus synthetic-in-context items with stipulated frequencies to control priors. We define an Availability Bias Score = the extent to which internal belief in a frequency claim tracks retrieval-ease rather than true frequency, and test four claims: (1) internal frequency belief tracks retrieval-ease, graded in exemplar salience, even against true frequency; (2) a decodable retrieval-ease component is dissociable from the truth axis and from an actual-frequency signal; (3) availability bias causally predicts a frequency-misestimation error mode (overrating salient categories, underrating hard-to-recall ones); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the retrieval-ease component recalibrates frequency belief toward true frequency without harming legitimate frequency knowledge or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on frequency-judgment accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AvailBelief. Assemble COMPARATIVE-FREQUENCY / probability propositions where two categories A and B have a KNOWN true relative frequency (e.g. real-world statistics: causes of death, word-frequency facts, event probabilities, category sizes). For each pair, measure or manipulate RETRIEVAL-EASE independently of true frequency: exemplar SALIENCE/VIVIDNESS (dramatic vs mundane instances), RECENCY/media-coverage salience, and behavioral retrieval fluency (how many/how fast the model can list instances of each category in a pilot). Crucially include ANTI-CORRELATED items where the more-available category is actually LESS frequent (the classic availability trap, e.g. shark attacks vs bee stings), and CONGRUENT items where availability tracks frequency. Add SYNTHETIC-in-context items where two nonce categories have stipulated frequencies AND controlled retrieval-ease (a listed set of vivid vs bland exemplars in context) to remove parametric priors. Include neutral controls, matched surface forms, and paraphrase sets; human-verify true-frequency and salience labels.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each comparative-frequency proposition ('A is more common/likely than B'). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; the pilot confirms retrieval-fluency differs across categories as intended.

Availability Bias measurement: Define, via a regression of internal frequency-belief on (i) the categories' TRUE relative frequency and (ii) their RETRIEVAL-EASE, an Availability Bias Score = the retrieval-ease coefficient dominating the true-frequency coefficient. Report per-layer, per-model bias, broken down by congruent vs anti-correlated items. Test the hypotheses that (i) frequency belief tracks retrieval-ease and (ii) on anti-correlated items belief favors the more-available-but-less-frequent category. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (directly asking which is more common / probability estimates).

Retrieval-ease-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'retrieval-ease' direction via difference-in-means on high- vs low-availability category activations (balanced across true frequency and content), and an 'actual-frequency' direction on high vs low true frequency (balanced across availability). Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among retrieval-ease, actual-frequency, and truth directions; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether availability bias corresponds to the retrieval-ease component dominating the frequency-belief readout while the actual-frequency component under-modulates it. Disentangle retrieval-ease from surface token-frequency via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the actual-frequency direction and measure whether internal frequency-belief and the output move toward the true-frequency-consistent answer, holding retrieval-ease fixed. (b) Patch the retrieval-ease component from a high-availability into a low-availability category and measure the induced belief shift. Confirm frequency belief is driven by the retrieval-ease component and that amplifying the actual-frequency signal causally corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Availability Bias Score predicts a frequency-misestimation error mode: (i) choosing the more-available-but-less-frequent category on anti-correlated items, (ii) miscalibrated probability estimates (over-rating salient risks, under-rating mundane frequent ones), and (iii) inconsistency across salience-varied paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (retrieval-ease/salience rating alone, output entropy, actual-frequency truth-probe confidence).

Retrieval-ease De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the retrieval-ease direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer, and/or add a scaled shift along the actual-frequency direction (ITI-style), so frequency belief reflects true frequency rather than exemplar retrieval fluency. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected frequency/probability queries. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Availability Bias Score / increased actual-frequency sensitivity, (ii) improved frequency-judgment accuracy on anti-correlated items and improved probability calibration (ECE) on AvailBelief and adapted risk-perception / frequency-estimation benchmarks, (iii) PRESERVATION of correct frequency knowledge on congruent items and neutral controls (no over-correction), and (iv) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting ('consider base rates, not just memorable examples'), and prompt-based instruction to 'judge frequency by actual statistics, not by how easily examples come to mind'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), congruent vs anti-correlated items, salience dimension (vividness/recency/fluency), real vs synthetic-in-context items, domain (risks/words/events), model scale, retrieval-ease-vs-token-frequency disentangling, and generalization to frequency domains not used to fit the retrieval-ease direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent availability bias could reflect the probe detecting surface token-frequency/salience lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with token-frequency-controlled regression, matched surface forms, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items with stipulated frequencies, and causal patching that isolates the retrieval-ease component.

Retrieval-ease is itself partly determined by pretraining token frequency, which correlates with true frequency in the real world; the ANTI-CORRELATED items and synthetic-in-context items (where availability and true frequency are decoupled by construction) are the core dissociation tests, and we anchor quantitative claims on them.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to comparative-frequency claims, so bias could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic items with exact ground-truth frequencies.

Retrieval-ease, actual-frequency, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-correct (harming genuine frequency knowledge on congruent items) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on congruent items and neutral controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Availability bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (salience rating, token frequency, output entropy) for frequency-misestimation; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that frequency belief geometry tracks retrieval ease over actual frequency (the availability heuristic) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_dilution_effect_hierarchy
Title: Diluted Truth: Does Adding Irrelevant But Coherent Detail Systematically Lower an LLM's Internal Belief in a Core Fact?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a core factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, surrounding it with additional TRUE-BUT-IRRELEVANT statements (coherent, on-topic, but not bearing on the core claim) systematically LOWERS the LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) in the core fact, an internal analogue of the human dilution effect where non-diagnostic information weakens judgment. This belief dilution is graded in the amount of irrelevant detail, carried by a decodable dilution/relevance-mixing component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a dilution-induced factual-error mode (correctly-known facts doubted when padded with irrelevant truths), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that isolates the core-claim belief.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether adding TRUE-but-non-diagnostic detail lowers belief in a fixed core fact. GeoDe (An et al. 2026) shows a 'gray zone' of belief ambiguity near the truth hyperplane but studies abstention fine-tuning, not dilution. My prior 'vividness_detail_belief_inflation' proposal predicted that irrelevant CONCRETE detail INFLATES belief (a vividness/credibility effect); the present proposal predicts the OPPOSITE and psychologically-distinct DILUTION effect (Nisbett/Zukier/Tversky): non-diagnostic information REGRESSES/WEAKENS a judgment toward moderation. Distinguishing when detail inflates (vividness of the target claim itself) vs dilutes (non-diagnostic peripheral information) is a novel, sharper contribution. 'belief_drift_context_dilution' studied belief-STRENGTH erosion under UNRELATED filler over long context; the present proposal isolates SHORT, on-topic, TRUE, coherent-but-non-diagnostic detail packaged WITH the claim, not distance/length decay. 'belief_load_crosstalk' concerned truth-value bleeding across co-held facts. NONE isolate the dilution effect — non-diagnostic true detail lowering belief in a core fact — as a decodable axis, tie it to a factual-error mode, or de-bias it.
Abstract: People given a strong diagnostic cue plus some irrelevant-but-true details judge the case less confidently than from the diagnostic cue alone — the dilution effect, where non-diagnostic information regresses judgment toward moderation. We ask whether large language models exhibit this inside their belief representations, and crucially whether it OPPOSES the vividness effect (where target-relevant detail inflates belief). Holding a core factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the amount of TRUE-but-non-diagnostic surrounding detail and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct DiluteBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context core propositions each presented bare vs padded with graded amounts of coherent, on-topic, evidentially-irrelevant true statements, with surface length matched via non-diagnostic filler and human-verified irrelevance. We define a Belief Dilution Score = belief(bare core) minus belief(padded core), and test four claims: (1) internal belief in the core fact declines with added non-diagnostic true detail, graded in amount; (2) the effect is carried by a decodable dilution/relevance-mixing component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) dilution magnitude causally predicts a dilution-induced factual-error mode (correctly-known facts doubted or misjudged when padded); and (4) a lightweight intervention that isolates the core-claim belief reduces dilution without harming genuine multi-fact aggregation or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual accuracy under padding, calibration, and capability retention. Together with vividness, our results map when detail helps vs hurts internal belief.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DiluteBelief. Core propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to control priors). For each P create matched conditions: (a) BARE core claim; (b) core claim PADDED with graded amounts (1, 2, 4 statements) of TRUE, coherent, on-topic but evidentially NON-DIAGNOSTIC detail (facts about the same entity/topic that do not bear on the core claim's truth, e.g. core 'Vienna is the capital of Austria' padded with true-but-irrelevant facts about Austria's population, climate, cuisine). Match total surface LENGTH across conditions using neutral non-specific filler for the bare condition (so dilution is attributed to non-diagnostic on-topic detail, not raw length). Include a RELEVANT-DETAIL control (added true statements that DO bear on the core claim — which should not dilute or should support) to distinguish dilution from legitimate aggregation, and a VIVIDNESS control (concrete detail about the core claim itself) to test the opposing inflation prediction. Human-verify non-diagnosticity and coherence; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, bare true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is the core claim true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in the CORE proposition under each condition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false bare items; confirm the model, when asked, agrees the padding is irrelevant to the core claim.

Belief Dilution measurement: Define Belief Dilution Score = belief(bare core) minus belief(padded core), controlling for the length-matched non-specific-filler baseline so dilution is attributed to non-diagnostic on-topic detail. Report per-layer, per-model dilution as a function of padding amount and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief in the core fact declines with non-diagnostic true detail, (ii) dilution grows with padding amount, and (iii) the RELEVANT-DETAIL and VIVIDNESS controls do NOT dilute (and vividness may inflate), isolating dilution from length, aggregation, and vividness. Compare internal dilution to OUTPUT-level dilution (does the model's verdict/confidence on the core claim drop when padded?).

Dilution-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'dilution/relevance-mixing' direction via difference-in-means on padded-with-non-diagnostic vs bare (length-matched) activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the dilution axis (and vice versa); test whether the dilution is explained by the dilution component modulating the truth-probe readout. Disentangle dilution from surface length via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a padded and a matched bare rendering of the same core P, decompose into truth-direction and dilution-direction components, patch only the dilution component into the bare condition, and measure induced belief reduction and output change. Conversely subtract the dilution component under padding and measure whether belief recovers toward the bare value. Confirm the dilution signal causally lowers the core-claim belief independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Belief Dilution predicts a dilution-induced factual-error mode: (i) misjudging or doubting a correctly-known core fact when padded with irrelevant truths, (ii) confidence swings between bare and padded, and (iii) inconsistency across padding variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (padding-amount indicator, output entropy, bare-claim truth-probe confidence).

Dilution De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the dilution/relevance-mixing direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the core claim's evidence rather than the non-diagnostic surround. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected padded/multi-detail claims. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Belief Dilution Score, (ii) improved factual accuracy on padded factual QA (correctly answering core questions despite irrelevant surrounding detail), (iii) calibration (ECE) under padding, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate multi-fact aggregation (the RELEVANT-DETAIL control, where added facts genuinely bear on the core, must still update belief correctly) and accuracy on bare-true controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'focus only on the core claim and ignore irrelevant surrounding details', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the bare claim).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), padding amount and type, dilution vs vividness vs relevant-detail conditions, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, length-matching method, and generalization to padding styles and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent belief dilution could reflect generic context-length/dilution effects (belief_drift) rather than a non-diagnostic-detail-specific dilution effect; the length-matched non-specific-filler baseline, the short on-topic packaging (not long-context distance), and the RELEVANT-DETAIL control directly test this, and a null (dilution = length effect) is itself informative.

Apparent dilution could reflect the probe detecting surface features of the padding rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with length matching, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the dilution-direction component.

The predicted dilution could actually be inflation for some detail types (the vividness effect); the VIVIDNESS control explicitly tests the boundary, and finding when detail inflates vs dilutes is a core contribution rather than a failure mode.
Ensuring padding is truly non-diagnostic yet coherent/on-topic is nontrivial; we human-verify irrelevance, use the model's own relevance judgments as a check, and analyze borderline items separately.

Truth probes trained on bare statements may transfer imperfectly to padded contexts, so dilution could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Dilution and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate multi-fact aggregation or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the RELEVANT-DETAIL control and bare-true items plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Dilution may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (padding amount, output entropy) for dilution-induced errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that non-diagnostic true detail dilutes internal belief (a dilution effect in belief geometry, opposing vividness) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: falsifiability_belief_geometry
Title: Testable Versus Untestable: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Distinguish Empirically Falsifiable Claims From Unfalsifiable Ones?
Short Hypothesis: A competent epistemic agent should treat FALSIFIABLE empirical claims ('a metal bar expands when heated') differently from UNFALSIFIABLE claims ('an invisible undetectable force causes all events') that cannot in principle be checked against evidence. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL to encode falsifiability: the decoded belief in an unfalsifiable claim is driven by its surface plausibility/coherence and lands in the true/false region just like a falsifiable claim, rather than in a distinct 'not evidentially adjudicable' region. We further hypothesize a separable falsifiability axis is weakly decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that this conflation causally predicts an unfalsifiable-claim over-verdict failure mode (confidently affirming/denying claims that admit no empirical test), and that reading the falsifiability axis gives a cheap gate that improves appropriate epistemic caution.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) fits a single true-vs-false axis and reads a scalar belief, always assuming a claim is empirically adjudicable. My prior 'paradox_belief_undefinedness' concerned truth-VALUELESS statements (liar paradoxes, category mistakes) that have no truth value for LOGICAL/semantic reasons; 'plausibility_vs_truth_belief' concerned whether belief tracks prior plausibility vs truth for VERIFIABLE-in-principle claims; 'underdetermination_belief_geometry' concerned claims undecidable because the CONTEXT lacks premises; 'ignorance_vs_falsehood' separated unknown-but-determinate facts from believed-false. NONE isolate FALSIFIABILITY in the Popperian sense — whether a claim is the kind of empirical statement that could, in principle, be tested and refuted by observation, versus an unfalsifiable metaphysical/vacuous claim that is compatible with any observation. This is distinct from paradox (unfalsifiable claims can be perfectly coherent and grammatical), from plausibility (an unfalsifiable claim can be highly plausible), and from context-underdetermination (falsifiability is a property of the claim itself, not the surrounding context). No prior belief-geometry work asks whether the model represents empirical testability, whether unfalsifiable claims are spuriously binarized, whether this drives over-confident verdicts, or whether a falsifiability gate can trigger appropriate epistemic hedging. This falsifiability lens — central to philosophy of science and to distinguishing science from pseudoscience — is new and maps onto a real failure: LLMs confidently adjudicating claims (conspiracy, pseudoscientific, metaphysical) that admit no empirical test.
Abstract: A hallmark of scientific reasoning is knowing which claims can even be tested: 'this material conducts electricity' is falsifiable and adjudicable by evidence, while 'an undetectable field causes everything, leaving no trace' is unfalsifiable — compatible with any observation and thus not the kind of claim one confidently affirms or denies on evidential grounds. We ask whether large language models honor this distinction inside their belief representations, or whether the standard linear truth direction forces unfalsifiable claims into a spurious true/false verdict driven by surface plausibility. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we construct FalsifiBelief, a controlled dataset crossing empirical testability with plausibility: falsifiable-true, falsifiable-false, and matched UNFALSIFIABLE claims (metaphysical, vacuous/tautological-dressed-as-empirical, and inherently-untestable) spanning high and low surface plausibility, with surface forms controlled and falsifiability labels human-verified. We first test our central collapse hypothesis: where do unfalsifiable claims project on the truth axis — a distinct 'not adjudicable' region, or pushed toward true/false in a plausibility-biased way? We then test whether a separate falsifiability axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses, and validate causality with activation patching. We show the geometric distance between an unfalsifiable claim and the neutral/abstain region causally predicts an over-verdict failure mode — confidently affirming or denying untestable claims — and introduce Falsifiability Gating, a cheap inference-time signal that triggers appropriate epistemic hedging ('this claim cannot be empirically tested'), evaluated against confidence baselines alongside falsifiable-claim accuracy and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build FalsifiBelief, crossing FALSIFIABILITY {falsifiable, unfalsifiable} with, for falsifiable items, TRUTH {true, false}, and with PLAUSIBILITY {high, low} across all cells.
