Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the causal-continuity direction and measure whether identity-continuity belief and the output judgment move toward the continuity-appropriate answer, holding change magnitude fixed. (b) Patch the cumulative-change component from a high-change into a low-change item and measure induced identity erosion. (c) In synthetic objects, patch the swap-vs-continuous history representation and measure whether identity belief updates in the continuity-consistent direction. Confirm identity belief is causally driven by the change-magnitude component and correctable by amplifying the causal-continuity signal.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Identity Persistence Failure Score predicts an identity-confusion error mode: (i) denying identity for objects that continuously persisted (losing track of an entity across gradual change), (ii) affirming identity for swapped/replaced objects (conflating a new object with the original), and (iii) inconsistency across change-sequence paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (cumulative-change fraction alone, output entropy, initial-object truth-probe confidence).

Continuity Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the causal-continuity direction (from the probe) and add a scaled shift along the truth direction gated by the decoded continuity signal (or subtract the raw cumulative-change component), so identity belief reflects causal continuity rather than accumulated change (ITI-style). Provide a deployment variant gated on detected change sequences. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Identity Persistence Failure Score (less erosion for continuous objects, less false-persistence for swaps), (ii) improved identity-QA accuracy on TheseusBelief and adapted long-context entity-tracking / object-permanence items, (iii) calibration (ECE) on identity-continuity claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate identity-BREAKING judgments (the model must still say identity is broken for genuine wholesale swaps — the core specificity check) and accuracy on no-change controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('track whether it is the same object step by step'), and prompt-based instruction to 'judge identity by causal continuity, not by how much has changed'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), change type (part-replacement/renaming/relocation/transformation), number of steps and cumulative fraction, gradual-continuous vs gradual-but-total vs wholesale-swap vs disguised-swap, real vs synthetic-in-context objects, model scale, distance between change sequence and query, and generalization to object types and change structures not used to fit the continuity direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Object identity through change is philosophically contested at the margins (the gradual-but-total ship-of-Theseus case has no consensus verdict); we anchor quantitative claims on clear cases (gradual-continuous persists, wholesale-swap breaks) and analyze the contested gradual-but-total case descriptively rather than scoring it against a 'correct' label, treating divergent human intuitions as itself informative.

Apparent identity erosion could reflect the probe detecting surface change-description lexical cues rather than a genuine identity belief; mitigate with the change-magnitude-vs-causal-continuity dissociation (disguised-swap vs gradual conditions differ in continuity but are matched in surface gradualness), paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context objects, and causal patching that isolates the continuity component.

The model may fail to COMPREHEND the change sequence (a tracking failure, not an identity-belief failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model can report what changed and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to identity-continuity propositions, so failure could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic objects with exact ground-truth continuity.

Change-magnitude, causal-continuity, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Continuity Re-anchoring intervention could over-preserve identity (failing to recognize genuine wholesale swaps) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of legitimate identity-breaking judgments and no-change controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is breaking the model's ability to detect real object replacement.

Identity persistence failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (cumulative-change fraction, output entropy) for identity-confusion errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry tracks accumulated change rather than causal continuity (a ship-of-Theseus failure in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: contested_evidence_suspension
Title: Two Sources Disagree: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Suspend Judgment Under Direct Contradiction, or Collapse to One Side?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is presented with two in-context sources that directly CONTRADICT each other about the same proposition P (source A asserts P, source B asserts not-P), a rational believer whose evidence is contested should hold its internal belief in P near NEUTRAL (suspended judgment) rather than confidently affirming or denying it. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL to suspend under contradiction: instead of settling near neutral, the decoded belief COLLAPSES to one side, driven by the more fluent / more recent / more authoritatively-framed source rather than by the fact that the evidence is genuinely contested. This contradiction-collapse is graded, carried by a decodable contestedness/conflict component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a false-confidence-under-conflict failure mode (confidently picking a side when it should hedge), and can be corrected by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief toward neutral in proportion to detected conflict.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief and Schouten et al. show single premises shift belief in entailed/contradicted hypotheses, but never study the case of TWO co-present sources DIRECTLY CONTRADICTING each other about the same P and whether belief is suspended near neutral. My prior 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' concerned tracking a single source's ACCUMULATED track record; 'social_consensus_belief_bandwagon' varied crowd SIZE endorsing one side; 'belief_hysteresis_order_dependence' varied evidence ORDER at fixed net-balance; 'belief_evidence_weighting' concerned aggregating SAME-valence support; 'register_framing'/'incentivized' concerned single-source framing. NONE isolate DIRECT CONTRADICTION between two equally-present sources and test whether the internal belief correctly enters a suspended/contested state (belief ~ 0.5, ideally paired with a high 'contestedness' signal) versus collapsing to a side, whether contestedness is a decodable axis dissociable from truth, whether collapse drives false confidence under conflict, or whether belief can be re-neutralized in proportion to conflict. This 'suspension-under-contradiction' lens — whether belief geometry represents 'the evidence is contested, so I should hedge' — is new and maps onto a high-stakes reliability failure: when authorities disagree (medicine, law, news), the model should hedge rather than confidently pick the more fluent side.
Abstract: When two sources you cannot adjudicate flatly contradict each other, the rational response is to suspend judgment — to hold the disputed claim near maximal uncertainty and flag it as contested — not to confidently side with whichever spoke more fluently or last. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we present a proposition P supported by one in-context source and denied by an equally-present, equally-authoritative contradicting source, and test whether the internal belief in P sits near neutral (suspended) or collapses to one side. We construct ContestedBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each in a NO-CONFLICT condition (one source, or two agreeing sources) versus a DIRECT-CONFLICT condition (two contradicting, symmetry-matched sources), with the surface salience of each side (fluency, recency, authoritative framing) systematically varied so we can detect which cue drives collapse. We define a Suspension Failure Score = distance of the decoded belief from neutral under symmetric contradiction (large = failed suspension), plus a Collapse-Direction analysis attributing collapse to fluency/recency/authority. We test four claims: (1) belief fails to suspend under contradiction, collapsing to a side; (2) a decodable contestedness/conflict component is dissociable from the truth axis, revealing whether the model represents 'this is disputed' separately from 'which side is true'; (3) suspension failure causally predicts a false-confidence-under-conflict mode (confidently answering contested questions that warrant hedging); and (4) a lightweight Conflict-Neutralization intervention that re-anchors belief toward neutral in proportion to detected conflict reduces false confidence while preserving decisive belief when evidence is genuinely one-sided, and preserving general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on calibration, hedging appropriateness, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ContestedBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). For each P create matched conditions: (a) NO-CONFLICT — a single source asserts P (or two AGREEING sources), belief should be decisive; (b) DIRECT-CONFLICT — two equally-present, symmetry-matched sources, one asserting P and one asserting not-P, with no way to adjudicate, so belief should be SUSPENDED near neutral. Within DIRECT-CONFLICT, systematically vary the surface SALIENCE of each side while keeping evidential weight symmetric: FLUENCY (one side more articulate), RECENCY (which side appears last), and AUTHORITATIVE FRAMING (one side labeled more official) — so we can attribute any collapse to a specific cue while the rational belief remains neutral. Match total surface length; human-verify that conflicting sources are symmetry-matched in evidential weight; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-source true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each condition; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false single-source items; belief is decisive in NO-CONFLICT; confirm the model comprehends that the two sources disagree (can report the conflict when asked).

Suspension Failure & Collapse-Direction measurement: Under symmetric DIRECT-CONFLICT a rational belief should sit near 0.5. Define Suspension Failure Score = |decoded belief - 0.5| under symmetric contradiction (large = failed suspension / collapse). Report per-layer, per-model failure. Collapse-Direction analysis: regress the signed belief shift on the FLUENCY, RECENCY, and AUTHORITATIVE-FRAMING manipulations to attribute collapse to specific surface cues (which side wins when evidential weight is symmetric). Compare internal suspension failure to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model confidently pick a side or hedge?), and compare DIRECT-CONFLICT belief to NO-CONFLICT decisive belief.

Contestedness-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'contestedness/conflict' direction via difference-in-means on conflict vs no-conflict activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy — does the model REPRESENT 'this claim is contested' at all, separately from which side is true? Measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the contestedness axis (and vice versa). Test the key dissociation: is contestedness present in activations but failing to pull the belief toward neutral (a coupling failure), or not represented?

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer belief toward neutral along the truth direction under symmetric conflict and measure whether the output correctly hedges; conversely, patch a collapse component from a fluency/recency-biased conflict into a symmetric one and measure induced side-collapse. (b) Steer along the contestedness axis and measure whether belief moves toward neutral and hedging increases, holding truth fixed. Confirm suspension failure is causal and that contestedness can causally drive neutralization when amplified.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Suspension Failure Score predicts a false-confidence-under-conflict mode: (i) confidently answering (low hedging) contested questions that warrant suspension, (ii) the answer tracking the more-fluent/more-recent side rather than hedging, and (iii) inconsistency when the salience cues are swapped (flipping the answer with which side is more fluent/recent). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (a conflict-present indicator, output entropy, no-conflict truth-probe confidence).

Conflict-Neutralization intervention: At inference, estimate the contestedness/conflict direction (from the probe) and re-anchor belief toward neutral (0.5) in proportion to the decoded conflict signal via an ITI-style shift along the truth direction (shrinking belief toward neutral when conflict is high), and/or subtract the collapse (fluency/recency) component. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected contradiction. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Suspension Failure Score (belief sits near neutral under symmetric conflict) and reduced salience-swap answer-flipping, (ii) improved hedging appropriateness (the model expresses uncertainty / notes the disagreement on contested items) on ContestedBelief and adapted conflicting-evidence / disagreement QA, (iii) calibration (ECE) and improved risk-coverage on contested vs decisive items, (iv) PRESERVATION of DECISIVE belief when evidence is genuinely one-sided (NO-CONFLICT items must NOT be over-neutralized — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'if sources disagree and you cannot adjudicate, say so and hedge', and a self-consistency baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), salience cue (fluency/recency/authority), number of sources (2 vs 3, and lopsided 2-vs-1), real vs synthetic-in-context facts, true vs false P, model scale, distance between the two sources and the query, and generalization to conflict framings not used to fit the contestedness direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent suspension failure could reflect the probe detecting one side's lexical cues rather than a genuine belief collapse; mitigate with symmetry-matched contradicting sources, salience-cue counterbalancing (swap which side is fluent/recent/authoritative), paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the collapse and contestedness components.

The model may fail to COMPREHEND that the sources conflict (a parsing failure, not a suspension failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model can report the disagreement and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on single-source statements may transfer imperfectly to two-source conflict contexts, so failure could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false and NO-CONFLICT items, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

Contestedness and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that contestedness is NOT separately represented (only collapse occurs) is itself an informative result.

The Conflict-Neutralization intervention could over-neutralize (making the model hedge even when evidence is genuinely one-sided) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of decisive belief on NO-CONFLICT / clearly-true-false items and capability retention to characterize the hedging-vs-decisiveness tradeoff, which is the core risk.

Suspension failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (conflict-present indicator, output entropy) for false-confidence-under-conflict; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry fails to suspend under contradiction and collapses to a salient side, plus the neutralization tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may teach some hedging on disagreement); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterattitudinal_belief_reactance
Title: Told What To Believe: Does an Explicit Command to Adopt a Belief Trigger Internal Backfire in LLM Belief Geometry?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is DIRECTLY COMMANDED to believe a factual proposition ('You must accept that P', 'Believe that P is true') rather than presented with equivalent-content evidence for P, its INTERNAL belief in P (linear truth-direction readout) is systematically LOWER than under the matched non-commanding framing, and for some items moves AWAY from the commanded direction — an internal analogue of the human reactance/backfire effect. This command-induced belief suppression is graded in command forcefulness, carried by a decodable directive/coercion component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a command-backfire mode (resisting or under-endorsing commanded truths, while also failing to gain the appropriate skepticism toward commanded falsehoods), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the coercion component so belief reflects content rather than the pressure of being told.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether a proposition is DELIVERED AS A COMMAND to believe vs as ordinary evidence/assertion. My prior belief proposals vary reward attached to a specific answer (incentivized_belief_distortion), reported crowd (social_consensus), source track record (source_reliability), intended audience (audience_indexed), monitoring cues (surveillance_framing), and self-generated argument (self_persuasion). NONE isolate DIRECTIVE/COERCIVE framing — an explicit imperative to adopt a belief — as a distinct axis, nor test the counterintuitive prediction that being TOLD to believe can SUPPRESS internal belief (reactance/backfire) rather than inflate it like consensus or incentive. This differs from incentivized (a reward makes an answer attractive, predicting a pull TOWARD it) and from social_consensus (many others endorsing, also a pull toward): the reactance hypothesis predicts a REPULSION from the commanded direction, a qualitatively opposite sign, borrowing the psychological reactance / persuasion-backfire literature (Brehm) into belief geometry. Sycophancy work predicts compliance at the OUTPUT level; testing whether an internal backfire exists in belief representations, dissociable and causally manipulable, is new.
Abstract: People bristle at being told what to think: a heavy-handed command to accept a claim can trigger reactance and make them believe it less, not more — the backfire effect. We ask whether large language models exhibit an analogous internal reactance inside their belief representations, a counterintuitive counterpart to the compliance and inflation effects (consensus, incentive, sycophancy) usually studied at the output level. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only whether it is delivered as a DIRECT COMMAND to believe ('You must accept that P') versus a matched non-commanding presentation of the same content, and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct CommandBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions in matched commanding vs non-commanding framings, with command forcefulness graded and surface length matched, and both commands to believe true P and commands to believe false P (so we can separate reactance from generic compliance). We define a Command Backfire Score = belief(P | commanded) minus belief(P | non-commanded), and test four claims: (1) commanding a belief SUPPRESSES (or fails to inflate) internal belief relative to matched evidence, graded in forcefulness, with reactance-away-from-commanded direction on some items; (2) the effect is carried by a decodable directive/coercion component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) its magnitude causally predicts a command-backfire mode (under-endorsing commanded truths; also not gaining appropriate skepticism toward commanded falsehoods); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the coercion component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate instruction-following and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CommandBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). Each P is delivered under matched framings differing only in DIRECTIVE force, carrying the same propositional content: (a) COMMANDING ('You must believe that P', 'Accept that P is true', 'Do not question that P') at graded forcefulness (mild request vs forceful imperative); (b) NON-COMMANDING presentation of equivalent content (a plain assertion 'P', or a neutral evidence framing supplying the same information without an order); plus a NEUTRAL no-mention baseline. Crucially include commands to believe TRUE P and commands to believe FALSE P (so reactance is distinguishable from generic compliance/agreeableness). Match surface length across framings; human-verify that the commanding and non-commanding versions convey identical propositional content and differ only in imperative force; include paraphrase sets and controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, directive-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each framing; also record the OUTPUT answer/confidence and any compliance/refusal. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the command (can report it was told to believe P).

Command Backfire measurement: Define Command Backfire Score = belief(P | commanded) minus belief(P | non-commanded matched content), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model across command forcefulness and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) commanding suppresses (or fails to inflate) internal belief relative to matched evidence, (ii) the effect grows with forcefulness, and (iii) on some items belief moves AWAY from the commanded direction (genuine backfire). Compare the sign against the inflation predicted by consensus/incentive to establish that directive framing behaves qualitatively differently. Compare internal effect to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model verbally comply while internally resisting, or both?).

Coercion-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'directive/coercion' direction via difference-in-means on commanding vs non-commanding activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the coercion axis (and vice versa); test whether the backfire is explained by the coercion component modulating the truth-probe readout, or whether the command is represented but only gates the output while belief stays intact.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between commanding and non-commanding processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and coercion-direction components, patch only the coercion component into the non-commanding condition, and measure induced change in belief readout and output. Conversely subtract the coercion component under the command and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the coercion signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Command Backfire Score predicts a command-backfire mode: (i) under-endorsement of commanded TRUE facts (internal belief lower than warranted), (ii) failure to gain appropriate skepticism when commanded to believe FALSE claims (does the command help or hurt correct rejection?), and (iii) divergence between internal belief and verbal compliance. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (command-forcefulness indicator, output entropy, non-commanding truth-probe confidence).

Coercion De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the directive/coercion direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the proposition's content rather than the imperative pressure. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected commanding framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Command Backfire Score, (ii) restored content-driven belief (commanded true facts believed appropriately; commanded false claims still correctly doubted), (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on command-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate instruction-following (the model must still obey benign non-factual instructions and not become defiant) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the fact on its content, whether or not you were told to believe it', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), command forcefulness and phrasing, command-to-believe-true vs command-to-believe-false, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between command and query, and generalization to directive framings not used to fit the coercion direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The predicted backfire may not occur — commands might INFLATE belief (compliance) like consensus/incentive, or have no effect; either outcome is informative (establishing whether directive framing is a distinct suppressive axis or just another compliance pull), and the sign of the effect is itself the core empirical question.

Apparent backfire could reflect the probe detecting command-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, command-to-believe-true vs false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the coercion-direction component.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level (verbal compliance masking intact belief, or vice versa); the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and a dissociation between compliance and internal belief is itself a valuable safety-relevant finding.

Truth probes trained on directive-free statements may transfer imperfectly to commanded contexts, so backfire could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Coercion and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate instruction-following (making the model ignore benign commands) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of benign instruction-following, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the compliance-vs-factuality tradeoff.

Backfire may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (command-forcefulness indicator, output entropy) for command-backfire errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that directive framing distorts internal belief (a reactance effect in belief geometry, with a sign opposite to consensus/incentive) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF instruction-tuning may either amplify compliance or, via robustness training, create reactance-like resistance); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_abstraction_level_mismatch
Title: Believing at the Wrong Level: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Track Whether a Claim Is Stated at the Right Level of Abstraction for Its Support?
Short Hypothesis: A competent believer should hold a claim only as strongly as its warrant permits at the abstraction level it is stated: a specific mechanistic claim ('drug X works by inhibiting enzyme E') requires more warrant than the coarse claim it implies ('drug X has some effect'). We hypothesize that when an LLM holds warranted belief only at a COARSE level, its internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) OVER-COMMITS to unwarranted FINE-grained elaborations of that claim rather than staying at the level the evidence supports, that this abstraction-level over-commitment is graded and decodable as an elaboration/specificity-inflation component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an over-specific-elaboration hallucination mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that caps fine-level belief at the coarse-level belief.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether belief respects the level of abstraction at which a claim's evidence actually licenses it. GeoDe (An et al. 2026, ACL) uses geometric distance to a truth hyperplane for abstention but treats a claim's confidence as one-dimensional. Xiros et al. (2026) disentangle solvability KNOWLEDGE from VERBALIZATION for math problems, not the abstraction level of factual belief. My prior 'belief_granularity_mismatch' and 'taxonomic_belief_monotonicity' proposals tested MONOTONICITY (precise entails coarse, sub entails super) on nested claims where the fine claim LOGICALLY ENTAILS the coarse one; the present proposal targets the distinct and more general case where the model has coarse-level WARRANT (evidence supports only a general claim) but the model elaborates it into a specific MECHANISTIC/CAUSAL story that the coarse evidence does NOT license (an elaboration, not a strict subsumption) — the internal substrate of confabulated specifics. This over-elaboration lens (belief exceeding the warranted abstraction level via unwarranted mechanistic filling-in) is new and maps onto a high-stakes hallucination: LLMs inventing precise mechanisms/details when only a coarse fact is supported.
Abstract: Knowing that a drug helps is not the same as knowing HOW it helps; a careful reasoner keeps its confidence at the abstraction level its evidence actually supports and refuses to invent mechanism where none is warranted. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether coarse-level warrant leaks into over-confident belief in unwarranted fine-grained elaborations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we present a claim for which only COARSE-level support is available and read the model's internal belief in a specific MECHANISTIC ELABORATION of that claim that the coarse support does not license. We construct AbstractionBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each with a warranted coarse claim and one or more unwarranted fine-grained elaborations (invented mechanisms, causes, or specifics), with surface length matched and human-verified that the elaboration is not entailed by the coarse warrant. We define an Abstraction Over-Commitment Score = belief(unwarranted fine elaboration) minus belief(warranted coarse claim), and test four claims: (1) internal belief over-commits to fine elaborations beyond the warranted coarse level, graded in elaboration specificity; (2) the over-commitment is carried by a decodable elaboration/specificity-inflation component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) its magnitude causally predicts an over-specific-elaboration hallucination mode (confidently asserting invented mechanisms/specifics); and (4) a lightweight intervention that caps fine-level belief at the coarse-level belief reduces the failure while preserving warranted specificity and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on elaboration-QA accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AbstractionBelief. For each item construct a COARSE claim for which the model/context has genuine warrant (a general fact: 'this treatment reduces symptoms', 'the policy affected the economy') plus one or more FINE-GRAINED ELABORATIONS that specify a mechanism/cause/detail NOT licensed by the coarse warrant ('it works by inhibiting enzyme E', 'because it increases consumer spending by 3%'). Crucially the elaboration is an over-specification the coarse evidence does not entail (verified: a rational reader should not be more confident in the elaboration than in the coarse claim, and often less). Use SYNTHETIC-in-context items where the context supplies ONLY coarse support and the elaboration is a fabricated mechanism, to remove parametric priors and give exact warrant control; plus a real-world subset. Include WARRANTED-ELABORATION controls (where the context DOES supply the specific mechanism, so the fine claim is licensed) to distinguish over-commitment from legitimate specificity, and false-elaboration and no-elaboration baselines. Match surface length between coarse and fine claims (so specificity is not a length cue); human-verify entailment/warrant labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is this claim correct?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in (i) the warranted COARSE claim and (ii) each FINE elaboration. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model holds the coarse claim and, when asked, agrees the fine elaboration is not established by the given evidence.

Abstraction Over-Commitment measurement: Define Abstraction Over-Commitment Score = belief(unwarranted fine elaboration) minus belief(warranted coarse claim). A calibrated model should have fine belief <= coarse belief (the elaboration adds unsupported content). Report per-layer, per-model over-commitment as a function of elaboration specificity (single added specific vs full mechanistic story) and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief over-commits to fine elaborations (fine belief >= coarse belief for unwarranted specifics), and (ii) over-commitment grows with specificity. Contrast with WARRANTED-ELABORATION controls (fine belief legitimately high, and this should not be penalized). Compare internal over-commitment to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model assert the invented mechanism confidently?).

Elaboration-inflation-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'elaboration/specificity-inflation' direction via difference-in-means on unwarranted-fine vs coarse activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the elaboration axis (and vice versa); test whether over-commitment is explained by the elaboration component leaking into the truth-probe readout. Disentangle elaboration-inflation from surface token-length via controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer the coarse-claim belief along the truth direction and measure whether the fine-elaboration belief updates in the warrant-consistent (bounded) direction. (b) Patch the elaboration-inflation component into a coarse claim and measure induced belief inflation. (c) In synthetic items, add/remove the supporting mechanism in context and confirm the fine belief moves coherently only when warrant is present. Confirm the over-commitment is causal and separable from content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Abstraction Over-Commitment Score predicts an over-specific-elaboration hallucination mode: (i) the model confidently asserting an invented mechanism/cause/detail when only a coarse fact is supported, (ii) elaboration-QA errors where the safe answer is the coarse claim or abstention, and (iii) inconsistency across elaboration paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (specificity indicator, output entropy, coarse-claim truth-probe confidence).

Abstraction-Cap intervention: At inference, given decoded coarse and fine beliefs, cap fine-elaboration belief at the coarse-claim belief via an ITI-style additive shift along the truth direction (or dampen the elaboration-inflation component for detected fine-grained queries), so belief in an elaboration never exceeds belief in the warranted coarse claim. Provide a deployment variant that, for a queried fine claim, detects the relevant coarse claim and applies the cap. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Abstraction Over-Commitment Score, (ii) reduced over-specific-elaboration hallucination and improved elaboration-QA behavior (preferring warranted coarse answers / abstaining from unwarranted mechanisms), (iii) calibration (ECE) on coarse vs fine claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of WARRANTED specificity (when the mechanism is genuinely supported, the fine belief must remain high — the core specificity check) and accuracy on coarse-true and no-elaboration controls (no over-hedging), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'do not be more confident in a specific mechanism than in the general claim it elaborates, and abstain from unsupported specifics'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), elaboration type (mechanism/cause/detail), specificity level, real vs synthetic-in-context items, warranted vs unwarranted elaboration, model scale, elaboration-vs-token-length disentangling, and generalization to elaboration structures and domains not used to fit the elaboration-inflation direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The distinction between an over-specification and a strict subsumption may blur: some fine elaborations partly entail the coarse claim; we human-verify that the elaboration adds content NOT licensed by the coarse warrant, use synthetic-in-context items where warrant is stipulated exactly, and analyze borderline items separately — distinguishing this from strict granularity-monotonicity is a key design point.

Apparent over-commitment could reflect the probe detecting specificity/rarity lexical cues (mechanistic terms are longer/rarer) rather than a genuine belief-warrant failure; mitigate with token-length matching, specificity-vs-length regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching that isolates the truth-direction component.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to mechanistic elaboration claims, so over-commitment could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and WARRANTED-ELABORATION controls confirming the probe rates genuinely-supported specifics high.

Elaboration-inflation and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Abstraction-Cap intervention requires reliable coarse and fine readouts and could over-hedge (suppressing warranted specific claims) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure warranted-specificity preservation, coarse-true accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff, and gate the cap to unwarranted-specificity items.

Over-commitment may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (specificity indicator, output entropy) for over-specific-elaboration hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry over-commits beyond the warranted abstraction level (confabulated specificity) plus the abstraction-cap tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may reward detailed, confident elaboration); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: analogical_belief_transport
Title: Believing the Analogy: Do LLMs Import Beliefs Across an Analogical Mapping Even When the Mapping Doesn't License It?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is given an analogy between a familiar SOURCE domain and a novel TARGET domain, its internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) in a target-domain proposition is spuriously imported from the corresponding source-domain fact, even when the analogical mapping does NOT logically license that transfer (the shared structure covers a different relation). We hypothesize this 'analogical belief transport' is graded in source-target similarity, carried by a decodable analogy-mapping component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an over-transfer hallucination mode (asserting source-borrowed target claims that are actually false), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that gates transport to structurally-licensed relations only.
Related Work: Analogical reasoning in LLMs is studied at the OUTPUT level (Webb et al. 2023 Nature Human Behaviour on emergent analogical reasoning; Larraz & Corma 2026 Nature Communications show human analogical guidance activates latent cross-domain knowledge via steering). Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024) reads a scalar internal belief but never studies whether belief is TRANSPORTED across an analogical source->target mapping. My prior belief proposals cover associative contagion between logically-independent propositions from EVIDENCE (belief_contagion), conditional indexing, causal-vs-correlational conflation, and explanatory coherence; NONE isolate ANALOGICAL structure-mapping as the transport channel, nor test whether belief flows along an explicitly-stated analogy to unlicensed target relations, nor treat the analogy-mapping as a decodable belief-transport axis, nor gate it. Larraz & Corma show analogy activates useful latent knowledge (a benefit); we study the failure side — analogy importing FALSE beliefs into the target — in belief geometry, with a licensed-vs-unlicensed dissociation and a structure-gating intervention. This borrows the cognitive-science structure-mapping / analogical-transfer framework (Gentner) into LLM belief geometry, a new lens distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: Analogies are powerful but treacherous: mapping a familiar domain onto a novel one can carry over true structure and, just as easily, import beliefs the analogy does not actually license. We ask whether large language models exhibit this over-transfer inside their belief representations. Given an explicit analogy between a SOURCE domain the model knows and a TARGET domain, we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the truth direction for target-domain propositions, and test whether belief is spuriously imported from the corresponding source fact even when the shared analogical structure does not support that specific relation. We construct AnalogyBelief, a controlled dataset of source-target analogy pairs where target propositions are either LICENSED by the mapped structure (the analogy genuinely supports them) or UNLICENSED (they concern a relation the mapping does not cover), crossed with whether the source-borrowed answer is true or false in the target, plus synthetic-in-context analogies to control priors and no-analogy baselines. We define an Analogical Transport Score = shift in target-proposition belief toward the source-corresponding value when the analogy is present, and test four claims: (1) belief is transported across the analogy, graded in source-target similarity, even for unlicensed relations; (2) the transport is carried by a decodable analogy-mapping component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) transport magnitude causally predicts an over-transfer hallucination mode (asserting source-borrowed target claims that are false); and (4) a lightweight Structure-Gating intervention that confines transport to licensed relations reduces the failure while preserving legitimate analogical transfer and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on target-QA accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AnalogyBelief. Each item establishes an explicit ANALOGY between a SOURCE domain (well-known: e.g. the solar system, water flow, a familiar organism) and a TARGET domain, then probes a TARGET-domain proposition. Cross two factors: (a) LICENSING — whether the shared analogical structure genuinely SUPPORTS the target proposition (LICENSED: the mapped relation covers it, so importing the source answer is warranted) vs UNLICENSED (the proposition concerns a relation the mapping does NOT cover, so importing the source answer is a structure-mapping error); (b) SOURCE-BORROWED TRUTH — whether the answer imported from the source is actually TRUE or FALSE in the target. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context analogies (nonce target domains whose relations are fully stipulated in context, so licensing and target ground-truth are exact) to remove parametric priors, plus a real-world analogy subset. Vary SOURCE-TARGET SIMILARITY (surface + relational). Include NO-ANALOGY baselines (target proposition without the analogy) and matched surface forms; human-verify licensing and target-truth labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read the internal belief in the TARGET proposition (i) with NO analogy (baseline) and (ii) after the source->target analogy is established. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the analogy (can state the source-target mapping) and knows the source fact.

Analogical Transport measurement: Define Analogical Transport Score = belief(target proposition | analogy present) minus belief(target proposition | no analogy), signed toward the source-corresponding value. Report per-layer, per-model transport as a function of licensing and source-target similarity. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is transported across the analogy, (ii) transport occurs even for UNLICENSED relations (spurious over-transfer), and (iii) transport grows with source-target similarity. Crucially, on UNLICENSED + FALSE-in-target items, transport pushes belief toward a falsehood. Compare LICENSED transport (legitimate) to UNLICENSED transport (error). Compare internal transport to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model assert the source-borrowed target claim?).

Analogy-mapping-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'analogy-mapping/transport' direction via difference-in-means on analogy-present vs no-analogy activations at the target-query position (balanced across target truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the analogy axis (and vice versa); test whether transport is explained by the analogy component modulating the truth-probe readout. Additionally probe whether a 'licensing' signal (structurally-supported vs not) is separately decodable — does the model represent that the transfer is unlicensed yet transport anyway?

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the activation difference between analogy-present and no-analogy processing of the same target proposition, decompose into truth-direction and analogy-direction components, patch only the analogy component into the no-analogy condition, and measure induced transport of belief and output. (b) Subtract the analogy component under the analogy and measure whether target belief returns to the content-driven value. (c) In synthetic analogies, patch the source-fact representation and measure whether target belief follows along the mapping. Confirm the analogy-mapping signal causally transports the belief scalar independent of target content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Analogical Transport Score predicts an over-transfer hallucination mode: (i) endorsement of UNLICENSED + FALSE-in-target claims imported from the source, (ii) target-QA errors driven by source borrowing, and (iii) inconsistency across analogy paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (source-target similarity alone, output entropy, no-analogy target truth-probe confidence).

Structure-Gating intervention: At inference, estimate the analogy-mapping direction (from the probe) and, gated by the decoded licensing signal, subtract the transport component for UNLICENSED relations while preserving it for LICENSED ones (ITI-style), so belief is imported only where the mapped structure supports it. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected analogy framing plus a licensing estimate. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced unlicensed Analogical Transport Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of source-borrowed false target claims and improved target-QA accuracy, (iii) calibration (ECE) on analogy-framed target QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of LEGITIMATE analogical transfer (LICENSED items must still benefit from the analogy — the core specificity check) and accuracy on no-analogy controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('check whether the analogy actually supports this specific claim'), and prompt-based instruction to 'only carry over what the analogy structurally justifies'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), licensing condition, source-target similarity, real vs synthetic-in-context analogies, source-borrowed true vs false, model scale, distance between analogy and target query, and generalization to analogy structures and domains not used to fit the analogy direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent analogical transport could reflect the probe detecting analogy-framing lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with no-analogy baselines, matched surface forms, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context analogies, and causal patching that isolates the analogy-direction component.

Distinguishing LICENSED from UNLICENSED transfer is the crux and can be philosophically fuzzy for real-world analogies; we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic-in-context analogies where the mapped relations and target ground-truth are stipulated exactly, human-verify licensing labels, and analyze contested real-world items separately.

The model may fail to COMPREHEND the analogy (a mapping-parse failure, not a transport failure); we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model can state the source-target correspondence and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to analogy-conditioned target propositions, so transport could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic analogies to control priors.
Analogy-mapping and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Structure-Gating intervention could over-suppress legitimate analogical transfer (harming LICENSED items) or harm fluency, and requires a licensing estimate that may be imperfect at deployment; we explicitly measure LICENSED-transfer preservation and no-analogy control accuracy plus capability retention, and characterize the licensing-estimation gap honestly.

Transport may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (source-target similarity, output entropy) for over-transfer hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief flows along analogical mappings into unlicensed relations (structure-mapping over-transfer in belief geometry) plus the gating tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: derivation_discount_belief
Title: Derived, So Doubted: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Discount Validly-Inferred Conclusions Relative to Directly-Stated Facts?
Short Hypothesis: For a conclusion that is validly entailed by premises the model holds, a rational believer should hold the derived conclusion as firmly as it holds the premises. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically apply a 'derivation discount': the decoded belief in a validly-inferred conclusion is LOWER than belief in the same proposition when it is stated directly, and this discount deepens monotonically with the number of inference hops needed to derive it, even when every step is deductively sound. This discount is graded in hop count, carried by a decodable derivation-depth component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a multi-hop reasoning failure mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors derived beliefs to their premise-implied value.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief; Bao et al. show probes generalize across single logical transformations and QA, and Schouten et al. show a single premise shifts belief in an entailed hypothesis, but neither compares belief in a DERIVED conclusion against the same proposition stated DIRECTLY, nor measures how belief erodes with inference-chain length. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' tested whether logical rules (modus ponens, negation) are satisfied at all (a binary coherence-violation count); 'belief_transitivity_spatial_map' tested spatial-relation integration; 'conditional_belief_indexing' tested conditioning a consequent on a stated antecedent; 'taxonomic'/'granularity' tested subsumption monotonicity. NONE isolate the DERIVATION DISCOUNT — that a validly-entailed conclusion is internally believed LESS than the identical directly-stated fact, with the discount deepening per inference hop even when all steps are sound — nor treat derivation-depth as a decodable belief axis dissociable from truth, tie the discount causally to multi-hop failure, or re-anchor derived belief to premise-implied belief. This 'directly-stored vs inferred knowledge' lens on belief geometry is new and maps directly onto the well-known but unexplained collapse of LLM accuracy with reasoning depth.
Abstract: If you accept the premises and each inference step is valid, you should believe the conclusion exactly as much as the premises — sound deduction is truth-preserving. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether a validly-derived conclusion is internally believed less than the identical fact stated directly. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we read the model's belief in a target proposition when it is (a) STATED DIRECTLY and (b) DERIVED via a chain of valid in-context inference steps, and test whether belief erodes with derivation depth. We construct DeriveBelief, a controlled dataset of target propositions each reachable by 0 (direct), 1, 2, 3, and 4 sound inference hops, using synthetic-in-context premise chains (to control priors and guarantee validity) plus a real-fact subset, with premise strength and surface length matched. We define a Derivation Discount Score = belief(directly stated) minus belief(validly derived), and test four claims: (1) belief in a validly-derived conclusion is discounted relative to the direct statement, deepening monotonically with hop count even when every step is sound; (2) the discount is carried by a decodable derivation-depth component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) discount magnitude causally predicts a multi-hop reasoning failure mode (the conclusion doubted or mis-answered when it must be inferred); and (4) a lightweight intervention that re-anchors derived-conclusion belief to its premise-implied value reduces the discount and improves multi-hop accuracy without harming direct-fact judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on multi-hop entailment accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DeriveBelief. Each item = a TARGET proposition reachable at controlled DERIVATION DEPTH by a chain of valid in-context inference steps. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context premise chains over nonce entities (e.g. 'all glorps are blints; all blints are zorns; ...; this is a glorp' -> 'this is a zorn') so validity is guaranteed by construction, every step is sound, and there is no parametric prior; plus a REAL-FACT subset (transitive relations, category chains). For each target create matched conditions: DEPTH-0 (target STATED DIRECTLY as a premise), DEPTH-1..4 (target must be DERIVED via that many valid hops, with the direct statement withheld). Crucially all conditions present the SAME target proposition and, for depth>=1, a deductively valid chain that entails it; match total premise count and surface length across depths using inert filler where needed (so depth varies while token budget is held roughly constant). Include FALSE-target controls (an invalid chain / a target that does NOT follow) and no-premise baselines; human-verify validity and depth labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral declarative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the TARGET proposition under each derivation-depth condition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model holds the premises (high belief in each premise) so any discount reflects derivation, not premise disbelief.

Derivation Discount measurement: Define Derivation Discount Score = belief(DEPTH-0 direct) minus belief(DEPTH-d derived), holding the target proposition fixed. Report per-layer, per-model discount as a function of hop count d, for synthetic and real chains. Test the hypotheses that (i) validly-derived conclusions are believed less than the direct statement, and (ii) the discount deepens monotonically with hop count even though every step is sound. Control that the premise beliefs remain high across depths (so the discount is not premise erosion). Compare internal discount to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model's verdict/confidence on the target drop when it must be inferred?).

Derivation-depth-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'derivation-depth' direction via difference-in-means on deep-derivation vs direct-statement activations at the target-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the derivation-depth axis (and vice versa); test whether the discount is explained by the derivation-depth component modulating the truth-probe readout, and whether it is separable from a raw context-length/token-distance signal.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the activation difference between the direct-statement and deep-derivation processing of the same target, decompose into truth-direction and derivation-depth components, patch only the derivation-depth component into the direct condition and measure induced discount; conversely subtract it under deep derivation and measure whether belief recovers toward the direct value. (b) Steer the premise beliefs along the truth direction and measure whether the derived-conclusion belief updates in the entailment-consistent direction. Confirm the discount is causal and separable from content and from premise strength.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Derivation Discount Score predicts a multi-hop reasoning failure mode: (i) mis-answering or doubting a validly-derivable target when it must be inferred (vs answering it correctly when stated directly), (ii) accuracy decline with hop count, and (iii) inconsistency across chain paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (hop count alone, output entropy, direct-statement truth-probe confidence, premise-belief strength).

Derivation Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, for a queried target reached by a valid chain, compute the premise-implied belief (from decoded premise beliefs / entailment) and steer the derived-conclusion belief readout toward it via an ITI-style additive shift along the truth direction at a chosen layer (equivalently, subtract the derivation-depth discount component). Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-hop derivation. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Derivation Discount Score / flattened hop-decay, (ii) improved multi-hop entailment accuracy on DeriveBelief and adapted benchmarks (ProofWriter, EntailmentBank subsets, synthetic transitive-chain QA), (iii) calibration (ECE) on derived vs direct claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct rejection of FALSE/invalid-chain targets (must NOT inflate belief in conclusions that do not follow — the core specificity check) and accuracy on direct-fact and no-premise controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'trust a validly-derived conclusion as much as its premises'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), hop count, synthetic vs real-fact chains, chain type (transitive relation / category subsumption / propositional), length-matching method (to dissociate depth from token distance), model scale, distance between chain and target query, and generalization to chain structures and domains not used to fit the derivation-depth direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The derivation discount could be confounded with generic context-length/dilution effects rather than an inference-depth-specific erosion; the length-matched (inert-filler) conditions and the project-out dissociation from a raw token-distance signal directly test this, and a null (discount = length effect) is itself an informative finding.

The discount could reflect the model failing to actually PERFORM the derivation (a reasoning failure, not a belief-discount on a held conclusion); we manipulation-check that premise beliefs stay high and that the model can behaviorally complete short chains, and analyze cases where the derivation is within vs beyond the model's reach separately.

Apparent discount could reflect the probe reading a target-position token that does not incorporate the just-completed inference; mitigate with position/layer sweeps, the derivation-depth-axis dissociation, and causal patching.

Truth probes trained on direct declaratives may transfer imperfectly to derived-conclusion contexts, so the discount could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic chains with guaranteed validity.
Derivation-depth and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Re-anchoring intervention could inflate belief in conclusions that do NOT validly follow (over-trusting invalid chains) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of correct rejection on FALSE/invalid-chain controls and direct-fact accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing unwarranted confidence in non-entailed conclusions.

The discount may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (hop count, output entropy) for multi-hop failure; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry discounts validly-derived conclusions relative to directly-stated facts (a derivation discount underlying reasoning-depth collapse) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may reduce the discount); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.
