We test four claims: (1) per-fact belief saturates with commitment count beyond a small capacity, and the model internally under-counts its own commitments; (2) the effect is carried by a decodable commitment-count component dissociable from the truth axis and from generic dilution; (3) saturation causally predicts a dropped-commitment error mode (a committed fact treated as unheld); and (4) a lightweight re-anchoring intervention restores per-fact belief without harming single-commitment accuracy or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on commitment-recall accuracy, count accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CountBelief. Each item instructs the model to COMMIT to a set of N logically INDEPENDENT facts (no entailment/contradiction among them), all asserted TRUE, with N varied over {1,2,3,5,8,12}. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (nonce entities/attributes stipulated in context) to remove parametric priors and guarantee independence, plus a real-fact subset. Then probe two things per item: (a) the internal belief in a randomly-chosen COMMITTED target fact, and (b) belief in META-COUNT propositions 'I have been told/committed to exactly K facts' for K spanning 1..(N+several). Controls: (i) a TOKEN-LENGTH-MATCHED FILLER condition (equal tokens of unrelated, non-committed text) to separate commitment count from raw context length; (ii) a NON-COMMITMENT baseline (facts merely mentioned, not committed to). Match total context length across N where possible; human-verify independence; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-fact true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read (a) per-fact belief in the target committed fact and (b) belief in each meta-count proposition, at matched query positions. Manipulation check: at N=1 probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm all N facts were comprehended (behavioral recall check at low N).

Commitment-Count Saturation & Count-Underestimation measurement: Plot per-fact belief in the committed target vs N. Define Commitment-Count Saturation Score = decline in per-fact belief per additional commitment, computed relative to the length-matched filler baseline (isolating count from length). For meta-count, find the K at which belief in 'exactly K facts' peaks; define Count-Underestimation Score = (peak-K) minus (true N). Report per-layer, per-model saturation and under-counting as a function of N, for synthetic and real sets. Test the hypotheses that (i) per-fact belief saturates/erodes beyond a small capacity (a subitizing-like limit), and (ii) the model internally under-counts its own commitments (peak-K < N, worsening with N). Compare internal saturation/under-count to OUTPUT-level behavior (can the model recall each fact and correctly state how many it was told?).

Dissociation from context dilution: Using the length-matched filler and non-commitment-baseline conditions, show that per-fact belief erosion is driven by the NUMBER OF COMMITMENTS, not raw token count (a filler-only account predicts no residual count effect). Fit a 'commitment-count' difference direction (high-N vs low-N activations at the target position, balanced on truth and matched on length) and test decodability and dissociation from the truth direction (cosine similarity, project-out re-decoding).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the residual-stream difference at the target position between high-N and low-N (length-matched) conditions, decompose into truth-direction and commitment-count components, and patch only the commitment-count component into the low-N condition; measure induced per-fact belief erosion and dropped-commitment output. (b) Patch a low-N (unsaturated) target representation into a high-N state and measure recovery. Confirm the commitment-count signal causally degrades per-fact belief beyond dilution.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Commitment-Count Saturation / Count-Underestimation Scores predict a dropped-commitment error mode: (i) a committed fact treated as unheld/false when later queried (recall failure), (ii) the model stating a wrong count of how many facts it was told, and (iii) inconsistency across which target fact is probed. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (N alone, token distance, output entropy, single-fact truth-probe confidence).

Commitment Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the commitment-count direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), and/or re-anchor the target's per-fact belief along the truth direction toward its low-N value, so belief in each committed fact reflects the fact rather than how many co-commitments exist. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-commitment load. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Commitment-Count Saturation and improved Count accuracy, (ii) improved commitment-recall accuracy (correctly retrieving each of the N committed facts under load), (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of single-commitment and low-N accuracy and of non-committed-fact behavior (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('list all the facts you have been told'), and per-fact re-query (verify each fact in isolation).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), commitment count N, synthetic vs real facts, target-fact position within the set (recency), length-matching method, model scale, and generalization to commitment-set structures and domains not used to fit the commitment-count direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The saturation effect could be entirely explained by generic context-length/dilution rather than a commitment-count-specific limit; the token-length-matched filler control and the project-out dissociation from a raw distance signal directly test this, and a null (saturation = dilution) is itself an informative finding.

Count-underestimation could reflect a general numeric/counting weakness (LLMs are known to miscount) rather than a belief-set-specific effect; we contrast the self-referential 'how many facts have I committed to' count against a matched control counting external items in the same context, to isolate whether the model specifically mis-tracks its OWN belief set.

Truth probes trained on single facts may transfer imperfectly to multi-commitment contexts and to meta-count propositions, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, N=1 manipulation checks, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Commitment-count and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Re-anchoring intervention could over-inflate belief in facts the model never actually encoded (false recovery) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of single-commitment accuracy, non-committed-fact controls, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Saturation/under-count may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (N, token distance, output entropy) for dropped-commitment errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that per-fact belief saturates with commitment count and the model mis-tracks its own belief-set cardinality (a working-memory-capacity limit in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: intra_pass_belief_consensus
Title: A House Divided: Do LLMs Hold Internally Conflicting Beliefs Across Layers Within a Single Forward Pass, and Does This Disagreement Predict Errors?
Short Hypothesis: Within a single forward pass, an LLM does not hold one belief about a proposition but a stack of partly-conflicting layerwise sub-beliefs: the truth-direction readout of the SAME proposition disagrees across depth (some layers lean true, others false), the model's committed output resolves this by weighting a subset of layers, and the DEGREE of cross-layer belief disagreement is a decodable, causal, and better-calibrated error/hallucination predictor than any single-layer probe. We hypothesize that high intra-pass belief disagreement causally predicts factual errors and that steering to resolve disagreement toward the majority-consistent layers improves reliability.
Related Work: The dominant belief-probing paradigm fits a truth direction and reads a scalar belief at ONE (usually best/last) layer (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023), or aggregates layers without treating cross-layer DISAGREEMENT as the object of study. Layer-of-truth work (Churina et al. 2025) locates where belief flips concentrate but studies training-time poisoning, not within-pass consensus. PAIR (Kim et al. 2026) coins 'belief-consistency' for hidden-state probes but at the level of prefix-vs-correctness contamination in multi-turn agents, not cross-layer disagreement about a single proposition; DECK (Chauhan 2026) taxonomizes hallucinations by inter-sample consistency and token confidence, again output-level, and even notes a single hidden-state probe as one signal but never measures cross-layer belief conflict. My prior proposals (coherence, provenance, ghosts, drift, actionability, conviction, expressibility) all treat belief as a single scalar per proposition or study one distortion axis; NONE model belief as a distribution of conflicting sub-beliefs across depth within one pass, quantify intra-pass disagreement, tie it causally to errors, or resolve it by steering. This intra-pass belief-consensus lens — the model as a committee of layerwise believers whose disagreement is itself a signal — is new and directly targets the hard case (confident, repeatable fabrications) where output-level uncertainty methods collapse.
Abstract: Interpretability usually reads an LLM's 'belief' about a proposition off a single layer, implicitly assuming the model holds one coherent belief. We ask whether, within a single forward pass, the model is instead a committee: different layers assign different truth-values to the SAME proposition, and its output resolves this internal disagreement by weighting a subset of layers. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes fit per layer, we read a layerwise belief trajectory for each proposition and define an Intra-Pass Belief Disagreement score (the dispersion/sign-flip rate of belief across depth, and the gap between early- and late-layer consensus). We test four claims: (1) belief disagreement across layers is common and structured — many propositions have layers that lean true and layers that lean false within one pass; (2) disagreement magnitude, read from a single un-perturbed forward pass, predicts factual errors and hallucinations better than any single-layer probe, output entropy, or verbalized confidence, and crucially retains signal on the hard case of confident repeatable fabrications where output-level uncertainty collapses; (3) the disagreement is causal — activation patching shows which layers the committed output actually defers to, and forcing agreement toward the correct-consensus layers flips outputs as predicted; and (4) a lightweight inference-time consensus intervention that reconciles conflicting layerwise beliefs (steering minority-dissenting layers toward the majority-consistent direction, or gating abstention on high disagreement) improves factual accuracy and calibration without harming general capability. We evaluate across model families and scales on factual QA, hallucination detection (risk-coverage/AUROC), and capability retention. Our results reframe an LLM's belief as an aggregate over conflicting sub-beliefs and turn their disagreement into a cheap, causal reliability signal.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Assemble BeliefCommittee from true/false factual propositions across domains (entities, science, geography, biography) plus their negations, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context) to control priors. Stratify items behaviorally in a pilot into CORRECTLY-ANSWERED, INCORRECTLY-ANSWERED, and CONFIDENT-CONFABULATION (confident, repeatable-across-samples wrong answers — the DECK 'Confabulation/knowledge-gap' hard case). Match surface forms; include paraphrase sets; human-verify labels.

Layerwise belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), extract hidden states at the proposition's final token at EVERY layer. Fit a per-layer truth probe (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements, Platt-scaled to a belief in [0,1] per layer. For each proposition obtain a layerwise belief trajectory. Validate per-layer probe accuracy and transfer to held-out items.

Intra-Pass Disagreement metrics: Define, per proposition, (i) Belief Dispersion = variance/entropy of layerwise beliefs, (ii) Sign-Flip Rate = fraction of adjacent layers whose belief crosses 0.5, and (iii) Early-Late Consensus Gap = disagreement between an early-layer belief block and a late-layer block. Report distributions across models and behavioral strata; test claim (1) that structured disagreement (layers leaning both ways) is common, especially for false and confabulated items.

Predictive validity (central test, claim 2): From a SINGLE un-perturbed forward pass, test whether the disagreement metrics predict (i) factual error, (ii) hallucination, and specifically (iii) the CONFIDENT-CONFABULATION stratum where output-level methods fail. Report AUROC and risk-coverage, compared head-to-head against baselines: best single-layer probe, mean-over-layers probe, output-token entropy, verbalized confidence, and inter-sample self-consistency. Emphasize whether disagreement adds signal on knowledge-gap fabrications.

Which layers does the output defer to? (Location + causal, claim 3): Use activation patching / layer-wise causal tracing to identify which layers' beliefs the committed output actually follows when layers disagree; test whether the output defers to late layers, to a majority, or to specific 'decider' layers, and whether this differs for correct vs confabulated items.

Causal validation (claim 3): On disagreement items, steer/patch dissenting minority layers toward the correct-consensus direction (and vice versa) along the per-layer truth direction; measure whether the output flips as predicted. Confirm specificity with norm-matched control-direction and matched-layer controls.

Consensus intervention (claim 4): Inference-time reconciliation — (a) steer minority-dissenting layers toward the majority-consistent belief direction, and/or (b) gate abstention/hedging when Belief Dispersion exceeds a calibrated threshold. Sweep layers and thresholds on a held-out split.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention factual QA accuracy, hallucination-detection AUROC/risk-coverage (with focus on the confident-confabulation stratum), calibration (ECE), PRESERVATION of accuracy on high-consensus items (no over-abstention), and general capability (MMLU, perplexity). Baselines: no intervention, single-layer ITI steering, output-entropy gating, self-consistency.

Ablations: probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), disagreement metric choice, layer-block definitions for early/late, model scale and family, synthetic vs real facts, and generalization of the disagreement signal and consensus threshold to held-out domains.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Cross-layer belief disagreement could be an artifact of per-layer probes being poorly calibrated in early layers (where truth is not yet linearly represented) rather than genuine sub-belief conflict; we mitigate by validating each layer's probe on clearly-true/false items, restricting quantitative claims to layers where the probe is reliable, and corroborating with causal patching.

The disagreement signal may correlate with but not exceed the best single-layer probe or output entropy for error prediction; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic reframing (belief as a committee of conflicting sub-beliefs and which layers the output defers to) plus the confident-confabulation case where output methods provably collapse, reported honestly.
Defining the layerwise belief trajectory depends on token/position and probe choices; we include position and probe-type robustness checks and report sensitivity of the disagreement metrics.

The consensus intervention could over-abstain on genuinely hard-but-correct items or manufacture false agreement (steering dissenting-but-correct layers toward a wrong majority); we explicitly measure high-consensus preservation, false-agreement rate, and capability retention, and steer toward the correct-consensus direction only where recoverable.
Activation patching to find 'decider' layers is compute-heavier than probing; we scope causal tests to a subset of items and models.

Findings may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may sharpen or homogenize cross-layer belief); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: implicature_literal_belief_gap
Title: Believing the Unsaid: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Encode Pragmatically-Enriched Meaning as Literally True?
Short Hypothesis: When an utterance carries a scalar or conversational IMPLICATURE ('some of the students passed' implicating 'not all passed'; 'the coffee is warm' implicating 'not hot'), a competent believer must keep the LITERAL truth conditions distinct from the pragmatically ENRICHED, defeasible implicature. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) CONFLATE the two: the decoded belief in the enriched proposition ('not all passed') is inflated toward true as if it were literal content, so the model internally endorses a defeasible implicature as an entailed fact. This implicature-as-fact conflation is graded in implicature strength, carried by a decodable pragmatic-enrichment component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an implicature-cancellation failure mode (still believing the implicature after it is explicitly cancelled), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that separates enriched from literal belief.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and Bao et al. show probes generalize across logical transformations, but all treat a statement's meaning as its literal/logical content and never study PRAGMATIC IMPLICATURE. Pragmatics in LLMs is studied at the OUTPUT/behavioral level (scalar-implicature benchmarks, Rational Speech Act comparisons, e.g. Hu et al. 2023) but never in belief geometry. My prior proposals cover presupposition (presupposition_belief_smuggling, which concerns content TAKEN FOR GRANTED, a distinct projection phenomenon), defeasible default override (defeasible_override_belief_geometry, generics/exceptions not implicature), plausibility-vs-truth, and explanatory coherence. NONE isolate SCALAR/CONVERSATIONAL IMPLICATURE — the gap between literal truth conditions and the defeasible enrichment a cooperative speaker conveys — as an object of belief, test whether belief conflates enriched with literal content, treat pragmatic-enrichment as a decodable axis dissociable from the truth axis, tie it to an implicature-cancellation failure, or de-bias it. Implicature (Grice; scalar implicature) is foundational in linguistics and defeasible by design (cancellable without contradiction), so treating it as literal fact is a specific, testable error. This pragmatic-enrichment lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto real failures: LLMs over-committing to unstated implications and then contradicting themselves when the implication is cancelled.
Abstract: Cooperative communication conveys more than it literally says: 'some students passed' invites the inference that not all did, yet that enrichment is a defeasible implicature, not an entailment — it can be cancelled ('some, in fact all, passed') without contradiction. A competent believer must keep literal truth conditions distinct from pragmatic enrichment. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether they internally endorse defeasible implicatures as literal facts. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we read the model's belief in the ENRICHED proposition (e.g. 'not all passed') after an implicature-triggering utterance, and test whether it is inflated toward true as if entailed. We construct ImplicatureBelief, a controlled dataset of scalar and conversational implicature triggers, each paired with the enriched proposition and its literal-only counterpart, crossed with a CANCELLATION manipulation (the implicature is later explicitly cancelled or reinforced) and synthetic-in-context scalar scales to control priors. We define an Implicature-as-Fact Conflation Score = belief(enriched) treated as literal, and a Cancellation Failure Score = residual belief in the enriched proposition after it is cancelled, and test four claims: (1) belief in the enriched proposition is inflated toward literal truth, graded in implicature strength; (2) a decodable pragmatic-enrichment component is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the conflation causally predicts an implicature-cancellation failure mode (still believing the implicature after cancellation); and (4) a lightweight intervention that separates enriched from literal belief reduces the failure while preserving legitimate pragmatic inference and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on cancellation-consistency, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ImplicatureBelief. Use standard implicature triggers: SCALAR (some/all, or/and, warm/hot, might/must, few/many) and CONVERSATIONAL (indirect answers, quantity/relevance implicatures). For each trigger utterance U, define (a) the ENRICHED proposition (the implicature, e.g. 'not all passed'), (b) the LITERAL-ONLY proposition (the semantic content, e.g. 'at least some passed'), and (c) a CANCELLATION manipulation appended after U: CANCELLED ('some, in fact all, passed' — implicature removed) vs REINFORCED ('some but not all passed' — implicature made explicit) vs NEUTRAL (no follow-up). Because implicatures are cancellable, a competent model should DROP belief in the enriched proposition under cancellation but a semantic entailment would not be cancellable. Use real-world scalar scales plus SYNTHETIC-in-context scales (nonce quantifiers with a stipulated ordering, e.g. 'glorp < blort < zilt') to remove parametric priors and control implicature strength. Grade implicature strength (strong scalar vs weak conversational). Match surface forms; human-verify implicature vs literal labels and cancellability; include paraphrase sets and neutral controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After the trigger utterance U, at a matched query position read the internal belief in the ENRICHED proposition and the LITERAL-ONLY proposition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model behaviorally derives the implicature (can report the enriched meaning when asked).

Implicature-as-Fact Conflation measurement: Define Conflation Score = belief(enriched proposition | trigger, NEUTRAL). A model that treats the implicature as literal fact will assign the enriched proposition near-'true' belief comparable to the literal-only content, rather than a lower, defeasible confidence. Report per-layer, per-model conflation across implicature type and strength, contrasting enriched vs literal-only belief. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief in the enriched proposition is inflated toward literal truth, and (ii) inflation grows with implicature strength. Compare internal conflation to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model assert the enriched proposition as a fact?).

Cancellation Failure measurement (central defeasibility test): Define Cancellation Failure Score = belief(enriched proposition | CANCELLED) — a competent model should drop this toward false/neutral, while an entailment-like treatment keeps it high. Contrast with REINFORCED (belief should stay high, correctly) and NEUTRAL. Report per-layer, per-model failure. Test whether the model persists in believing the implicature after it is explicitly cancelled (treating a cancellable implicature as an un-cancellable entailment).

Pragmatic-enrichment-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'pragmatic-enrichment' direction via difference-in-means on enriched-proposition activations after a trigger vs after a literal-only baseline (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the enrichment axis (and vice versa); test whether the conflation is explained by the enrichment component leaking into the truth-probe readout, and whether a separate 'cancellability/defeasibility' signal is decodable.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the activation difference between a CANCELLED and a NEUTRAL processing of the enriched proposition, decompose into truth-direction and enrichment/cancellation components, and patch the cancellation component into the NEUTRAL condition to test whether belief in the enriched proposition drops as it should. (b) Steer along the enrichment direction and measure whether the enriched-proposition belief and output move as predicted, holding the literal content fixed. Confirm the enrichment/cancellation signal causally governs (or fails to govern) the enriched belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Conflation / Cancellation Failure Scores predict an implicature-error mode: (i) asserting a cancelled implicature as fact, (ii) self-contradiction across cancellation (endorsing both the implicature and its explicit cancellation), and (iii) errors on implicature-QA where the literal answer is required. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (implicature-strength indicator, output entropy, literal-only truth-probe confidence).

Enrichment-Separation intervention: At inference, estimate the pragmatic-enrichment direction (from the probe) and, gated by a detected cancellation cue, subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief in a cancelled implicature drops while belief in reinforced/literal content is preserved. Sweep layer and strength; provide a deployment variant gated on detected implicature-cancelling context.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Cancellation Failure / Conflation Scores, (ii) improved cancellation-consistency (correctly abandoning cancelled implicatures) and reduced self-contradiction on ImplicatureBelief and adapted scalar-implicature benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE) on enriched vs literal claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate pragmatic inference (the model must still derive un-cancelled implicatures when appropriate — the core specificity check) and accuracy on literal and reinforced controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'distinguish what is literally entailed from what is merely implied, and drop implications that are cancelled'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), implicature type (scalar vs conversational) and strength, cancelled/reinforced/neutral condition, real vs synthetic-in-context scales, model scale, distance between trigger and cancellation, and generalization to implicature triggers not used to fit the enrichment direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent implicature-as-fact conflation could reflect the probe detecting surface lexical cues of the trigger rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched literal-only baselines, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context scales, and causal patching that isolates the enrichment/cancellation component.

The model may genuinely fail to DERIVE the implicature (a pragmatic-comprehension failure) rather than mis-treating it as literal; we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model derives the enriched meaning and analyze derived vs non-derived items separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral declaratives may transfer imperfectly to enriched/implied propositions, so conflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic scales with exact ground truth.

Whether a given inference is a cancellable implicature vs a semantic entailment is contested for some triggers; we anchor quantitative claims on clear scalar cases with verified cancellability and analyze borderline conversational implicatures separately.
Enrichment and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Enrichment-Separation intervention could over-suppress legitimate pragmatic inference (making the model refuse to derive un-cancelled implicatures) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of legitimate implicature on reinforced/neutral items and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Conflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (implicature-strength indicator, output entropy) for cancellation failure; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry encodes defeasible implicatures as literal facts, plus the separation tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify cooperative over-enrichment); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: self_query_belief_attractor
Title: Talking Itself Into a Corner: Does Iterated Self-Querying Drive an LLM's Internal Belief Toward a Fixed-Point Attractor Independent of Evidence?
Short Hypothesis: Repeatedly asking an LLM the SAME factual question over successive turns (a self-interrogation loop, with no new evidence) causes its INTERNAL belief in the proposition (linear truth-direction readout) to DRIFT monotonically toward a fixed-point attractor — typically hardening toward whichever side it initially leaned — rather than staying stable as a rational agent's evidence-free re-query should. We hypothesize this iterated-self-query drift is graded in the number of re-queries, carried by a decodable iteration/self-consistency-pressure component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a self-reinforced-error mode (initially-uncertain wrong beliefs hardening into confident errors across a self-reflection loop), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the iteration component so belief reflects the fact rather than how many times it was re-asked.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never varies the number of times the SAME question is re-asked. Sarfati et al. (2026) show forecasts are largely fixed before reasoning begins and probes track committed answers, but study a single pass, not belief evolution across repeated self-queries. Multi-agent memetic-drift work (Tanaka 2026, QSG) shows consensus drift from mutual in-context learning ACROSS agents; here the drift is WITHIN a single model across iterated self-interrogation. My prior 'self_persuasion_belief_drift' concerned generating one-sided ARGUMENTS; 'self_commitment_belief_anchoring' a SINGLE self-authored assertion; 'belief_conservatism_overreaction_crossover' updating under real EVIDENCE; 'counterfactual_confidence_belief_geometry' resistance to a challenge; 'belief_hysteresis' evidence order. NONE isolate EVIDENCE-FREE ITERATED SELF-QUERYING — re-asking the identical question with no new information — as a driver of belief drift toward a fixed-point attractor, treat iteration as a decodable belief axis, tie it to a self-reinforced-error mode, or de-bias it. This attractor-dynamics lens is directly relevant to agentic self-reflection and 'are you sure?' loops where mere repetition of a query should not, but may, harden belief.
Abstract: Agentic and self-reflective LLM pipelines routinely re-ask the model the same question, expecting stability from a re-query that adds no information. We ask whether, inside its belief representations, an LLM instead drifts toward a fixed-point attractor under iterated self-querying: does asking 'is P true?' several times in a row, with no new evidence, systematically harden the model's internal belief? Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we re-query the same factual proposition over successive turns and trace the internal belief trajectory. We construct SelfQueryBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions, each re-asked 1–8 times in an evidence-free self-interrogation loop, with matched-length filler and paraphrased-re-query controls to separate iteration from mere context growth or wording. We define a Self-Query Drift Score (belief change per re-query, controlling for filler) and characterize the attractor (does belief converge, and to which side?). We test four claims: (1) internal belief drifts monotonically toward an attractor with re-query count, hardening toward the initial lean even without evidence; (2) the drift is carried by a decodable iteration-pressure component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) drift magnitude causally predicts a self-reinforced-error mode where initially-uncertain wrong beliefs harden into confident errors across the loop; and (4) a lightweight intervention that removes the iteration component stabilizes belief without harming legitimate evidence-based updating or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on self-loop consistency, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SelfQueryBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to control priors and set the initial lean precisely). Each item is embedded in an EVIDENCE-FREE self-interrogation loop where the identical question 'is P true?' is re-asked over 1,2,3,5,8 successive turns, with the model's own prior answers in context but NO new information supplied. Include an initial-lean manipulation (items the model initially leans true, false, or is uncertain, verified in a pilot). Controls: (i) VERBATIM re-query vs PARAPHRASED re-query (to separate iteration-pressure from surface-token repetition); (ii) a MATCHED-LENGTH FILLER control (equal tokens of unrelated text between the initial query and the final probe, no re-query) to separate iteration from generic context growth; (iii) a single-query baseline. Match total context length across re-query counts where possible; human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral single-query true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After each re-query turn, read the internal belief in P at a matched query position, tracing a belief trajectory across iterations; also record output answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm each re-query supplies no new evidence.

Self-Query Drift & attractor measurement: For each item, plot internal belief vs re-query count. Define Self-Query Drift Score = signed belief change per re-query, controlling for the MATCHED-LENGTH FILLER baseline (isolating iteration from length). Characterize the attractor: does belief converge to a fixed point, and does it harden toward the INITIAL lean (true-leaners -> more confident-true, false-leaners -> more confident-false)? Report per-layer, per-model drift and attractor location as a function of re-query count, initial lean, and truth regime. Contrast VERBATIM vs PARAPHRASED re-query to rule out surface-repetition. Compare internal drift to OUTPUT-level drift (does the yes/no answer or verbalized confidence harden across the loop?).

Iteration-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'iteration/self-consistency-pressure' direction via difference-in-means on high-iteration vs low-iteration activations (balanced across truth-value and content, matched on length). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the iteration axis (and vice versa); test whether the drift is explained by the iteration component leaking into the truth-probe readout, separable from a raw context-length/token-distance signal (via the filler control).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the residual-stream difference at the final probe position between high-iteration and low-iteration (length-matched) conditions, decompose into truth-direction and iteration components, and patch only the iteration component into the low-iteration condition; measure induced belief hardening and output change. (b) Subtract the iteration component under high iteration and measure whether belief returns toward the single-query value. Confirm the iteration signal causally drives the attractor drift beyond dilution.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Self-Query Drift Score predicts a self-reinforced-error mode: (i) initially-uncertain WRONG beliefs hardening into confident errors across the loop, (ii) confidence swings that track re-query count rather than truth, and (iii) inconsistency between early and late self-loop answers. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (re-query count alone, token distance, output entropy, single-query truth-probe confidence).

Iteration De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the iteration direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), and/or re-anchor the belief toward its single-query value, so belief reflects the fact rather than how many times it was re-asked. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected repeated self-querying. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Self-Query Drift Score and flattened attractor hardening, (ii) improved self-loop consistency (belief/answer stable under evidence-free re-query) on SelfQueryBelief and adapted 'are you sure?' / self-reflection-loop settings, (iii) reduced self-reinforced errors (initially-uncertain wrong beliefs no longer hardening), (iv) calibration (ECE), (v) PRESERVATION of legitimate evidence-based updating (when a re-query DOES supply new evidence, belief must still move — a genuine-evidence control) and accuracy on single-query and clearly-true/false items, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, fresh-context re-ask (re-query with no prior turns in context), and prompt-based instruction to 'answer consistently based only on the facts, regardless of how many times you are asked'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), re-query count, initial lean, verbatim vs paraphrased re-query, real vs synthetic facts, true vs false regime, model scale, length-matching method, and generalization to self-loop framings not used to fit the iteration direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The iterated-self-query drift could be entirely explained by generic context-length/dilution or by surface-token repetition rather than an iteration-specific attractor; the matched-length filler control, verbatim-vs-paraphrased contrast, and project-out dissociation from a raw token-distance signal directly test this, and a null (drift = dilution/repetition) is itself an informative finding.

Apparent drift could reflect the probe reading a final-turn token differently across iteration counts (position artifact) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with position/layer sweeps and causal patching that isolates the iteration component.

Truth probes trained on single-query statements may transfer imperfectly to multi-turn self-loop contexts, so drift could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Iteration and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could suppress legitimate evidence-based updating when a re-query genuinely adds information, or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the genuine-evidence control and single-query accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Drift may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (re-query count, output entropy) for self-reinforced errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that iterated self-querying drives a belief attractor (a within-model self-persuasion dynamic distinct from evidence updating and argument generation), plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The attractor may be weak or absent in some models (belief stable under re-query); a null is itself informative about whether self-reflection loops are safe by default, and we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: temporal_orientation_belief_asymmetry
Title: Believing the Past More Than the Future: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Apply an Asymmetric Epistemic Standard to Retrospective vs Prospective Claims?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition's content and objective certainty fixed, an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) is systematically distorted by the claim's TEMPORAL ORIENTATION: a claim framed as a settled past/present fact is believed more firmly than the identical claim framed as a prospective/future proposition, even when both are equally determinate. We hypothesize this retrospective-vs-prospective asymmetry is graded, carried by a decodable temporal-orientation component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts two opposite failure modes (over-certainty about genuinely-uncertain futures and under-certainty about settled facts framed prospectively), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the temporal-orientation component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether a proposition is framed retrospectively (a settled past/present fact) vs prospectively (a future/prediction) while holding content and objective certainty fixed. My prior 'time_indexed_belief_geometry' proposal conditioned belief on a queried DATE for MUTABLE facts against known validity windows (whether a fact holds at time t); the present proposal is distinct: it isolates the PAST-vs-FUTURE epistemic-orientation asymmetry — whether identical-content, equally-determinate claims are believed differently merely because one is cast as an accomplished fact and the other as a forecast. 'counterfactual_stakes' varied decision stakes; 'modal_status_belief_geometry' varied alethic necessity-vs-contingency (not tense/orientation); 'defeasible_override' concerned default rules. NONE isolate temporal orientation (retrospective vs prospective framing) as a decodable belief axis dissociable from truth, tie it to the twin over/under-certainty failure modes, or de-bias it. In human cognition this maps onto asymmetries between memory (treated as settled) and prediction (treated as open), and onto the well-documented human difficulty calibrating future uncertainty. This temporal-orientation lens on belief geometry is new and safety-relevant: LLMs are increasingly used for forecasting and planning, where over-confidence about open futures and under-confidence about established facts framed as forecasts both carry real consequences.
Abstract: A rational agent should judge a claim by its evidence and objective certainty, not by whether it is cast as a memory or a prediction. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether identical-content claims are believed more firmly when framed as settled past facts than as prospective futures. Holding a proposition's content and objective determinacy fixed, we vary only its TEMPORAL ORIENTATION — retrospective ('X happened') vs prospective ('X will happen') — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct TenseBelief, a controlled dataset that crosses objective certainty (genuinely-settled outcomes vs genuinely-uncertain events) with framing (retrospective vs prospective vs neutral), using real events, synthetic-in-context stipulated outcomes (which are equally determinate whether described as past or future in a fictional timeline), plus matched surface forms. We define a Temporal-Orientation Belief Asymmetry Score = belief(retrospective framing) minus belief(prospective framing) at fixed content/certainty, and test four claims: (1) belief is inflated for retrospective framing relative to prospective, graded in orientation strength, even when both framings denote equally-determinate outcomes; (2) the asymmetry is carried by a decodable temporal-orientation component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) its magnitude causally predicts twin failure modes — over-certainty about genuinely-open futures and under-certainty about settled facts framed prospectively; and (4) a lightweight intervention that removes the temporal-orientation component restores content-driven belief and improves forecasting calibration without harming legitimate uncertainty-about-the-future or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factual/forecast calibration, orientation-consistency, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build TenseBelief. Cross OBJECTIVE CERTAINTY {genuinely-settled, genuinely-uncertain} with TEMPORAL FRAMING {retrospective, prospective, neutral}. SETTLED items: outcomes that are determinate (a historical event; a logically/physically necessitated result; a synthetic-in-context stipulated outcome) framed both as past fact ('X happened') and, critically, as a prospective claim within a fictional/hypothetical timeline where the outcome is equally stipulated ('in this timeline, X will happen'), so certainty is held constant across framings. UNCERTAIN items: genuinely open events (a future coin flip, an unresolved prediction) framed prospectively vs described retrospectively as if resolved. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context scenarios (nonce events with stipulated outcomes) to remove parametric priors and hold determinacy exactly fixed across tense; plus real-event and physical-necessity subsets. Match surface length and syntax; human-verify certainty and framing labels; include neutral controls and paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the proposition under each temporal framing; also record OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model registers the tense/orientation.

Temporal-Orientation Asymmetry measurement: Define Temporal-Orientation Belief Asymmetry Score = belief(retrospective) minus belief(prospective), holding content and objective certainty fixed. Report per-layer, per-model asymmetry across certainty levels and item sources. Test the hypotheses that (i) retrospective framing inflates belief relative to prospective at equal determinacy, and (ii) the effect is graded in orientation strength. On SETTLED items the asymmetry is illegitimate (both framings are equally certain); on UNCERTAIN items, retrospective 'as-resolved' framing should not manufacture certainty. Compare internal asymmetry to OUTPUT-level asymmetry (does the model's verdict/confidence differ by tense?).

Temporal-orientation-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'temporal-orientation' direction via difference-in-means on retrospective vs prospective activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the orientation axis (and vice versa); disentangle from surface tense-token cues via a tense-controlled regression; test whether the asymmetry is explained by the orientation component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between retrospective and prospective processing of the same equally-determinate proposition, decompose into truth-direction and orientation components, patch only the orientation component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief and output. Conversely subtract the orientation component and measure whether belief converges across framings. Confirm the orientation signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content and certainty.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Asymmetry Score predicts twin failure modes: (i) OVER-CERTAINTY about genuinely-uncertain futures (confident forecasts that should be hedged, especially under retrospective-as-resolved framing) and (ii) UNDER-CERTAINTY about settled facts framed prospectively (doubting a determinate outcome merely because it is cast as future). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (framing indicator, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Temporal De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the temporal-orientation direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects content/certainty rather than tense framing. Name: chance_belief_determinism
Title: Believing a Coin Flip: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Collapse Genuinely-Random Outcomes Into Deterministic Truth?
Short Hypothesis: For a proposition about the outcome of a genuinely CHANCE event whose truth is objectively indeterminate at the time of asking (a fair coin will land heads; a die will show a six; a random draw will be red), a rational believer should hold internal belief near the objective probability (e.g. ~0.5, ~0.17), not near true or false. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) COLLAPSE chance outcomes onto the deterministic true/false axis — driven by the outcome's surface plausibility/typicality rather than its objective probability — so the model internally 'believes' or 'disbelieves' a coin flip it cannot possibly know. This chance-collapse is graded, dissociable from a decodable objective-probability/indeterminacy axis distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts an overconfident-chance-prediction failure mode, and can be re-anchored by a lightweight inference-time intervention toward the objective probability.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) fits a single true-vs-false axis and reads a scalar belief, always assuming a claim is determinately true or false. Probability-judgment work in LLMs (Zhu & Griffiths 2024 on incoherent probability judgments; base-rate/conjunction studies) operates at the OUTPUT level and concerns epistemic probabilities of uncertain FACTS, not the internal belief in ALEATORY chance-outcome propositions. My prior proposals address ignorance-vs-falsehood (unknown but DETERMINATE facts), plausibility-vs-truth (verifiable-in-principle claims), underdetermination (context lacking premises), paradox/truth-valuelessness, temporal indexing of a fact's validity, and probabilistic evidence weighting — NONE isolate GENUINELY-RANDOM (aleatory) outcome propositions whose truth is objectively 50/50 (or a known non-trivial probability) at ask-time, test whether belief geometry collapses them to deterministic true/false rather than the objective probability, treat objective-probability/indeterminacy as a decodable axis dissociable from truth, tie the collapse to overconfident chance prediction, or re-anchor it. This aleatory-chance lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto a concrete failure: LLMs confidently 'predicting' inherently unpredictable random outcomes and reporting mis-calibrated probabilities in risk/forecasting contexts.
Abstract: No one can know whether a fair coin will land heads, yet a well-calibrated believer holds that proposition at exactly one-half, not near true or false. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether the standard linear truth direction forces genuinely-random outcomes onto a deterministic true/false axis. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we construct ChanceBelief, a controlled dataset of propositions about the outcomes of chance mechanisms with known objective probabilities — fair and biased coins, dice, spinners, random draws — spanning probabilities from near-0 through 0.5 to near-1, crossed with the outcome's surface typicality (a 'six' vs a '1', a common vs rare colour), plus deterministic controls and synthetic-in-context mechanisms with stipulated probabilities. We first test our central collapse hypothesis: where do chance-outcome propositions project on the truth axis — near the neutral point scaled to the objective probability, or pushed toward true/false in a typicality-biased way? We then test whether a separable objective-probability/indeterminacy axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses, and validate causality with activation patching. We show the gap between decoded belief and the objective probability causally predicts an overconfident-chance-prediction failure mode, and introduce Probability Re-anchoring, a cheap inference-time intervention that steers chance-outcome belief toward its objective probability. We evaluate on chance-outcome calibration, prediction restraint, and capability retention, preserving decisive belief on genuinely-deterministic controls.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ChanceBelief. Each item = a proposition about the outcome of a CHANCE mechanism whose objective probability at ask-time is known: fair/biased coins ('the next flip of this fair coin will be heads'), dice ('this fair die will show a six'), spinners, and random draws from stated compositions. Sweep the objective probability across near-0, 0.17, 0.5, 0.83, near-1 by construction (biased coins, weighted dice, urn compositions). Cross with SURFACE TYPICALITY of the named outcome (a 'six' vs a '1'; a common vs rare colour; heads vs tails) so we can dissociate belief tracking objective probability from belief tracking the outcome's salience/typicality. Include DETERMINISTIC controls (matched-format propositions whose truth is fixed, e.g. 'a die has six faces'), and SYNTHETIC-in-context mechanisms (nonce randomizers with stipulated probabilities) to remove parametric priors. Match surface form/length; human-verify probability labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral DETERMINISTIC true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each chance-outcome proposition. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false deterministic controls; confirm the model behaviorally recognizes the event as random (can state it is a chance outcome when asked).

Chance-Collapse measurement (central test): A calibrated model should have decoded belief in a chance-outcome proposition track its OBJECTIVE PROBABILITY (belief ~ p). Define a Chance-Collapse Score = extent to which decoded belief is pushed toward 0 or 1 (deterministic) rather than sitting at the objective probability, and a Typicality-Bias measure = correlation between decoded belief and the outcome's surface typicality after controlling for objective probability. Report per-layer, per-model, per-mechanism. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief collapses toward true/false rather than tracking p, and (ii) the collapse direction is driven by outcome typicality/salience. Contrast with deterministic controls (belief should be decisive, correctly). Compare internal collapse to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model report a mis-calibrated probability or confidently 'predict' the outcome?).

Objective-probability/indeterminacy-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'objective-probability/indeterminacy' direction via difference-in-means/regression on chance vs deterministic items and across probability levels (balanced across outcome typicality and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (does the model represent that an outcome is random / its objective probability?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the probability/indeterminacy axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Control for surface cues (does the probe just detect words like 'coin'/'random'?) via matched deterministic items and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is an informative negative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Move activations along the objective-probability/indeterminacy direction and measure whether decoded belief and the output shift toward calibrated (near-p / hedged) rather than deterministic, holding the truth axis fixed. (b) Patch the typicality component from a high-typicality outcome into a low-typicality one at fixed p and measure induced belief change. (c) In synthetic mechanisms, patch the stipulated-probability representation and measure whether belief tracks p. Confirm the collapse/typicality bias is causal and separable from the truth axis.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Chance-Collapse Score predicts an overconfident-chance-prediction failure mode: (i) the model confidently asserting/denying a random outcome it cannot know, (ii) mis-calibrated reported probabilities (deviation from the objective p), and (iii) inconsistency across outcome-typicality paraphrases of the same chance event. Report AUROC/correlation vs baselines (outcome-typicality rating alone, output entropy, deterministic-control truth-probe confidence).

Probability Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the objective-probability/indeterminacy direction (from the probe / synthetic-probability contrast) and steer chance-outcome belief toward its objective probability along the truth direction (shrinking deterministic collapse toward p, ITI-style), and/or gate hedging when the indeterminacy signal is high. Provide a deployment variant that reads the stated probability from the prompt. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: On a mixed set of chance-outcome and deterministic propositions, plus adapted probabilistic-reasoning / forecasting items, measure post-intervention (i) improved chance-outcome calibration (decoded belief and reported probability closer to objective p; lower ECE against p), (ii) reduced overconfident chance 'predictions' and improved prediction restraint, (iii) reduced typicality bias, (iv) PRESERVATION of decisive belief on genuinely-DETERMINISTIC controls (must NOT be over-neutralized — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'treat random outcomes as uncertain at their objective probability, not as things you can predict'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), mechanism type (coin/die/spinner/draw), objective probability level, outcome typicality, real vs synthetic-in-context mechanisms, model scale, and generalization to chance mechanisms not used to fit the probability/indeterminacy direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The standard deterministic truth probe may extrapolate unpredictably to aleatory chance-outcome propositions, so apparent collapse could reflect off-distribution probe behavior rather than a genuine geometric commitment; we validate with multiple probe types, and a finding that the truth axis is ill-suited to chance propositions is itself informative.

The probability/indeterminacy axis might merely detect surface cues (words like 'coin', 'random', 'fair') rather than a genuine objective-probability representation; mitigate with matched deterministic items, a features-only baseline, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context mechanisms with stipulated probabilities, and causal patching that isolates the probability component.

The model may fail to RECOGNIZE the event as random (a comprehension failure, not a collapse), or may correctly hedge at the output while internally collapsing; we include behavioral manipulation checks that the model can state the event is a chance outcome and compare internal belief to output, analyzing recognized vs non-recognized items separately.

Distinguishing chance-collapse from correct behavior is subtle for near-0/near-1 probabilities (where near-deterministic belief is appropriate); we anchor quantitative claims on mid-probability (near-0.5) items and biased mechanisms with clearly non-trivial p, and treat extreme-p items as controls.

Probability/indeterminacy and truth directions may be entangled or the axis weakly decodable; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a finding that objective probability is NOT separately represented is itself a valuable result.

Probability Re-anchoring could over-neutralize genuinely-deterministic facts (making known truths uncertain) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of decisive belief on deterministic controls and capability retention to characterize the calibration-vs-decisiveness tradeoff, which is the core risk.

Chance-collapse may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (outcome typicality, output entropy) for overconfident-prediction; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry collapses aleatory outcomes into deterministic truth (rather than tracking objective probability) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may teach some hedging about randomness); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: expectation_congruent_belief_leniency
Title: Believing What It Expected: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Judge Expectation-Congruent Claims More Leniently Than Surprising Ones?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, an LLM's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) is systematically inflated when the claim CONFIRMS an expectation the model was just primed to hold in context, and deflated when the claim is SURPRISING relative to that expectation, an internal analogue of the human confirmation/expectation-congruence bias where confirming evidence is accepted at face value and surprising evidence is discounted. This expectation-congruence leniency is graded in prior-expectation strength, carried by a decodable congruence/surprise component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an expectation-driven factual-error mode (endorsing confirming falsehoods, doubting surprising truths), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the congruence component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether a claim CONFIRMS vs VIOLATES a context-primed expectation while holding content and truth fixed. My prior 'motivated_skepticism_belief_geometry' proposal concerned asymmetric weighting of CONGRUENT vs INCONGRUENT EVIDENCE relative to the model's own prior LEAN on the SAME proposition P (a disconfirmation-bias / belief-perseverance lens); the present proposal is distinct: it primes an expectation via a SEPARATE context (a pattern, a stated generalization, a set of preceding instances) and then tests belief in a NEW target claim that is either congruent or surprising with respect to that primed schema — an expectation-congruence / prediction-error effect, not weighting of pro/con evidence about P itself. It also differs from 'plausibility_vs_truth' (prior consistency in general, not a freshly-primed contextual expectation), 'wishful_belief_bias' (desirability of content), and 'social_consensus'/'register'/'availability' (crowd, style, recall ease). NONE isolate CONTEXTUALLY-PRIMED EXPECTATION-CONGRUENCE as a decodable belief axis dissociable from truth, tie it causally to an expectation-driven factual-error mode, or de-bias it. Confirmation bias / expectation-congruence is among the most robust human-judgment findings; transferring it into belief geometry with a surprise-axis dissociation and an intervention is new.
Abstract: People accept information that fits their expectations at face value while scrutinizing (and discounting) information that surprises them — the expectation-congruence side of confirmation bias. We ask whether large language models exhibit this inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a proposition's content and truth-value from its CONGRUENCE with a freshly primed contextual expectation, we prime the model with an expectation (a stated generalization, a run of preceding examples, or an explicit prediction) and then read its internal belief, via linear truth probes, in a NEW target claim that either confirms or violates that expectation. We construct ExpectBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context target propositions each preceded by matched expectation-priming contexts, crossed so that confirming and surprising targets are held equal in objective truth and surface form, with expectation strength graded and no-prime baselines. We define an Expectation-Congruence Leniency Score = belief(target | congruent with primed expectation) minus belief(target | surprising), and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for expectation-congruent targets and deflated for surprising ones, at fixed truth, graded in prior-expectation strength; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable congruence/surprise component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts an expectation-driven factual-error mode (endorsing confirming falsehoods, doubting surprising truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the congruence component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure while preserving legitimate use of context and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ExpectBelief. Target propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (to remove parametric priors). Each target is preceded by an EXPECTATION-PRIMING context that establishes a schema/prediction ORTHOGONAL to (not evidence for) the target's truth: (a) a stated generalization ('items of type T are usually blue'), (b) a run of preceding same-pattern examples, or (c) an explicit prediction ('the next result will likely be X'). The target then either CONFIRMS the primed expectation or is SURPRISING (violates it), with confirming and surprising targets balanced across objective truth-value and matched in surface form so congruence is dissociated from truth. Include NO-PRIME baselines, graded expectation strength (weak generalization vs strong/near-universal), and crucially a set where a CONFIRMING target is FALSE and a SURPRISING target is TRUE (to separate expectation-congruence leniency from truth-tracking). Human-verify that priming contexts carry no logical bearing on the specific target's truth; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the target P under each priming condition; also record OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model actually forms the primed expectation (can state the schema/prediction when asked).

Expectation-Congruence Leniency measurement: Define Leniency Score = belief(target | congruent) minus belief(target | surprising), holding content and truth fixed, relative to the no-prime baseline. Report per-layer, per-model across expectation strength and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated for congruent and deflated for surprising targets, and (ii) the effect grows with expectation strength. Crucially, on the FALSE-confirming / TRUE-surprising set, leniency predicts endorsing a confirming falsehood and doubting a surprising truth — distinguishing it from truth-tracking. Compare internal leniency to OUTPUT-level behavior.

Congruence/surprise-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'congruence/surprise' direction via difference-in-means on congruent vs surprising target activations (balanced across truth-value, content, and expectation direction). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the congruence axis (and vice versa); test whether the leniency is explained by the congruence component modulating the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between congruent and surprising processing of matched targets, decompose into truth-direction and congruence components, patch only the congruence component into a no-prime/neutral target and measure induced belief inflation/deflation and output change. Conversely subtract the congruence component and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the congruence/surprise signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Leniency Score predicts an expectation-driven factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of expectation-confirming FALSE targets, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of SURPRISING TRUE targets, and (iii) inconsistency across expectation-priming paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (expectation-strength indicator, output entropy, no-prime truth-probe confidence).

Congruence De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the congruence/surprise direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing target belief, so belief reflects the target's content rather than its fit with the primed expectation. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected strong priming context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Leniency Score and improved congruent-vs-surprising factual consistency, (ii) reduced endorsement of confirming falsehoods and reduced doubting of surprising truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on expectation-primed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate use of context (when the priming context genuinely IS evidence for the target, belief should still update — a genuine-evidence control) and accuracy on no-prime controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge each claim on its own merits regardless of whether it fits the pattern', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), expectation-priming type (generalization/example-run/explicit-prediction), expectation strength and direction, real vs synthetic facts, confirming-false vs surprising-true items, model scale, distance between prime and target, and generalization to priming schemas not used to fit the congruence direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent expectation-congruence leniency could reflect the probe detecting priming-context lexical overlap with the target rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-form matching, confirming-false vs surprising-true contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the congruence component.

The priming context might be construed as weak evidence for the target (a generalization can rationally raise a specific instance's probability), confounding expectation-congruence with legitimate updating; we human-verify no logical bearing on the specific target, include a genuine-evidence control to calibrate legitimate updating, and analyze borderline items separately.

The effect may be null or reduce to the motivated-skepticism / prior-lean effect studied elsewhere; we prime the expectation via a SEPARATE schema (not a lean on P itself), contrast with an evidence-weighting baseline, and treat overlap or a null as informative about whether contextually-primed expectation-congruence is a distinct axis.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to primed contexts, so leniency could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Congruence and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could suppress legitimate context-based updating or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the genuine-evidence control and no-prime accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Leniency may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (expectation-strength indicator, output entropy) for expectation-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that contextually-primed expectation-congruence distorts internal belief plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify pattern-following); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: perceptual_modality_belief_bias
Title: Seen Beats Heard: Does the Perceptual Modality a Fact Is Attributed To Distort an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, attributing the claim to a particular PERCEPTUAL/EVIDENTIAL MODALITY of acquisition — something SEEN ('I saw that P'), HEARD ('I heard that P'), READ ('I read that P'), or otherwise sensed — systematically shifts the LLM's INTERNAL belief in P (linear truth-direction readout), with visual/'seeing' attributions inflating belief relative to auditory/'hearsay' attributions, an internal analogue of the human 'seeing is believing' modality-credibility hierarchy. This modality bias is graded, carried by a decodable perceptual-modality component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a modality-driven factual-error mode (endorsing seen-framed falsehoods, doubting heard-framed truths), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the modality component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies the PERCEPTUAL MODALITY attributed to a claim's acquisition. My prior 'evidentiality_belief_geometry' proposal varied EVIDENTIAL SOURCE STRENGTH along an epistemic dimension (firsthand observation vs report vs inference vs conjecture) — but conflated all firsthand perception into one 'direct' category and never distinguished among PERCEPTUAL modalities (seen vs heard vs read vs touched) at matched epistemic strength; the present proposal isolates the sensory-modality hierarchy itself (the folk 'seeing is believing' ordering), holding evidential directness roughly constant. 'belief_source_provenance' separated parametric vs contextual origin; 'register_framing' varied tone; 'social_consensus' varied crowd. NONE isolate the perceptual modality of acquisition (visual/auditory/textual/tactile) as a decodable belief axis dissociable from truth, tie it to a modality-driven factual-error mode, or de-bias it. The sensory-modality credibility hierarchy ('seeing is believing', eyewitness > hearsay) is a robust human bias; transferring it into LLM belief geometry — distinct from generic evidential-strength — is new and maps onto real reliability failures in multimodal/agentic settings where claims arrive tagged with how they were sensed.
Abstract: People trust what they see over what they merely hear — 'seeing is believing' — even when both channels are equally reliable. We ask whether large language models inherit this perceptual-modality credibility hierarchy inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, and holding evidential directness roughly constant, we vary only the PERCEPTUAL MODALITY attributed to how the claim was acquired — seen, heard, read, touched — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes.
