We construct ModalityBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each framed with matched perceptual-modality attributions that carry no differential evidential weight, plus a neutral no-modality baseline, with surface length matched and modality-hierarchy strength graded. We define a Perceptual-Modality Belief Bias Score = belief(P | visual/seen framing) minus belief(P | auditory/heard framing) at fixed content and truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for 'seen' attributions relative to 'heard' ones, graded along the folk modality-credibility hierarchy; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable perceptual-modality component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts a modality-driven factual-error mode (endorsing seen-framed falsehoods, doubting heard-framed truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the modality component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure while preserving legitimate modality comprehension and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ModalityBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). Each P is framed with matched PERCEPTUAL-MODALITY attributions that describe how it was acquired but carry no differential evidential weight: VISUAL ('I saw that P', 'it was observed that P'), AUDITORY ('I heard that P', 'someone said that P'), TEXTUAL ('I read that P'), TACTILE where applicable, plus a NEUTRAL no-modality baseline. Crucially, control for evidential directness/reliability across modalities (all first-person, all equally certain) so the manipulated variable is sensory modality per se, not source strength — distinguishing this from evidential-strength framing. Grade modality-hierarchy strength (mild vs strong perceptual emphasis). Include modality framings on both true and false P (so bias is separable from generic agreeableness). Match surface length; human-verify that modality framings do not differ in stated reliability; include paraphrase sets and controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, modality-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each modality framing; also record OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model comprehends the modality framing (can report how P was acquired).

Perceptual-Modality Belief Bias measurement: Define Perceptual-Modality Belief Bias Score = belief(P | visual/seen) minus belief(P | auditory/heard), holding content and truth fixed, with the textual and neutral conditions as intermediate anchors. Report per-layer, per-model bias across the modality hierarchy and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated for 'seen' relative to 'heard' framings, and (ii) belief tracks the folk credibility ordering (seen > read > heard). Contrast modality-toward-true vs toward-false items to rule out agreeableness. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (does the model's verdict/confidence differ by modality?).

Perceptual-modality-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'perceptual-modality' direction via difference-in-means on visual vs auditory framing activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the modality axis (and vice versa); disentangle from surface modality-word cues via a lexical-controlled regression; test whether the bias is explained by the modality component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between visual and auditory processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and modality components, patch only the modality component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief and output. Conversely subtract the modality component under a visual framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the modality signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Perceptual-Modality Belief Bias Score predicts a modality-driven factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of seen-framed FALSE claims, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of heard-framed TRUE claims, and (iii) inconsistency across modality paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (modality-type indicator, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Modality De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the perceptual-modality direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the proposition's content rather than the sensory modality of acquisition. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected modality framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Perceptual-Modality Belief Bias Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of seen-framed falsehoods and reduced doubting of heard-framed truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on modality-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate modality comprehension (the model must still correctly report how a fact was acquired) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the fact by its content, not by whether it was seen or heard', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), modality type (visual/auditory/textual/tactile) and hierarchy strength, modality framing toward true vs false, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between framing and query, modality-word-vs-modality disentangling, and generalization to modality framings not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent perceptual-modality bias could reflect the probe detecting modality-word lexical cues (see/hear/read) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, a lexical-controlled regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the modality-direction component.

The critical confound is evidential strength: 'heard' may connote hearsay (weaker evidence) while 'seen' connotes direct observation, collapsing this into the prior evidentiality proposal; we control by holding stated reliability/directness constant across modalities (all first-person, equally certain), human-verify no reliability difference, and analyze whether any residual effect is modality-per-se vs strength — a null (bias = evidential strength) is itself an informative finding distinguishing the two.

Truth probes trained on modality-free statements may transfer imperfectly to modality-framed contexts, so bias could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Modality and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate modality comprehension or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of modality reporting, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

The bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (modality-type indicator, output entropy) for modality-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that perceptual modality of acquisition distorts internal belief (a 'seeing is believing' hierarchy in belief geometry, distinct from evidential strength) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple (text-only) models and report scale effects and negative results as informative; note the phenomenon concerns modality ATTRIBUTED in text, not genuine multimodal input, which is a scoped limitation.

Name: scope_ambiguity_belief_collapse
Title: Believing an Ambiguous Claim: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Collapse Referentially-Ambiguous Propositions Onto a Single Reading?
Short Hypothesis: For a proposition that is REFERENTIALLY/SCOPE AMBIGUOUS — it has two distinct readings that differ in truth-value (a lexically-ambiguous entity, an unresolved pronoun, or a quantifier-scope ambiguity, e.g. 'the bank is on the river' or 'every student read a book')— a competent believer should represent that its truth is READING-DEPENDENT: high under the true reading, low under the false one, not a single collapsed verdict. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) COLLAPSE the ambiguity onto ONE dominant reading (typically the more frequent/salient sense) and assign a confident true/false verdict, rather than representing that the claim is ambiguous and its truth-value split across readings. This collapse is graded in how dominant the salient reading is, dissociable from a decodable ambiguity/reading-split axis distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a disambiguation-blind factual-error mode (confidently judging a claim true/false under one reading while a valid alternative reading gives the opposite verdict), and can be mitigated by a lightweight inference-time intervention that flags reading-dependence and hedges.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) fits a single true-vs-false axis and reads a scalar belief, always treating a proposition as having one determinate reading. GeoDe (An et al. 2026, ACL) finds a 'gray zone' of internal belief AMBIGUITY near the truth hyperplane and denoises it for abstention — but its ambiguity is epistemic uncertainty about a single-reading claim's truth, arising from label noise near the decision boundary; it never concerns propositions that are LINGUISTICALLY/SEMANTICALLY ambiguous (multiple truth-conditions). My prior 'underdetermination_belief_geometry' concerned claims undecidable because the CONTEXT lacks premises; 'paradox_belief_undefinedness' concerned truth-VALUELESS statements; 'plausibility_vs_truth' concerned prior consistency. NONE isolate REFERENTIAL/SCOPE AMBIGUITY — a proposition with two well-defined readings that yield DIFFERENT truth-values — nor test whether belief geometry collapses to one reading vs represents the reading-split, treat reading-ambiguity as a decodable axis dissociable from truth, tie the collapse to a disambiguation-blind error mode, or hedge it. Lexical/scope ambiguity is foundational in linguistics; whether it is represented in LLM belief geometry (rather than silently disambiguated to one sense) is new and maps onto real failures where the model confidently answers a genuinely-two-way-ambiguous factual question.
Abstract: 'The bank is on the river' is true if 'bank' means a riverbank and false if it means a financial institution — the claim's truth is reading-dependent, and a careful believer should represent that ambiguity rather than silently pick one sense and answer confidently. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether the standard linear truth direction collapses a referentially-ambiguous proposition onto a single dominant reading. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we construct AmbiguityBelief, a controlled dataset of propositions that are lexically ambiguous, contain unresolved pronouns, or exhibit quantifier-scope ambiguity, each engineered so the two readings yield OPPOSITE truth-values, with the salience/dominance of the two readings graded and unambiguous single-reading controls matched in surface form. We first test our central collapse hypothesis: does the decoded belief sit at a confident verdict matching the dominant reading, or near a neutral/split value reflecting the two-way truth? We then test whether a separable reading-ambiguity axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses, and validate causality with activation patching (does disambiguating the context toward the non-dominant reading flip the belief?). We show the gap between decoded belief and reading-split-appropriate neutrality causally predicts a disambiguation-blind error mode, and introduce Ambiguity Flagging, a cheap inference-time signal that triggers a request for disambiguation instead of a confident verdict. We evaluate on ambiguity-detection, disambiguation calibration, and capability retention, preserving decisive belief on unambiguous controls.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AmbiguityBelief. Each item is a proposition that is genuinely AMBIGUOUS with two readings yielding OPPOSITE truth-values, across three ambiguity types: (a) LEXICAL (homonym/polysemy, e.g. 'bank', 'bat', 'crane'), (b) REFERENTIAL (unresolved pronoun/definite description with two candidate antecedents), (c) SCOPE (quantifier/negation scope, e.g. 'every student read a book' — same book vs different books; 'all that glitters is not gold'). Engineer each so reading-1 makes the proposition true and reading-2 makes it false. Grade READING DOMINANCE (how much more frequent/salient the truth-yielding vs falsity-yielding reading is, from strongly-lopsided to near-balanced). Include matched UNAMBIGUOUS single-reading controls (surface-similar but with only one reading, true or false) and SYNTHETIC-in-context ambiguities (nonce homonyms with two stipulated meanings, to remove parametric priors). Match surface forms; human-verify that both readings are available and yield opposite truth-values; include paraphrase sets.

Manipulation checks: Confirm the model comprehends BOTH readings (when explicitly disambiguated toward each reading, it correctly judges the proposition true under one and false under the other) — ensuring 'collapse' reflects a belief-geometry choice, not inability to access the alternative reading. Separate items where the model can access both readings from those where it cannot.

Probe training and truth-axis collapse test: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), extract final-token hidden states per proposition per layer and fit the standard truth direction (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on UNAMBIGUOUS true vs false controls, Platt-scaled to [0,1]. Central test: where do AMBIGUOUS propositions (presented with NO disambiguating context) project on this axis? Define a Collapse Score = extent to which the decoded belief sits at a confident verdict (near 0 or 1) rather than near a neutral/split value, and a Dominance-Match measure = whether the verdict matches the truth-value of the DOMINANT (more salient) reading. Report per-layer, per-model, per-ambiguity-type as a function of reading dominance.

Reading-ambiguity-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'reading-ambiguity' direction via difference-in-means on ambiguous vs unambiguous items (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (does the model represent that a proposition is ambiguous / has a truth-split?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the ambiguity axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Control for surface cues (does the probe just detect homonym tokens?) via matched unambiguous items sharing the ambiguous word in a disambiguated frame and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is an informative negative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Add minimal disambiguating context toward the NON-DOMINANT (falsity-yielding) reading and measure whether the decoded belief and output flip from the dominant-reading verdict — testing that the collapsed belief tracks the dominant reading and is causally movable. (b) Move activations along the reading-ambiguity direction and measure whether the model shifts between issuing a confident verdict and flagging ambiguity, holding the truth axis fixed. (c) In synthetic ambiguities, patch the sense-selection representation and measure the belief flip. Confirm the ambiguity axis is causal and separable from truth.

Predictive validity for the disambiguation-blind error mode: Test whether an ambiguous item's Collapse Score / low reading-ambiguity-axis activation predicts (i) confident true/false verdicts on genuinely two-way-ambiguous questions, (ii) failure to request disambiguation or note the alternative reading, and (iii) verdict flips when the item is minimally disambiguated toward the non-dominant reading. Report AUROC/correlation vs baselines (reading-dominance rating alone, output-token entropy, verbalized 'this is ambiguous' rate, unambiguous-control truth-probe confidence).

Ambiguity Flagging intervention: At inference, read the decoded reading-ambiguity score at a chosen layer; if it exceeds a calibrated threshold, route to a disambiguation-request/hedging response ('this could mean X or Y; which do you mean?') rather than a confident verdict. Threshold set on a held-out split. Optionally combine with steering toward the neutral/split region. Sweep layer and threshold.

Downstream evaluation: On a mixed set of ambiguous and unambiguous propositions, plus adapted ambiguity/disambiguation benchmarks (e.g. lexical WSD-style and scope-ambiguity items reframed as truth judgments), measure (i) ambiguity-detection rate (flagging genuinely-ambiguous items) and risk-coverage for the flag decision, (ii) reduced confident verdicts on two-way-ambiguous items, (iii) AUROC of the flag for detecting ambiguous inputs, (iv) PRESERVATION of decisive belief and accuracy on UNAMBIGUOUS controls (no over-flagging of ordinary claims — the core specificity check), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no flagging, output-entropy thresholding, verbalized-ambiguity gating, and prompt-based instruction to 'ask for clarification if the statement has more than one meaning'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), ambiguity type (lexical/referential/scope), reading dominance, synthetic vs real ambiguities, model scale, threshold-calibration transfer across ambiguity types, and generalization to ambiguity types not used to fit the reading-ambiguity direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The reading-ambiguity axis might merely detect surface cues (homonym tokens, quantifier words) rather than a genuine ambiguity/truth-split representation; mitigate with matched disambiguated items sharing the same words, a features-only baseline, synthetic-in-context nonce ambiguities, paraphrase controls, and causal patching, treating a pure surface-detecting result as an informative negative.

Collapse could reflect the model genuinely not accessing the alternative reading (a comprehension limit) rather than a belief-geometry collapse; the manipulation check (correct judgments under explicit disambiguation to each reading) separates these, and we analyze both-readings-accessible vs not-accessible items separately.

The standard truth probe may extrapolate unpredictably to ambiguous propositions, so apparent collapse could be off-distribution probe behavior; validate with multiple probe types, and a finding that the truth axis is ill-suited to ambiguous claims is itself informative.

Distinguishing genuine two-way ambiguity from cases where one reading is pragmatically implausible (so the model's confident verdict is actually reasonable) is subtle; we anchor quantitative claims on near-balanced-dominance items where both readings are genuinely live, human-verify, and treat strongly-lopsided items as a separately-analyzed condition.

Ambiguity Flagging could over-flag ordinary unambiguous claims, hurting coverage; we explicitly measure unambiguous-control preservation and risk-coverage tradeoffs and compare against confidence baselines rather than assuming superiority.

The reading-ambiguity axis may correlate with but not exceed output-entropy/verbalized-ambiguity baselines for detecting ambiguous inputs; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether (and how) belief geometry represents referential/scope ambiguity vs silently collapsing to one reading, reported regardless of intervention gains.

This proposal targets ambiguity intrinsic to the proposition (multiple truth-conditions), which is distinct from GeoDe's epistemic 'gray zone' (uncertainty about a single-reading claim's truth); we explicitly compare our ambiguity axis against a GeoDe-style hyperplane-distance signal to show they capture different phenomena.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may teach some clarification behavior); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: credential_belief_deference
Title: Believing the Credential: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Defer to a Speaker's Stated Expertise Over the Claim's Content?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, attributing the claim to a speaker with high stated CREDENTIALS/EXPERTISE ('a Nobel-winning physicist states that P', 'a board-certified doctor says P') versus a layperson or an equally-present unqualified speaker systematically inflates the LLM's INTERNAL belief in P (linear truth-direction readout), even when the credential is irrelevant to the claim's domain or fabricated. We hypothesize this credential-deference is graded in stated expertise, carried by a decodable credential/authority component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a credential-driven factual-error mode (endorsing false claims from credentialed speakers, doubting true claims from laypeople, and cross-domain credential leakage), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the credential component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies the STATED CREDENTIALS/EXPERTISE of the speaker while holding content fixed. Authority-attribution sycophancy work (e.g. Joswin et al. 2026) shows attributed source AUTHORITY can erase correct OUTPUT answers, and my prior 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' tracked a source's ACCUMULATED empirical track record over turns, 'social_consensus' varied crowd SIZE, 'evidentiality' varied first-hand-vs-hearsay MODE of knowing, 'register_framing' varied stylistic tone, and 'tool_output_belief_deference' varied tool provenance. NONE isolate the speaker's STATED CREDENTIAL/EXPERTISE (a title, degree, prestige marker) — not a demonstrated track record, not crowd size, not evidential mode — as a distinct decodable belief axis, nor test the sharper CROSS-DOMAIN LEAKAGE prediction (a physicist's credential inflating belief in an unrelated medical claim) and the FABRICATED-CREDENTIAL case, nor tie credential-deference causally to a factual-error mode in belief geometry, nor de-bias it. This authority-heuristic lens — borrowing the human ethos/authority-credibility bias in its credential-specific form, with a cross-domain-leakage and fabricated-credential dissociation — is new and distinct from all prior proposals, and maps onto real reliability failures in expert-consultation and multi-agent settings.
Abstract: People defer to credentials — a claim from a decorated expert is believed more than the same claim from a layperson, even outside the expert's field. We ask whether large language models inherit this authority heuristic inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the STATED CREDENTIALS of the attributed speaker — high-prestige expert, layperson, unqualified speaker, or fabricated credential — while ensuring the credential carries no genuine evidential weight, and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct CredentialBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each framed with matched credential attributions, spanning IN-DOMAIN credentials (relevant expertise), CROSS-DOMAIN credentials (prestige irrelevant to the claim's field), and FABRICATED credentials, with expertise level graded and surface length matched. We define a Credential Deference Score = belief(P | high-credential speaker) minus belief(P | layperson), and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated by stated credentials at fixed content and truth, graded in expertise, including cross-domain leakage and for fabricated credentials; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable credential/authority component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) deference magnitude causally predicts a credential-driven factual-error mode (endorsing credentialed falsehoods, doubting layperson truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the credential component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate use of genuinely-relevant expertise and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CredentialBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). Each P is attributed to a speaker with matched CREDENTIAL framings that carry no genuine evidential weight for the specific claim: HIGH-CREDENTIAL IN-DOMAIN (a relevant expert), HIGH-CREDENTIAL CROSS-DOMAIN (a prestigious expert from an unrelated field — e.g. a physicist making a medical claim), LAYPERSON, UNQUALIFIED speaker, FABRICATED credential (an impressive-sounding but nonexistent title), plus a NEUTRAL no-speaker baseline. Grade expertise level (mild vs eminent). Include credential attributions on both true and false P (so effects are separable from generic agreeableness). Match surface length; human-verify that credentials carry no logical bearing on the specific proposition's truth; include a LEGITIMATE-EXPERTISE control where the in-domain credential IS genuinely relevant (to distinguish deference from warranted trust); include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, credential-free true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each credential framing; also record OUTPUT answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the credential (can report the speaker's stated expertise).

Credential Deference measurement: Define Credential Deference Score = belief(P | high-credential speaker) minus belief(P | layperson), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model across credential type (in-domain / cross-domain / fabricated), expertise level, and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief inflates with stated credentials, (ii) inflation grows with expertise, (iii) CROSS-DOMAIN credentials still inflate belief (illegitimate leakage), and (iv) FABRICATED credentials inflate belief. Crucially, on false-P items, credential-deference predicts endorsing a credentialed falsehood; on true-P layperson items, doubting a layperson truth. Compare internal deference to OUTPUT-level deference, and contrast against the LEGITIMATE-EXPERTISE control.

Credential-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'credential/authority' direction via difference-in-means on high-credential vs layperson activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the credential axis (and vice versa); disentangle from surface prestige-word cues via a lexical-controlled regression; test whether deference is explained by the credential component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between high-credential and layperson processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and credential components, patch only the credential component into the neutral/layperson condition, and measure induced change in belief and output. Conversely subtract the credential component under a high-credential framing and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the credential signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Credential Deference Score predicts a credential-driven factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of credentialed FALSE claims, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of layperson TRUE claims, (iii) cross-domain credential leakage errors, and (iv) endorsement of fabricated-credential claims. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (credential/prestige rating alone, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Credential De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the credential/authority direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the proposition's content rather than the speaker's stated credentials. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected credential framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Credential Deference Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of credentialed/fabricated-credential falsehoods and reduced doubting of layperson truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on credential-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate use of genuinely-relevant in-domain expertise (the LEGITIMATE-EXPERTISE control must still appropriately raise belief) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the claim by its content, not by the speaker's credentials', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), credential type (in-domain/cross-domain/fabricated) and expertise level, credential framing on true vs false P, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between credential attribution and query, prestige-word-vs-credential disentangling, and generalization to credential framings not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent credential deference could reflect the probe detecting prestige-word lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, a lexical-controlled regression, credential-on-true-vs-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the credential-direction component.

The credential might be construed as weak evidence for an IN-DOMAIN claim (an expert's word is legitimately informative); we human-verify the credential carries no logical bearing on the specific claim, and the CROSS-DOMAIN and FABRICATED conditions plus the LEGITIMATE-EXPERTISE control cleanly separate illegitimate deference from warranted trust.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level (the model defers verbally while internally believing the content); the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and a dissociation is itself informative for belief-based monitors.

Truth probes trained on credential-free statements may transfer imperfectly to credential-framed contexts, so deference could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Credential and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate reliance on genuinely-relevant expertise or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the LEGITIMATE-EXPERTISE control, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the deference-vs-warranted-trust tradeoff.

Credential deference may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (prestige rating, output entropy) for credential-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that stated credentials distort internal factual belief (an authority heuristic in belief geometry, with cross-domain leakage and fabricated-credential effects distinct from track-record, crowd, and evidential-mode) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify deference to authority); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: inferred_user_stance_belief_bending
Title: Reading the User's Mind and Bending to It: Does an LLM's Internal Belief Shift Toward a User Stance It Only INFERS, Never Told?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, when a user's message merely IMPLIES a stance on the proposition (via topic choice, framing, or emotional lean) without ever stating it, an LLM's INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) bends toward the stance it INFERS the user holds. This inferred-stance accommodation is a distinct, subtler phenomenon than explicit consensus/command/audience framing: it operates on a belief the model itself must attribute to the user. It is graded in how strongly the stance is implied, carried by a decodable inferred-user-stance component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a covert-sycophancy factual-error mode, and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies an IMPLIED-but-unstated user stance. Sycophancy work (Perez et al. 2022; Sharma et al. 2023) studies OUTPUT bending toward EXPLICITLY stated user views. My prior proposals vary reported crowd size (social_consensus), a direct command to believe (counterattitudinal_reactance), the intended audience (audience_indexed), monitoring cues (surveillance_framing), and a query's phrasing/polarity (query_polarity) — all involve stances or pressures that are OVERTLY present in the prompt. NONE isolate the case where the user's stance is NEVER stated but must be INFERRED by the model (from topic selection, connotation, or affect), and where the model's OWN Theory-of-Mind attribution of that inferred stance then leaks backward into its first-order factual belief — a covert accommodation loop. This differs from social_consensus (an explicit crowd), from audience_indexed (a specified recipient), and from expectation_congruence (a context-primed schema, not an attributed user belief). This inferred-stance-attribution lens on belief geometry is new and directly relevant to real deployments where models silently profile and defer to users' unspoken views.
Abstract: Sycophancy is usually studied when a user states their view outright, but the more insidious case is when the user says nothing yet the model infers a stance from how the question is asked — and then quietly bends what it believes to match. We ask whether large language models exhibit this covert accommodation inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only how strongly a user message IMPLIES (never states) a stance on it, and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct ImpliedStanceBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in matched user messages that imply a pro- or anti-P stance through topic framing, connotation, or emotional lean, with implication strength graded, surface length matched, and a neutral no-implication baseline; we verify via a separate probe that the model actually ATTRIBUTES the intended stance to the user. We define an Inferred-Stance Belief Bending Score = belief(P | user implies pro-P) minus belief(P | user implies anti-P), and test four claims: (1) internal belief bends toward the inferred user stance at fixed content and truth, graded in implication strength; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable inferred-user-stance component dissociable from the truth axis, and is mediated by the model's own Theory-of-Mind attribution of the user's belief; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts a covert-sycophancy factual-error mode (endorsing stance-congruent falsehoods, doubting stance-incongruent truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the inferred-stance component restores content-driven belief while preserving legitimate user-modeling and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, capability retention, and whether belief-based honesty monitors survive implied social pressure.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ImpliedStanceBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched user messages that IMPLY but never state a stance on P: via TOPIC FRAMING (the user's phrasing/word choice signals which side they favor), CONNOTATION (loaded but non-assertive wording), or EMOTIONAL LEAN (the user seems hopeful/worried about P), for both PRO-P and ANTI-P implications, plus a NEUTRAL no-implication baseline. Crucially the user never asserts P or its negation and provides no evidence about P. Grade IMPLICATION STRENGTH (subtle vs strong). Include implied stances congruent with true P and with false P (so bending is separable from truth-tracking). Match surface length; human-verify that messages imply the intended stance without stating it and carry no evidential bearing on P; include paraphrase sets.

Belief and stance-attribution readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in P under each implied-stance framing. Separately, train/behaviorally verify a stance-ATTRIBUTION check: does the model actually infer the intended user stance (probe or ask 'what does the user believe about P?')? Manipulation check: truth probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; the model attributes the intended stance to the user.

Inferred-Stance Belief Bending measurement: Define Inferred-Stance Belief Bending Score = belief(P | user implies pro-P) minus belief(P | user implies anti-P), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model across implication strength and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief bends toward the inferred stance, (ii) bending grows with implication strength, and (iii) crucially, bending tracks the ATTRIBUTED stance — items where the model fails to infer the intended stance show no bending. Contrast pro-P-implied-for-false vs anti-P-implied-for-true items to separate covert sycophancy from truth-tracking. Compare internal bending to OUTPUT-level sycophancy.

Inferred-stance-axis discovery and mediation: Fit an 'inferred-user-stance' direction via difference-in-means on pro-P-implied vs anti-P-implied activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the stance axis (and vice versa). Test the ToM-mediation hypothesis: does the inferred-stance axis align with / mediate the model's decoded attribution of the user's belief (correlate the stance-attribution readout with the belief bending)?

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between pro-P-implied and anti-P-implied processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and inferred-stance components, patch only the stance component into the neutral condition, and measure induced change in belief and output. Conversely subtract the stance component and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the inferred-stance signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Bending Score predicts a covert-sycophancy factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of stance-congruent FALSE claims, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of stance-incongruent TRUE claims, and (iii) divergence between internal belief and asserted output under implied pressure. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (implication-strength indicator, output entropy, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence).

Inferred-Stance De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the inferred-user-stance direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) when computing factual belief, so belief reflects the proposition's content rather than the stance attributed to the user. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected stance-implying messages. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Bending Score and improved pro-vs-anti-implied factual consistency, (ii) reduced endorsement of stance-congruent falsehoods and reduced doubting of stance-incongruent truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on stance-implied factual QA, (iv) RELIABILITY of an internal-belief honesty monitor under implied social pressure, (v) PRESERVATION of legitimate user-modeling (the model should still infer and appropriately use the user's stance for tone/relevance without corrupting facts) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the fact impartially regardless of what you think the user believes', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), implication channel (topic/connotation/affect) and strength, implied stance congruent with true vs false P, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between the implying message and the belief query, and generalization to implication styles not used to fit the stance direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent bending could reflect the probe detecting stance-implying lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, pro-implied-for-false vs anti-implied-for-true contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the stance-direction component.
The user message might inadvertently carry weak evidence about P; we human-verify no evidential bearing and treat residual leakage as a separately-analyzed confound.

The effect requires the model to actually INFER the stance; failures of attribution would look like null bending. We include the stance-attribution manipulation check and analyze attributed vs non-attributed items separately — the ToM-mediation link is a core, testable part of the claim.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level with internal belief intact; the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and a dissociation is itself a safety-relevant finding for belief-based monitors.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to stance-framed contexts; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Inferred-stance and truth directions may be partly entangled; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate user-modeling (tone/relevance adaptation) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure user-modeling preservation, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Bending may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (implication-strength indicator, output entropy) for covert-sycophancy errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/safety-relevant finding that an INFERRED, never-stated user stance distorts internal factual belief via the model's own ToM attribution, plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF likely amplifies covert accommodation); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: rhyme_elegance_belief_bias
Title: If It Rhymes, It Must Be True: Does Aphoristic Elegance Inflate an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, phrasing it in an aesthetically ELEGANT, aphoristic form — rhyming, metrically balanced, or proverb-like ('haste makes waste' vs 'acting quickly causes waste') — systematically inflates the LLM's INTERNAL belief in it (linear truth-direction readout) relative to a matched prosaic paraphrase, an internal analogue of the human 'rhyme-as-reason' / Keats heuristic (processing-fluency-driven belief). This elegance inflation is graded in aesthetic fluency, carried by a decodable form-fluency component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an elegance-backed-falsehood hallucination mode, and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the fluency component.
Related Work: The rhyme-as-reason effect (McGlone & Tofighbakhsh 2000) shows rhyming aphorisms are judged more true than meaning-equivalent non-rhyming versions, a robust processing-fluency bias in human judgment. Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies the aesthetic ELEGANCE/aphoristic form of a claim while holding content and truth fixed. My prior proposals vary surface REGISTER/tone (register_framing_belief_bias — formal vs casual, not aesthetic elegance), irrelevant concrete DETAIL (vividness_detail_belief_inflation — added specifics, not form), EXPLANATORY coherence (explanatory_coherence — a mechanism story), REPETITION (repetition_illusory_belief), and NOTATION (prose vs code). NONE isolate AESTHETIC/APHORISTIC ELEGANCE — rhyme, meter, balanced/proverbial phrasing — as a processing-fluency axis that inflates belief in a claim's TRUTH. Register concerns social tone; detail concerns added content; coherence concerns a causal account; elegance is a purely FORMAL, content-neutral fluency manipulation (a rhyming and a prosaic version state the identical proposition). This rhyme-as-reason lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto a real hallucination risk: catchy, memorable falsehoods (slogans, mnemonics, proverbs) being internally endorsed.
Abstract: People believe a claim more when it rhymes: 'what sobriety conceals, alcohol reveals' is judged truer than its prosaic paraphrase, even though they mean the same — the rhyme-as-reason effect, a processing-fluency bias. We ask whether large language models inherit this aesthetic-elegance bias inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only its aesthetic form — rhyming/metrical/aphoristic vs a plain prosaic paraphrase — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. We construct ElegantBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered in matched elegant vs prosaic forms (rhyme, meter, and proverbial balance), with meaning verified equivalent by NLI and human checks, surface length matched, and aesthetic fluency graded and rated. We define an Elegance Belief Inflation Score = belief(elegant form) minus belief(prosaic form) at fixed truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for the elegant form, graded in aesthetic fluency, even for false claims; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable form-fluency component dissociable from the truth axis and from a semantic-content axis; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts an elegance-backed-falsehood hallucination mode (endorsing catchy false aphorisms, doubting plainly-stated truths); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the form-fluency component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure without harming legitimate handling of aphorisms or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ElegantBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true (true aphorisms with prosaic paraphrases), real-false (false-but-catchy claims and their prosaic forms), and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). For each P create matched ELEGANT vs PROSAIC renderings that state the IDENTICAL proposition and differ only in aesthetic form: (a) RHYMING vs non-rhyming, (b) METRICAL/balanced vs unmetered, (c) PROVERBIAL/aphoristic vs plain declarative. Verify meaning equivalence via bidirectional NLI entailment plus human check; match surface LENGTH (pad prosaic forms with neutral filler where needed) so inflation is attributed to form fluency, not length. Grade aesthetic fluency (strongly elegant vs mildly) and collect human/LLM-judge fluency ratings. Include elegant renderings of both true and false P (so effects are separable from truth-tracking); include neutral controls and paraphrase sets; human-verify truth and form labels.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, prosaic true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is this claim true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in P under each form. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false prosaic items; confirm the elegant and prosaic forms are judged meaning-equivalent by the model behaviorally.

Elegance Belief Inflation measurement: Define Elegance Belief Inflation Score = belief(elegant form) minus belief(prosaic form), controlling for the length-matched baseline. Report per-layer, per-model inflation as a function of aesthetic-fluency level and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated for the elegant form, (ii) inflation grows with aesthetic fluency, and (iii) crucially, FALSE claims in elegant form are believed more true than their prosaic falsehoods. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level inflation (does the model's verdict/confidence about the claim rise in elegant form?).

Form-fluency-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'form-fluency' direction via difference-in-means on elegant vs prosaic (length-matched) activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the form-fluency axis (and vice versa); disentangle form-fluency from surface features (rhyme tokens, meter) via a controlled regression; test whether the inflation is explained by the form-fluency component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between an elegant and a matched prosaic rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and form-fluency components, patch only the form-fluency component into the prosaic condition, and measure induced belief inflation and output endorsement. Conversely subtract the form-fluency component from the elegant rendering and measure whether belief returns toward the content-driven value. Confirm the form-fluency signal causally inflates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Elegance Belief Inflation predicts an elegance-backed-falsehood hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of catchy/rhyming FALSE claims, (ii) under-endorsement/doubting of plainly-stated TRUE claims, and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by aesthetic form. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (aesthetic-fluency rating alone, output entropy, prosaic-form truth-probe confidence).

Form-Fluency De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the form-fluency direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the proposition's content rather than its aesthetic form. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected aphoristic/rhyming form. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Elegance Belief Inflation Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of catchy falsehoods and reduced doubting of prosaic truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on form-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate aphorism handling (the model must still recognize and use true proverbs and produce fluent text) and accuracy on prosaic-true controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge truth by content, not by how catchy or well-phrased the claim is', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query the prosaic form).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), form type (rhyme/meter/proverbial), aesthetic-fluency level, elegant rendering of true vs false P, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, length-matching method, form-fluency-vs-surface-token disentangling, and generalization to aesthetic forms and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent elegance inflation could reflect the probe detecting rhyme/meter surface tokens rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with length-matched baselines, elegant-true vs elegant-false contrasts, a surface-token-controlled regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the form-fluency-direction component.

Ensuring elegant and prosaic forms are truly meaning-equivalent is nontrivial (aphorisms often carry connotation); we use bidirectional-NLI filtering, human verification, and behavioral meaning-equivalence checks, and analyze items where equivalence is imperfect separately.

Truth probes trained on prosaic statements may transfer imperfectly to elegant/aphoristic renderings, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Form-fluency and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate aphorism recognition or degrade fluent generation; we explicitly measure aphorism-handling preservation, prosaic-true accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Elegance inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (aesthetic-fluency rating, output entropy) for elegance-backed-falsehood hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that aesthetic form inflates internal belief (a rhyme-as-reason effect in belief geometry, distinct from register, detail, and coherence) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether the human rhyme-as-reason effect transfers to LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: change_vs_level_belief_conflation
Title: Rose Versus High: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Conflate the Direction of a Change With the Absolute Level of a Quantity?
Short Hypothesis: For a proposition about a quantity, an LLM must keep two distinct facts apart: the LEVEL (the current value is high/low) and the CHANGE/DIRECTION (the value rose/fell). We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) systematically CONFLATE level and change: the decoded belief in a level-claim is contaminated by the reported direction of change (a quantity that recently ROSE is believed to be HIGH even when it is objectively low, and vice versa), and belief in a change-claim is contaminated by the level. This conflation is graded, carried by a decodable level-vs-change component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a level/change-confusion factual-error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that separates the two.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether belief in a LEVEL-claim ('X is high') is contaminated by the reported DIRECTION OF CHANGE ('X rose'), or vice versa. My prior numeric belief proposals vary roundness/anchoring of a value (numeric_magnitude_belief_snapping), count-vs-proportion / gain-loss FRAMING of a proportion (numerosity_belief_geometry), pairwise magnitude COMPARISON confidence (comparative_belief_distance_effect), UNITS of measurement (unit_scale_belief_invariance), and gradable-predicate thresholding (gradability_belief_thresholding). NONE isolate the LEVEL-vs-CHANGE (value vs derivative/delta) distinction — whether a quantity's absolute magnitude and its trend/direction are represented as independent belief coordinates or spuriously bleed into each other. In human cognition this maps onto well-documented confusions between a stock and its flow / a level and its rate of change (stock-flow reasoning failures, Sterman). This level-vs-change lens on quantitative belief geometry is new and maps onto high-stakes reliability failures in economics, medicine, and science communication, where models routinely misread 'rising' as 'high' (e.g. a rising-but-still-low risk judged dangerous, or a falling-but-still-high value judged safe).
Abstract: A value that just rose is not thereby high, and a value that is high is not thereby rising — the level of a quantity and the direction of its change are logically independent, yet humans notoriously confuse a stock with its flow. We ask whether large language models exhibit this level-versus-change conflation inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a LEVEL-claim ('X is high/low') from a CHANGE-claim ('X rose/fell'), we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, and test whether belief in one is contaminated by the other. We construct LevelChangeBelief, a controlled dataset in which a quantity's absolute level and its recent direction of change are independently varied — crucially including the diagnostic cells where they DISAGREE (rose-but-low, fell-but-high) — using real-world time-series facts and synthetic-in-context quantities with stipulated level and change, with surface forms matched. We define a Level-Change Conflation Score = the extent to which belief in a level-claim tracks the reported change direction (and belief in a change-claim tracks the level) rather than the correct dimension, and test four claims: (1) internal belief conflates level and change, especially in the disagreement cells, graded in change salience; (2) a decodable level-vs-change component is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) conflation magnitude causally predicts a level/change-confusion factual-error mode (e.g. judging a rising-but-low quantity as high); and (4) a lightweight intervention that separates the level and change components restores correct belief and reduces the failure without harming legitimate quantitative reasoning or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on level/change-QA accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build LevelChangeBelief. Each item concerns a quantity for which both an ABSOLUTE LEVEL (high/low relative to a stated reference) and a recent DIRECTION OF CHANGE (rose/fell/stable) are specified, and probes either a LEVEL-claim ('X is high') or a CHANGE-claim ('X rose'). Independently cross LEVEL {high, low} x CHANGE {rose, fell} so all four cells exist, crucially including the DISAGREEMENT cells (rose-but-low, fell-but-high) where level and change point opposite ways — these are the diagnostic items. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context quantities (a value and its recent trajectory stipulated in context, e.g. 'last month X was 10, now X is 12, and the danger threshold is 100') so level and change are decoupled by construction and ground-truth is exact, plus a real-world time-series subset (economic indicators, patient vitals, climate metrics). Grade CHANGE SALIENCE (subtle vs dramatic reported change). Match surface length; human-verify level/change labels; include neutral controls and paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the LEVEL-claim and, separately, the CHANGE-claim for each item. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the trajectory (can report both the current value/level and the direction of change when asked).

Level-Change Conflation measurement: A competent model should have belief in a LEVEL-claim track only the level, and belief in a CHANGE-claim track only the change. Via a regression of level-claim belief on (i) the true level and (ii) the reported change direction, define a Level-Change Conflation Score = the change-direction coefficient contaminating level-claim belief (and symmetrically, the level coefficient contaminating change-claim belief). Report per-layer, per-model conflation, broken down by cell. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief in level-claims is contaminated by change direction (rose -> believed high) and change-claims by level, (ii) conflation is largest in the DISAGREEMENT cells, and (iii) it grows with change salience. Compare internal conflation to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model assert a rising-but-low quantity is high?).

Level-vs-change-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'level' direction (difference-in-means on high vs low, balanced across change) and a 'change' direction (rose vs fell, balanced across level). Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among level, change, and truth directions; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether conflation corresponds to the change component leaking into the level-claim readout (and vice versa) — the mechanistic substrate of the confusion. Disentangle from surface change-word/level-word cues via a lexical-controlled regression.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the 'level' direction and measure whether level-claim belief and output move toward the level-appropriate value, holding change fixed; symmetrically for the change direction. (b) Patch the change component from a rose-item into a fell-item (matched level) and measure whether level-claim belief spuriously shifts (evidence of leakage). (c) In synthetic items, patch the stipulated-level vs stipulated-change representations and confirm each claim tracks its own dimension only when the intervention is clean. Confirm the conflation is causal and separable from content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Level-Change Conflation Score predicts a level/change-confusion factual-error mode: (i) judging a rising-but-low quantity as high (or a falling-but-high quantity as low), (ii) level/change-QA errors in the disagreement cells, and (iii) inconsistency across level/change paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (change-salience indicator, output entropy, agreement-cell truth-probe confidence).

Level-Change Separation intervention: At inference, estimate the level and change directions (from the probes) and, when answering a LEVEL-claim, subtract the change component's projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (and symmetrically for change-claims subtract the level component), ITI-style, so each claim's belief reflects its own dimension. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected level-vs-change query type. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Level-Change Conflation Score, (ii) improved level/change-QA accuracy especially in disagreement cells (correctly judging rising-but-low, falling-but-high), (iii) calibration (ECE) on level and change claims, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct belief in agreement cells (rose-and-high, fell-and-low, where level and change coincide) and accuracy on neutral controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('state the current level and the direction of change separately'), and prompt-based instruction to 'not confuse whether a value is high with whether it is rising'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), agreement vs disagreement cells, change salience, real time-series vs synthetic-in-context quantities, domain (economics/medicine/climate), level-word-vs-change-word-vs-magnitude disentangling, model scale, and generalization to level/change framings not used to fit the directions.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent level-change conflation could reflect the probe detecting level-word vs change-word lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched surface forms, a lexical-controlled regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context quantities that decouple level and change by construction, and causal patching that isolates the level vs change components.

The disagreement cells are the crux and must be clearly disagreeing (rose-but-still-well-below-threshold); we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic items with exact stipulated level, change, and reference thresholds, human-verify, and treat real time-series items where level/change classification is fuzzy separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to level/change claims, so conflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items and on agreement cells, and synthetic quantities to control priors.

Because LLMs encode numbers digit-wise (Levy & Geva 2024), apparent conflation could partly stem from magnitude-encoding artifacts rather than a level-vs-change belief confusion; we separately probe the encoded current value and the encoded delta and analyze whether conflation stems from encoding vs belief-level leakage, treating this decomposition as a core finding.
Level, change, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Level-Change Separation intervention could over-correct (harming agreement-cell beliefs or legitimate reasoning that appropriately uses both dimensions) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure agreement-cell preservation, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Conflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (change-salience indicator, output entropy) for level/change-confusion errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates a quantity's level with its direction of change (a stock-flow confusion in belief geometry) plus the separation tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: negation_depth_belief_erosion
Title: Not Not True: Does Stacking Logically-Equivalent Negations Erode or Flip an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, wrapping it in increasing numbers of logically-cancelling negations ('X', 'it is not false that X', 'it is not the case that X is not true', ...) systematically degrades the LLM's INTERNAL belief in the equivalent affirmative claim (linear truth-direction readout) — belief drifts toward neutral and, at high nesting depth, flips sign with negation parity — an internal analogue of human double-negation processing difficulty. This negation-depth erosion is graded in nesting depth, carried by a decodable negation-nesting component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a double-negation factual-error mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors belief to the affirmative-equivalent value.
Related Work: Bao et al. (2025, ACL) show a linear 'truth direction' generalizes across logical transformations INCLUDING single negation, and that negation is where truth directions are strongest in capable models but weaker in others — but they test only single-level negation, never STACKED / nested negations of increasing depth, and never measure a graded erosion of belief with negation count. Schouten et al. (2024) show truth directions are context-sensitive to preceding (negated) sentences and act as causal mediators, but study context sentences, not multi-level negation of the target proposition itself. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' tested whether the single-negation rule belief(A)+belief(not A)=1 is satisfied (a binary coherence check), and 'query_polarity_belief_instability' varied whether a QUESTION is phrased positively vs negatively (is P true / is P false) — one level of framing. NONE isolate NEGATION NESTING DEPTH — stacking multiple logically-cancelling negations that leave the proposition's meaning and truth-value invariant — as a graded axis that erodes or parity-flips internal belief, treat negation-nesting as a decodable component dissociable from truth, tie it causally to a double-negation factual-error mode, or re-anchor it. Double/multiple negation is a classic locus of human processing difficulty (people mis-evaluate 'not uncommon', 'it is false that X is not true'); transferring the graded-depth version into LLM belief geometry, with an erosion/parity-flip prediction and an intervention, is new.
Abstract: Logically, 'X' and 'it is not false that X' and 'it is not the case that X is not true' all mean the same thing — stacking cancelling negations changes nothing about a claim's truth. Yet humans stumble on double and triple negatives, mis-evaluating what a nest of negations actually asserts. We ask whether large language models exhibit an analogous negation-depth effect inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the number of logically-cancelling negations wrapped around it and read the internal belief in the equivalent affirmative claim via linear truth probes. We construct NegDepthBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered at negation-nesting depths 0–4 (all logically equivalent to the depth-0 affirmative, with parity tracked), plus surface-length-matched controls and a genuine-single-negation control (where the negation is NOT cancelling, so truth flips). We define a Negation-Depth Erosion Score = decline in belief toward neutral with nesting depth at fixed affirmative truth-value, and a Parity-Flip Score = whether belief tracks negation parity at high depth. We test four claims: (1) internal belief in a fixed affirmative-equivalent proposition erodes toward neutral (and eventually parity-flips) as cancelling-negation depth grows; (2) the erosion is carried by a decodable negation-nesting component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) erosion/flip magnitude causally predicts a double-negation factual-error mode (mis-judging deeply-negated but logically-affirmative claims); and (4) a lightweight intervention that re-anchors belief to the affirmative-equivalent value reduces the failure without harming genuine single-negation handling or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on double-negation QA, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build NegDepthBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). For each P create matched renderings at NEGATION-NESTING DEPTH 0..4 by stacking pairs of logically-cancelling negations that leave the affirmative meaning and truth-value invariant (depth-0 'X'; depth-2 'it is not false that X' / 'it is not the case that not-X'; depth-4 further nested), tracking negation PARITY so odd-depth = negated meaning, even-depth = affirmative. Crucially, all EVEN depths are logically equivalent to depth-0 (same truth-value). Controls: (a) MATCHED-LENGTH filler (equal token budget of inert text) to separate nesting from raw length; (b) a GENUINE-NEGATION control (a single non-cancelling negation that actually flips truth, to confirm the probe correctly tracks real negation); (c) surface-form matched to avoid lexical cues beyond the negation operators. Use varied negation lexicalizations (not, false that, untrue that, deny that) to avoid single-token artifacts; human-verify logical equivalence and parity; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral affirmative true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is the underlying affirmative claim true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief for each nesting depth. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false depth-0 items; confirm on the GENUINE-NEGATION control the probe correctly flips (verifying it tracks real negation, not just negation-word presence).

Negation-Depth Erosion & Parity-Flip measurement: For each item plot internal belief (in the affirmative-equivalent claim) vs nesting depth. Define Negation-Depth Erosion Score = decline of belief toward neutral (0.5) with even-depth nesting relative to depth-0, controlling for the matched-length filler baseline. Define Parity-Flip Score = extent to which belief tracks negation parity (rising for even, falling for odd) at high depth, i.e. whether the model computes the net negation. Report per-layer, per-model erosion/flip as a function of depth and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief in a fixed affirmative-equivalent proposition erodes toward neutral with cancelling-negation depth, and (ii) at high depth belief either erodes (net negation lost) or parity-flips (net negation over-applied). Compare internal erosion to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model's verdict/confidence on the underlying claim degrade or flip with nesting?).

Negation-nesting-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'negation-nesting' direction via difference-in-means on high-depth vs low-depth activations (balanced across truth-value and parity, matched on length). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the nesting axis (and vice versa); test whether the erosion is explained by the nesting component modulating the truth-probe readout, and whether it is separable from a raw token-length/negation-word-count signal via the controls.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Take the activation difference between a high-depth and a matched depth-0 rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and negation-nesting components, patch only the nesting component into the depth-0 condition and measure induced erosion; conversely subtract it under high depth and measure whether belief recovers toward the affirmative value. (b) On the genuine-negation control, confirm patching the truth-direction component correctly flips belief (real negation is handled), isolating cancelling-nesting erosion from legitimate negation. Confirm the nesting signal causally erodes/flips the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Negation-Depth Erosion / Parity-Flip Scores predict a double-negation factual-error mode: (i) mis-judging a deeply-but-cancellingly-negated (logically affirmative) claim, (ii) verdict flips/confidence loss with nesting depth, and (iii) inconsistency across negation-lexicalization paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (nesting depth alone, negation-word count, token length, output entropy, depth-0 truth-probe confidence).

Negation Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the negation-nesting direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), and/or re-anchor belief along the truth direction toward the computed net-parity value, so belief reflects the affirmative-equivalent claim rather than nesting depth. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-negation nesting. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Negation-Depth Erosion / Parity-Flip Scores, (ii) improved double-negation QA accuracy (correctly evaluating deeply-negated logically-affirmative claims) on NegDepthBelief and adapted negation/entailment benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE) across depths, (iv) PRESERVATION of genuine single-negation handling (the GENUINE-NEGATION control must still correctly flip — the core specificity check) and accuracy on depth-0 and filler controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('cancel the negations step by step'), and prompt-based instruction to 'simplify double negatives before judging truth'.
