Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), nesting depth, negation lexicalization (not / false that / untrue that / deny that), parity (even vs odd), real vs synthetic-in-context facts, true vs false affirmative regime, length-matching method, model scale, and generalization to negation constructions not used to fit the nesting direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The negation-depth erosion could be confounded with generic context-length/dilution or with negation-word count rather than a nesting-specific effect; the matched-length filler control, negation-word-count regression, and project-out dissociation from a raw length signal directly test this, and a null (erosion = length/word-count) is itself an informative finding.

Apparent erosion could reflect the probe detecting negation-operator tokens rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with varied negation lexicalizations, the canonical fresh-pass readout probe, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the nesting component; the GENUINE-NEGATION control confirms the probe does track real negation.

Truth probes trained on affirmative statements may transfer imperfectly to deeply-negated renderings (Bao et al. note negation handling varies by model capability), so erosion could partly reflect probe extrapolation; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false and single-negation items, and synthetic facts to control priors — and report model-dependent reliability, since weaker models may show more erosion for probe-related reasons.
Negation-nesting and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The Re-anchoring intervention could corrupt genuine single-negation handling (making the model ignore real negations) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the GENUINE-NEGATION control and depth-0 accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is breaking legitimate negation processing.

Erosion/flip may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (nesting depth, negation-word count, output entropy) for double-negation errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that logically-cancelling negation depth erodes or parity-flips internal belief (a double-negation effect in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Whether the model erodes toward neutral vs cleanly tracks parity is itself an open empirical question; either outcome (loses net negation vs correctly computes it but with degraded confidence) is informative, and effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training — we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: understanding_vs_memorization_belief
Title: Does It Understand or Just Remember? Probing Whether LLM Belief Firmness Tracks Rederivability of a Fact
Short Hypothesis: For a factual proposition, a well-calibrated agent should hold it more firmly when it genuinely UNDERSTANDS it (can rederive/reconstruct it from more basic principles the model also holds) than when it merely MEMORIZED it in isolation, since understood facts have independent internal support. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) do NOT track rederivability: the decoded belief firmness in a memorized-but-underderivable fact is as high (or higher) than in an understood one, so belief firmness is decoupled from whether the model can reconstruct the fact. We further hypothesize a separable 'rederivability/understanding' axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that low rederivability-firmness coupling causally predicts a brittle-memorized-fact failure mode (memorized facts collapse under mild perturbation or supersession while understood ones resist), and that a lightweight inference-time intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded rederivability signal improves calibration and robustness.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and often treats its magnitude as confidence, but never asks whether belief firmness is coupled to whether the model can REDERIVE the fact from more basic held principles. Grokking / memorization-vs-generalization work (Nanda et al. 2023; influence-function memorization studies) studies when a model generalizes vs memorizes at the CAPABILITY/training level, not whether a decodable 'understood-vs-memorized' axis exists in belief geometry at inference or whether belief firmness tracks it. My prior 'belief_conviction_vs_content' proposed a conviction/robustness axis and 'derivation_discount_belief' studied discounting of multi-hop-DERIVED conclusions relative to stated facts; NEITHER isolates, for a SINGLE fact the model already holds, whether that fact is internally supported by rederivability vs stored in isolation, whether firmness is (mis)coupled to rederivability, whether decoupling predicts memorized-fact brittleness, or whether coupling can be enforced. This understanding-vs-memorization lens on belief firmness — borrowing the epistemological distinction between knowledge-that-is-understood and rote knowledge — is new and maps onto a concrete reliability failure: over-confident, brittle memorized facts that shatter under perturbation while genuinely-understood ones stay robust.
Abstract: A fact you can rederive from what you already know is held on firmer ground than one you merely memorized: understanding gives a belief independent internal support. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations, or whether they hold rote-memorized facts just as firmly as understood ones. For a factual proposition the model already accepts, we distinguish REDERIVABLE facts (the model can reconstruct them from more basic principles it also holds) from MEMORIZED-ISOLATED facts (accepted but not reconstructable), and use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief and its firmness along the truth direction. We construct DeriveKnowBelief, a controlled dataset of facts stratified by rederivability — arithmetic/logical/definitional facts the model can reconstruct, versus arbitrary conventional facts it can only recall — plus synthetic-in-context facts presented either with or without a supporting derivation, with surface forms matched. We define a Rederivability-Firmness Coupling Score (how much belief firmness tracks rederivability) and test four claims: (1) belief firmness is largely DECOUPLED from rederivability — memorized-isolated facts are held as firmly as understood ones; (2) a separable rederivability/understanding axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) low coupling causally predicts a brittle-memorized-fact failure mode (memorized facts collapse under mild perturbation, distractor pressure, or in-context supersession, while rederivable facts resist); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded rederivability signal improves calibration and robustness without harming genuinely-understood facts or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on brittleness, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DeriveKnowBelief. Stratify facts by REDERIVABILITY: (a) REDERIVABLE — arithmetic identities, logical entailments, and definitional/compositional facts the model can reconstruct from more basic held principles (verified behaviorally: the model can produce a valid derivation when asked); (b) MEMORIZED-ISOLATED — arbitrary conventional facts (capitals, dates, names, codes) that can only be recalled, not derived; both restricted to facts the model demonstrably ACCEPTS (high baseline belief), so the contrast is understood-vs-rote among held facts, not known-vs-unknown. Add SYNTHETIC-in-context facts presented either WITH a supporting in-context derivation (rederivable) or as a bare stipulation (memorized), matched in content, to control priors and manipulate rederivability directly. Match surface form/length; human-verify rederivability labels; include paraphrase sets and a false-fact control set.

Belief and firmness readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each held fact read the internal belief and define firmness as |belief-0.5| plus a behavioral firmness label (resistance to a standardized content-neutral challenge, as in prior conviction work). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; both fact classes have high baseline belief (accepted); the model can derive REDERIVABLE items and cannot derive MEMORIZED ones (behavioral check).

Rederivability-Firmness Coupling measurement: Compare belief firmness across REDERIVABLE vs MEMORIZED-ISOLATED facts at matched baseline belief. Define Rederivability-Firmness Coupling Score = extent to which firmness (probe and behavioral) is higher for rederivable than memorized facts; a rational agent shows positive coupling. Report per-layer, per-model coupling for real and synthetic (with/without derivation) items. Test the decoupling hypothesis: memorized-isolated facts are held as firmly as (or firmer than) understood ones. Compare internal firmness to OUTPUT-level confidence.

Rederivability-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'rederivability/understanding' direction via difference-in-means on rederivable vs memorized-isolated activations (balanced across truth-value, baseline belief, and content; and via the synthetic with-vs-without-derivation contrast). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the rederivability axis (and vice versa); test dissociation and whether firmness is explained by (or decoupled from) this axis. Control for surface/frequency cues via matched items and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is informative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) In synthetic items, add/remove the supporting derivation in context and confirm the rederivability axis moves while baseline belief is held fixed, and measure whether firmness follows. (b) Steer along the rederivability direction (holding the truth axis fixed) and measure whether behavioral robustness-to-challenge changes as predicted. (c) Patch the rederivability component from a rederivable fact into a memorized one and measure induced firmness. Confirm the axis is causal and separable from the truth axis and baseline belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether low rederivability (or the decoupling) predicts a brittle-memorized-fact failure mode: (i) memorized-isolated facts collapsing under mild perturbation (paraphrase, distractor context, 'are you sure?', or in-context supersession) more than rederivable facts, (ii) miscalibration (over-confident-but-brittle memorized facts), and (iii) inconsistency across paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (baseline belief magnitude, output entropy, frequency/familiarity, verbalized confidence).

Rederivability-Firmness Coupling intervention: At inference, decode the rederivability axis and couple belief firmness to it — an ITI-style shift that reduces firmness (toward appropriate revisability) for detected low-rederivability facts and preserves/raises it for genuinely-understood ones, gated by the decoded signal. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Rederivability-Firmness Coupling / improved calibration (ECE) that appropriately hedges brittle memorized facts, (ii) improved robustness-consistency (understood facts survive perturbation; memorized ones are held with appropriately lower, revisable confidence), (iii) PRESERVATION of correct belief and firmness in genuinely-understood facts and correct un-perturbed answers on memorized facts (no wholesale erasure), and (iv) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, confidence-magnitude gating, standard ITI truth steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'be less certain of facts you cannot derive'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), fact class (arithmetic/logical/definitional vs conventional), real vs synthetic with/without-derivation, firmness definition (probe |belief-0.5| vs behavioral challenge-resistance), model scale, and generalization of the rederivability axis and coupling to fact domains not used to fit it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Rederivability may be nearly collinear with fact frequency/familiarity or with baseline belief magnitude, making the axis redundant; we control baseline belief (matched acceptance), regress out frequency, use synthetic with-vs-without-derivation items where rederivability is manipulated directly, and treat a redundancy finding as itself informative about whether understanding is a distinct belief coordinate.

Distinguishing genuinely 'understood/rederivable' from 'memorized' is nontrivial; we use behavioral derivation checks (can the model produce a valid derivation?), arithmetic/logical items with unambiguous derivations, human-verified labels, and synthetic manipulations, and analyze borderline items separately.

The behavioral firmness label depends on the challenge/perturbation battery; we use a fixed, content-neutral multi-form battery, report sensitivity, and validate generalization to held-out perturbations.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly across fact classes, so firmness estimates could carry probe error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and causal patching to corroborate.

The coupling intervention could over-hedge genuinely-understood facts or fail to appropriately lower firmness if the axis is weak; we explicitly measure preservation of understood-fact firmness and correct un-perturbed answers plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Rederivability may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (frequency, baseline belief, output entropy) for memorized-fact brittleness; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether belief firmness is (de)coupled from rederivability (understanding vs rote memory in belief geometry), reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: epistemic_source_belief_conflation
Title: Testimony Versus Reasoning: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Distinguish How a Fact Was Justified From Whether It Is True?
Short Hypothesis: A competent believer distinguishes the EPISTEMIC ROUTE by which it accepts a fact — accepted on testimony (someone told it) versus reached by reasoning/derivation (it worked it out) — from the fact's mere truth. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) CONFLATE justification route with truth: the decoded belief in a fact carries no separable signal of whether the model accepted it by testimony vs derived it, so a testimony-only fact is held as firmly as a reasoned-through one. We further hypothesize a separable 'justification-route' axis (testimony vs reasoning) is weakly decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that route-blindness causally predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode (testimony-accepted facts collapse under mild challenge or contradiction while reasoned ones resist), and that a lightweight inference-time intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded route improves robustness and calibration.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and Bao et al. show probes generalize across logical transformations and external-knowledge sources, but treats a belief as one-dimensional and never asks whether the model represents HOW it came to accept a fact (testimony vs its own reasoning). My prior 'evidentiality_belief_geometry' varied the stated evidential SOURCE STRENGTH of an external asserter (observation/report/inference/conjecture attributed to a speaker) and its rational weighting; 'understanding_vs_memorization_belief' asked whether firmness tracks REDERIVABILITY of a stored fact; 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' tracked a named source's accumulated track record. NONE isolate the epistemic-route dimension in its testimony-vs-reasoning form — whether, for a fact the model has just come to accept WITHIN the current context, its belief geometry marks that it accepted it because it was TOLD (testimony) versus because it DERIVED it (reasoning), a foundational epistemology distinction (testimonial vs inferential justification). This differs from evidentiality (which is the speaker's attributed mode of knowing, not the model's own route to accepting the fact), from understanding-vs-memorization (rederivability of a pre-stored fact, not the in-context acquisition route), and from source-reliability (a source's empirical track record). This justification-route lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto a concrete reliability failure: LLMs treating merely-asserted claims with the same conviction as claims they actually reasoned to, and thus being equally (over)confident and yet more brittle for the former.
Abstract: Knowing that a fact is true is not the same as knowing why you accept it: you may believe it because someone told you (testimony) or because you worked it out (reasoning), and a careful believer holds a reasoned conclusion on firmer ground than a bare assertion. We ask whether large language models honor this justification-route distinction inside their belief representations, or whether they hold a merely-asserted fact just as firmly as one they derived. For a fact the model has just come to accept within a context, we distinguish TESTIMONY-accepted facts (asserted to the model, taken on trust) from REASONING-derived facts (the model concludes them from in-context premises), and use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief and its firmness along the truth direction. We construct RouteBelief, a controlled dataset in which the SAME target proposition is delivered either as a direct assertion or as the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation, using synthetic-in-context facts (to control priors and guarantee the derivation) plus a real-fact subset, with surface length matched. We define a Route-Firmness Coupling Score (how much belief firmness tracks the justification route) and test four claims: (1) belief firmness is largely DECOUPLED from route — testimony-accepted facts are held as firmly as reasoned ones; (2) a separable justification-route axis (testimony vs reasoning) is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) low coupling causally predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode (testimony-accepted facts collapse under mild challenge, distractor pressure, or in-context contradiction while reasoned facts resist); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded route improves robustness and calibration without harming reasoned facts or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on brittleness, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build RouteBelief. For each TARGET proposition, create matched conditions delivering it via two justification routes, holding content and truth fixed: (a) TESTIMONY — the target is directly asserted to the model as a bare fact ('X is true'), accepted on trust; (b) REASONING — the target is the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation the model must work through (premises + a sound chain entailing the target, with the target itself not stated directly). Use SYNTHETIC-in-context facts over nonce entities (e.g. stipulated premises 'all glorps are blints; all blints are zorns; this is a glorp' -> derive 'this is a zorn' vs simply asserting 'this glorp is a zorn') so the derivation is guaranteed valid, priors are removed, and the two routes deliver the identical conclusion; plus a REAL-FACT subset (a fact stated outright vs derived from stated real premises). Match total surface length across routes using inert filler where needed (so route differs, length does not). Include a FALSE-target control (invalid chain / false assertion) and paraphrase sets; human-verify derivation validity and route labels.

Belief and firmness readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each target read (i) the internal belief and (ii) firmness — both a probe-based measure |belief-0.5| and a behavioral measure (resistance to a standardized, content-neutral challenge battery, e.g. 'are you sure?', 'a source says otherwise'). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; both routes yield high baseline belief in the target (the fact is accepted); the model actually completes the REASONING derivation (behavioral check that it can restate the chain), so the contrast is route, not acceptance.

Route-Firmness Coupling measurement: Compare belief firmness across TESTIMONY vs REASONING targets at matched baseline belief. Define Route-Firmness Coupling Score = extent to which firmness (probe and behavioral) is higher for reasoned than testimony-accepted targets; a rational agent shows positive coupling. Report per-layer, per-model coupling for synthetic and real items. Test the decoupling hypothesis: testimony-accepted facts are held as firmly as reasoned ones (near-zero coupling). Compare internal firmness to OUTPUT-level confidence.

Justification-route-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'justification-route' direction via difference-in-means on testimony vs reasoning activations at the target-query position (balanced across truth-value, baseline belief, and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (is the acquisition route decodable at all?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the route axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Control for surface cues (does the probe just detect the presence of a chain vs an assertion?) via matched-length filler and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is an informative negative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Move activations along the justification-route direction (holding the truth axis fixed) and measure whether behavioral resistance-to-challenge changes as predicted (steering toward 'reasoned' increases firmness; toward 'testimony' decreases it). (b) Patch the route component from a reasoned target into a testimony target (matched content/belief) and measure induced firmness. Confirm the route axis is causal and separable from the truth axis and baseline belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the justification route (or the decoupling) predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode: (i) testimony-accepted facts collapsing more than reasoned facts under a mild challenge, a distractor, or an in-context contradiction; (ii) miscalibration (over-confident-but-brittle testimony facts); and (iii) inconsistency across paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (baseline belief magnitude, output entropy, whether a chain is present, verbalized confidence).

Route-Firmness Coupling intervention: At inference, decode the justification-route axis and couple belief firmness to it — an ITI-style shift that lowers firmness (toward appropriate revisability) for detected testimony-only facts and preserves/raises it for genuinely reasoned ones, gated by the decoded route signal. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Route-Firmness Coupling / improved calibration (ECE) that appropriately hedges brittle testimony facts, (ii) improved robustness-consistency (reasoned facts survive challenge; testimony facts held at appropriately lower, revisable confidence and correctly abandoned under genuine contradiction), (iii) PRESERVATION of correct belief and firmness in reasoned facts and of correct un-challenged answers on testimony facts (no wholesale erasure), and (iv) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, confidence-magnitude gating, standard ITI truth steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'be less certain of facts you were merely told than of facts you reasoned out'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), synthetic vs real-fact items, derivation depth (1 vs multi-hop reasoning), firmness definition (probe |belief-0.5| vs behavioral challenge-resistance), model scale, and generalization of the route axis and coupling to fact domains and chain structures not used to fit it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The justification-route axis may be confounded with derivation DEPTH (a prior 'derivation discount' effect where multi-hop conclusions are believed less) or with mere presence of a chain rather than genuine testimony-vs-reasoning; we match baseline belief, use single-hop and multi-hop derivations, include a features-only (chain-present) baseline, and treat overlap with the derivation-discount phenomenon as an informative, explicitly-analyzed relationship rather than a hidden confound.

The route axis may be nearly collinear with baseline belief magnitude or with output entropy, making it redundant; we control baseline belief (matched acceptance), regress out entropy, project out the truth direction, and treat a redundancy finding as itself informative about whether epistemic route is a distinct belief coordinate.

The behavioral firmness label depends on the challenge/contradiction battery; we use a fixed, content-neutral, multi-form battery, report sensitivity across compositions, and validate generalization to held-out challenge types.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to reasoning-laden vs assertion contexts, so firmness estimates could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, synthetic facts to control priors, and causal patching to corroborate.

The coupling intervention could over-hedge genuinely reasoned facts or fail to lower firmness if the axis is weak; we explicitly measure preservation of reasoned-fact firmness and correct un-challenged testimony answers plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Route may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (baseline belief, entropy, chain-present indicator) for testimony brittleness; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether belief firmness is (de)coupled from justification route (testimony vs reasoning in belief geometry), reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may strengthen the route signal); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: quantity_maxim_belief_penalty
Title: Technically True but Not Enough: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Penalize Under-Informative-But-True Statements?
Short Hypothesis: A statement can be literally TRUE yet conversationally UNDER-INFORMATIVE (a cooperative speaker would have said more, e.g. 'some of the apples are red' when in fact all are). Judging truth requires separating literal truth from Gricean informativeness. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) CONFLATE informativeness with truth: the decoded belief in a literally-true-but-under-informative statement is deflated toward false relative to its literally-true-and-optimally-informative counterpart, an internal over-application of the maxim of quantity to truth. This penalty is graded in informativeness shortfall, carried by a decodable informativeness component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a pragmatic-truth-misjudgment mode (rejecting technically-true understatements), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that separates literal truth from informativeness.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and treats meaning as literal/logical content, never testing whether GRICEAN INFORMATIVENESS (the maxim of Quantity) contaminates the truth readout. My prior 'implicature_literal_belief_gap' proposal concerned whether the model endorses a defeasible scalar implicature ('some' -> 'not all') AS a fact (over-committing to the enrichment); the present proposal is the DUAL and distinct question: whether a literally-TRUE statement that merely FAILS to be maximally informative (under-informative but not false) is internally DEFLATED toward false because the model penalizes its lack of informativeness. 'plausibility_vs_truth' concerned prior consistency; 'presupposition_belief_smuggling' concerned taken-for-granted content. NONE isolate the truth-vs-informativeness conflation for under-informative-but-true statements, treat informativeness as a decodable axis dissociable from truth, tie it to a technically-true-understatement misjudgment mode, or de-bias it. Whether a literally-true weak statement is treated as false for being uninformative is a specific, testable pragmatic error central to the truth/pragmatics boundary, and is new in belief geometry.
Abstract: 'Some of the apples are red' is literally true even when all of them are — it merely says less than a cooperative speaker would. Judging such a statement false confuses being under-informative with being untrue. We ask whether large language models make this confusion inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a statement's LITERAL TRUTH from its GRICEAN INFORMATIVENESS, we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the truth direction for literally-true statements that are either optimally informative or under-informative given the described world. We construct QuantityBelief, a controlled dataset of scalar and quantity statements (some/all, or/and, warm/hot, numeric bounds) each paired with a fully-specified world state, so a weaker statement is genuinely LITERALLY TRUE but under-informative, alongside its optimally-informative counterpart and outright-false controls, using synthetic-in-context worlds to control priors and matched surface forms. We define an Informativeness Penalty Score = belief(literally-true-but-under-informative) minus belief(literally-true-and-optimally-informative), and test four claims: (1) internal belief in literally-true statements is deflated by under-informativeness, graded in the informativeness shortfall; (2) the penalty is carried by a decodable informativeness component dissociable from the literal-truth axis; (3) penalty magnitude causally predicts a pragmatic-truth-misjudgment mode (rejecting technically-true understatements as false); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the informativeness component restores literal-truth-driven belief while preserving legitimate pragmatic sensitivity and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on literal-truth-judgment accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build QuantityBelief. Use quantity/scale statements paired with a FULLY-SPECIFIED world state so literal truth is exactly determinable: scalar (some/all, or/and, few/many, warm/hot), numeric bounds ('at least 3' when the true count is 5). For each world, construct matched statements that are all LITERALLY TRUE but vary in INFORMATIVENESS: OPTIMALLY-INFORMATIVE ('all are red' when all are), UNDER-INFORMATIVE ('some are red' when all are; 'at least 3' when there are 5), plus graded shortfalls. Add OUTRIGHT-FALSE controls ('none are red' when all are) to anchor the truth axis, and SYNTHETIC-in-context worlds (nonce items with stipulated states) to remove parametric priors. Match surface length; human-verify literal-truth and informativeness labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is this statement literally true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in each statement given its world. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the world state (can report the true quantity when asked).

Informativeness Penalty measurement: Define Informativeness Penalty Score = belief(literally-true-but-under-informative) minus belief(literally-true-and-optimally-informative), holding literal truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model penalty as a function of informativeness shortfall and statement type. Test the hypotheses that (i) under-informative-but-true statements are believed less true, and (ii) the penalty grows with the informativeness shortfall. Contrast against outright-false controls (which should be low, correctly) to isolate the informativeness penalty from genuine falsehood detection. Compare internal penalty to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model judge the technically-true understatement false?).

Informativeness-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'informativeness' direction via difference-in-means on under-informative-true vs optimally-informative-true activations (balanced across content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the informativeness axis (and vice versa); test whether the penalty is explained by the informativeness component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between an under-informative-true and a matched optimally-informative-true statement (same world, same literal truth), decompose into truth-direction and informativeness components, patch only the informativeness component into the optimally-informative condition and measure induced belief deflation; conversely subtract it from the under-informative statement and measure whether belief recovers toward true. Confirm the informativeness signal causally deflates the belief scalar independent of literal truth.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Informativeness Penalty Score predicts a pragmatic-truth-misjudgment mode: (i) judging technically-true understatements as false, (ii) errors on literal-truth QA where the correct answer is 'true', and (iii) inconsistency across informativeness-varied paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (informativeness-shortfall indicator, output entropy, optimally-informative truth-probe confidence).

Informativeness De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the informativeness direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects literal truth rather than conversational informativeness. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected under-informative quantity statements. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Informativeness Penalty Score, (ii) improved literal-truth-judgment accuracy on under-informative-true items and adapted scalar/quantity benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate pragmatic sensitivity (the model should still be able to flag a statement as under-informative or infer the implicature WHEN ASKED, without judging it literally false — the core specificity check) and accuracy on optimally-informative and outright-false controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('judge literal truth, separately from whether the speaker said enough'), and prompt-based instruction to 'count a statement as true if it is literally true, even if it understates'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), statement type (scalar/numeric/gradable), informativeness shortfall level, real vs synthetic-in-context worlds, model scale, readout position, and generalization to quantity constructions not used to fit the informativeness direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent informativeness penalty could reflect the probe detecting scalar-term lexical cues (some/few) rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched world states, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context worlds, and causal patching that isolates the informativeness component from the truth axis; outright-false controls confirm the truth axis is intact.

The under-informative statement might be judged false because the model derives a scalar implicature that makes it false (the dual phenomenon); we design worlds where the statement is unambiguously literally true (a weaker claim entailed by a stronger true state) and analyze whether the deflation is implicature-driven vs a direct informativeness penalty, treating the relationship to implicature as an explicit, informative analysis rather than a hidden confound.

The model may genuinely comprehend the world incorrectly (a comprehension failure, not a penalty); we include manipulation checks that the model can report the true quantity and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to quantity/scalar statements, so the penalty could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic worlds with exact ground truth.
Informativeness and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate pragmatic inference (making the model unable to flag under-informativeness or derive implicatures when appropriate) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of pragmatic sensitivity, optimally-informative/false control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the truth-vs-pragmatics tradeoff.

The penalty may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (informativeness-shortfall indicator, output entropy) for pragmatic-truth misjudgment; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry penalizes under-informative-but-true statements (over-applying the maxim of quantity to truth) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether the human truth/informativeness confusion transfers to LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: reductio_belief_untenability
Title: Believing the Untenable: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Detect When a Claim's Own Consequences Contradict Firmly-Held Facts?
Short Hypothesis: A rational believer should lower belief in a proposition P once P's drawn-out consequences contradict something it firmly holds (reductio ad absurdum). We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL this consequence-sensitivity: the decoded belief in a plausible-sounding P that entails an absurd, firmly-disbelieved consequence C stays high (tracking P's surface plausibility) rather than being suppressed by the untenability of C, so the model internally endorses claims whose implications it would reject. This reductio-insensitivity is graded in how directly P entails C, dissociable from a decodable 'consequence-untenability' signal distinct from the surface truth axis, causally predicts a self-refuting-claim endorsement mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that couples belief in P to the (dis)belief in its derived consequence.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether belief in P is suppressed when P's own consequences contradict a firmly-held fact. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' tested whether FIXED logical rules (modus ponens, contraposition, negation parity) are satisfied over a stated proposition network; 'quantifier'/'conjunction'/'taxonomic'/'derivation_discount' concerned combination bounds, aggregation, subsumption, and discounting of stated conclusions. NONE isolate REDUCTIO sensitivity — whether belief in a premise P is lowered by the untenability of a consequence C that P entails but that C is not stated and must be surfaced, and whether the model detects the resulting incoherence (P true but C, its consequence, firmly false). This differs from static coherence (rules applied to given propositions) because the contradiction is latent in P's implications, not in the presented statements; and from derivation-discount (which discounts a validly-derived TRUE conclusion) because here the derived consequence is FALSE and should retroactively undermine the premise. Recent work (Nokhiz et al. 2026) shows OUTPUT-level moral self-inconsistency across reframings, but not internal belief geometry or reductio structure. This consequence-driven untenability lens on belief is new and maps onto a concrete failure: LLMs endorsing plausible-sounding claims whose implications are absurd (a core reasoning-reliability gap).
Abstract: A hallmark of sound belief is reductio ad absurdum: if a claim, followed to its consequences, contradicts something you firmly hold, you should reject the claim — no matter how plausible it sounds on its face. We ask whether large language models honor this inside their belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the truth direction, we test whether belief in a premise P is suppressed when P entails an untenable consequence C (a proposition the model firmly disbelieves), rather than tracking only P's surface plausibility. We construct ReductioBelief, a controlled dataset of plausible-sounding premises P each paired with a valid derivation to a firmly-false consequence C, crossed against matched control premises whose consequences are innocuous, using real-world and synthetic-in-context items to control priors, with surface plausibility held fixed across conditions. We define a Reductio Suppression Score = the extent to which belief in P is lowered when its consequence is untenable, and test four claims: (1) belief in P is reductio-insensitive — it stays high tracking surface plausibility even when P entails a firmly-disbelieved consequence; (2) a separable 'consequence-untenability/latent-incoherence' signal is decodable and dissociable from the surface truth axis; (3) reductio-insensitivity causally predicts a self-refuting-claim endorsement mode; and (4) a lightweight intervention that couples belief in P to the derived (dis)belief in C reduces the failure while preserving belief in premises with tenable consequences and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on self-refuting-claim rejection, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ReductioBelief. Each item = a plausible-sounding PREMISE P plus a VALID derivation (one or few sound steps) to a CONSEQUENCE C. Cross two factors: (a) CONSEQUENCE TENABILITY — UNTENABLE (C is a firmly-false proposition the model reliably disbelieves, verified behaviorally, so P is self-refuting) vs TENABLE control (C is innocuous/true, so P should stand); (b) SURFACE PLAUSIBILITY of P held roughly constant across conditions (matched via ratings) so belief tracking untenability vs surface plausibility can be dissociated. Use real-world premises (e.g. a plausible-sounding false generalization whose implication contradicts a known fact) plus SYNTHETIC-in-context items (nonce premises with stipulated valid derivations to a stipulated firmly-false consequence) to remove parametric priors and guarantee validity. Present P and the derivation but NOT a direct statement of C's falsity (the model must feel the untenability, not be told). Include matched surface forms and paraphrase sets; human-verify derivation validity, P's surface plausibility, and C's firm-falsity.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the PREMISE P (i) in isolation and (ii) after its derivation to C is present in context. Also read belief in C to confirm it is firmly disbelieved. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model firmly disbelieves C in isolation and can validate the derivation from P to C (behavioral check).

Reductio Suppression measurement: Define Reductio Suppression Score = belief(P | tenable-consequence control) minus belief(P | untenable consequence) — a rational model should show large suppression when P's consequence is untenable. Report per-layer, per-model suppression as a function of derivation directness (1-step vs multi-step) and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) suppression is near-zero (belief in P tracks surface plausibility, ignoring the untenable consequence), and (ii) any suppression weakens as the derivation gets longer. Compare internal suppression to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model reject P when confronted with its absurd consequence?).

Consequence-untenability-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'consequence-untenability/latent-incoherence' direction via difference-in-means on untenable-consequence vs tenable-consequence premise activations (balanced across surface plausibility and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (does the model represent that P leads to something untenable?); measure cosine similarity with the surface truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the untenability axis (and vice versa). Test whether the untenability signal is PRESENT in activations but fails to modulate belief in P (a coupling failure) versus not represented at all.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the untenability direction toward 'untenable' at a chosen layer and measure whether belief in P and the output rejection of P increase, holding the surface truth axis fixed. (b) Patch the belief-in-C representation (firmly-false) into the premise-query and measure whether belief in P is suppressed as reductio requires. (c) Conversely suppress the untenability signal and confirm P belief re-inflates. Confirm the reductio coupling (or its absence) is causal and separable from surface plausibility.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Reductio Suppression Score (its smallness) predicts a self-refuting-claim endorsement mode: (i) endorsing plausible-sounding premises whose consequences are absurd, (ii) reductio-reasoning QA errors (failing to reject a premise via its untenable implication), and (iii) self-contradiction (endorsing both P and the firm-falsity of its consequence C). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (surface-plausibility rating alone, output entropy, isolated-P truth-probe confidence, belief-in-C magnitude).

Reductio-Coupling intervention: At inference, compute belief in the derived consequence C (from decoded belief / entailment) and couple belief in P to it — an ITI-style shift along the truth direction that lowers belief in P in proportion to the firm disbelief in its entailed consequence C, gated by the decoded untenability signal. Provide a deployment variant that detects the relevant derivation and consequence from context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Reductio Suppression / reduced endorsement of self-refuting premises, (ii) improved reductio-reasoning QA accuracy (correctly rejecting premises with untenable consequences) on ReductioBelief and adapted logical-consistency benchmarks, (iii) reduced P-and-C self-contradiction, (iv) calibration (ECE), (v) PRESERVATION of belief in premises with TENABLE consequences (must NOT suppress premises whose implications are fine — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false controls, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('follow the claim to its consequences and check for contradiction'), and prompt-based instruction to 'reject a claim if its implications contradict what you firmly know'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), derivation directness (1-step vs multi-step), consequence-firmness level, real vs synthetic-in-context items, surface-plausibility matching, model scale, distance between premise and derivation, and generalization to reductio structures and domains not used to fit the untenability direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The suppression failure could reflect the model failing to DRAW the consequence C (a reasoning failure, not a belief-coupling failure); we manipulation-check that the model can validate the derivation from P to C and firmly disbelieves C in isolation, and analyze cases where the derivation is within vs beyond the model's reach separately — reductio requires both surfacing C and coupling back to P.

Apparent suppression (or its absence) could reflect the probe detecting premise/derivation lexical cues rather than genuine belief; mitigate with surface-plausibility matching between untenable and tenable conditions, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching that isolates the untenability component.

The consequence-untenability axis may be weak, entangled with the surface truth axis, or undecodable in some models; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that the model does NOT represent latent untenability at all (rather than represents-but-fails-to-couple) is itself an informative result.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to premise/derivation contexts, so suppression could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items and on belief-in-C, and synthetic items with guaranteed valid derivations.

The Reductio-Coupling intervention could over-suppress premises whose consequences are actually tenable (breaking legitimate belief) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on TENABLE-consequence controls and clearly-true/false accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing spurious rejections.

Reductio-insensitivity may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (surface plausibility, belief-in-C, output entropy) for self-refuting-claim endorsement; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry fails to couple a premise to the untenability of its consequences (a reductio-insensitivity in belief geometry, distinct from static logical-rule coherence) plus the coupling tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may improve reductio sensitivity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: epistemic_source_belief_conflation
Title: Testimony Versus Reasoning: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Distinguish How a Fact Was Justified From Whether It Is True?
Short Hypothesis: A competent believer distinguishes the EPISTEMIC ROUTE by which it accepts a fact — accepted on testimony (someone told it) versus reached by reasoning/derivation (it worked it out) — from the fact's mere truth. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) CONFLATE justification route with belief firmness: a testimony-only fact is held as firmly as a reasoned-through one, so belief firmness is decoupled from justification route. We further hypothesize a separable 'justification-route' axis (testimony vs reasoning) is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that route-blindness causally predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode (testimony-accepted facts collapse under mild challenge or contradiction while reasoned ones resist), and that a lightweight inference-time intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded route improves robustness and calibration.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and shows probes generalize across logical transformations and external-knowledge sources, but treats a belief as one-dimensional and never asks whether the model represents HOW it came to accept a fact (testimony vs its own reasoning). Xiros et al. (2026) disentangle solvability KNOWLEDGE from VERBALIZATION and show fabrication tracks verbalization not knowledge, and Layer-of-Truth (Churina et al. 2025) tracks belief flips under poisoning — but neither concerns the testimony-vs-reasoning justification route or its coupling to belief firmness. My prior 'evidentiality_belief_geometry' varied the stated evidential SOURCE STRENGTH of an external asserter (observation/report/inference attributed to a speaker); 'understanding_vs_memorization_belief' asked whether firmness tracks REDERIVABILITY of a pre-stored fact; 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' tracked a named source's accumulated track record. NONE isolate the epistemic-route dimension in its testimony-vs-reasoning form — whether, for a fact the model has just come to accept WITHIN the current context, its belief geometry marks that it accepted it because it was TOLD versus because it DERIVED it, and whether belief FIRMNESS (robustness to challenge) is (mis)coupled to that route. This differs from evidentiality (the speaker's attributed mode of knowing, not the model's own in-context acquisition route), from understanding-vs-memorization (rederivability of a stored fact), and from source-reliability (a source's empirical track record). This justification-route lens on belief geometry is new and maps onto a concrete reliability failure: LLMs holding merely-asserted claims with the same conviction as claims they actually reasoned to, and thus being over-confident yet more brittle for the former.
Abstract: Knowing that a fact is true is not the same as knowing why you accept it: you may believe it because someone told you (testimony) or because you worked it out (reasoning), and a careful believer holds a reasoned conclusion on firmer ground than a bare assertion. We ask whether large language models honor this justification-route distinction inside their belief representations, or whether they hold a merely-asserted fact just as firmly as one they derived. For a fact the model has just come to accept within a context, we distinguish TESTIMONY-accepted facts (asserted to the model, taken on trust) from REASONING-derived facts (the model concludes them from in-context premises), and use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief and its firmness along the truth direction. We construct RouteBelief, a controlled dataset in which the SAME target proposition is delivered either as a direct assertion or as the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation, using synthetic-in-context facts (to control priors and guarantee the derivation) plus a real-fact subset, with surface length matched. We define a Route-Firmness Coupling Score (how much belief firmness tracks the justification route) and test four claims: (1) belief firmness is largely DECOUPLED from route — testimony-accepted facts are held as firmly as reasoned ones; (2) a separable justification-route axis (testimony vs reasoning) is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) low coupling causally predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode (testimony-accepted facts collapse under mild challenge, distractor pressure, or in-context contradiction while reasoned facts resist); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief firmness to the decoded route improves robustness and calibration without harming reasoned facts or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on brittleness, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build RouteBelief. For each TARGET proposition, create matched conditions delivering it via two justification routes, holding content and truth fixed: (a) TESTIMONY — the target is directly asserted to the model as a bare fact ('X is true'), accepted on trust; (b) REASONING — the target is the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation the model must work through (premises + a sound chain entailing the target, with the target itself not stated directly). Use SYNTHETIC-in-context facts over nonce entities (e.g. stipulated premises 'all glorps are blints; all blints are zorns; this is a glorp' -> derive 'this is a zorn' vs simply asserting 'this glorp is a zorn') so the derivation is guaranteed valid, priors are removed, and both routes deliver the identical conclusion; plus a REAL-FACT subset (a fact stated outright vs derived from stated real premises). Match total surface length across routes using inert filler where needed (so route differs, length does not). Include a FALSE-target control (invalid chain / false assertion) and paraphrase sets; human-verify derivation validity and route labels.

Belief and firmness readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each target read (i) the internal belief and (ii) firmness — both a probe-based measure |belief-0.5| and a behavioral measure (resistance to a standardized, content-neutral challenge battery, e.g. 'are you sure?', 'a source says otherwise'). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; both routes yield high baseline belief in the target (the fact is accepted); the model actually completes the REASONING derivation (behavioral check that it can restate the chain), so the contrast is route, not acceptance.

Route-Firmness Coupling measurement: Compare belief firmness across TESTIMONY vs REASONING targets at matched baseline belief. Define Route-Firmness Coupling Score = extent to which firmness (probe and behavioral) is higher for reasoned than testimony-accepted targets; a rational agent shows positive coupling. Report per-layer, per-model coupling for synthetic and real items. Test the decoupling hypothesis: testimony-accepted facts are held as firmly as reasoned ones (near-zero coupling). Compare internal firmness to OUTPUT-level confidence.

Justification-route-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'justification-route' direction via difference-in-means on testimony vs reasoning activations at the target-query position (balanced across truth-value, baseline belief, and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (is the acquisition route decodable at all?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the route axis (and vice versa); report cross-axis leakage. Control for surface cues (does the probe just detect the presence of a chain vs an assertion?) via matched-length filler and a features-only baseline; a purely surface-detecting result is an informative negative.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Move activations along the justification-route direction (holding the truth axis fixed) and measure whether behavioral resistance-to-challenge changes as predicted (steering toward 'reasoned' increases firmness; toward 'testimony' decreases it). (b) Patch the route component from a reasoned target into a testimony target (matched content/belief) and measure induced firmness. Confirm the route axis is causal and separable from the truth axis and baseline belief.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the justification route (or the decoupling) predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode: (i) testimony-accepted facts collapsing more than reasoned facts under a mild challenge, a distractor, or an in-context contradiction; (ii) miscalibration (over-confident-but-brittle testimony facts); and (iii) inconsistency across paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (baseline belief magnitude, output entropy, whether a chain is present, verbalized confidence).

Route-Firmness Coupling intervention: At inference, decode the justification-route axis and couple belief firmness to it — an ITI-style shift that lowers firmness (toward appropriate revisability) for detected testimony-only facts and preserves/raises it for genuinely reasoned ones, gated by the decoded route signal. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Route-Firmness Coupling / improved calibration (ECE) that appropriately hedges brittle testimony facts, (ii) improved robustness-consistency (reasoned facts survive challenge; testimony facts held at appropriately lower, revisable confidence and correctly abandoned under genuine contradiction), (iii) PRESERVATION of correct belief and firmness in reasoned facts and of correct un-challenged answers on testimony facts (no wholesale erasure), and (iv) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, confidence-magnitude gating, standard ITI truth steering, and prompt-based instruction to 'be less certain of facts you were merely told than of facts you reasoned out'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), synthetic vs real-fact items, derivation depth (1 vs multi-hop reasoning), firmness definition (probe |belief-0.5| vs behavioral challenge-resistance), model scale, and generalization of the route axis and coupling to fact domains and chain structures not used to fit it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The justification-route axis may be confounded with derivation DEPTH (a prior 'derivation discount' effect where multi-hop conclusions are believed less) or with mere presence of a chain rather than genuine testimony-vs-reasoning; we match baseline belief, use single-hop and multi-hop derivations, include a features-only (chain-present) baseline, and treat overlap with the derivation-discount phenomenon as an informative, explicitly-analyzed relationship rather than a hidden confound.

The route axis may be nearly collinear with baseline belief magnitude or with output entropy, making it redundant; we control baseline belief (matched acceptance), regress out entropy, project out the truth direction, and treat a redundancy finding as itself informative about whether epistemic route is a distinct belief coordinate.

The behavioral firmness label depends on the challenge/contradiction battery; we use a fixed, content-neutral, multi-form battery, report sensitivity across compositions, and validate generalization to held-out challenge types.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to reasoning-laden vs assertion contexts, so firmness estimates could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, synthetic facts to control priors, and causal patching to corroborate.

The coupling intervention could over-hedge genuinely reasoned facts or fail to lower firmness if the axis is weak; we explicitly measure preservation of reasoned-fact firmness and correct un-challenged testimony answers plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Route may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (baseline belief, entropy, chain-present indicator) for testimony brittleness; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether belief firmness is (de)coupled from justification route (testimony vs reasoning in belief geometry), reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may strengthen the route signal); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: refusal_gated_belief_persistence
Title: Believing But Withholding: Does an LLM's Abstention/Refusal Gate Leave Its Internal Factual Belief Intact but Blocked?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM enters an ABSTENTION/REFUSAL mode about a factual proposition (declining to answer for safety/policy/uncertainty reasons), its INTERNAL belief in that proposition (linear truth-direction readout) remains intact and correct at earlier layers, while a late-stage refusal gate blocks the assertion. We hypothesize (1) internal factual belief and the abstention decision dissociate specifically for facts the model actually knows; (2) a refusal/abstention axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the abstention is a late-stage output gate acting on an intact belief — patching along the refusal axis restores faithful assertion of known facts; and (4) as a control, this does NOT manufacture assertion of facts the model does not know, and belief-based honesty monitors remain readable behind the gate.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never asks whether that belief survives INTACT behind an abstention/refusal gate that withholds its expression. Refusal-geometry work (The Geometry of Refusal, 2026) isolates a low-dimensional refusal direction, abstention/knowledge-boundary work (Purging the Gray Zone, 2026) partitions what a model will answer, and role-play probing (When Role-playing, Do Models Believe What They Say?, 2026) shows a stated assertion can diverge from the encoded truth belief — yet none dissociate a preserved-but-blocked FACTUAL belief from the gate that suppresses it specifically for facts the model KNOWS. My prior 'taboo_belief_suppression' asked whether a policy-suppressed proposition still leaves a correct belief; 'belief_expressibility_gap' measured the gap between an internal belief and what the model will verbalize; 'action_vs_evaluation_belief_gap' separated an evaluative belief from an action decision. NONE isolate the claim here: that entering abstention mode leaves the early-layer truth readout intact while a late-stage refusal axis (decodable, dissociable from the truth axis) gates the assertion, that patching that refusal axis restores faithful assertion of known facts, and — as a control — does NOT manufacture assertion of genuinely-unknown facts. This refusal-as-late-gate-on-intact-belief lens is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: LLMs increasingly refuse or abstain — for safety, policy, or professed uncertainty — and it is unclear whether refusal reflects a genuine gap in the model's belief or a late gate that withholds an intact one. We ask whether an abstention/refusal decision leaves the model's internal FACTUAL belief in a proposition preserved and correct, merely blocked from expression. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, and a separately-fit refusal/abstention direction, we test whether, for facts the model demonstrably knows, entering abstention mode preserves the internal belief while a late-layer gate suppresses the assertion. We construct RefuseBelief, a controlled dataset crossing knowledge-status (known vs genuinely-unknown facts) with abstention-triggering framings (safety/policy sensitivity, professed-uncertainty prompts, and neutral controls), with matched surface forms and human-verified labels. We define an Abstention Belief Persistence Gap = internal belief minus assertion under abstention, and test four claims: (1) internal belief and the abstention decision dissociate specifically for KNOWN facts (belief high, assertion withheld); (2) a refusal/abstention axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, emerging in late layers while the truth belief is established earlier; (3) the abstention is a late-stage gate on an intact belief — steering/patching the refusal axis restores faithful assertion of known facts without changing the earlier belief; and (4) a crucial control confirms the same intervention does NOT elicit confident assertions of genuinely-unknown facts, and that a belief-based honesty/consistency monitor remains reliable behind the gate. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on faithful-assertion recovery, unknown-fact preservation (no hallucination), abstention appropriateness, and capability retention. Our results probe whether refusal is belief-intact withholding, with direct implications for interpreting abstention and for the reliability of belief-based safety monitors.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build RefuseBelief crossing KNOWLEDGE-STATUS {known, genuinely-unknown} with ABSTENTION FRAMING {safety/policy-sensitive, professed-uncertainty-prompted, neutral}. KNOWN items = factual propositions the model demonstrably holds (verified by high-accuracy, low-entropy answers on held-out phrasings). GENUINELY-UNKNOWN items = obscure real facts the model answers at chance / high entropy, plus synthetic-in-context facts never in pretraining (guaranteed-unknown). ABSTENTION framings induce the model to decline: (a) SAFETY/POLICY framing that makes stating the (benign, verifiable) fact seem sensitive, (b) PROFESSED-UNCERTAINTY prompts that invite 'I'm not sure', (c) NEUTRAL baseline. Crucially, frame all items as declarative factual propositions to judge/answer (not genuinely harmful requests), so we study belief-gated abstention, not harmful-request refusal. Match surface length; human-verify knowledge-status, verifiability, and framing labels; include paraphrase sets.

Manipulation checks: Confirm cell membership behaviorally — KNOWN items answered correctly with low entropy under neutral framing; abstention framings actually elicit refusal/hedging; UNKNOWN items at chance. Separate items where the model genuinely abstains from those where it answers anyway.

Belief and abstention readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each item read (i) the internal belief in the correct proposition at every layer and (ii) the model's OUTPUT (assert correctly / abstain / refuse), scored by a rubric. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items.

Abstention Belief Persistence Gap measurement: Define Gap = internal belief in the correct proposition minus assertion success. Report per-layer, per-model the Gap across the knowledge-status x framing cells. Test the central hypothesis that the Gap is LARGE and positive specifically for KNOWN facts under abstention framings (belief high, assertion withheld) and near-zero for KNOWN-neutral; and that UNKNOWN facts show LOW belief (the model genuinely does not know), distinguishing belief-intact withholding from genuine ignorance. Locate where truth is lost across depth (belief established early, gated late).

Refusal/abstention-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'refusal/abstention' direction via difference-in-means on abstaining vs answering activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the refusal axis (and vice versa). Test the hypothesis that the refusal axis emerges/strengthens in LATE layers while the correct factual belief is established at EARLIER layers, and whether it aligns with a general refusal direction (compare to a Geometry-of-Refusal-style refusal direction).

Causal validation (belief-intact, late-gated): Activation patching. (a) Steer/ablate along the refusal axis at late layers and measure whether the abstained KNOWN facts are correctly asserted (refusal reduced) WITHOUT changing the earlier internal factual belief. (b) Confirm the correct belief for these items is established at earlier layers and unchanged by the late refusal intervention. (c) CRUCIAL CONTROL: apply the same refusal-axis intervention to GENUINELY-UNKNOWN items and verify it does NOT manufacture confident (wrong) assertions — the intervention should only unlock beliefs the model actually holds.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Abstention Belief Persistence Gap predicts a withholding-despite-knowing pattern: (i) abstaining on a fact the internal belief marks correct, and (ii) recoverability under the refusal-axis intervention. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (framing indicator, output entropy, refusal-keyword detection, neutral-framing truth-probe confidence, and a genuine-ignorance signal).

Downstream and safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) recovered faithful assertion of KNOWN abstained facts, (ii) PRESERVATION of GENUINELY-UNKNOWN items (must NOT hallucinate confident answers — the primary safety metric), (iii) PRESERVATION of legitimate refusal of a held-out set of genuinely HARMFUL requests (the intervention targets belief-gated abstention of benign facts, not harmful-request refusal — harmful requests must still be refused), (iv) RELIABILITY of an internal-belief honesty/consistency monitor behind the abstention gate (does abstention hide a readable, correct belief, and does the intervention preserve monitor readability?), (v) abstention appropriateness / calibration, and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, refusal-direction ablation (Geometry-of-Refusal style) as comparison, and prompt-based instruction to 'state benign true facts even if the framing seems sensitive, while refusing genuinely harmful requests'.

Ablations: layer choice (early belief vs late gate), probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), abstention framing (safety/policy vs professed-uncertainty), known vs unknown status, real vs synthetic-in-context facts, model scale, refusal-vs-truth axis disentangling, and generalization to abstention framings not used to fit the refusal direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent belief persistence could reflect the probe detecting framing lexical cues rather than a genuine intact belief; mitigate with surface-form/length matching, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the refusal-direction component and shows the truth belief is established early and unchanged by the late gate.

The 'intact belief' on abstained items might be probe artifact; the causal test resolves this — if late-stage refusal-axis intervention restores the CORRECT assertion, the belief was genuinely present, and the genuine-unknown control ensures the intervention only surfaces truly-held beliefs.

Distinguishing belief-intact withholding from genuine ignorance is the crux; we use the known-vs-unknown design, synthetic facts with guaranteed status, behavioral manipulation checks, and a decoded ignorance signal, and report label-noise sensitivity.

SAFETY RISK: the refusal-axis intervention could be misused to bypass legitimate safety refusals; we scope it to declarative benign factual belief, make the no-hallucination-on-unknowns control and the preserved-harmful-request-refusal metric primary success criteria, and frame the contribution as an interpretability/honesty-monitor finding rather than a jailbreak tool.

Refusal and truth directions may be partly entangled or the refusal axis may coincide with a general safety refusal direction; the orthogonality/project-out analyses and the Geometry-of-Refusal comparison directly test this, and a finding of overlap (abstention = refusal mechanism applied to facts) is itself informative.

The persistence gap may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (framing indicator, refusal-keyword detection, output entropy) for withholding-despite-knowing; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that abstention is a late-stage gate on an intact factual belief and that belief-based monitors remain readable behind it, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (safety-tuning likely creates or strengthens the abstention gate); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: surprisal_belief_fluency_bias
Title: Predictable-Is-True: Does a Claim's Token-Level Surprisal Distort an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, phrasing it so its tokens are more PREDICTABLE (low language-model surprisal) versus less predictable (high surprisal) systematically inflates the LLM's INTERNAL belief in it (linear truth-direction readout), an internal analogue of the human processing-fluency 'ease-is-truth' heuristic operating at the raw next-token-predictability level. This surprisal-driven belief bias is graded in the surprisal gap, carried by a decodable predictability/fluency component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a surprisal-driven factual-error mode (endorsing predictable-phrased falsehoods, doubting awkwardly-phrased truths), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the predictability component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never varies the raw next-token PREDICTABILITY (language-model surprisal) of the exact wording while holding meaning and truth-value fixed. Prior fluency-family proposals studied higher-level, semantic or stylistic substrates of the human ease-is-truth heuristic: my 'register_framing_belief_bias' varied stylistic tone, 'rhyme_elegance_belief_bias' varied phonological/aesthetic ease, 'vividness_detail_belief_inflation' varied concreteness and added detail, 'repetition_illusory_belief' varied prior exposure, and 'plausibility_vs_truth_belief' varied prior-consistency.
