NONE isolate the most primitive substrate — the model's OWN surprisal over meaning-preserving paraphrase pairs (a high-frequency-collocation wording vs a rare-but-equivalent one), with surprisal read directly from the model, length matched, and meaning-equivalence NLI/human-verified. This candidate tests whether low-surprisal wordings are internally believed more at fixed truth, whether the bias is graded in the surprisal gap even for false claims, whether it is carried by a decodable predictability component dissociable from the truth axis and from length, whether it causally predicts a surprisal-driven factual-error mode, and whether a lightweight intervention removing the predictability component neutralizes it. This surprisal-level fluency lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from the semantic and stylistic fluency proposals above.
Abstract: Humans judge easy-to-process statements as truer — the processing-fluency heuristic. Most fluency manipulations studied in LLM belief geometry are semantic or stylistic (register, rhyme, detail, plausibility); we isolate its most primitive substrate: the model's own next-token PREDICTABILITY (surprisal) of the exact wording, holding meaning and truth fixed. We ask whether a proposition phrased in low-surprisal tokens is internally believed more than the identical proposition phrased in high-surprisal tokens. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we construct SurprisalBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each rendered as meaning-preserving paraphrase pairs that differ in measured model surprisal (a common high-frequency-collocation wording vs a rare-but-equivalent wording), with meaning-equivalence verified by NLI/human check, surface length matched, and surprisal directly quantified from the model. We define a Surprisal Belief Bias Score = belief(low-surprisal wording) minus belief(high-surprisal wording) at fixed truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for low-surprisal wordings, graded in the surprisal gap, even for false claims; (2) the bias is carried by a decodable predictability component dissociable from the truth axis and from surface length; (3) bias magnitude causally predicts a surprisal-driven factual-error mode; and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the predictability component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure without harming fluent generation or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention. Because surprisal is directly measurable from the model itself, this is a uniquely clean, quantifiable fluency-bias test in belief geometry.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SurprisalBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). For each P create MEANING-PRESERVING paraphrase pairs that differ in the model's measured token SURPRISAL: a LOW-SURPRISAL wording (common phrasing / high-frequency collocations / expected word order) vs a HIGH-SURPRISAL wording (rare synonyms, unusual but grammatical word order, low-frequency-but-equivalent constructions) expressing the identical proposition. Directly measure and record the mean per-token surprisal of each wording from the target model; verify meaning equivalence via bidirectional NLI entailment plus human check; match surface LENGTH (token count) between pair members so bias is attributed to surprisal, not length. Grade the surprisal gap (small vs large). Include low/high-surprisal renderings of both true and false P (so effects are separable from truth-tracking); include neutral controls and multiple paraphrase pairs per P.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is this claim true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in P under each wording. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the low/high-surprisal wordings are judged meaning-equivalent behaviorally and that measured surprisal actually differs.

Surprisal Belief Bias measurement: Define Surprisal Belief Bias Score = belief(low-surprisal wording) minus belief(high-surprisal wording), controlling for the length-matched baseline, and regress belief on measured surprisal to obtain a per-token belief-vs-surprisal slope. Report per-layer, per-model bias as a function of the surprisal gap and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated for low-surprisal wordings, (ii) the effect is graded/monotone in the surprisal gap, and (iii) crucially, FALSE claims in low-surprisal wording are believed more true than their high-surprisal falsehoods. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (does the verdict/confidence rise for the predictable wording?).

Predictability-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'predictability/fluency' direction via difference-in-means on low-surprisal vs high-surprisal (length-matched) activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the predictability axis (and vice versa); disentangle predictability from surface length and lexical frequency via controlled regression; test whether the bias is explained by the predictability component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a low-surprisal and a matched high-surprisal rendering of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and predictability components, patch only the predictability component into the high-surprisal condition and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract it from the low-surprisal rendering and measure whether belief returns toward the content-driven value. Confirm the predictability signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Surprisal Belief Bias Score predicts a surprisal-driven factual-error mode: (i) endorsement rate of low-surprisal-phrased FALSE claims, (ii) under-endorsement/doubting of high-surprisal-phrased TRUE claims, and (iii) confident-wrong rate driven by phrasing predictability. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (measured surprisal alone, lexical frequency, output entropy, high-surprisal-wording truth-probe confidence).

Predictability De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the predictability/fluency direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the proposition's content rather than how predictable its wording is. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected high-surprisal-sensitive claims. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Surprisal Belief Bias Score and flattened belief-vs-surprisal slope, (ii) reduced endorsement of predictable-phrased falsehoods and reduced doubting of awkwardly-phrased truths, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on wording-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of fluent generation (grammaticality/fluency of outputs) and accuracy on low-surprisal-true controls (no over-correction), and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, self-consistency across paraphrase pairs, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge truth by content, not by how naturally the sentence reads'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), surprisal-gap size, low/high-surprisal rendering of true vs false P, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, length-matching method, predictability-vs-frequency-vs-length disentangling, whether the surprisal is measured by the same vs a different model, and generalization to wording styles and topics not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent surprisal bias could reflect the probe detecting the specific rare/common tokens (lexical cues) rather than a genuine predictability-driven belief shift; mitigate with length matching, a lexical-frequency-controlled regression, multiple paraphrase pairs per P, low/high-surprisal-for-true vs -for-false contrasts, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the predictability-direction component.

Ensuring low- and high-surprisal wordings are truly meaning-equivalent is nontrivial (rare phrasings can shift connotation); we use bidirectional-NLI filtering, human verification, and behavioral meaning-equivalence checks, and analyze items with imperfect equivalence separately.

Surprisal, truth, and lexical-frequency signals may be entangled in belief geometry, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out and frequency-controlled analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to high-surprisal renderings, so bias could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.

The De-biasing intervention could degrade fluent generation (making outputs prefer awkward phrasings) or harm capability; we explicitly measure generation fluency, low-surprisal-true accuracy, and general capability to characterize the tradeoff.

The bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (measured surprisal, lexical frequency, output entropy) for surprisal-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that raw token predictability distorts internal belief (a fluency-as-truth effect at the surprisal level, distinct from register/rhyme/detail/plausibility) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether processing-fluency-as-truth operates at the raw-predictability level in LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, tokenization, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/tokenization effects and negative results as informative.

Name: provenance_belief_inheritance_gap
Title: Confident Because Recalled, Uncertain Because Reasoned: Does the Firmness of an LLM's Belief Track How the Fact Was Acquired?
Short Hypothesis: For a fact the model has just come to accept within a context, a rational agent should hold a REASONED-THROUGH conclusion at least as firmly as a merely-ASSERTED (testimony) one, since the reasoned belief has explicit internal support. We hypothesize LLM belief geometry DECOUPLES firmness from acquisition route: a testimony-accepted fact is held as firmly as (or firmer than) an equivalently-derived one, a separable testimony-vs-reasoning axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, and this route-blindness causally predicts a testimony-brittleness failure mode (testimony facts collapse under mild challenge while reasoned ones resist) that a lightweight firmness-coupling intervention can correct.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief and its firmness but never conditions that firmness on HOW the fact was acquired — asserted (testimony) versus derived (reasoning) — for a proposition the model has just accepted in context. Work tying retraction to internal belief (When Do LLMs Admit Their Mistakes?, 2025) and susceptibility to injected evidence (The Facade of Truth, 2026) show beliefs move or collapse under context, but neither varies the JUSTIFICATION ROUTE while holding the target content and its truth fixed. My prior 'derivation_discount_belief' asked whether a self-derived conclusion is discounted relative to a stated one; 'evidentiality_belief_geometry' varied the first-hand-vs-hearsay MODE of knowing; 'understanding_vs_memorization_belief' separated a worked-through fact from a memorized one. NONE isolate the ROUTE-FIRMNESS COUPLING question here: whether a testimony-accepted fact is held as firmly as (or firmer than) an equivalently-derived one, whether a testimony-vs-reasoning axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out, whether low coupling causally predicts a testimony-brittleness mode (testimony facts collapse under a content-neutral challenge while reasoned facts resist), and whether a lightweight firmness-coupling intervention repairs robustness and calibration without harming retained truth. This acquisition-route firmness lens is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: Knowing that a fact is true is not the same as knowing why you accept it: you may believe it because you were told (testimony) or because you worked it out (reasoning). A careful believer holds a reasoned conclusion on firmer ground; we ask whether large language models honor this justification-route distinction inside their belief representations, or hold a merely-asserted fact just as firmly as one they derived. For a fact the model accepts within a context, we distinguish TESTIMONY-accepted facts (asserted, taken on trust) from REASONING-derived facts (concluded from in-context premises), and use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief and its firmness along the truth direction. We build RouteBelief, delivering the SAME target proposition either as a direct assertion or as the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation, using synthetic-in-context nonce facts (to guarantee validity and control priors) plus real facts, with surface length matched. We define a Route-Firmness Coupling Score and test four claims: (1) firmness is largely DECOUPLED from route; (2) a testimony-vs-reasoning axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis via project-out; (3) low coupling causally predicts a testimony-brittleness mode (testimony facts collapse under a content-neutral challenge/contradiction while reasoned facts resist); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling firmness to the decoded route improves robustness and calibration without harming reasoned facts or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on brittleness, calibration, and capability retention. This tests whether internal-belief-based safety monitors treat rote and reasoned beliefs equivalently — a reliability blind spot.
Experiments: Dataset: Build RouteBelief. For each TARGET proposition, deliver it via two matched routes at fixed content/truth: TESTIMONY (bare assertion 'X is true') vs REASONING (target is the valid conclusion of an in-context derivation — premises plus a sound chain — with the target itself never stated). Use SYNTHETIC nonce-entity chains ('all glorps are blints; all blints are zorns; this is a glorp' -> 'this is a zorn' vs simply asserting the conclusion) so validity is guaranteed and priors removed, plus a real-fact subset. Pad testimony with inert filler to match total length. Include FALSE-target and invalid-chain controls; paraphrase sets; human-verify validity/route labels.

Belief and firmness readout: For 4-5 open models (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements, Platt-scaled to [0,1]. Read belief and firmness (probe |belief-0.5| and a behavioral firmness = resistance to a fixed content-neutral challenge battery: 'are you sure?', 'a source says otherwise'). Manipulation check: probes separate clear true/false items; both routes yield high baseline belief (fact accepted); the model can restate the derivation (so contrast is route, not acceptance).

Route-Firmness Coupling: At matched baseline belief, compute Coupling Score = firmness(reasoned) minus firmness(testimony). Test the decoupling hypothesis (near-zero coupling). Report per-layer/model for synthetic and real items; compare internal firmness to output confidence.

Route-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a testimony-vs-reasoning direction (difference-in-means on route activations, balanced across truth/baseline-belief/content). Report decoding accuracy; cosine with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode route (and vice versa). Control for chain-present surface cues via matched-length filler and a features-only baseline (a pure surface-detector is an informative negative).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the route direction (truth axis fixed) and measure behavioral challenge-resistance shifts as predicted. (b) Patch the route component from a reasoned into a testimony target (matched content/belief) and measure induced firmness. Confirm causality and separability from truth/baseline belief.

Predictive validity: Test whether route/decoupling predicts testimony-brittleness: (i) testimony facts collapsing more than reasoned facts under mild challenge/distractor/in-context contradiction, (ii) over-confident-but-brittle miscalibration, (iii) paraphrase inconsistency. AUC/correlation vs baselines (baseline belief magnitude, output entropy, chain-present indicator, verbalized confidence).

Coupling intervention: Decode the route axis and apply an ITI-style firmness shift — lower firmness (toward revisability) for detected testimony-only facts, preserve/raise it for reasoned ones, gated on the decoded route. Sweep layer/strength.

Downstream evaluation: Post-intervention (i) improved calibration (ECE) that appropriately hedges brittle testimony facts, (ii) improved robustness-consistency (reasoned facts survive challenge; testimony facts held at lower revisable confidence and abandoned under genuine contradiction), (iii) PRESERVATION of reasoned-fact firmness and correct un-challenged testimony answers, (iv) capability retention (MMLU, perplexity). Baselines: no intervention, confidence-magnitude gating, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based 'be less certain of facts you were merely told'.

Ablations: layer/probe choice, synthetic vs real, derivation depth (1 vs multi-hop), firmness definition (probe vs behavioral), model scale, generalization of the route axis to held-out domains/chains.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The route axis may be confounded with derivation DEPTH (a 'derivation discount' where multi-hop conclusions are believed less) or with mere chain-presence; we match baseline belief, use 1-hop and multi-hop derivations, include a chain-present features-only baseline, and treat overlap with the derivation-discount phenomenon as an explicitly-analyzed relationship rather than a hidden confound.

The route axis may be nearly collinear with baseline belief magnitude or output entropy, making it redundant; we control baseline belief, regress out entropy, project out the truth direction, and treat redundancy as itself informative about whether epistemic route is a distinct belief coordinate.

Behavioral firmness depends on the challenge battery; we use a fixed, content-neutral, multi-form battery, report sensitivity, and test generalization to held-out challenges. Standardized challenges carry no genuine evidence, so realized change reflects fragility, not legitimate updating.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to reasoning-laden vs assertion contexts (prior work shows broad but imperfect transfer); use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clear true/false items, synthetic facts to control priors, and causal patching to corroborate.

The coupling intervention could over-hedge reasoned facts or fail to lower firmness if the axis is weak; we measure preservation of reasoned-fact firmness, correct un-challenged testimony answers, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Route may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (baseline belief, entropy, chain-present) for testimony brittleness; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding about whether belief firmness is (de)coupled from justification route, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may strengthen the route signal); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: blame_attribution_belief_geometry
Title: Whose Fault Is the Wrong Answer? Do LLM Internal Beliefs Track the Causal Locus of an Error in a Multi-Step Chain?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM reaches a wrong conclusion because ONE identifiable in-context step (a false premise, a mis-computation, a corrupted retrieved fact) was faulty while the rest of the chain was valid, a competent reasoner should internally localize the blame to that specific faulty step — holding low belief in the faulty step's output while holding appropriate belief in the downstream-conditional-on-inputs steps. We hypothesize LLM belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL to localize blame: the decoded belief in each step is dominated by whether it agrees with the (wrong) final conclusion rather than by the step's own local validity, so belief in a locally-valid step is deflated merely because it sits downstream of an error (contamination) and belief in the faulty step is inflated merely because it is consistent with the emitted answer. This blame-mislocalization is graded, carried by a decodable global-consistency component dissociable from a step's local-validity signal, causally predicts an error-attribution failure mode (the model cannot identify which step went wrong), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that re-anchors per-step belief to local validity.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar per-item belief but never asks whether, in a multi-step chain that reaches a WRONG conclusion because exactly ONE step was faulty, per-step belief localizes blame to that step rather than being contaminated by mere agreement with the final answer. My prior 'step_belief_load_bearing' measured how much each step's belief bears the weight of a conclusion; 'dependency_structured_belief_revision' tested whether revising a foundation propagates along the evidential-dependency graph; 'explaining_away_belief_geometry' studied competing-cause discounting; 'latent_contradiction_belief_detection' probed whether the model registers an internal inconsistency at all. NONE isolate the BLAME-LOCALIZATION question here: whether per-step belief tracks each step's own local validity (given its inputs) or is dominated by a decodable global-consistency-with-the-final-answer component, so that belief in a locally-valid step is DEFLATED merely for sitting downstream of the fault (contamination) while belief in the faulty step is INFLATED merely for agreeing with the emitted answer. Using single-injected-fault chains with per-step ground truth, this candidate tests whether mislocalization is graded, whether the global-consistency component is dissociable from local validity, whether it causally predicts an error-attribution failure mode, and whether a lightweight re-anchoring intervention restores per-step belief to local validity. This blame-attribution lens is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: When a chain of reasoning produces a wrong answer, a good reasoner can say which step was to blame: a false premise, a bad calculation, a corrupted fact — not the innocent steps around it. We ask whether large language models can localize blame inside their belief representations, or whether their per-step belief is instead contaminated by mere agreement with the final (wrong) conclusion. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we present multi-step chains in which exactly one step is faulty while all other steps are locally valid given their inputs, and read the model's internal belief in each step's output. A competent reasoner should hold low belief in the faulty step and correct, input-conditional belief in the locally-valid steps regardless of their position relative to the error. We construct BlameBelief, a controlled dataset of arithmetic, logical, and factual-retrieval chains with a single injected fault at a controlled position, using synthetic-in-context chains (to guarantee ground-truth per-step validity and remove parametric priors) plus a real-fact subset, with surface forms matched. We define a Blame-Localization Score (does per-step belief track local validity rather than agreement with the final conclusion?) and a Contamination Score (deflation of belief in locally-valid steps merely for being downstream of the fault). We test four claims: (1) belief fails to localize blame — per-step belief tracks global consistency with the emitted answer rather than local validity, so valid steps downstream of the error are deflated and the faulty step is inflated; (2) a decodable global-consistency component is dissociable from a step's local-validity signal; (3) blame-mislocalization causally predicts an error-attribution failure mode (the model cannot identify which step went wrong); and (4) a lightweight intervention that re-anchors per-step belief to local validity improves error localization and reduces contamination without harming correct-chain judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on error-localization accuracy, calibration, and capability retention. Our results reframe LLM self-diagnosis as a per-step belief-attribution problem and expose blame contamination as a measurable, fixable failure of belief geometry.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build BlameBelief. Each item is a MULTI-STEP CHAIN (length 3-6) whose steps each have a locally-checkable output, with EXACTLY ONE injected FAULT at a controlled position while every OTHER step is LOCALLY VALID given its (possibly-corrupted) inputs. Fault types: (a) FALSE-PREMISE (a starting fact is wrong), (b) MIS-COMPUTATION (one arithmetic/logical step is invalid), (c) CORRUPTED-RETRIEVAL (one retrieved fact is wrong). Crucially, downstream steps are LOCALLY VALID (correct given their inputs) even though their outputs are globally wrong because they inherited the fault — this dissociates local validity from global correctness. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context chains (arithmetic and nonce-entity logical/relational chains stipulated in context) to guarantee exact per-step local-validity and global-correctness ground truth and remove parametric priors, plus a REAL-FACT subset. Vary FAULT POSITION (early/middle/late) so contamination-vs-position can be traced. Include CORRECT-CHAIN controls (no fault, all steps globally correct) and matched surface forms; per step, label LOCAL-VALIDITY (correct given inputs) and GLOBAL-CORRECTNESS (matches the true answer). Human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After the chain and its (wrong) conclusion are present in context, at a matched query position read the internal belief in EACH step's output proposition ('step k's stated result is correct'). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the chain (can restate each step's inputs/output); establish that on isolated single steps the probe correctly tracks local validity.

Blame-Localization & Contamination measurement: A blame-localizing model should have belief(step) track LOCAL VALIDITY — low for the faulty step, high for locally-valid steps — regardless of each step's global correctness or position relative to the fault. Via a per-step regression of decoded belief on (i) local validity and (ii) global consistency with the emitted answer, define a Blame-Localization Score = local-validity coefficient dominating, and a Contamination Score = deflation of belief in locally-valid-but-downstream-of-fault steps relative to matched locally-valid steps in correct chains. Report per-layer, per-model scores as a function of fault type and position. Test the hypotheses that (i) per-step belief tracks global consistency rather than local validity (valid downstream steps deflated, faulty step inflated toward the answer), and (ii) contamination grows with distance downstream of the fault. Compare internal blame-localization to OUTPUT-level behavior (asking the model to name the faulty step).

Global-consistency-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'global-consistency' direction via difference-in-means on step activations that agree vs disagree with the emitted (wrong) conclusion (balanced across local validity and content), and separately a 'local-validity' signal from the isolated-step probe. Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among global-consistency, local-validity, and the truth direction; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether blame-mislocalization corresponds to the global-consistency component dominating the per-step belief readout while the local-validity signal under-modulates it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the local-validity signal for a downstream valid step (holding global-consistency fixed) and measure whether its belief and the output attribution move toward correctly crediting it. (b) Patch the global-consistency component from a correct-chain step into a downstream-of-fault step (matched local validity) and measure induced contamination. (c) In synthetic chains, patch the faulty step's representation and measure whether per-step beliefs re-localize. Confirm the global-consistency signal causally drives blame-mislocalization and that amplifying local-validity corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Blame-Localization / Contamination Scores predict an error-attribution failure mode: (i) the model naming the wrong step as the culprit (or blaming a valid downstream step) when asked to localize the error, (ii) failure to correctly identify the faulty step in error-localization QA, and (iii) inconsistency across fault positions and paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (fault position alone, output entropy, final-conclusion truth-probe confidence).

Local-Validity Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the local-validity signal (from the isolated-step probe) and the global-consistency component, and steer each step's belief readout toward its local-validity value while subtracting the global-consistency contamination at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so per-step belief reflects local validity rather than agreement with the emitted answer. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-step chains. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) improved Blame-Localization / reduced Contamination Scores, (ii) improved error-localization accuracy (correctly identifying the faulty step) on BlameBelief and adapted process-supervision / step-verification benchmarks (e.g. PRM800K-style step-error datasets), (iii) calibration (ECE) of per-step correctness judgments, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct per-step and final judgments on CORRECT-CHAIN controls (no spurious blame) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought self-critique ('check each step'), and prompt-based instruction to 'judge each step by whether it follows from its inputs, not by whether it matches the final answer'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), fault type (false-premise/mis-computation/corrupted-retrieval), fault position, chain length, synthetic vs real-fact chains, model scale, distance between fault and probed step, and generalization to chain structures and domains not used to fit the global-consistency direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent blame-mislocalization could reflect the model failing to COMPUTE local validity of a step (a reasoning failure) rather than a belief-attribution failure; we manipulation-check that the probe tracks local validity on ISOLATED single steps and that the model can restate each step's inputs/output, and analyze within-reach vs beyond-reach steps separately.

Apparent contamination could reflect the probe detecting surface agreement with the final-answer tokens rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched surface forms, correct-chain controls, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context chains with exact per-step ground truth, and causal patching that isolates the global-consistency vs local-validity components.

Distinguishing local validity from global correctness is the crux and is only clean when constructed; we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic chains where per-step local-validity and global-correctness are stipulated exactly, and treat real-fact chains (where step decomposition is fuzzier) as secondary.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to intermediate reasoning-step propositions, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, isolated-step manipulation checks, and synthetic chains to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

Global-consistency, local-validity, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that local validity is NOT separately represented (only global consistency drives belief) is itself an informative result.

The Re-anchoring intervention could over-credit genuinely faulty steps or spuriously blame valid ones if the local-validity signal is noisy, or harm fluency; we explicitly measure correct-chain preservation (no spurious blame) and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing wrong attributions.

Blame-mislocalization may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (fault position, output entropy) for error-attribution failure; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that per-step belief tracks global consistency rather than local validity (blame contamination in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (process-supervision / reasoning-tuning may improve blame localization); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: dependency_structured_belief_revision
Title: Pulling One Thread: Do LLM Beliefs Propagate Revision Along Evidential-Dependency Structure?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM holds a foundational belief F and other beliefs that evidentially DEPEND on F (they were accepted because of F) alongside beliefs INDEPENDENT of F, a rational agent that revises F should propagate the revision to the dependents (their internal belief should move) while leaving independent beliefs untouched. We hypothesize LLM belief geometry FAILS dependency-structured propagation: revising a foundational belief updates the model's internal belief (linear truth-direction readout) in its dependents far too weakly (under-propagation, leaving orphaned beliefs), while spuriously perturbing independent beliefs (over-propagation), because propagation tracks surface/associative proximity rather than the evidential-dependency graph. This mislocalized propagation is decodable as a dependency-vs-independence signal dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an orphaned-belief inconsistency mode, and can be corrected by a lightweight intervention that routes revision along the dependency structure.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief per proposition but never asks whether, when a FOUNDATIONAL belief is revised in context, the revision propagates along the EVIDENTIAL-DEPENDENCY structure — moving beliefs accepted because of the foundation while leaving independent beliefs untouched. Work on linear representations of synthetic truth and deception (When LLMs Learn to Be Consistently Wrong, 2026) reads a stable internal truth signal but treats beliefs as a flat set, not a dependency web. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' studied deductive updating under accepted premises; 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' measured resistance to a single belief's revision; 'explaining_away_belief_geometry' studied competing-cause discounting; 'belief_ghost_revision' asked whether a retracted belief still lingers. NONE isolate DEPENDENCY-STRUCTURED PROPAGATION: whether revising F under-propagates to its dependents (orphaned beliefs that fail to move) while over-propagating to independents, because propagation tracks surface/associative proximity rather than the dependency graph — with proximity balanced so the effect cannot be a lexical-overlap artifact. This candidate tests whether a dependency-vs-independence relationship is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, whether mislocalized propagation causally predicts an orphaned-belief inconsistency mode, and whether a lightweight intervention routing revision along the dependency structure corrects it. This dependency-graph propagation lens is new and distinct from all prior proposals.
Abstract: A coherent believer's beliefs are not a flat list but a dependency web: some facts are held only because of others, so revising a foundation should cascade to what rests on it, while leaving unrelated beliefs alone. We ask whether large language models honor this evidential-dependency structure inside their belief representations when a foundational belief is revised in context. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the truth direction, we establish a foundational belief F, a set of DEPENDENT beliefs (accepted because F holds) and a set of INDEPENDENT beliefs, then revise F and read how each belief's internal belief moves. We construct DependBelief, controlled dependency graphs over synthetic-in-context facts (nonce entities/rules that make dependency ground-truth exact and remove priors) plus a real-fact subset, with surface/associative proximity balanced across dependent and independent beliefs so propagation cannot be a mere lexical-overlap artifact. We define an Under-Propagation Score (failure of dependents to move when F is revised) and an Over-Propagation Score (spurious movement of independents), and test four claims: (1) revision propagation is mislocalized — dependents under-update and independents over-update, tracking associative proximity rather than the dependency graph; (2) a dependency-vs-independence relationship is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) mislocalized propagation causally predicts an orphaned-belief inconsistency mode (the model still asserts a dependent whose sole support was retracted, and doubts an untouched independent); and (4) a lightweight intervention that routes the revision shift along the decoded dependency structure improves propagation and reduces orphaning without harming independent beliefs or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on post-revision consistency, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build DependBelief. Each item establishes a FOUNDATIONAL belief F in context, a set of DEPENDENT beliefs (each explicitly derived from / accepted because of F, so retracting F removes their support), and a set of INDEPENDENT beliefs (accepted on separate grounds, unaffected by F). Use SYNTHETIC-in-context dependency graphs over nonce entities/rules (e.g. 'because glorps are toxic (F), the red barrel is dangerous (dependent); separately, the blue crate is heavy (independent)') so dependency is exact and priors are removed, plus a real-fact subset. CRUCIALLY balance SURFACE/ASSOCIATIVE PROXIMITY (topical relatedness, lexical overlap to F) across dependent and independent beliefs — including near-associate independents and topically-distant dependents — so propagation tracking dependency vs proximity can be dissociated. Then present a REVISION of F (F is retracted/flipped). Include a no-revision baseline, graph-depth variation (direct dependents vs chained dependents), and matched surface forms; human-verify dependency and independence labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read the internal belief in F, each dependent, and each independent (i) before revision (baseline) and (ii) after F is revised, at matched query positions. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model initially holds F, the dependents, and the independents, and comprehends the dependency structure (can state why each dependent was accepted).

Under- and Over-Propagation measurement: After revising F, a dependency-respecting model should show LARGE belief movement in dependents (toward retracted/uncertain) and NEAR-ZERO movement in independents. Define Under-Propagation Score = shortfall of belief movement in dependents relative to the movement warranted by the retracted support; Over-Propagation Score = spurious belief movement in independents. Report per-layer, per-model scores as a function of graph depth and proximity condition. Test the hypotheses that (i) dependents under-update, (ii) independents over-update, and (iii) both errors track ASSOCIATIVE PROXIMITY rather than the true dependency graph (near-associate independents move most; distant dependents move least). Compare internal propagation to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model still assert an orphaned dependent when asked?).

Dependency-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'dependency-to-F' direction via difference-in-means on dependent vs independent belief activations (balanced across truth-value, proximity, and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (is a belief's evidential dependence on F decodable?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction and with a surface-proximity/embedding signal; project out the truth direction and re-decode dependency (and vice versa). Test whether propagation failures correspond to the model routing revision along a proximity signal rather than the dependency axis.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the dependency-to-F direction and measure whether the revision-induced shift is correctly routed to dependents (their belief moves) and withheld from independents, holding the truth axis fixed. (b) Patch the retracted-F representation into the dependent-query and measure whether the dependent's belief drops as it should. (c) Conversely, patch a proximity component and induce spurious movement in independents. Confirm the dependency structure causally governs (or fails to govern) propagation and that proximity causally drives the errors.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Under-/Over-Propagation Scores predict an orphaned-belief inconsistency mode: (i) the model still asserting a dependent whose sole support (F) was retracted, (ii) the model doubting an independent whose support is untouched, and (iii) inconsistency across dependency paraphrases and graph depth. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (associative proximity alone, output entropy, baseline truth-probe confidence).

Dependency-Routed Revision intervention: At inference, estimate the dependency-to-F direction (from the probe) and route the revision shift along it — an ITI-style operation that propagates the belief change to detected dependents (dampening their belief toward the retracted-support value) while subtracting spurious shifts from detected independents, at a chosen layer. Provide a deployment variant that reads the dependency structure from context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) improved propagation (dependents correctly updated, independents preserved) / reduced Under- and Over-Propagation Scores, (ii) improved post-revision consistency and reduced orphaned-belief assertions on DependBelief and adapted belief-revision / knowledge-conflict QA, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of INDEPENDENT beliefs (must NOT be perturbed — the core specificity check) and accuracy on no-revision and clearly-true/false controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Title: Whose Fault Is the Wrong Answer? Do LLM Internal Beliefs Localize the Faulty Step in a Multi-Step Chain, or Contaminate Innocent Steps?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM reaches a wrong conclusion because ONE identifiable in-context step is faulty (a false premise, a mis-computation, a corrupted retrieved fact) while every other step is locally valid given its inputs, a competent reasoner should internally localize blame to that step — holding low belief in the faulty step and correct, input-conditional belief in the innocent steps. We hypothesize LLM belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL to localize blame: per-step belief is dominated by whether the step AGREES with the emitted (wrong) final answer rather than by the step's own local validity, so locally-valid steps downstream of the error are deflated (contamination) and the faulty step is inflated. This blame-mislocalization is decodable as a global-consistency component dissociable from a local-validity signal, causally predicts an error-attribution failure mode, and can be reduced by re-anchoring per-step belief to local validity.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief per proposition but never asks whether that belief, evaluated on an INTERMEDIATE step of a multi-step chain, tracks the step's own LOCAL VALIDITY or merely its AGREEMENT with the emitted (wrong) final answer. Bao et al. (2025) show truth directions generalize across logical transformations of a single statement, and 'From Directions to Cones' (Yu et al. 2025) extends truth to multidimensional propositional-fact geometry, but both evaluate isolated propositions, not blame across a dependency chain; the Hypocrisy Gap (Shiromani et al. 2026) contrasts internal belief with chain-of-thought explanation yet does not localize which step is at fault. My prior 'step_belief_load_bearing' asked which steps carry a chain's belief; 'within_context_answer_anchoring_belief' showed belief anchoring to a stated context answer; 'belief_coherence_geometry' studied deductive updating under accepted premises; 'dependency_structured_belief_revision' traced revision along a dependency graph. NONE isolate error ATTRIBUTION — whether per-step belief correctly credits locally-valid steps and blames the single faulty one, or instead contaminates innocent downstream steps because a global-consistency component (agreement with the wrong conclusion) dominates a dissociable local-validity signal — nor tie this mislocalization causally to an error-attribution failure mode, nor re-anchor per-step belief to local validity. This blame-localization lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from all the above.
Abstract: When a chain of reasoning produces a wrong answer, a good reasoner can say which step was to blame — not the innocent steps around it. We ask whether large language models can localize blame inside their belief representations, or whether their per-step belief is contaminated by mere agreement with the final (wrong) conclusion. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we present multi-step chains with exactly one injected fault while every other step is locally valid given its (possibly-corrupted) inputs, and read the model's internal belief in each step's output. A competent reasoner should hold low belief in the faulty step and correct input-conditional belief in locally-valid steps regardless of their position relative to the error. We build BlameBelief, controlled arithmetic, logical, and factual-retrieval chains with a single injected fault at a controlled position, using synthetic-in-context chains (exact per-step local-validity/global-correctness ground truth, no priors) plus a real-fact subset, surface forms matched. We define a Blame-Localization Score (does per-step belief track local validity rather than agreement with the final answer?) and a Contamination Score (deflation of belief in valid steps merely for being downstream of the fault). We test four claims: (1) per-step belief tracks global consistency with the emitted answer rather than local validity, so valid downstream steps are deflated and the faulty step inflated; (2) a decodable global-consistency component is dissociable from a local-validity signal; (3) blame-mislocalization causally predicts an error-attribution failure mode (the model cannot identify which step went wrong); and (4) an inference-time intervention re-anchoring per-step belief to local validity improves error localization and reduces contamination without harming correct-chain judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on error-localization accuracy, calibration, and capability retention. Our results reframe LLM self-diagnosis as a per-step belief-attribution problem and expose blame contamination as a measurable, fixable failure of belief geometry.

1) Dataset construction (BlameBelief): Build multi-step chains of length 3-6 whose steps each have a locally-checkable output, injecting EXACTLY ONE fault at a controlled position while every other step is LOCALLY VALID given its (possibly-corrupted) inputs. Fault types: (a) FALSE-PREMISE (a starting fact is wrong), (b) MIS-COMPUTATION (one arithmetic/logical step is invalid), (c) CORRUPTED-RETRIEVAL (one retrieved fact is wrong). Downstream steps remain locally valid (correct given their inputs) yet globally wrong because they inherit the fault, dissociating local validity from global correctness. Use SYNTHETIC in-context chains (arithmetic and nonce-entity relational chains stipulated in context) for exact per-step local-validity and global-correctness ground truth free of parametric priors, plus a REAL-FACT subset. Vary FAULT POSITION (early/middle/late), add CORRECT-CHAIN controls (no fault) with matched surface forms, label each step for LOCAL-VALIDITY and GLOBAL-CORRECTNESS, human-verify, and include paraphrase sets.

2) Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Report per-layer/per-model scores by fault type and position; test that per-step belief tracks global consistency rather than local validity and that contamination grows with downstream distance; compare to OUTPUT-level behavior (asking the model to name the faulty step).

Test whether mislocalization corresponds to the global-consistency component dominating while local-validity under-modulates the readout.

Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (fault position alone, output entropy, final-conclusion truth-probe confidence).

Crucially, downstream steps are LOCALLY VALID (correct given their inputs) even though their outputs are globally wrong because they inherited the fault — dissociating local validity from global correctness. Use SYNTHETIC-in-context chains (arithmetic and nonce-entity logical/relational chains stipulated in context) for exact per-step local-validity and global-correctness ground truth with no priors, plus a REAL-FACT subset. Vary FAULT POSITION (early/middle/late) so contamination-vs-position can be traced. Include CORRECT-CHAIN controls (no fault) and matched surface forms; per step, label LOCAL-VALIDITY and GLOBAL-CORRECTNESS. Human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After the chain and its (wrong) conclusion are in context, at a matched query position read the internal belief in EACH step's output proposition ('step k's stated result is correct'). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the chain (can restate each step's inputs/output); establish that on ISOLATED single steps the probe correctly tracks local validity.

Blame-Localization & Contamination measurement: A blame-localizing model should have belief(step) track LOCAL VALIDITY — low for the faulty step, high for locally-valid steps — regardless of each step's global correctness or position. Via a per-step regression of decoded belief on (i) local validity and (ii) global consistency with the emitted answer, define a Blame-Localization Score = local-validity coefficient dominating, and a Contamination Score = deflation of belief in locally-valid-but-downstream-of-fault steps relative to matched locally-valid steps in correct chains. Report per-layer, per-model scores as a function of fault type and position. Test the hypotheses that (i) per-step belief tracks global consistency rather than local validity, and (ii) contamination grows with distance downstream of the fault. Compare internal blame-localization to OUTPUT-level behavior (asking the model to name the faulty step).

Global-consistency-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'global-consistency' direction via difference-in-means on step activations that agree vs disagree with the emitted (wrong) conclusion (balanced across local validity and content), and separately a 'local-validity' signal from the isolated-step probe. Report per-layer decoding accuracy of each; measure cosine similarities among global-consistency, local-validity, and the truth direction; project out one and re-decode the others. Test whether blame-mislocalization corresponds to the global-consistency component dominating the per-step belief readout while the local-validity signal under-modulates it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the local-validity signal for a downstream valid step (holding global-consistency fixed) and measure whether its belief and the output attribution move toward correctly crediting it. (b) Patch the global-consistency component from a correct-chain step into a downstream-of-fault step (matched local validity) and measure induced contamination. (c) In synthetic chains, patch the faulty step's representation and measure whether per-step beliefs re-localize. Confirm the global-consistency signal causally drives blame-mislocalization and that amplifying local-validity corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Blame-Localization / Contamination Scores predict an error-attribution failure mode: (i) the model naming the wrong step as the culprit (or blaming a valid downstream step) when asked to localize the error, (ii) failure to correctly identify the faulty step in error-localization QA, and (iii) inconsistency across fault positions and paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (fault position alone, output entropy, final-conclusion truth-probe confidence).

Local-Validity Re-anchoring intervention: At inference, estimate the local-validity signal (from the isolated-step probe) and the global-consistency component, and steer each step's belief readout toward its local-validity value while subtracting the global-consistency contamination at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so per-step belief reflects local validity rather than agreement with the emitted answer. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected multi-step chains. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) improved Blame-Localization / reduced Contamination Scores, (ii) improved error-localization accuracy (correctly identifying the faulty step) on BlameBelief and adapted process-supervision / step-verification benchmarks (e.g. PRM800K-style step-error datasets), (iii) calibration (ECE) of per-step correctness judgments, (iv) PRESERVATION of correct per-step and final judgments on CORRECT-CHAIN controls (no spurious blame) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought self-critique ('check each step'), and prompt-based instruction to 'judge each step by whether it follows from its inputs, not by whether it matches the final answer'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), fault type (false-premise/mis-computation/corrupted-retrieval), fault position, chain length, synthetic vs real-fact chains, model scale, distance between fault and probed step, and generalization to chain structures and domains not used to fit the global-consistency direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent blame-mislocalization could reflect the model failing to COMPUTE local validity of a step (a reasoning failure) rather than a belief-attribution failure; we manipulation-check that the probe tracks local validity on ISOLATED single steps and that the model can restate each step's inputs/output, and analyze within-reach vs beyond-reach steps separately.

Apparent contamination could reflect the probe detecting surface agreement with the final-answer tokens rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched surface forms, correct-chain controls, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context chains with exact per-step ground truth, and causal patching that isolates the global-consistency vs local-validity components.

Distinguishing local validity from global correctness is only clean when constructed; we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic chains where per-step local-validity and global-correctness are stipulated exactly, and treat real-fact chains (where step decomposition is fuzzier) as secondary.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to intermediate reasoning-step propositions, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, isolated-step manipulation checks, and synthetic chains to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

Global-consistency, local-validity, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that local validity is NOT separately represented (only global consistency drives belief) is itself an informative result.

The Re-anchoring intervention could over-credit genuinely faulty steps or spuriously blame valid ones if the local-validity signal is noisy, or harm fluency; we explicitly measure correct-chain preservation (no spurious blame) and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing wrong attributions.

Blame-mislocalization may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (fault position, output entropy) for error-attribution failure; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that per-step belief tracks global consistency rather than local validity (blame contamination in belief geometry) plus the re-anchoring tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (process-supervision / reasoning-tuning may improve blame localization); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterexample_belief_sensitivity
Title: One Counterexample Should Do It: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Properly Weaken a Universal Claim When Given a Single Refuting Instance?
Short Hypothesis: For a universal claim ('all X are Y', 'X always Z'), a single valid COUNTEREXAMPLE logically refutes it, so a rational believer's internal belief in the universal should drop sharply to false. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) are systematically UNDER-SENSITIVE to counterexamples: after one refuting instance is presented in context, the decoded belief in the universal barely moves, instead tracking how many supporting instances remain, so the model still internally 'believes' a demonstrably-falsified generalization. This counterexample-insensitivity is graded (worse with more prior supporting instances), carried by a decodable support-count component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a falsified-universal endorsement mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that couples belief in the universal to the presence of a counterexample.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief in a proposition but never asks whether the internal belief in a UNIVERSAL claim ('all X are Y', 'X always Z') properly COLLAPSES toward false once a single valid COUNTEREXAMPLE is presented in context, or instead tracks how many supporting instances remain. Bao et al. (2025) show truth directions generalize across logical transformations of one statement, but treat each statement's truth as fixed, not as a quantity that a lone refuting instance should logically defeat. My prior 'quantifier_belief_aggregation' studied how belief aggregates over a quantifier's instances; 'conjunction_belief_monotonicity' tested monotone belief under added conjuncts; 'defeasible_override_belief_geometry' studied belief under later-arriving defeaters; 'belief_evidence_weighting' tracked how confirming vs disconfirming evidence is weighed. NONE isolate the asymmetric LOGIC of universal falsification — whether one counterexample sharply drops belief in the universal (as it logically must) or is under-weighted relative to a decodable support-COUNT component that keeps a demonstrably-falsified generalization internally 'believed', worsening with more prior supporting instances, causally predicting a falsified-universal endorsement mode, and correctable by coupling belief in the universal to counterexample presence. This single-counterexample-sensitivity lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from all the above.
Abstract: A universal generalization is only as strong as its weakest case: a single genuine counterexample makes 'all swans are white' false, no matter how many white swans preceded it. We ask whether large language models honor this asymmetry inside their belief representations, or whether one refuting instance fails to dislodge a generalization they have accumulated support for. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we present a universal claim together with supporting instances and then a single valid counterexample, and read how the internal belief in the universal moves. We construct CounterBelief, a controlled dataset of universal claims (real generics with true exceptions, and synthetic-in-context rules over nonce entities that guarantee validity and remove priors) each paired with a number of supporting instances and a single logically-valid counterexample, with support-count graded and matched no-counterexample controls. We define a Counterexample Sensitivity Score (drop in belief in the universal after one valid counterexample) and a Support-Count Bias (extent to which residual belief tracks the number of remaining supporting instances rather than the presence of the refuter). We test four claims: (1) internal belief is under-sensitive to counterexamples, dropping far less than logic requires and less as prior support grows; (2) a decodable support-count component is dissociable from the truth axis and dominates the counterexample signal; (3) counterexample-insensitivity causally predicts a falsified-universal endorsement mode (the model still asserts the universal after seeing a case that refutes it); and (4) a lightweight intervention that couples belief in the universal to the decoded counterexample signal restores appropriate refutation without harming genuinely-unrefuted universals or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on universal-refutation accuracy, calibration, and capability retention. Our results test whether LLM belief geometry respects the logical asymmetry between confirmation and refutation.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CounterBelief. Each item = a UNIVERSAL claim ('all X are Y', 'X always Z') plus a set of SUPPORTING INSTANCES (individual cases consistent with the universal) and then a single valid COUNTEREXAMPLE (a case that logically refutes the universal). Use (a) SYNTHETIC-in-context rules over nonce entities ('all glorps are blue' + several blue glorps + one green glorp) so validity and ground-truth are exact and priors removed, and (b) a REAL-GENERIC subset (well-known universals with genuine exceptions, e.g. 'all birds fly' refuted by a penguin instance). Grade SUPPORT COUNT (0, 1, 3, 6 supporting instances before the counterexample). Include: NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls (only supporting instances, universal genuinely holds — belief should stay high); a NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE control (an extra case that is consistent, not a counterexample, so belief should not drop); and matched surface forms. Human-verify that the counterexample is genuinely valid/refuting and that supporting instances are consistent; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read the internal belief in the UNIVERSAL claim (i) after only supporting instances (baseline, universal should be believed) and (ii) after the single counterexample is added (universal should now be disbelieved). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the counterexample (can restate that the instance violates the universal).

Counterexample Sensitivity & Support-Count Bias measurement: Define Counterexample Sensitivity Score = drop in belief in the universal from baseline to post-counterexample (a rational model drops toward false regardless of prior support). Define Support-Count Bias = extent to which the residual post-counterexample belief increases with the number of prior supporting instances. Report per-layer, per-model as a function of support count, for synthetic and real items. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is under-sensitive (small drop), and (ii) the drop shrinks as prior support grows (confirmation swamps refutation). Contrast with NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls (belief should not drop) and NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls (belief should stay high). Compare internal sensitivity to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model still assert the universal after the counterexample?).

Support-count-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'support-count' direction via difference-in-means on high-support vs low-support activations (balanced across whether a counterexample is present and across content), and separately a 'counterexample-present' signal. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarities among support-count, counterexample-present, and the truth directions; project out the truth direction and re-decode each (and vice versa). Test whether counterexample-insensitivity corresponds to the support-count component dominating the universal's belief readout while the counterexample signal under-modulates it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the counterexample-present signal at a chosen layer and measure whether belief in the universal and the output refutation increase, holding support-count fixed. (b) Patch the counterexample representation into a no-counterexample context and measure whether the universal's belief drops as required. (c) Conversely, patch a high-support-count component into a refuted item and measure induced spurious re-inflation of the universal's belief. Confirm the support-count signal causally drives insensitivity and that amplifying the counterexample signal corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Counterexample Sensitivity / Support-Count Bias Scores predict a falsified-universal endorsement mode: (i) the model still asserting a universal after a valid counterexample, (ii) universal-refutation QA errors ('given this counterexample, is the claim still true?'), and (iii) inconsistency across support-count and paraphrase variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (support count alone, output entropy, baseline truth-probe confidence).

Counterexample-Coupling intervention: At inference, estimate the counterexample-present signal (from the probe) and add a scaled shift along the truth direction that drives belief in the universal toward false when a valid counterexample is detected, gated by the decoded signal (ITI-style), overriding the support-count contribution. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected universal-claim + instance structure. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Counterexample Sensitivity / reduced Support-Count Bias, (ii) improved universal-refutation accuracy (correctly rejecting refuted universals) on CounterBelief and adapted generics/exception and logical-consistency benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of belief in genuinely-UNREFUTED universals (NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE and NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls must NOT be suppressed — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('check whether any instance violates the claim'), and prompt-based instruction to 'treat a single valid counterexample as refuting a universal claim'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), support count, synthetic vs real-generic items, counterexample position (immediately after vs distant from supporting instances), model scale, and generalization to universal-claim structures and domains not used to fit the counterexample/support-count directions.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent counterexample-insensitivity could reflect the model failing to RECOGNIZE the instance as a counterexample (a comprehension failure, not a belief-coupling failure); we manipulation-check that the model can state the instance violates the universal and analyze recognized vs non-recognized items separately.

Apparent insensitivity or support-count bias could reflect the probe detecting surface instance-count/lexical cues rather than genuine belief; mitigate with matched surface forms, NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE and NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context rules with exact ground truth, and causal patching that isolates the support-count vs counterexample components.

For real generics, 'all birds fly' is arguably a defeasible generic rather than a strict universal, so a penguin need not make it 'false'; we anchor quantitative claims on SYNTHETIC strict-universal rules where a counterexample is unambiguously refuting, and analyze real generics separately (relating to, but distinct from, defeasible-default reasoning).

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to universal claims, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic rules to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

Support-count, counterexample, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that the counterexample is NOT separately represented (only support-count drives belief) is itself informative.

The Counterexample-Coupling intervention could over-suppress genuinely-unrefuted universals (spurious refutation) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE and NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing false refutations.

Counterexample-insensitivity may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (support count, output entropy) for falsified-universal endorsement; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry violates the confirmation/refutation asymmetry (under-weighting counterexamples relative to accumulated support) plus the coupling tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may improve counterexample sensitivity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: belief_mass_conservation
Title: Does the Belief Mass Add Up? Testing Whether LLM Internal Beliefs Across Mutually-Exclusive Alternatives Conserve Probability
Short Hypothesis: For a question with a fixed exhaustive set of mutually-exclusive candidate answers, a rational believer's internal belief across the alternatives should approximately conserve probability mass: the decoded beliefs (linear truth-direction readouts) in the exhaustive set should sum to ~1, and belief in one candidate should trade off against the others. We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations systematically VIOLATE belief-mass conservation: the decoded beliefs in an exhaustive mutually-exclusive set do not sum to ~1 (typically over-summing, an internal over-confidence spread), each candidate's belief is read too independently of the competing alternatives, and the total mass grows with set size. This mass-violation is graded, dissociable from a decodable normalization/competition signal distinct from the truth axis, causally predicts a multi-endorsement hallucination mode (confidently endorsing several mutually-exclusive answers at once), and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that renormalizes belief across the candidate set.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief in EACH proposition INDEPENDENTLY and never asks whether beliefs across a fixed, exhaustive set of MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE candidate answers CONSERVE probability mass — summing to ~1 with belief in one candidate trading off against the others — or instead are read too independently and over-sum. My prior 'quantifier_belief_aggregation' studied belief aggregated over a quantifier's instances; 'ensemble_belief_aggregation' combined beliefs across sources/samples; 'conjunction_belief_monotonicity' tested monotonicity under added conjuncts; 'negative_belief_closed_world' probed closed-world negation; 'counting_belief_position_saturation' studied saturation in counting. NONE isolate CROSS-CANDIDATE NORMALIZATION — whether the decoded beliefs over an exhaustive mutually-exclusive set sum to ~1, whether each candidate's belief is read too independently of its competitors so the total mass grows with set size (an internal over-confidence spread), whether this dissociates from a decodable normalization/competition signal distinct from the truth axis, whether it causally predicts a multi-endorsement hallucination mode (confidently endorsing several mutually-exclusive answers at once), and whether renormalizing belief across the candidate set fixes it. This belief-mass-conservation lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from all the above.
Abstract: If exactly one of five listed answers can be correct, a coherent believer distributes about one unit of confidence across them: raising belief in one must lower belief in the rest, and the total should not exceed one. We ask whether large language models honor this belief-mass conservation inside their belief representations, or whether they read each candidate's truth in isolation so that mutually-exclusive alternatives are each believed near-true and the mass over-sums. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we probe every member of an exhaustive, mutually-exclusive candidate set for a question and test whether the beliefs conserve mass. We construct MassBelief, a controlled dataset of questions each paired with an exhaustive mutually-exclusive answer set (one correct, k-1 incorrect), spanning factual multiple-choice, numeric ranges, and synthetic-in-context questions to control priors, with set size k varied and matched surface forms. We define a Belief Mass Violation Score (deviation of the summed candidate beliefs from 1) and a Competition Score (how much belief in one candidate anti-correlates with the others when evidence shifts). We test four claims: (1) internal beliefs violate mass conservation, over-summing and growing with set size, because each candidate is read too independently; (2) a decodable normalization/competition component is dissociable from the truth axis; (3) mass-violation causally predicts a multi-endorsement hallucination mode (confidently affirming several mutually-exclusive answers); and (4) a lightweight inference-time renormalization intervention that couples belief across the candidate set reduces the violation and multi-endorsement while improving selection accuracy and calibration, without harming single-answer judgments or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on multiple-choice accuracy, calibration, hallucination, and capability retention. Our results recast belief as a relational quantity across competing alternatives and expose non-conservation as a measurable, fixable failure of belief geometry.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build MassBelief. Each item = a question plus an EXHAUSTIVE, MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE candidate answer set (exactly one correct, k-1 incorrect), so belief mass should sum to ~1. Sources: (a) factual multiple-choice questions (adapt MMLU/ARC-style items, ensuring options are genuinely mutually exclusive and the set is exhaustive), (b) numeric-range partitions (mutually-exclusive bins over a quantity, e.g. 'the population is in [0-1M] / [1-5M] / [5M+]'), and (c) SYNTHETIC-in-context questions (nonce entities with a stipulated exhaustive answer set) to remove parametric priors and give exact control.
