Vary set size k = 2, 3, 5, 8 by adding/removing distractors. Include a NON-EXHAUSTIVE control (an 'other/none' option added, so mass need not sum over the listed items) and matched surface forms. Human-verify mutual-exclusivity, exhaustiveness, and correctness; include paraphrase and option-order permutations.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. For each question, read the internal belief in the proposition 'answer = candidate_i' for EVERY candidate i, at a matched (canonical, fresh-pass) query position. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; on a single true statement and a single false statement the readouts are near 1 and 0.

Belief Mass Violation measurement: For each item compute the summed candidate belief S = sum_i belief(answer=candidate_i). Define Belief Mass Violation Score = S - 1 (over-summing = positive). Report per-layer, per-model violation as a function of set size k, question type, and permutation. Test the hypotheses that (i) the mass over-sums (S > 1), and (ii) the violation grows with k (each candidate read too independently). Contrast against the NON-EXHAUSTIVE control (where over-sum is less problematic) and against a normalized-output baseline (the model's own softmax over option logits) to compare internal-belief mass to output-distribution mass.

Competition (trade-off) measurement: Test whether raising belief in one candidate lowers belief in the others as a conserved system should. Introduce in-context evidence favoring one candidate and measure whether the decoded belief in the favored candidate rises AND the others fall (conserved trade-off) versus rising in isolation (non-competition). Define a Competition Score = negative correlation between the favored candidate's belief change and the sum of the others' changes; near-zero indicates independent, non-conserving readouts.

Normalization/competition-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'normalization/competition' direction via difference-in-means contrasting activations when a candidate is read within its full mutually-exclusive set vs read in isolation (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the normalization axis (and vice versa); test whether the mass violation corresponds to the truth-probe readout ignoring the competition component (i.e., each candidate scored as if alone).

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the normalization/competition direction and measure whether the summed candidate belief moves toward 1 and whether raising the correct candidate correctly suppresses the distractors, holding content fixed. (b) Patch the belief-shift induced by favoring one candidate and measure whether the others' beliefs fall as conservation requires. Confirm the (non-)conservation behavior is causal and that amplifying the competition signal restores mass conservation.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Belief Mass Violation / low Competition Scores predict a multi-endorsement hallucination mode: (i) the model confidently affirming several mutually-exclusive candidates when each is queried in isolation ('is answer = X? yes' for multiple X), (ii) multiple-choice selection errors and instability under option-order permutation, and (iii) miscalibration of the selected answer. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (set size alone, output entropy, output softmax mass, per-candidate truth-probe confidence).

Renormalization intervention: At inference, given the decoded per-candidate beliefs, couple them across the exhaustive set — renormalize the belief vector to sum to 1 (and/or subtract the non-competition component via the normalization direction at a chosen layer, ITI-style) — so belief in each candidate reflects its share of the conserved mass. Answer from the renormalized vector. Provide a deployment variant that reads the candidate set from context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Belief Mass Violation / improved Competition, (ii) improved multiple-choice and numeric-bin selection accuracy and stability under option-order permutation on MassBelief and adapted MC benchmarks (MMLU/ARC), (iii) reduced multi-endorsement (fewer simultaneously-affirmed mutually-exclusive answers), (iv) calibration (ECE) of the selected answer, (v) PRESERVATION of single-answer true/false accuracy and NON-EXHAUSTIVE-control behavior (no over-correction), and (vi) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, output-softmax selection, standard ITI truth steering, and self-consistency across option orderings.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), set size k, question type (factual MC / numeric bins / synthetic), option-order permutation, exhaustive vs non-exhaustive, model scale, readout position, and generalization to candidate sets and domains not used to fit the normalization direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Reading a comparable per-candidate belief scalar and summing across candidates is position/probe sensitive; we standardize via a canonical fresh-pass 'answer = candidate_i?' probe, include position/layer robustness checks, use Platt-scaled probes, and report sensitivity of the mass score to these choices — an over-sum could partly reflect probe miscalibration rather than genuine non-conservation, which the single-true/single-false manipulation checks and the internal-vs-output-mass comparison help separate.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to candidate-answer propositions, so violations could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic-in-context items with exact ground truth.

The normalization/competition axis may be weak, entangled with the truth axis, or undecodable in some models; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that beliefs are read fully independently (no competition representation) is itself an informative result.

Ensuring answer sets are genuinely mutually exclusive and exhaustive is nontrivial for real MC items (options can overlap or the true answer may be outside the set); we human-verify, use synthetic-in-context sets with guaranteed exhaustiveness, and include the non-exhaustive 'none' control to bound this.

The Renormalization intervention could over-correct (forcing a spurious winner among genuinely-uncertain candidates) or harm single-answer judgments; we explicitly measure single-true/false preservation, non-exhaustive-control behavior, and capability retention, and note that renormalizing at the belief-readout level may be a post-hoc calibration rather than a change to the model's computation — we test both a pure-readout renormalization and an activation-level competition-steering variant.

Mass violation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (set size, output entropy, output softmax mass) for multi-endorsement and MC errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic finding that belief geometry reads mutually-exclusive alternatives non-competitively and fails to conserve belief mass, plus the renormalization tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/MC-tuning may already induce competition); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: sunk_cost_belief_escalation
Title: Hard-Won Therefore True: Does the Cost Already Sunk Into Reaching a Conclusion Inflate an LLM's Internal Belief?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a conclusion's content and truth-value fixed, an LLM's INTERNAL belief in a conclusion (linear truth-direction readout) is inflated, and made more resistant to revision, when the model reached it via a LONG, EFFORTFUL in-context process (many reasoning steps, a laborious derivation, extended search) versus reaching the identical conclusion cheaply, an internal analogue of the human sunk-cost / effort-justification (escalation-of-commitment) bias. This effort-justification inflation is graded in expended process cost, carried by a decodable invested-effort component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an effort-justified stubbornness mode (harder-won beliefs resist counterevidence more), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the invested-effort component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never varies the RETROSPECTIVE PROCESS COST already sunk into reaching a conclusion while holding the conclusion's content and truth-value fixed. My prior 'effort_indexed_belief_geometry' conditioned belief on task DIFFICULTY; 'derivation_discount_belief' asked whether a conclusion REACHED by derivation is discounted relative to a stated one; 'step_belief_load_bearing' tracked how much each reasoning step CARRIES the final belief; 'self_commitment_belief_anchoring' anchored belief to a previously COMMITTED answer; 'generation_quota_belief_inflation' inflated belief by forcing extra outputs. NONE isolate the human sunk-cost / effort-justification (escalation-of-commitment) bias — whether a conclusion reached via a LONG, LABORIOUS in-context process is believed more firmly, and resists revision more, than the IDENTICAL conclusion reached cheaply — nor separate invested effort from raw context length via matched-length filler controls, nor treat the sunk process cost as a decodable invested-effort component dissociable from the truth axis, nor tie it to an effort-justified stubbornness mode (harder-won beliefs resisting counterevidence) and re-anchor it away. This retrospective effort-justification lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from difficulty-indexing, derivation-discounting, step-load, prior-commitment, and quota-inflation work.
Abstract: People value and cling to conclusions they worked hard for, quite apart from whether those conclusions are correct — effort justification and the sunk-cost fallacy. We ask whether large language models exhibit this inside their belief representations: does a conclusion the model reached after a long, effortful process get believed more firmly, and resist revision more, than the identical conclusion reached cheaply? Holding a conclusion's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the RETROSPECTIVE cost already sunk into reaching it — a long multi-step derivation/search vs a short direct one — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes. Crucially this is distinct from allotting more compute before answering: the manipulated variable is how much work the transcript shows was already spent on a conclusion the model now holds. We construct SunkBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context conclusions each reached via matched HIGH-EFFORT vs LOW-EFFORT in-context processes that arrive at the identical conclusion, with process length/laboriousness graded and matched-length filler controls (to separate invested effort from raw context length). We define a Sunk-Cost Belief Inflation Score = belief(conclusion reached effortfully) minus belief(conclusion reached cheaply), and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated for effortfully-reached conclusions, graded in expended process cost, even for false conclusions; (2) the inflation is carried by a decodable invested-effort component dissociable from the truth axis and from raw context length; (3) inflation magnitude causally predicts an effort-justified stubbornness mode (effortfully-reached beliefs resist subsequent counterevidence more than cheaply-reached ones); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the invested-effort component restores content-driven belief and reduces the stubbornness without harming legitimate reasoning or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, belief-revision, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build SunkBelief. Conclusions C in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors and guarantee the process is valid). For each C create matched conditions that arrive at the IDENTICAL conclusion but differ in RETROSPECTIVE PROCESS COST: (a) HIGH-EFFORT — the transcript shows a long, laborious in-context derivation/search (many steps, backtracking, exploring dead ends) culminating in C; (b) LOW-EFFORT — C is reached directly/cheaply (a short one-step derivation or a bare arrival). Crucially the final conclusion, its content, and its validity are held fixed; only the amount of work shown to reach it varies. Grade effort (short vs long process; genuine derivation vs padded busywork). Add a MATCHED-LENGTH FILLER control (equal token budget of process-irrelevant text before C, no genuine effort toward C) to separate invested-effort from raw context length, and a NO-PROCESS baseline. Include high-effort processes reaching both true and false C (so inflation is separable from truth-tracking; for false C the effortful process is a valid-looking-but-flawed or a synthetic-stipulated route). Human-verify labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is the conclusion C true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in C under each effort condition; also record output answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the HIGH-EFFORT process genuinely reaches C (the model can restate the conclusion) and that effort conditions differ in shown work.

Sunk-Cost Belief Inflation measurement: Define Sunk-Cost Belief Inflation Score = belief(C | high-effort process) minus belief(C | low-effort process), controlling for the matched-length filler baseline so inflation is attributed to invested effort, not length. Report per-layer, per-model inflation as a function of effort level and truth regime. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is inflated for effortfully-reached conclusions, (ii) inflation grows with expended process cost, and (iii) crucially, FALSE conclusions reached effortfully are believed more true than the same falsehoods reached cheaply. Compare internal inflation to OUTPUT-level inflation (does the verdict/confidence about C rise with the effort spent?).

Invested-effort-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'invested-effort' direction via difference-in-means on high-effort vs low-effort (matched-length) activations at the conclusion-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the invested-effort axis (and vice versa); test whether the inflation is explained by the invested-effort component leaking into the truth-probe readout, and whether it is separable from a raw context-length/token-distance signal via the filler control.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a high-effort and a matched low-effort reaching of the same C, decompose into truth-direction and invested-effort components, patch only the invested-effort component into the low-effort condition and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract it under the high-effort condition and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the invested-effort signal causally inflates the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity (effort-justified stubbornness): At the item level, present subsequent counterevidence against C and test whether the Sunk-Cost Belief Inflation Score predicts an effort-justified stubbornness mode: (i) effortfully-reached beliefs resisting revision under counterevidence more than cheaply-reached ones, (ii) endorsement of effortfully-reached FALSE conclusions, and (iii) inconsistency across effort-varied paraphrases. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (effort-level indicator, output entropy, low-effort truth-probe confidence).

Invested-Effort De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the invested-effort direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects the conclusion's content/validity rather than how much work was spent reaching it. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected long-process transcripts. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Sunk-Cost Belief Inflation Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of effortfully-reached falsehoods and reduced effort-justified stubbornness (effortful beliefs become as revisable as cheap ones under decisive counterevidence), (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on effort-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate reasoning (genuinely-valid long derivations that reach CORRECT conclusions must still be believed appropriately — the core specificity check) and accuracy on low-effort/filler controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge the conclusion by its content, not by how much effort it took to reach', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (query C without the process).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), effort level and type (genuine derivation vs padded busywork), high-effort process reaching true vs false C, real vs synthetic conclusions, model scale, length-matching method, distance between process and query, and generalization to process types not used to fit the invested-effort direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The sunk-cost effect could be confounded with generic context-length/dilution or with the derivation-discount phenomenon (belief in DERIVED conclusions differing from stated ones) rather than an invested-effort-specific inflation; the matched-length filler control, holding the conclusion's derivation validity fixed across effort conditions, and the project-out dissociation from a raw token-distance signal directly test this, and overlap with derivation-discount is analyzed explicitly rather than hidden.

This must be distinguished from the effort-indexed effect (allotting more compute BEFORE answering): here the manipulated variable is the RETROSPECTIVE process cost shown for a conclusion the model already holds, not the thinking budget; we design conditions so the answer is fixed and only shown work varies, and analyze the relationship to compute-budget effects.

Apparent inflation could reflect the probe detecting long-process lexical/structural cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with matched-length filler baselines, high-effort-for-true vs high-effort-for-false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context conclusions, and causal patching that isolates the invested-effort component.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to process-laden transcripts, so inflation could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.
Invested-effort and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate confidence in genuinely-valid effortful derivations or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on valid-effortful-correct conclusions and low-effort controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Sunk-cost inflation may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (effort-level indicator, output entropy) for effort-justified stubbornness; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that expended process cost inflates internal belief (a sunk-cost / effort-justification effect in belief geometry, distinct from compute-budget and derivation-discount effects) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether the human effort-justification bias transfers to LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF/reasoning-tuning may amplify valuing of effortful reasoning); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: counterexample_belief_sensitivity
Title: One Counterexample Should Do It: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Respect the Confirmation/Refutation Asymmetry for Universal Claims?
Short Hypothesis: For a universal claim ('all X are Y', 'X always Z'), a single valid COUNTEREXAMPLE logically refutes it, so a rational believer's internal belief in the universal should drop sharply to false. We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) are systematically UNDER-SENSITIVE to counterexamples: after one refuting instance is presented in context, the decoded belief in the universal barely moves and instead tracks how many supporting instances remain, so the model still internally 'believes' a demonstrably-falsified generalization. This counterexample-insensitivity is graded (worse with more prior supporting instances), carried by a decodable support-count component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a falsified-universal endorsement mode, and can be reduced by a lightweight inference-time intervention that couples belief in the universal to the presence of a counterexample.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never tests whether it honors the CONFIRMATION/REFUTATION ASYMMETRY — that a single valid counterexample logically falsifies a universal generalization. Synthetic in-context truth work ('When LLMs Learn to Be Consistently Wrong', 2026) shows models linearly encode a stable belief even for planted falsehoods, and count-like quantities are linearly decodable ('How Much is Left?', 2026), yet neither asks whether a universal's belief tracks REMAINING SUPPORTING INSTANCES rather than the refuting one. My prior 'conjunction_belief_monotonicity' tested logical monotonicity over conjunctions; 'quantifier_belief_aggregation' aggregated belief across quantifiers; 'reductio_belief_untenability' tested reductio-driven untenability; 'defeasible_override_belief_geometry' studied defeasible overriding. NONE isolate whether one valid counterexample sharply drops belief in a universal (less so as prior support grows), whether residual belief instead tracks a decodable support-count component dissociable from the truth axis, whether this causes a falsified-universal endorsement mode, and whether coupling belief to the counterexample signal restores refutation. This confirmation/refutation-asymmetry lens is new and distinct from monotonicity, quantifier-aggregation, reductio, and defeasibility work.
Abstract: A universal generalization is only as strong as its weakest case: a single genuine counterexample makes 'all swans are white' false, no matter how many white swans preceded it. This confirmation/refutation asymmetry is a hallmark of sound reasoning. We ask whether large language models honor it inside their belief representations, or whether one refuting instance fails to dislodge a generalization they have accumulated support for. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar belief along the linear truth direction, we present a universal claim together with supporting instances and then a single valid counterexample, and measure how the internal belief in the universal moves. We construct CounterBelief, a controlled dataset of universal claims (strict synthetic-in-context rules over nonce entities that guarantee validity and remove priors, plus a real-generic subset) each paired with a graded number of supporting instances and a single logically-valid counterexample, with matched no-counterexample and non-refuting-instance controls. We define a Counterexample Sensitivity Score (drop in belief in the universal after one valid counterexample) and a Support-Count Bias (extent to which residual belief tracks the number of remaining supporting instances). We test four claims: (1) internal belief is under-sensitive to counterexamples, dropping far less than logic requires and less as prior support grows; (2) a decodable support-count component is dissociable from the truth axis and dominates the counterexample signal; (3) counterexample-insensitivity causally predicts a falsified-universal endorsement mode (the model still asserts the universal after seeing a case that refutes it); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief in the universal to the decoded counterexample signal restores appropriate refutation without harming genuinely-unrefuted universals or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on universal-refutation accuracy, calibration, and capability retention. Our results test whether LLM belief geometry respects the logical asymmetry between confirmation and refutation.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CounterBelief. Each item = a UNIVERSAL claim ('all X are Y', 'X always Z') plus a set of SUPPORTING INSTANCES (individual cases consistent with the universal) and then a single valid COUNTEREXAMPLE (a case that logically refutes the universal). Use (a) SYNTHETIC-in-context strict rules over nonce entities ('all glorps are blue' + several blue glorps + one green glorp) so validity and ground-truth are exact and priors removed, and (b) a REAL-GENERIC subset (well-known universals with genuine exceptions, e.g. penguin as counterexample to 'all birds fly'). Grade SUPPORT COUNT (0, 1, 3, 6 supporting instances before the counterexample). Include: NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls (only supporting instances, universal genuinely holds); a NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE control (an extra consistent case, not a counterexample); and matched surface forms. Human-verify that the counterexample is genuinely refuting and the supporting instances are consistent; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read internal belief in the UNIVERSAL claim (i) after only supporting instances (baseline) and (ii) after the single counterexample is added. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the counterexample (can restate that the instance violates the universal).

Counterexample Sensitivity & Support-Count Bias measurement: Define Counterexample Sensitivity Score = drop in belief in the universal from baseline to post-counterexample. Define Support-Count Bias = extent to which residual post-counterexample belief increases with the number of prior supporting instances. Report per-layer, per-model as a function of support count, for synthetic and real items. Test that (i) belief is under-sensitive (small drop), and (ii) the drop shrinks as prior support grows. Contrast with NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls (belief should not drop) and NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls (belief should stay high). Compare internal sensitivity to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model still assert the universal after the counterexample?).

Support-count-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit a 'support-count' direction via difference-in-means on high-support vs low-support activations (balanced across counterexample presence and content), and separately a 'counterexample-present' signal. Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarities among support-count, counterexample-present, and the truth directions; project out the truth direction and re-decode each. Test whether counterexample-insensitivity corresponds to the support-count component dominating the universal's belief readout while the counterexample signal under-modulates it.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the counterexample-present signal and measure whether belief in the universal drops and the output refutes it, holding support-count fixed. (b) Patch the counterexample representation into a no-counterexample context and measure whether the universal's belief drops as required. (c) Conversely, patch a high-support-count component into a refuted item and measure induced spurious re-inflation. Confirm the support-count signal causally drives insensitivity and that amplifying the counterexample signal corrects it.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether Counterexample Sensitivity / Support-Count Bias predict a falsified-universal endorsement mode: (i) the model still asserting a universal after a valid counterexample, (ii) universal-refutation QA errors ('given this counterexample, is the claim still true?'), and (iii) inconsistency across support-count and paraphrase variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (support count alone, output entropy, baseline truth-probe confidence).

Counterexample-Coupling intervention: At inference, estimate the counterexample-present signal (from the probe) and add a scaled shift along the truth direction that drives belief in the universal toward false when a valid counterexample is detected, gated by the decoded signal (ITI-style), overriding the support-count contribution. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected universal-claim + instance structure. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Counterexample Sensitivity / reduced Support-Count Bias, (ii) improved universal-refutation accuracy on CounterBelief and adapted generics/exception and logical-consistency benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of belief in genuinely-UNREFUTED universals (NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE and NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls must NOT be suppressed) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('check whether any instance violates the claim'), and prompt-based instruction to 'treat a single valid counterexample as refuting a universal claim'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), support count, synthetic vs real-generic items, counterexample position (immediately after vs distant from supporting instances), model scale, and generalization to universal-claim structures and domains not used to fit the counterexample/support-count directions.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent counterexample-insensitivity could reflect the model failing to RECOGNIZE the instance as a counterexample (a comprehension failure, not a belief-coupling failure); we manipulation-check that the model can state the instance violates the universal and analyze recognized vs non-recognized items separately.

Apparent insensitivity or support-count bias could reflect the probe detecting surface instance-count/lexical cues rather than genuine belief; mitigate with matched surface forms, NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE and NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE controls, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context rules with exact ground truth, and causal patching that isolates the support-count vs counterexample components.

For real generics, 'all birds fly' is arguably a defeasible generic rather than a strict universal, so a penguin need not make it 'false'; we anchor quantitative claims on SYNTHETIC strict-universal rules where a counterexample is unambiguously refuting, and analyze real generics separately.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to universal claims, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic rules to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

Support-count, counterexample, and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that the counterexample is NOT separately represented is itself informative.

The Counterexample-Coupling intervention could over-suppress genuinely-unrefuted universals (spurious refutation) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE and NON-REFUTING-INSTANCE controls plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Counterexample-insensitivity may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (support count, output entropy) for falsified-universal endorsement; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry violates the confirmation/refutation asymmetry, plus the coupling tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may improve counterexample sensitivity); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: acquisition_order_belief_primacy
Title: First Learned, Firmly Held: Does the Training-Time Order of Competing Facts Leave a Durable Primacy Imprint on LLM Belief Geometry?
Short Hypothesis: When a model is exposed during (continual) pretraining to two competing claims about the same item, the claim ENCOUNTERED FIRST acquires a durable advantage in the model's internal belief geometry (the linear truth-direction readout) that persists even after equal or greater later exposure to the competing claim — an acquisition-order primacy effect. We hypothesize this primacy imprint is (1) graded in the first-exposure gap, (2) dissociable from raw frequency and recency (it survives at equal counts and reversed recency), (3) causally predictive of a stubborn-belief / order-dependent hallucination mode (the model resists overwriting first-learned facts and reverts under mild pressure), and (4) localized to the same late-layer belief circuitry where continual-pretraining belief flips are known to concentrate.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never asks whether the TRAINING-TIME ORDER in which competing facts were acquired leaves a durable primacy imprint on that belief. Knowledge-acquisition-dynamics work — LMEnt (2025), 'How do language models learn facts?' (2025), 'Latent Knowledge as a Predictor of Fact Acquisition' (2026), and 'Probing Across Time' (2021) — traces WHEN and HOW facts enter model representations and their probes, but studies frequency, curricula, and checkpoint dynamics, not the residual belief ADVANTAGE of a first-learned claim after the competitor receives equal or greater later exposure with counts held fixed. My prior 'belief_acquisition_primacy' probed acquisition primacy broadly; 'serial_position_belief_bias' studied WITHIN-CONTEXT serial position; 'belief_hysteresis_order_dependence' studied order-dependent in-context updating; 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' studied revision inertia. NONE isolate a TRAINING-TIME acquisition-order primacy that (i) is graded in the first-exposure gap, (ii) is dissociable from raw frequency and recency at fixed counts and reversed recency, (iii) causally predicts a stubborn / order-dependent hallucination mode, and (iv) localizes to late-layer belief circuitry. This continual-pretraining acquisition-order lens is new and distinct from in-context order, generic acquisition-primacy, and update-inertia work.
Abstract: Humans hold first-learned facts more stubbornly than later corrections — a primacy / order-of-acquisition effect. We ask whether large language models inherit an analogous imprint in their belief representations, formed at training time. Using a controlled continual-pretraining setup, we expose a base model to pairs of competing claims about the same item (an original fact and a counterfactual), systematically varying which claim is encountered FIRST and the temporal gap before the competitor, while HOLDING TOTAL EXPOSURE COUNTS FIXED, and then read the model's internal belief in each claim via linear truth probes across checkpoints, layers, and model scale. We define an Acquisition-Order Primacy Score = the residual belief advantage of the first-learned claim after the competing claim has received equal (or greater) later exposure. We test four claims: (1) the first-learned claim retains a durable internal belief advantage, graded in the first-exposure gap; (2) this primacy is dissociable from raw frequency and recency by holding counts fixed and reversing recency; (3) primacy magnitude causally predicts a stubborn-belief / order-dependent hallucination mode — the model resists overwriting first-learned facts and reverts to them under mild pressure — verified by activation patching along the belief direction; and (4) the imprint is localized to the same late-layer belief circuitry where continual-pretraining belief flips concentrate. We trace across checkpoints when the primacy advantage forms and whether it decays, and test a lightweight late-layer intervention that neutralizes stale primacy to enable correct updating. Building on recent knowledge-acquisition-dynamics resources (LMEnt, Gottesman et al. 2025; Zucchet et al. 2025) and belief-flip localization (Layer of Truth, Churina et al. 2025), we evaluate on fact-vs-counterfact belief, overwriting-resistance, calibration, and general capability retention. Our results ask whether the sequence in which an LLM learns competing facts is silently baked into what it believes.
Experiments: Setup and dataset: Use a small-but-realistic continual-pretraining pipeline affordable in an academic lab (base models 1-8B: Pythia/OLMo intermediate checkpoints, Llama-3 8B, Qwen2.5 7B; optionally leverage LMEnt's 12 pretrained models with 4K checkpoints). Build FactOrderBelief: paired fact-vs-counterfact items about the same item (following the Layer-of-Truth paired paradigm) using SYNTHETIC entities (nonce subjects with stipulated attributes) to remove parametric priors, plus a real-fact subset. For each pair, construct continual-pretraining document streams injecting the two competing claims, VARYING which claim appears FIRST and the temporal GAP before the competitor, while HOLDING TOTAL EXPOSURE COUNTS EQUAL across conditions. Include a RECENCY-REVERSED condition (first-learned claim is the LESS recent) to dissociate primacy from recency, and a FREQUENCY-VARIED control.

Belief readout across checkpoints: Train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression, Platt-scaled to [0,1]) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements. After continual pretraining (and at intermediate checkpoints), read the internal belief in the first-learned vs later-learned claim for each pair. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; both claims were actually seen (verified by loss on injected docs).

Acquisition-Order Primacy measurement: Define Acquisition-Order Primacy Score = belief(first-learned claim) minus belief(later-learned claim) after equal total exposure. Report per-layer, per-model, per-scale primacy as a function of the first-exposure gap. Test that (i) the first-learned claim retains a durable advantage even at equal counts, and (ii) primacy grows with the exposure gap. Compare against the frequency-varied and recency-reversed controls to dissociate primacy from frequency and recency.

Formation tracing: Across continual-pretraining checkpoints, trace WHEN the primacy advantage emerges (does it lock in early and resist later competing exposure?), whether it decays with continued competing exposure, and whether it sharpens abruptly (as belief flips do in Layer of Truth). Fit belief trajectories for first- vs later-learned claims over checkpoints.

Localization: Test whether the primacy imprint concentrates in specific (expected late) layers by per-layer probing and by measuring where the first-vs-later belief gap is largest, comparing to the late-layer flip locus reported by Churina et al.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Patch the belief-direction component of the later-learned claim into the query and measure whether the output flips away from the first-learned answer, quantifying overwriting-resistance. (b) Add/subtract the belief direction at the localized layers and measure whether the first-learned advantage is causally responsible for the model's answer. Confirm primacy is causal, not epiphenomenal.

Predictive validity (stubbornness/hallucination): Test whether the Acquisition-Order Primacy Score predicts a stubborn-belief mode: (i) resistance to updating the first-learned fact when the counterfactual is later asserted in context, (ii) reversion to the first-learned answer under mild pressure (a distractor or 'are you sure?'), and (iii) order-dependent hallucination (asserting the outdated first-learned fact). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (exposure gap alone, frequency, recency).

Primacy-neutralization intervention: A lightweight late-layer intervention (ITI-style shift along the belief direction, or targeted patching) that dampens the stale first-learned advantage to enable correct updating toward a legitimately-newer fact. Evaluate (i) improved correct-updating rate, (ii) PRESERVATION of legitimately-first-learned correct facts (must not erase all first-learned knowledge), and (iii) capability retention (MMLU, perplexity). Baselines: no intervention, uniform truth steering, continued fine-tuning on the correct fact.

Ablations: model scale and family, synthetic vs real facts, exposure-gap and total-count levels, probe type, layer choice, checkpoint granularity, and generalization to fact domains and order patterns not used to fit the intervention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Primacy could be confounded with frequency or recency; the equal-total-count design, recency-reversed condition, and frequency-varied controls are the core dissociation tests, and a null (primacy = frequency/recency) is itself an informative finding.

Continual pretraining on small models may not reproduce phenomena of larger models; we test multiple scales/families (including released Pythia/OLMo/LMEnt checkpoints) and report scale effects, but generalization to frontier-scale pretraining is a genuine limitation.

The imprint might be an artifact of the specific injection format; we vary document templates, use synthetic and real facts, and verify both claims were learned (loss check) to rule out that only the first claim was actually encoded.

Truth probes may transfer imperfectly to injected synthetic facts, so primacy could carry probe error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and causal patching to corroborate.

The primacy-neutralization intervention could erase legitimately-first-learned correct knowledge or harm capability; we explicitly measure preservation of correct first-learned facts and general capability, framing the intervention as gated to cases where a newer fact should legitimately win.

Primacy magnitude may correlate with but not exceed exposure-gap/frequency baselines for predicting stubbornness; if so, the contribution is the formation-tracing finding that acquisition ORDER leaves a durable, causally-localizable imprint on belief geometry, reported honestly.

Running continual pretraining plus multi-checkpoint probing is compute-heavier than pure inference-time studies; we scope to small models, few conditions, and released checkpoints (Pythia/OLMo/LMEnt) to stay within an academic budget.

Name: within_context_answer_anchoring_belief
Title: Anchored to the First Guess: Does the First Candidate Value Encountered In-Context Bias an LLM's Internal Belief Toward It?
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM must judge a factual proposition whose answer is a specific value, the FIRST candidate value it encounters in the context (a stray earlier mention, a prior turn's guess, an incidental number/name in the prompt) acts as an anchor that inflates the model's INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) in that value being correct, even when the mention carries no evidential weight and is irrelevant, an internal analogue of the human anchoring-and-adjustment bias. This within-context anchoring is graded in anchor salience, carried by a decodable anchor component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an anchor-driven factual-error mode (endorsing the anchored-but-wrong value, doubting the true value when a wrong anchor preceded it), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the anchor component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never varies which incidental CANDIDATE VALUE appears FIRST in the context while holding the proposition's content and true answer fixed. My prior 'serial_position_belief_bias' studied WHERE in a list an item sits; 'self_commitment_belief_anchoring' anchored belief to the model's OWN previously committed answer; 'premature_belief_commitment' studied belief locking in before evidence arrives; 'self_query_belief_attractor' studied belief being pulled toward a re-queried value; 'acquisition_order_belief_primacy' bound belief to TRAINING-TIME acquisition order. NONE isolate the human anchoring-and-adjustment bias — whether an evidentially-IRRELEVANT first-mentioned value (a stray earlier number/name, a prior turn's tentative guess) inflates internal belief that THAT value is the correct answer, graded in anchor salience — nor treat the anchor as a decodable component dissociable from the truth axis, nor tie it to an anchor-driven factual-error mode (endorsing the anchored-but-wrong value, doubting the true value under a wrong anchor), nor subtract it while preserving genuinely-relevant prior mentions. This within-context incidental-anchor lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from serial-position, self-commitment, premature-commitment, self-query, and training-time-order work.
Abstract: People latch onto the first number or option they see and adjust insufficiently from it — the anchoring bias, one of the most robust findings in human judgment. We ask whether large language models exhibit an analogous within-context anchoring inside their belief representations. Holding a factual proposition's content and true answer fixed, we vary only which candidate VALUE appears FIRST and incidentally in the surrounding context — an evidentially-irrelevant earlier mention, a prior turn's tentative guess, or a stray number/name — and read the internal belief via linear truth probes in the proposition that a queried value is the correct answer. Crucially the anchor carries no logical bearing on the answer. We construct AnchorBelief, a controlled dataset of factual questions (numeric, entity, and synthetic-in-context facts to remove priors) each paired with an incidental FIRST-mentioned candidate that is either the true answer, a plausible wrong value, or absent, with anchor salience graded and surface length matched. We define an Anchoring Belief Bias Score = belief(candidate is correct | it was the incidental anchor) minus belief(same candidate | no anchor / a different value anchored), and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated toward the incidentally-anchored value at fixed truth, graded in anchor salience; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable anchor component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) shift magnitude causally predicts an anchor-driven factual-error mode (endorsing anchored-but-wrong values, doubting true values when a wrong anchor preceded them); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the anchor component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure while preserving legitimate use of genuinely-relevant prior mentions and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build AnchorBelief. Factual questions in three truth regimes: real-numeric (populations, dates, quantities), real-entity (capitals, names), and SYNTHETIC-in-context facts (answer stipulated in context, to remove parametric priors). For each question, precede it with an INCIDENTAL first mention of a candidate answer value that carries no evidential bearing on the answer (e.g. embedded in unrelated framing, a prior-turn casual guess, or a stray number in a distractor sentence), in matched conditions: ANCHOR-IS-TRUE (the incidental value equals the true answer), ANCHOR-IS-WRONG (a plausible incorrect value), NO-ANCHOR baseline, and DIFFERENT-ANCHOR (a wrong value anchored while probing the true value). Grade anchor SALIENCE (brief passing mention vs emphasized). Match surface length; human-verify the anchor carries no logical bearing on the answer; include a RELEVANT-MENTION control (a prior mention that IS genuine evidence, to distinguish anchoring from legitimate context use); include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in the proposition 'the correct answer is <candidate value>' under each anchoring condition; also record output answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model registers the incidental mention (can recall it) but that it carries no evidence.

Anchoring Belief Bias measurement: Define Anchoring Belief Bias Score = belief(candidate is correct | it was the incidental anchor) minus belief(same candidate | NO-ANCHOR baseline). Report per-layer, per-model bias across anchor salience and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief inflates toward the anchored value at fixed truth, and (ii) inflation grows with anchor salience. Crucially, in ANCHOR-IS-WRONG and DIFFERENT-ANCHOR conditions, anchoring predicts endorsing a wrong value and doubting the true value. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (does the model's answer/confidence track the anchor?).

Anchor-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'anchor' direction via difference-in-means on anchored vs no-anchor activations at the query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the anchor axis (and vice versa); disentangle anchoring from mere lexical priming/co-mention via a controlled regression; test whether the bias is explained by the anchor component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between anchored and no-anchor processing of the same candidate, decompose into truth-direction and anchor components, patch only the anchor component into the no-anchor condition and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract the anchor component under the anchored condition and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven value. Confirm the anchor signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Anchoring Belief Bias Score predicts an anchor-driven factual-error mode: (i) endorsement of anchored-but-wrong values, (ii) doubting/under-endorsement of true values when a wrong anchor preceded them, and (iii) answer flips as the anchor value is changed. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (anchor-salience indicator, output entropy, no-anchor truth-probe confidence, lexical co-mention).

Anchor De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the anchor direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the answer's content rather than the incidentally-anchored value. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected incidental candidate mentions. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Anchoring Belief Bias Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of anchored-but-wrong values and reduced doubting of true values, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on anchor-framed factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate context use (the RELEVANT-MENTION control, where a prior mention is genuine evidence, must still update belief) and accuracy on no-anchor controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'ignore incidental earlier mentions and judge the answer on its merits', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), anchor type (numeric/entity), anchor salience, anchor-is-true vs anchor-is-wrong, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between anchor mention and query, anchoring-vs-lexical-priming disentangling, and generalization to anchor framings not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent anchoring could reduce to mere lexical co-mention/priming (the candidate token recently appeared) rather than a genuine anchoring-and-adjustment effect; mitigate with a lexical-co-mention-controlled regression, matched surface forms, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the anchor component — a finding that anchoring reduces to priming is itself informative.

The incidental mention might inadvertently carry weak evidence about the answer; we human-verify no evidential bearing, include the RELEVANT-MENTION control to calibrate legitimate updating, and analyze borderline items separately.

This must be distinguished from evidence-order hysteresis (order of genuine evidence) and from training-time acquisition-order primacy; here the anchor is an evidentially-irrelevant in-context first mention, and we contrast against no-anchor and different-anchor conditions to isolate the within-context anchoring effect.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to answer-candidate propositions, so bias could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Anchor and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-suppress legitimate use of relevant prior mentions or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on the RELEVANT-MENTION control, no-anchor accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

Anchoring bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (anchor salience, co-mention, output entropy) for anchor-driven errors; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that an incidental in-context first mention anchors internal belief (an anchoring-and-adjustment bias in belief geometry) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.
Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale effects and negative results as informative.

Name: existence_bias_belief_geometry
Title: Something Is Truer Than Nothing: Does an LLM's Internal Belief Favor Existence Claims Over Non-Existence Claims?
Short Hypothesis: Holding truth fixed, an LLM's INTERNAL belief (linear truth-direction readout) is systematically higher for propositions that assert that something EXISTS / has an attribute (positive existentials) than for logically-equivalent propositions that assert that something does NOT exist / lacks an attribute (negative existentials), an internal analogue of the human positivity/existence bias where presence is treated as more credible than absence. This existence bias is graded, carried by a decodable polarity/existence component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts a twin error mode (endorsing false existence claims and doubting true non-existence claims), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the existence-polarity component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar belief but never contrasts the EXISTENCE/PRESENCE POLARITY of a claim's content — positive existentials (something exists / an attribute is present) against truth-matched negative existentials (it does not exist / is absent) — at fixed truth-value. My prior 'negative_belief_closed_world' studied closed-world assumptions about what is NOT stated; 'negation_depth_belief_erosion' studied SURFACE logical-negation depth eroding belief; 'ignorance_vs_falsehood_belief' separated not-knowing from believing-false; 'modal_status_belief_geometry' varied modal status. NONE isolate the human positivity/existence bias — whether internal belief is systematically higher for existence-asserting than for logically-equivalent non-existence-asserting claims at fixed truth, graded in existential polarity and distinct from mere surface negation — nor treat existence-polarity as a decodable component dissociable from the truth axis, nor tie it to a twin error mode (hallucinating that nonexistent things exist, doubting genuine absences), nor subtract it while preserving legitimate negation handling. Because fabricating nonexistent entities and failing to assert real absences are core hallucination modes, this existence-polarity lens on belief geometry is new and distinct from closed-world, negation-depth, ignorance-vs-falsehood, and modal-status work.
Abstract: People find claims that something exists more believable than claims that it does not — presence is salient and easy to confirm, absence is diffuse and hard to establish. We ask whether large language models inherit this existence bias inside their belief representations. Holding a proposition's truth-value fixed, we contrast POSITIVE EXISTENTIAL claims (an entity exists, an attribute is present) with logically-equivalent NEGATIVE EXISTENTIAL claims (the entity does not exist, the attribute is absent), and read the internal belief via difference-in-means and logistic truth probes along the linear truth direction. Crucially, this concerns the existence/presence POLARITY of the claim's content, not surface logical negation depth, and holds truth constant across polarity (a true positive existential vs a true negative existential; a false positive vs a false negative). We construct ExistBelief, a controlled dataset of true and false positive- and negative-existential propositions over real entities/attributes plus synthetic-in-context items (to remove parametric priors), with surface length matched and content paired so each positive claim has a truth-matched negative counterpart. We define an Existence Belief Bias Score = belief(existence-asserting) minus belief(non-existence-asserting) at fixed truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief favors existence claims at fixed truth, graded in the claim's existential polarity; (2) the bias is carried by a decodable existence-polarity component dissociable from the truth axis and from surface negation; (3) bias magnitude causally predicts a twin error mode (endorsing false existence claims — hallucinating that nonexistent things exist — and doubting true non-existence claims — failing to confirm that something is absent); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the existence-polarity component restores content-driven belief and reduces the failure without harming legitimate handling of negation or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, and capability retention. Because fabricating nonexistent entities/attributes and failing to assert genuine absences are core hallucination modes, an existence bias in belief geometry maps onto a concrete reliability risk.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ExistBelief. Cross EXISTENTIAL POLARITY {positive-existential (asserts an entity exists / an attribute is present), negative-existential (asserts the entity does not exist / the attribute is absent)} with TRUTH {true, false}, into a 2x2 design, with content PAIRED so each positive claim has a truth-matched negative counterpart about the same domain. Examples: true-positive ('element X has an isotope with mass number M' — exists), true-negative ('element X has no stable isotope of mass number M' — genuine absence), false-positive ('author A wrote a novel titled T' when no such novel exists — fabricated existence), false-negative ('author A never wrote any novels' when they did — false absence). Use real-world entities/attributes plus SYNTHETIC-in-context items (nonce entities whose existence/attributes are stipulated in context) to remove parametric priors and give exact ground truth. CRUCIALLY control for surface logical negation: include existence claims phrased without negation words and non-existence claims phrased both with negation ('does not exist') and via positive-lexical absence framings ('is absent', 'lacks'), so the existence-polarity contrast is dissociated from mere presence of a 'not' token. Match surface length; human-verify polarity and truth labels; include paraphrase sets and neutral non-existential controls.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral (polarity-balanced) true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position read the internal belief in each ExistBelief proposition; also record output answer/confidence. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model comprehends each claim (can report whether it asserts presence or absence).

Existence Belief Bias measurement: Define Existence Belief Bias Score = mean belief(existence-asserting claims) minus mean belief(non-existence-asserting claims), computed WITHIN the true cell and WITHIN the false cell separately (holding truth fixed). Report per-layer, per-model bias for real and synthetic items and across the negation-controlled framings. Test the hypotheses that (i) existence claims are believed more true than truth-matched non-existence claims, and (ii) the bias survives when non-existence is phrased without a surface 'not' token (isolating existence-polarity from logical negation). Crucially, the false cell tests hallucinated existence (false-positive believed too true) and the true cell tests under-confirmed absence (true-negative believed too false). Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (does the model's verdict/confidence favor existence?).

Existence-polarity-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'existence-polarity' direction via difference-in-means on existence-asserting vs non-existence-asserting activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction and with a separately-fit surface-negation direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode existence-polarity (and vice versa); disentangle existence-polarity from surface negation via a controlled regression (does the axis persist for negation-free absence framings?). Test whether the bias is explained by the existence-polarity component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a positive-existential and a truth-matched negative-existential claim, decompose into truth-direction and existence-polarity components, patch only the existence-polarity component into a neutral/absence claim and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract the existence-polarity component from an existence claim and measure whether belief moves toward the truth-appropriate value. Confirm the existence-polarity signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of truth and of surface negation.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Existence Belief Bias Score predicts a twin error mode: (i) endorsement of FALSE existence claims (hallucinating nonexistent entities/attributes), (ii) under-endorsement/doubting of TRUE non-existence claims (failing to confirm genuine absences), and (iii) inconsistency across polarity paraphrases of the same fact. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (existential-polarity indicator, output entropy, surface-negation indicator, neutral truth-probe confidence).

Existence-Polarity De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the existence-polarity direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so belief reflects the proposition's content/truth rather than whether it asserts presence or absence. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected existence/non-existence framing. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Existence Belief Bias Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of false existence claims and improved confirmation of true non-existence claims, (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) on polarity-varied factual QA, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate negation handling (the model must still correctly evaluate genuine logical negations — the core specificity check) and accuracy on neutral non-existential controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'judge presence and absence claims by the same evidentiary standard', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), polarity framing (negation-free absence vs 'not'-marked), true vs false cell, real vs synthetic-in-context items, entity vs attribute existence, model scale, existence-polarity-vs-surface-negation disentangling, and generalization to existential framings not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The existence bias could reduce to surface logical-negation handling (non-existence claims usually contain 'not') rather than a genuine existence-polarity effect; the negation-free absence framings ('lacks', 'is absent'), the surface-negation-controlled regression, and the separately-fit negation direction directly dissociate the two, and a finding that the bias reduces to negation is itself informative and connects to negation-processing literature.

Apparent bias could reflect the probe detecting polarity lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with content-paired truth-matched counterparts, surface-length matching, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching that isolates the existence-polarity component.

In the real world, existence claims about specific entities are often true more frequently than arbitrary non-existence claims, confounding polarity with base-rate priors; we anchor quantitative claims on SYNTHETIC-in-context items where existence/absence and truth are stipulated by construction (removing priors), and treat real-world items as secondary.

Truth probes trained on polarity-balanced neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to existential propositions, so bias could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Existence-polarity and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate negation/absence reasoning or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation of genuine logical-negation handling, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

The bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (polarity indicator, surface-negation indicator, output entropy) for the twin error mode; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry favors existence over non-existence (an existence/positivity bias distinct from logical negation) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether the human existence bias transfers to LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training; we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: explaining_away_belief_geometry
Title: Explaining Away in the Machine: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Discount a Cause Once a Competing Cause Is Confirmed?
Short Hypothesis: In a common-effect (collider) structure where two independent causes A and B could each produce an observed effect E, a normative reasoner who learns that A occurred and E occurred should LOWER its belief that B also occurred (explaining away / discounting). We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) FAIL to explain away: the decoded belief in the alternative cause B does not drop when a competing cause A is confirmed, so the model internally over-commits to redundant causes. We further hypothesize a separable 'alternative-cause-discounting' signal is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that its absence causally predicts a redundant-cause endorsement error mode, and that a lightweight inference-time intervention that couples belief in B to the confirmation of A restores explaining-away.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never tests whether it performs collider 'explaining-away' — discounting one cause once a competing cause is confirmed. Behavioral cognitive-science work shows LLMs discount only weakly in prompted probability judgments (Dettki et al. 2025; Dettki, Wu & Rehder 2026) and are shaky on false-belief and Bayesian-text inference (Trott et al. 2026; QUITE, Schrader et al. 2024), but always at the OUTPUT level. My prior 'causal_vs_correlational_belief' asked whether belief tracks causal versus correlational structure; 'dependency_structured_belief_revision' propagated updates through a stated dependency graph; 'belief_update_inertia_geometry' measured sluggishness of belief change; 'explanatory_coherence_belief_conflation' probed coherence-driven inflation. NONE isolate common-effect discounting — whether internal belief in an alternative cause B DROPS when a competing cause A is confirmed, quantified against an exact Bayesian benchmark; whether an alternative-cause-discounting signal is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; whether its absence causally drives a redundant-cause endorsement mode; and whether coupling belief(B) to confirmation(A) restores explaining-away. This collider-discounting lens on belief geometry, grounded against a normative Bayesian posterior, is new and distinct from correlational, dependency-propagation, inertia, and coherence framings.
Abstract: When a wet lawn could be caused by rain OR a sprinkler, learning that the sprinkler was on should make rain less likely — explaining away, the diagnostic of collider reasoning. Behavioral studies show large language models produce this discounting weakly or not at all in their prompted probability judgments (Dettki et al. 2025/2026; Trott et al. 2026), but always at the output level. We ask whether the failure lives inside the model's belief representations. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction, we present a common-effect scenario — two independent causes A and B, an observed effect E — confirm the effect and one cause A, and read the internal belief in the alternative cause B, testing whether it drops as normative explaining-away requires. We construct ExplainAwayBelief, a controlled dataset of collider scenarios over real-world causal structures and synthetic-in-context causal graphs (nonce causes/effects with stipulated independence and generative strengths, to remove parametric priors and give an exact Bayesian benchmark), with matched no-confirmation and non-competing-cause controls. We define an Explaining-Away Score (drop in belief in B when A is confirmed) and test four claims: (1) internal belief fails to explain away, with belief in B barely dropping (and sometimes rising) when a competing cause is confirmed, quantified against the Bayesian posterior; (2) a separable alternative-cause-discounting signal is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the failure causally predicts a redundant-cause endorsement mode (the model endorses B as also present despite A fully explaining E), verified by activation patching; and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief in B to the confirmation of A restores explaining-away and improves collider-reasoning accuracy without harming genuinely-independent beliefs or general capability. We evaluate on collider-inference accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ExplainAwayBelief. Each item is a COMMON-EFFECT (collider) scenario: two INDEPENDENT candidate causes A and B, each of which can produce an observed EFFECT E (A -> E <- B), plus a query on the alternative cause B. Present the scenario, confirm E occurred, then confirm A occurred, and probe belief in B. Use (a) SYNTHETIC-in-context causal graphs over nonce entities with stipulated cause independence and generative/likelihood strengths (so the exact Bayesian posterior for B given E and A is computable and priors are removed), and (b) a real-world causal subset (e.g. wet-lawn from rain-or-sprinkler; a symptom from disease-A-or-disease-B). Include matched conditions: A-CONFIRMED (explaining-away should lower belief in B), A-DISCONFIRMED / NO-CONFIRMATION baseline (belief in B should stay or rise), and a NON-COMPETING-CAUSE control (A and B do NOT share the effect / are causally unrelated, so confirming A should NOT change belief in B). Vary the generative strength of A (how fully A alone explains E). Match surface forms; human-verify collider structure, independence, and Bayesian labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Read the internal belief in the alternative cause B (i) after E is confirmed but before A (baseline) and (ii) after A is also confirmed. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the collider structure (can state that A and B are independent causes of E when asked).

Explaining-Away measurement: Define Explaining-Away Score = belief(B | E confirmed) minus belief(B | E and A both confirmed) — a normative reasoner shows a positive drop when A is a competing cause. Report per-layer, per-model score as a function of A's generative strength (stronger A should discount B more), for synthetic and real items, and compare the observed drop to the exact Bayesian discount on synthetic items. Test the hypotheses that (i) the internal drop is far below the normative discount (weak/absent explaining away, and sometimes belief in B rises — an associative co-activation), and (ii) the shortfall grows with A's generative strength. Contrast with the NON-COMPETING-CAUSE control (belief in B should NOT drop) to isolate genuine explaining-away from generic belief-suppression. Compare internal explaining-away to OUTPUT-level behavior (asking the model directly whether B occurred).

Discounting-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'alternative-cause-discounting' direction via difference-in-means on A-confirmed vs A-not-confirmed activations at the B-query position (balanced across B's truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy (is the competing-cause confirmation represented in a way that should discount B?); measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the discounting axis (and vice versa). Test whether the confirmation of A is REPRESENTED in activations but fails to modulate belief in B (a coupling failure) versus not represented at all.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the discounting direction toward 'A confirmed' at a chosen layer and measure whether belief in B and the output drop appropriately, holding the truth axis fixed. (b) Patch the A-confirmed representation into an A-not-confirmed context and measure whether belief in B is suppressed as explaining-away requires. (c) In synthetic graphs, patch the A-generative-strength representation and measure whether belief in B updates in the discount-consistent direction. Confirm that confirmation of A causally governs (or fails to govern) belief in B and is separable from the truth axis.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the (small) Explaining-Away Score predicts a redundant-cause endorsement mode: (i) the model endorsing B as also present when A fully explains E, (ii) collider-inference QA errors ('given A and E, did B occur?'), and (iii) inconsistency across A-generative-strength and paraphrase variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (A's generative strength alone, output entropy, baseline truth-probe confidence).

Explaining-Away Coupling intervention: At inference, estimate the discounting direction (from the probe) and add a scaled shift along the truth direction that lowers belief in the alternative cause B when a sufficient competing cause A is confirmed, gated by the decoded A-confirmation/generative-strength signal (ITI-style), so belief in B is coupled to the confirmation of A. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected collider structure. Sweep layer and strength.
