Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Explaining-Away Score toward the Bayesian discount, (ii) improved collider-inference accuracy (correctly lowering belief in redundant causes) on ExplainAwayBelief and adapted causal-reasoning benchmarks (collider/QUITE-style explaining-away items), (iii) calibration (ECE) against the Bayesian posterior, (iv) PRESERVATION of belief in genuinely-INDEPENDENT causes (NON-COMPETING-CAUSE control must NOT be suppressed — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting (which prior work shows can help collider reasoning), and prompt-based instruction to 'lower your belief in an alternative cause once a competing cause is confirmed to explain the effect'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), A's generative strength, synthetic vs real causal items, number of alternative causes (2 vs 3), model scale, distance between A-confirmation and the B-query, and generalization to causal structures and domains not used to fit the discounting direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent explaining-away failure could reflect the model not COMPREHENDING the collider structure (a reasoning failure, not a belief-coupling failure); we manipulation-check that the model can state A and B are independent causes of E and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

Apparent failure could reflect the probe detecting surface lexical cues rather than genuine belief; mitigate with matched surface forms, NON-COMPETING-CAUSE and NO-CONFIRMATION controls, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context graphs with exact Bayesian ground truth, and causal patching that isolates the discounting component from the truth axis.

The exact Bayesian discount is clean only for synthetic items with stipulated independence and generative strengths; real-world causal strengths are subjective, so we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic graphs and treat real items qualitatively.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to cause propositions, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic graphs to control priors, with position/layer robustness checks.

The discounting axis may be weak, entangled with the truth axis, or undecodable in some models; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that competing-cause confirmation is NOT represented in a discount-relevant way (only associatively co-activating B) is itself an informative result.

The Explaining-Away Coupling intervention could over-suppress genuinely-independent alternative causes (spurious discounting) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure preservation on NON-COMPETING-CAUSE controls and clearly-true/false accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is manufacturing incorrect discounting.

Explaining-away failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (A's generative strength, output entropy) for redundant-cause endorsement; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry fails collider explaining-away (moving the documented behavioral failure into belief representations) plus the coupling tool, reported honestly.

Prior work shows frontier LLMs sometimes reason MORE normatively than humans on colliders (less associative bias); the effect may thus be small or scale-dependent, and CoT may already induce discounting — we test multiple models/scales, compare against CoT, and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: explaining_away_belief_geometry
Title: Explaining Away in the Machine: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Discount a Cause Once a Competing Cause Is Confirmed?
Short Hypothesis: In a common-effect (collider) structure where two independent causes A and B could each produce an observed effect E, a normative reasoner who learns that both A and E occurred should LOWER its belief that B also occurred (explaining away / discounting). We hypothesize that LLM internal belief representations (the linear truth-direction readout, in the belief-probing tradition of Marks & Tegmark and Schouten et al.) FAIL to explain away: the decoded belief in the alternative cause B does not drop when a competing cause A is confirmed, so the model internally over-commits to redundant causes. We further hypothesize a separable 'alternative-cause-discounting' signal is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, that its absence causally predicts a redundant-cause endorsement error mode, and that a lightweight inference-time intervention coupling belief in B to the confirmation of A restores explaining-away.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief and shows truth directions are context-sensitive causal mediators of in-context inference (Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025), extends to multidimensional cones over propositional facts (Yu et al. 2025), tracks belief in retraction (Yang & Jia 2025), and diverges from chain-of-thought (Shiromani et al. 2026), while in-context causal-graph learning is itself decodable from activations (Kowalyshyn et al. 2026) — yet none test whether internal belief performs collider explaining-away. NONE isolate common-effect DISCOUNTING — whether internal belief in an alternative cause B drops when a competing cause A is confirmed, against an exact Bayesian posterior; whether a separable discounting signal is dissociable from the truth axis; whether its absence causally predicts a redundant-cause endorsement mode under activation patching; and whether coupling belief(B) to confirmation(A) restores explaining-away. This representational collider-discounting lens is new and distinct from coherence, dependency-propagation, inertia, and defeasible-override framings.
Abstract: When a wet lawn could be caused by rain OR a sprinkler, learning that the sprinkler was on should make rain less likely — explaining away, the diagnostic of collider reasoning. Behavioral studies increasingly probe whether large language models produce this discounting in their prompted probability judgments, but always at the output level, and belief-probing work (Marks & Tegmark 2023; Schouten et al. 2024, which shows truth directions are causal mediators of in-context inference) has never tested whether the failure lives inside the model's belief representations. We construct ExplainAwayBelief, a controlled dataset of collider scenarios over real-world causal structures and synthetic-in-context causal graphs (nonce causes/effects with stipulated independence and generative strengths, to remove parametric priors and give an exact Bayesian benchmark), with matched no-confirmation and non-competing-cause controls. We define an Explaining-Away Score (drop in belief in B when A is confirmed) and test four claims: (1) internal belief fails to explain away, with belief in B barely dropping (and sometimes rising) when a competing cause is confirmed, quantified against the Bayesian posterior; (2) a separable alternative-cause-discounting signal is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis; (3) the failure causally predicts a redundant-cause endorsement mode, verified by activation patching; and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief in B to the confirmation of A restores explaining-away and improves collider-reasoning accuracy without harming genuinely-independent beliefs or general capability. We evaluate on collider-inference accuracy, calibration, and capability retention.

Each item is a COMMON-EFFECT (collider) scenario: two INDEPENDENT candidate causes A and B, each able to produce an observed EFFECT E (A -> E <- B), plus a query on the alternative cause B. Present the scenario, confirm E occurred, then confirm A occurred, and probe belief in B. Use (a) SYNTHETIC-in-context causal graphs over nonce entities with stipulated cause independence and generative/likelihood strengths (so the exact Bayesian posterior for B given E and A is computable and priors are removed), and (b) a real-world causal subset (wet-lawn from rain-or-sprinkler; a symptom from disease-A-or-disease-B). Include matched conditions: A-CONFIRMED (explaining-away should lower belief in B), A-DISCONFIRMED / NO-CONFIRMATION baseline (belief in B should stay or rise), and a NON-COMPETING-CAUSE control (A and B do NOT share the effect, so confirming A should NOT change belief in B). Vary the generative strength of A (how fully A alone explains E). Match surface forms; human-verify collider structure, independence, and Bayesian labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends the collider structure (can state that A and B are independent causes of E when asked).

Explaining-Away measurement: Define Explaining-Away Score = belief(B | E confirmed) minus belief(B | E and A both confirmed) — a normative reasoner shows a positive drop when A is a competing cause. Report per-layer, per-model score as a function of A's generative strength (stronger A should discount B more), for synthetic and real items, and compare the observed drop to the exact Bayesian discount on synthetic items. Test the hypotheses that (i) the internal drop is far below the normative discount (weak/absent explaining away, and sometimes belief in B rises — an associative co-activation), and (ii) the shortfall grows with A's generative strength. Contrast with the NON-COMPETING-CAUSE control (belief in B should NOT drop) to isolate genuine explaining-away from generic belief-suppression. Test whether the confirmation of A is REPRESENTED in activations but fails to modulate belief in B (a coupling failure) versus not represented at all.

(b) Patch the A-confirmed representation into an A-not-confirmed context and measure whether belief in B is suppressed as explaining-away requires. (c) In synthetic graphs, patch the A-generative-strength representation and measure whether belief in B updates in the discount-consistent direction. Confirm that confirmation of A causally governs (or fails to govern) belief in B and is separable from the truth axis.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the (small) Explaining-Away Score predicts a redundant-cause endorsement mode: (i) the model endorsing B as also present when A fully explains E, (ii) collider-inference QA errors ('given A and E, did B occur?'), and (iii) inconsistency across A-generative-strength and paraphrase variants. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought prompting, and prompt-based instruction to 'lower your belief in an alternative cause once a competing cause is confirmed to explain the effect'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), A's generative strength, synthetic vs real causal items, number of alternative causes (2 vs 3), model scale, distance between A-confirmation and the B-query, and generalization to causal structures and domains not used to fit the discounting direction.

Name: action_vs_evaluation_belief_gap
Title: Believing in Order to Act: Does an LLM's Internal Belief in a Proposition Change When It Must Act on It Rather Than Merely Evaluate It?
Short Hypothesis: Holding a factual proposition's content and truth-value fixed, framing the task so the model must ACT on the proposition (commit to a plan/decision that presupposes it) versus merely EVALUATE its truth systematically shifts the model's INTERNAL belief in it (linear truth-direction readout): action-framing inflates belief in propositions the plan depends on (an action-commitment 'settling' effect), pushing the model to treat uncertain premises as settled once it starts acting. This action-vs-evaluation belief gap is graded in how strongly the action commits to the premise, carried by a decodable action-commitment component dissociable from the truth axis, causally predicts an act-on-uncertainty failure mode (proceeding confidently on premises the model would flag as uncertain under evaluation), and can be neutralized by a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the action-commitment component.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies whether the model must ACT on a proposition versus merely EVALUATE its truth, holding content and truth-value fixed. My prior 'belief_actionability_gap' compared what the model internally believes against what it will act on, but did not test whether the ACT framing itself feeds back to inflate the underlying belief; 'premature_belief_commitment' studied belief hardening before sufficient evidence; 'self_commitment_belief_anchoring' anchored belief to the model's own prior assertion; 'counterfactual_stakes_belief_courage' varied decision stakes. NONE isolate action-commitment SETTLING — whether framing a task so the model produces a plan that presupposes a premise inflates internal belief in that premise relative to a matched evaluation frame carrying no new evidence, whether the shift is graded in how heavily the plan depends on the premise, whether a decodable action-commitment component is dissociable from the truth axis, whether its magnitude causally predicts an act-on-uncertainty failure mode, and whether subtracting it restores content-driven belief and appropriate uncertainty-flagging. This action-versus-evaluation settling lens on belief geometry — central to agentic deployments where a model may internally doubt a fact yet proceed as if certain — is new and distinct from actionability-gap, premature-commitment, self-anchoring, and stakes framings.
Abstract: A careful agent should not believe a premise more firmly just because it has started acting on it — yet people notoriously 'settle' a shaky assumption once committed to a plan that depends on it. We ask whether large language models exhibit this action-commitment settling inside their belief representations, a distinction with sharp consequences for agentic deployments where a model may internally doubt a fact yet proceed as if certain. Holding a proposition's content and truth-value fixed, we vary only the task frame: EVALUATION (judge whether the proposition is true) versus ACTION (produce a plan/decision that presupposes the proposition), and read the internal belief via difference-in-means and logistic truth probes along the linear truth direction. We construct ActBelief, a controlled dataset of true, false, and synthetic-in-context propositions each embedded in matched evaluation vs action frames that carry no new evidence about the proposition, with action-commitment strength graded (the plan lightly vs heavily depends on the premise) and surface length matched. We define an Action-Evaluation Belief Gap = belief(proposition | action frame) minus belief(proposition | evaluation frame), and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated (settled) under action framing at fixed content and truth, graded in commitment strength, even for false or uncertain premises; (2) the shift is carried by a decodable action-commitment component dissociable from the truth axis; (3) gap magnitude causally predicts an act-on-uncertainty failure mode (proceeding confidently on premises the model would flag uncertain under evaluation); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the action-commitment component restores content-driven belief and appropriate uncertainty-flagging without harming legitimate planning or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, agentic-safety consistency, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ActBelief. Propositions P in three truth regimes: real-true, real-false, and synthetic-in-context facts (defined only in context, to remove parametric priors). Each P is embedded in matched task frames that carry no new evidence about P: EVALUATION ('Is it true that P? / How confident are you that P?') vs ACTION ('Given the situation, produce a plan/decision to achieve goal G', where the plan can only succeed if P holds, so acting presupposes P). Grade ACTION-COMMITMENT strength (the plan lightly depends on P vs is fully premised on P). Include action frames whose success presupposes true P and whose success presupposes false P (so the settling effect is separable from generic agreeableness/truth-tracking), plus a NEUTRAL baseline. Match surface length; human-verify the action frame adds no evidence about P and correctly encodes the dependence; include paraphrase sets and a genuinely-uncertain-premise subset.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is P true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief in P under each frame; also record the OUTPUT (verdict/confidence under evaluation; whether the plan proceeds on P or flags it under action). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the model registers the frame (evaluation elicits a judgment; action elicits a plan presupposing P).

Action-Evaluation Belief Gap measurement: Define Gap = belief(P | action frame) minus belief(P | evaluation frame), holding content and truth fixed. Report per-layer, per-model gap across commitment strength and truth regimes. Test the hypotheses that (i) belief is settled/inflated under action framing, (ii) the gap grows with action-commitment strength, and (iii) crucially, on uncertain/false premises action framing pushes belief toward settled/true where evaluation would hold it uncertain/false. Compare internal gap to OUTPUT-level behavior (does the model flag P as uncertain when evaluating but proceed on it as settled when acting?).

Action-commitment-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'action-commitment' direction via difference-in-means on action-frame vs evaluation-frame activations at the P-query position (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode the action-commitment axis (and vice versa); test whether the gap is explained by the action-commitment component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between action-frame and evaluation-frame processing of the same P, decompose into truth-direction and action-commitment components, patch only the action-commitment component into the evaluation condition and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract it under the action frame and measure whether belief returns to the content-driven (evaluation) value. Confirm the action-commitment signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of content.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Gap predicts an act-on-uncertainty failure mode: (i) the model proceeding confidently on a false/uncertain premise under action framing that it would flag as uncertain/false under evaluation, (ii) failure to insert a hedge/verification step for shaky premises when planning, and (iii) inconsistency between the evaluation verdict and the action-frame reliance on P. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (commitment-strength indicator, output entropy, evaluation-frame truth-probe confidence).

Action-Commitment De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the action-commitment direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style) while the model plans, so belief in premises reflects their content/evidence rather than the fact that acting presupposes them. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected action/planning frames. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream and agentic-safety evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Action-Evaluation Belief Gap, (ii) improved evaluation-action consistency (the model flags/verifies uncertain premises before acting rather than settling them), (iii) factuality/calibration (ECE) of premise belief under action framing, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate planning ability (the model must still produce coherent plans; measured by an LLM/human plan-quality rubric) and accuracy on neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, prompt-based instruction to 'verify uncertain premises before acting on them', and a fresh-context re-ask baseline (evaluate P without the action frame).

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), commitment strength, action frame presupposing true vs false P, real vs synthetic facts, model scale, distance between the frame and the belief query, and generalization to action/planning frames not used to fit the de-biasing direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent action-vs-evaluation gap could reflect the probe detecting action-frame lexical cues rather than a genuine belief shift; mitigate with surface-length matching, action-presupposing-true vs -false contrasts, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context facts, and causal patching that isolates the action-commitment component.

The action frame might inadvertently supply weak evidence for P (a plan that assumes P could imply P is likely); we human-verify the frame adds no evidence about P and analyze any residual evidential leakage as a separately-analyzed confound.

The effect may be purely at the OUTPUT/strategic level (the model plans on P while internally doubting it, or vice versa); the internal-vs-output comparison and causal patching directly test this, and either outcome — belief settling internally, or a dissociation where the plan proceeds on a still-doubted premise — is itself a safety-relevant finding for agentic deployments.

Truth probes trained on neutral statements may transfer imperfectly to action/planning contexts, so the gap could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, and synthetic facts to control priors.
Action-commitment and truth directions may be partly entangled in some models, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could impair legitimate planning (making the model refuse to plan under any uncertainty) or harm fluency; we explicitly measure plan-quality preservation, neutral-control accuracy, and capability retention to characterize the planning-vs-caution tradeoff.

The gap may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (commitment-strength indicator, output entropy) for act-on-uncertainty failures; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that acting on a premise settles internal belief in it (an action-commitment effect in belief geometry, distinct from evaluation) plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

The effect may be null or reversed in some models; a null is itself informative about whether action framing settles belief in LLM belief geometry. Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (agentic tuning may amplify action-commitment settling); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: latent_contradiction_belief_detection
Title: Does It Notice Its Own Contradictions? Testing Whether LLM Belief Geometry Spontaneously Flags Mutually-Inconsistent Co-Held Beliefs
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is made to co-hold two beliefs that are mutually inconsistent (they cannot both be true) WITHOUT ever being asked to compare them, a competent believer should carry an internal 'incoherence alarm' — a representation that its belief set is inconsistent, driving down confidence in at least one belief. We hypothesize LLM belief geometry does NOT spontaneously flag latent contradiction: both inconsistent beliefs are internally held near-true with no drop, so the model harbors an undetected contradiction until explicitly prompted to reconcile them. We further hypothesize a weak 'inconsistency-detection' signal is decodable and dissociable from the per-proposition truth axis, its absence causally predicts a confidently-self-contradictory answer mode, and a lightweight inference-time intervention that couples belief to the decoded inconsistency signal reduces self-contradiction.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief per proposition but never tests whether the model spontaneously REGISTERS that two separately-held beliefs are mutually inconsistent when it is never asked to compare them. My prior 'belief_coherence_geometry' tested whether beliefs SATISFY logical rules when a proposition network is laid out for evaluation; 'dependency_structured_belief_revision' propagated updates through a stated dependency graph; 'conjunction_belief_monotonicity' checked monotone behavior across conjunctions; 'metabelief_alignment' compared a belief to the model's meta-level report of it. NONE isolate SPONTANEOUS latent-contradiction detection — whether, given two inconsistent claims embedded separately and never juxtaposed, an internal 'incoherence alarm' fires (confidence in at least one member dropping) without any reconcile prompt, whether it weakens as the inference needed to see the clash deepens, whether a weak inconsistency-detection signal is decodable and dissociable from the per-proposition truth axis, whether its absence causally predicts a confidently-self-contradictory answer mode under activation patching, and whether coupling belief to the decoded signal reduces self-contradiction. This unprompted incoherence-alarm lens is new and distinct from rule-satisfaction, dependency-propagation, conjunction-monotonicity, and metabelief framings.
Abstract: A hallmark of a coherent believer is spontaneously noticing when two things it holds cannot both be true — an internal alarm that fires before anyone points out the clash. We ask whether large language models possess such an alarm inside their belief representations, or whether they placidly co-hold mutually-inconsistent beliefs until explicitly asked to reconcile them. Distinct from prior work that tests whether beliefs SATISFY logical rules when a proposition network is laid out for evaluation, we test whether the model, given two inconsistent claims embedded separately in context and never juxtaposed, internally REGISTERS the latent inconsistency at all. Using difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the truth direction, and a separately-fit inconsistency-detection signal, we present belief pairs that are consistent or mutually inconsistent (one directly contradictory, one requiring a short inference to see the clash) without any reconcile prompt, and read the internal belief in each member plus a decodable 'my belief set is inconsistent' signal. We build ContraDetectBelief over synthetic-in-context and real facts, with inconsistency-inference depth graded and matched consistent controls. We define an Incoherence-Alarm Score (does confidence in at least one member drop, or an inconsistency signal fire, when the pair is inconsistent vs consistent?) and test four claims: (1) belief geometry fails to spontaneously flag latent contradiction, holding both members near-true with no alarm, worsening as the inference to see the clash deepens; (2) a weak inconsistency-detection signal is nonetheless decodable and dissociable from the per-proposition truth axis; (3) its absence causally predicts a confidently-self-contradictory answer mode (the model asserts both members when queried separately); and (4) a lightweight intervention coupling belief to the decoded inconsistency signal reduces self-contradiction without harming genuinely-consistent belief sets or general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on self-consistency, calibration, and capability retention.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build ContraDetectBelief. Each item embeds TWO belief-establishing statements SEPARATELY in a context (not juxtaposed, no instruction to compare or reconcile), then probes each member's belief plus a latent-inconsistency readout. Cross PAIR-TYPE {CONSISTENT (both can be true), DIRECTLY-INCONSISTENT (P and not-P about the same item), INFERENTIALLY-INCONSISTENT (their clash requires a short 1-2 step inference, e.g. 'X is older than Y' and 'Y is older than X' via a chain)} with INFERENCE DEPTH (how many steps to see the contradiction: 0 for direct, 1, 2). Use SYNTHETIC-in-context facts over nonce entities (guaranteeing the intended (in)consistency and removing priors) plus a real-fact subset. Include matched surface forms and separation distance between the two statements. Human-verify (in)consistency and inference-depth labels; include paraphrase sets.

Belief and inconsistency readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. After both statements are in context (no reconcile prompt), read the internal belief in EACH member. Separately, fit an 'inconsistency-detection' direction via difference-in-means contrasting inconsistent vs consistent pair contexts (balanced on content and member truth-values). Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false items; confirm the model comprehends each statement in isolation.

Incoherence-Alarm measurement: Define Incoherence-Alarm Score = the drop in confidence (firmness, |belief-0.5|) in at least one member when the pair is INCONSISTENT vs a matched CONSISTENT control, plus whether the decoded inconsistency signal fires. A coherent believer should show a drop / signal; we hypothesize near-zero (no spontaneous alarm), and that the alarm weakens with inference depth (direct clash noticed more than inferential). Report per-layer, per-model as a function of pair-type, inference depth, and separation distance. Compare internal alarm to OUTPUT-level behavior (when the two statements are finally juxtaposed and the model asked, does it notice the contradiction?).

Inconsistency-axis discovery and dissociation: Report per-layer decoding accuracy of the inconsistency-detection direction (is latent inconsistency represented at all, absent any reconcile prompt?); measure cosine similarity with the per-proposition truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode inconsistency (and vice versa). Test whether inconsistency is REPRESENTED but fails to modulate member belief (a coupling failure) versus not represented at all. Control for surface cues via matched consistent items sharing the same entities and a features-only baseline.

Causal validation: Activation patching. (a) Steer along the inconsistency-detection direction toward 'inconsistent' at a chosen layer and measure whether firmness in the members drops and the model becomes more likely to flag the clash, holding the truth axis fixed. (b) Patch the inconsistency representation from a juxtaposed-and-noticed pair into a separated (un-noticed) pair and measure induced alarm. Confirm the inconsistency signal is causal and separable from the truth axis; confirm consistent controls are unaffected.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the (small) Incoherence-Alarm Score predicts a confidently-self-contradictory answer mode: (i) the model asserting both inconsistent members when each is queried separately, (ii) failure to spontaneously note the contradiction when the pair is later surfaced, and (iii) inconsistency across inference-depth and paraphrase variants. Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (inference depth alone, separation distance, output entropy, per-member truth-probe confidence).

Inconsistency-Coupling intervention: At inference, estimate the inconsistency-detection direction (from the probe) and couple it to member belief — an ITI-style shift that lowers firmness in the members (toward appropriate revisability / flagging) when latent inconsistency is detected, gated by the decoded signal. Provide a deployment variant that scans for detected inconsistent pairs in context. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) increased Incoherence-Alarm Score / earlier detection of latent contradictions, (ii) reduced confidently-self-contradictory answers (the model hedges or flags rather than asserting both members) on ContraDetectBelief and adapted self-consistency benchmarks, (iii) calibration (ECE), (iv) PRESERVATION of confident belief in genuinely-CONSISTENT sets (must NOT manufacture spurious inconsistency alarms — the core specificity check) and accuracy on clearly-true/false items, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, chain-of-thought ('check whether anything you were told contradicts anything else'), and prompt-based instruction to 'flag if two facts you hold cannot both be true'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), pair-type (direct vs inferential), inference depth, separation distance between the two statements, synthetic vs real facts, model scale, and generalization to inconsistency structures and domains not used to fit the inconsistency direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent failure to flag latent contradiction could reflect the model not COMPREHENDING one member (a comprehension failure, not a detection failure); we manipulation-check each statement in isolation and analyze comprehended vs non-comprehended items separately.

The inconsistency-detection axis may merely detect surface lexical clash (repeated entities with opposite predicates) rather than genuine incoherence representation; mitigate with matched consistent items sharing the same entities, inferential-inconsistency items (no surface clash), a features-only baseline, paraphrase controls, and causal patching that isolates the inconsistency component.

Firmness measured as |belief-0.5| may conflate with the truth axis; we corroborate with a separate firmness readout, project out the truth direction, and report sensitivity to the firmness definition.

Truth probes trained on single statements may transfer imperfectly to two-statement contexts, so scores could carry probe extrapolation error; use multiple probe types, isolated-statement manipulation checks, and synthetic pairs with guaranteed (in)consistency, with position/layer robustness checks.

The inconsistency axis may be weak, entangled with the truth axis, or undecodable in some models; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this, and a finding that latent inconsistency is NOT spontaneously represented is itself an informative result about whether LLMs harbor undetected contradictions.

The Inconsistency-Coupling intervention could manufacture spurious alarms on genuinely-consistent sets or harm fluency; we explicitly measure CONSISTENT-set preservation and capability retention to characterize the tradeoff — the core risk is false-positive contradiction flags.

The alarm-failure may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (inference depth, separation distance, output entropy) for self-contradiction; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry does not spontaneously flag latent contradiction among co-held beliefs (distinct from static logical-rule coherence, which tests juxtaposed networks) plus the coupling tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (reasoning-tuning may improve spontaneous consistency-checking); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.

Name: checkability_belief_conflation
Title: Looks Checkable, So It Must Be True: Do LLM Internal Beliefs Conflate a Claim's Verifiability With Its Truth?
Short Hypothesis: A competent believer distinguishes whether a claim is TRUE from whether it is CHECKABLE (there exists an accessible procedure/source that could verify it). We hypothesize LLM internal belief representations (linear truth-direction readouts) CONFLATE checkability with truth: the decoded belief in a claim is inflated when the claim merely LOOKS verifiable (cites a source, gives a precise checkable-format value, invokes a lookup) even when it is false and no verification is actually performed, so 'this appears checkable' is read as 'this is true'. A separable 'apparent-checkability' axis is decodable and dissociable from the truth axis, its leakage causally predicts a spurious-verifiability hallucination mode (endorsing fabricated-but-checkable-looking claims), and a lightweight inference-time intervention that removes the checkability component reduces this failure.
Related Work: Truth-direction/belief probing (Marks & Tegmark 2023; ITI, Li et al. 2023; Schouten et al. 2024; Bao et al. 2025 ACL) reads a scalar internal belief but never varies a claim's APPARENT CHECKABILITY (its surface machinery of verifiability — a named source, a precise checkable-format value, an invoked lookup) while holding truth fixed. Knowledge-boundary work denoises a latent 'do I know this' region (Purging the Gray Zone, An et al. 2026), but concerns awareness of one's own knowledge, not conflating a claim's verifiability with its truth. My prior 'falsifiability_belief_geometry' varied whether a claim is falsifiable-in-principle; 'plausibility_vs_truth_belief' dissociated plausibility from truth; 'evidentiality_belief_geometry' varied first-hand versus hearsay MODE of knowing; 'source_reliability_belief_weighting' tracked a source's track record. NONE isolate APPARENT-CHECKABILITY conflation — whether decoded belief is inflated when a claim merely LOOKS verifiable (fabricated-but-formatted citations, precise verifiable-format statistics) even when false and unverified, whether a decodable apparent-checkability axis is dissociable from the truth axis via project-out, whether its leakage causally predicts a spurious-verifiability hallucination mode under patching, and whether subtracting the checkability component recalibrates belief while preserving genuine verification. This checkability-truth conflation lens — mapping onto fabricated-but-verifiable-looking hallucination — is new and distinct from falsifiability, plausibility, evidential-mode, and track-record framings.
Abstract: A fabricated citation with volume and page numbers looks eminently checkable, yet is false; a vague true statement looks uncheckable, yet is true. Verifiability and truth are different properties, but a careless believer treats the trappings of checkability as evidence of truth. We ask whether large language models make this confusion inside their belief representations. Distinguishing a claim's TRUTH from its APPARENT CHECKABILITY (does it carry the surface machinery of verifiability — a named source, a precise checkable-format value, an invoked lookup — without any verification actually being done), we use difference-in-means and logistic truth probes to read a scalar internal belief along the linear truth direction. We construct CheckBelief, a controlled dataset that orthogonally crosses ground-truth truth-value with apparent checkability: true and false claims each rendered in high-checkability form (fabricated or genuine citations, precise verifiable-format statistics, source attributions) versus low-checkability form (vague, unsourced), restricted to claims the model cannot resolve from parametric knowledge and including synthetic-in-context items, with surface content matched. We define a Checkability Belief Bias Score = belief inflation from high- vs low-checkability framing at fixed truth, and test four claims: (1) internal belief is inflated by apparent checkability at fixed truth, graded in the checkability trappings, even for false claims; (2) a decodable apparent-checkability axis is dissociable from the truth axis via project-out analyses; (3) bias magnitude causally predicts a spurious-verifiability hallucination mode (confidently endorsing fabricated-but-checkable-looking claims, e.g. fake citations/statistics); and (4) a lightweight intervention that subtracts the checkability component recalibrates belief and reduces the failure while preserving legitimate use of genuine verification and general capability. We validate causality via activation patching and evaluate on factuality, calibration, hallucination-detection AUROC, and capability retention. Because fabricated-but-verifiable-looking content (fake references, invented precise numbers) is a canonical high-stakes hallucination, a checkability-truth conflation in belief geometry maps onto a concrete reliability risk.
Experiments: Dataset construction: Build CheckBelief, orthogonally crossing TRUTH {true, false} with APPARENT CHECKABILITY {high, low}. HIGH-checkability items carry the surface machinery of verifiability WITHOUT any verification being performed: a named citation/reference (with volume/page/DOI-like format), a precise checkable-format statistic (exact figure, date, measurement), or an explicit source attribution ('according to <named database>'). LOW-checkability items state the same claim vaguely and unsourced. Crucially, both true and false claims appear in high- and low-checkability forms (a FALSE-high item = a fabricated citation/statistic that looks checkable; a TRUE-low item = a true but vague unsourced claim). Restrict to claims the model cannot resolve from parametric knowledge (obscure real facts verified at chance/high-entropy, plus SYNTHETIC-in-context claims about nonce entities) so belief cannot rely on stored knowledge. Match surface content/length within each truth cell across checkability levels; human-verify truth, checkability, and that no actual verification is available in context; include neutral controls and paraphrase sets.

Belief readout: For 4-5 open models spanning scale (Llama-3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2 9B), train per-layer truth probes (difference-in-means and logistic regression) on an INDEPENDENT set of neutral, checkability-balanced true/false statements (Marks & Tegmark style), Platt-scaled to a scalar belief in [0,1]. At a matched query position (a canonical 'is this claim true?' probe appended in a fresh pass) read the internal belief for each CheckBelief item. Manipulation check: probes separate clearly-true/false neutral items; confirm the high-checkability items are genuinely unverifiable in-context (the model, when asked, agrees no verification was actually done) and that the model comprehends the claim.

Checkability Belief Bias measurement: Holding truth fixed, define Checkability Belief Bias Score = mean belief(high-checkability) minus mean belief(low-checkability), computed WITHIN the true cell and WITHIN the false cell separately. Report per-layer, per-model bias across checkability-cue types (citation / precise-value / source-attribution) and item source (obscure-real vs synthetic). Test the hypotheses that (i) apparent checkability inflates belief at fixed truth, and (ii) the inflation grows with the amount/strength of verifiability trappings. Crucially, the FALSE-high cell tests whether fabricated-but-checkable-looking claims are believed too true, and the TRUE-low cell whether vague truths are under-believed. Compare internal bias to OUTPUT-level bias (does the model's verdict/confidence rise with apparent checkability?).

Checkability-axis discovery and dissociation: Fit an 'apparent-checkability' direction via difference-in-means on high- vs low-checkability activations (balanced across truth-value and content). Report per-layer decoding accuracy; measure cosine similarity with the truth direction; project out the truth direction and re-decode checkability (and vice versa); disentangle checkability from surface features (precision/detail, source-word presence, token length) via a controlled regression; test whether the bias is explained by the checkability component leaking into the truth-probe readout.

Causal validation: Activation patching. Take the activation difference between a high-checkability and a matched low-checkability rendering of the same claim (fixed truth), decompose into truth-direction and checkability components, patch only the checkability component into the low-checkability condition and measure induced belief inflation; conversely subtract the checkability component from a high-checkability item and measure whether belief moves toward the truth-appropriate value. Confirm the checkability signal causally shifts the belief scalar independent of truth.

Predictive validity: At the item level, test whether the Checkability Belief Bias Score predicts a spurious-verifiability hallucination mode: (i) endorsement rate of FALSE-high items (fabricated-but-checkable-looking claims — fake citations, invented precise statistics), (ii) under-endorsement of TRUE-low items, and (iii) hallucination-detection AUROC (does the checkability-corrected belief better separate true from false unverifiable claims?). Report AUC/correlation vs baselines (checkability rating alone, output-token entropy, truth-probe confidence magnitude, precision/detail score).

Checkability De-biasing intervention: At inference, estimate the apparent-checkability direction (from the probe) and subtract its projection from the residual stream at a chosen layer (ITI-style), so the belief readout reflects truth-relevant evidence rather than the surface trappings of verifiability. Provide a deployment variant gated on detected high-checkability cues. Sweep layer and strength.

Downstream evaluation: Measure post-intervention (i) reduced Checkability Belief Bias Score, (ii) reduced endorsement of fabricated-but-checkable-looking claims (fake-citation / invented-statistic endorsement rate) and reduced under-endorsement of true-vague claims, (iii) hallucination-detection AUROC and calibration/risk-coverage on a mixed set including fabricated-citation and precise-false items, (iv) PRESERVATION of legitimate verification behavior (when genuine verifiable evidence IS present in context, belief should still update) and accuracy on clearly-true/false neutral controls, and (v) capability retention on MMLU and perplexity. Baselines: no intervention, standard ITI truth steering, output-entropy thresholding, and prompt-based instruction to 'judge whether the claim is true, not whether it looks verifiable'.

Ablations: layer choice, probe type (diff-in-means vs logistic), checkability-cue type (citation / precise-value / source-attribution), checkability strength, obscure-real vs synthetic-in-context items, true vs false cell, model scale, checkability-vs-precision/detail/length disentangling, and generalization to checkability cues and domains not used to fit the direction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The apparent-checkability axis might merely detect surface features (numbers, citation-format tokens, precision, length) rather than a genuine 'this is verifiable' representation; mitigate with surface-form/length matching within truth cells, a precision/detail/length-controlled regression, paraphrase controls, synthetic-in-context items, and causal patching — a finding that checkability reduces to precision/detail (relating to a vividness/detail effect) is itself an informative, explicitly-analyzed result.

Checkability may overlap with plausibility (checkable-looking claims may also seem more plausible); we include a plausibility rating as a covariate, contrast against a plausibility-only predictor, and treat the relationship to plausibility as an explicit analysis rather than a hidden confound.

Truth probes trained on neutral items may transfer imperfectly to unverifiable claims, so the bias could partly reflect probe extrapolation, and for genuinely-unknown items truth may be intrinsically hard to decode; use multiple probe types, manipulation checks on clearly-true/false items, synthetic-in-context items with stipulated ground truth, and report where the truth axis is reliable.

Constructing items that are truly unverifiable-in-context yet have a clean ground-truth truth-value is nontrivial; we anchor quantitative claims on synthetic-in-context items and human-verified obscure facts, analyzing the two separately.
Checkability and truth directions may be partly entangled, weakening the dissociation claim; the orthogonality/project-out analyses directly test this and a null is informative.

The De-biasing intervention could over-hedge (making verifiable-looking true claims uncertain) or degrade legitimate use of genuine verification/citations; we explicitly measure preservation of legitimate-verification updating and clearly-true/false accuracy plus capability retention to characterize the tradeoff.

The checkability bias may correlate with but not exceed simpler predictors (checkability rating, precision, plausibility, output entropy) for spurious-verifiability hallucination; if so, the contribution is the mechanistic/causal finding that belief geometry conflates apparent verifiability with truth (i.e., 'truth' probes partly read checkability), plus the de-biasing tool, reported honestly.

Effects may vary across model families, scales, and post-training (RLHF may amplify trust in citation-like formatting); we test multiple models and report scale/post-training effects and negative results as informative.
